title: About Things Happening
description: Things Happening is a local events and guides publisher for Chattanooga, TN, run by Jack Byrum. No algorithm, no login; just what's happening and where.
body: Who runs this . Things Happening is run by Jack Byrum, based in Chattanooga. He started the site in 2024 because finding out what was happening in the city required checking too many places at once. The goal is one place that covers events, guides, and local knowledge with easy to use tools. The site reaches 10,000+ readers each month. Chattanooga has a lot going on and we're here to help. We cover events, outdoor adventures, coffee shops, restaurants, live music, and history. All in one place. The calendar updates daily and the guides are built to filter, not just scroll. Simplicity . Finding things to do shouldn't require digging through five different websites. Events, guides, and search are all here, so you spend less time looking and more time going. One URL covers the whole city. Engaging . Our guides are interactive and filterable, not walls of text. We include photos, practical details, and links so you can actually plan something, not just read about it. The event calendar surfaces what's coming up so you're not finding out after the fact. You can also star events and guide items to save them for later. Straightforward . No fluff or filler. An event listing tells you what it is, where it is, and what it costs. Guides have quick filtering and content items that don't waste your time. If a detail is missing, we note it rather than guess. Platform independent . You shouldn't need a Facebook account to find out what's happening in your city. No login, no algorithm, no feed to scroll. Everything is public and indexed. But if you're on Facebook, we're there too — find us at Things Happening Chattanooga . Discoverability . Everything is tagged and searchable. Whether you're looking for a kid-friendly hike, live music this weekend, or a coffee shop to work from, tags and search make it easy to find what fits. Browse by tag on the events tags page or filter inside any guide. FAQ . How do I get my event listed? Email jack@thingshappening.com with the event name, venue, date, time, and a link. We review and add qualifying events within a day or two. What kinds of events do you cover? Live music, outdoor events, theater, comedy, food and drink events, markets, community gatherings, and sports. We do not cover private events or paid promotions. Do you cover events outside Chattanooga? Yes. The nearby cities page covers towns within about an hour of Chattanooga; Cleveland, Ringgold, Ooltewah, and others. Questions, tips, or feedback: jack@thingshappening.com

title: Contact
body: No contact form, no chatbot. If you have something genuine to say, email us at jack@thingshappening.com We read every message and reply when it's relevant to the site. Interested in working with us? See our sponsorship page . What we're open to . Collaborations: Guest posts, cross-promotion, or working together on content about things to do in and around Chattanooga. Corrections and feedback: Spotted a factual error, broken link, or have a genuine suggestion to improve a guide? Let us know. Questions: Anything about events, places, or content covered on this site. What we won't reply to . Marketing pitches, link exchange requests, or partnership spam Requests for personalized travel planning or custom itineraries Promotional content that doesn't fit the site's focus on local guides and events

title: Breweries & Wineries Near Chattanooga, TN - 21 Locations
description: An interactive guide to breweries, wineries, and cideries in and within an hour of Chattanooga: taprooms, wine trails, and day-trip spots in North Georgia.
body: ; ; ( })) })} /> This guide covers 21 breweries, wineries, cideries, and a distillery. Twelve are in Chattanooga or just across the city line. The rest are within about an hour's drive, mostly in North Georgia and East Tennessee. Chattanooga's craft brewing scene expanded steadily through the 2010s. The downtown cluster around Market Street and East MLK Boulevard anchors the scene. Southside, St. Elmo, and East Brainerd added taprooms over the years. Wanderlinger, Oddstory, and Hutton & Smith are the names locals mention most. Several Southside taprooms also host live music on weekends. The live music guide covers those venues in detail. The North Georgia day trip is a different kind of outing. The Cartecay River valley near Ellijay runs through Georgia wine country. Mercier Orchards covers the cider side of that trip. Cartecay Vineyards and Engelheim are within a few miles of each other. Fall weekends fill up fast in that area. Use the Type filter to separate breweries from wineries, cideries, and the distillery. Under Experience, Scenic narrows to spots where the setting is part of the draw. Dog friendly surfaces taprooms and beer gardens that welcome dogs. Food menu flags spots where you can eat well, not just drink. Missing a spot? Send an email with the name and a note on why it belongs. Map View of the Locations Featured Below Type : Brewery Winery Cidery Distillery Experience : Try Me ↓ ← Try Me Outdoor seating Food menu Taproom only Live music Dog friendly Tours & tastings Scenic Kid friendly Location : Downtown Southside North Shore Blue Ridge GA Dalton GA Cleveland TN St. Elmo Guild TN Jasper TN Ringgold GA East Brainerd Downtown Chattanooga . Market Street, Chestnut Street, and the Innovation District cluster most of Chattanooga's brewing history. This is where the scene started and where the most established taprooms and brewpubs are. Walkable to the riverfront and most Southside bars. Downtown coffee North Shore & Frazier Ave . Brewhaus sits on Frazier Ave a short walk from Coolidge Park and the Walnut Street Bridge. It's a bar rather than a brewery, but the tap selection and location make it the obvious North Shore stop for a post-walk pint. Outdoor adventures guide Southside & East Main . East Main and the Southside corridor hold some of the city's most active taprooms, with outdoor beer gardens and a live music presence on weekends. Easy to string together with dinner on the same stretch. Live music guide Blue Ridge & Ellijay, GA . About 55 minutes south of Chattanooga, the Cartecay River valley runs through some of Georgia's best wine country. Mercier Orchards anchors the cider side of the trip; Cartecay and Engelheim vineyards cover the wine trail. Blue Ridge's downtown strip has its own brewery and enough restaurants to make a full day of it. Go early on weekends. The town fills up fast in fall foliage season. Cleveland & Charleston, TN . About 25–30 minutes north of Chattanooga on 75. Morris Vineyard in Charleston is the closest winery to the city in this guide. Mash & Hops in downtown Cleveland covers the craft beer side. Pair the two for a low-key Tennessee day trip that doesn't require crossing into Georgia. St. Elmo . Historic neighborhood at the base of Lookout Mountain. The Tap House fits naturally into a St. Elmo afternoon: Incline Railway, a walk down Tennessee Ave, then a pint before heading back up the ridge. Lookout Mountain outdoors St. Elmo coffee Jasper Highlands, TN . About 35 minutes northwest of Chattanooga on the Cumberland Plateau above the Tennessee River Gorge. Top of the Rock is a brewpub with plateau views that make it a destination in its own right. Plan an afternoon. Guild, TN . A short drive west of downtown on US-41, just past Raccoon Mountain. Lookout Winery sits on a bluff with Tennessee River views. It earns its own afternoon. Raccoon Mountain outdoors Ringgold, GA . Six miles south of Chattanooga at I-75 Exit 350. The Georgia Winery is the closest winery to the city in this guide. It is barely a day trip. Dalton, GA . About 30 minutes south on I-75. Not a craft beer destination yet, but Dalton Brewing holds its own for a city that size. Easy add-on if you're already heading south. East Brainerd . Chattanooga's fast-growing east side, about 20 minutes from downtown. Mean King Brewing on Jenkins Road is the first craft brewery to plant a flag out here, so it stands on its own for now. Worth a stop if you live nearby or are heading toward Ooltewah. Most taprooms in this guide sell cans and bottles to go. Ask at the bar if you want something to take home. Hutton & Smith and Chattanooga Brewing Company both carry their core lineup in cans. If you're planning the Blue Ridge day trip, go early on fall weekends. Blue Ridge fills up fast during foliage season. Mercier Orchards, Cartecay, and Engelheim are within a 10-minute drive of each other. You can visit all three in a single afternoon. This guide is updated as new spots open and existing ones change. If something's moved, closed, or we missed a good one, send a note . A name and a quick reason it belongs is all we need. FAQ . What are the popular breweries in downtown Chattanooga? Hutton & Smith Brewing on East MLK Boulevard and Chattanooga Brewing Company near Market Street are both well-established downtown options. Both are walkable from each other and from the riverfront. Chattanooga Brewing has outdoor seating. Hutton & Smith has a brewhouse-facing bar and shuffleboard. Are there dog-friendly breweries in Chattanooga? Chattanooga Brewing Company and Wanderlinger Brewing both welcome dogs. Wanderlinger's East Main beer garden is the larger outdoor space. Confirm directly with the bar before bringing your dog. Are there wineries near Chattanooga? Several. The Georgia Winery in Ringgold is six miles south of the city. Morris Vineyard in Charleston is about 25 minutes north. For a wine trail day, the Blue Ridge and Ellijay area has Cartecay Vineyards, Engelheim, and Mercier Orchards Cider all within a short drive of each other. Which Chattanooga breweries serve food? Oddstory Brewing, TailGate Brewery, and The Tap House in St. Elmo all have food menus. Top of the Rock at Jasper Highlands and Lookout Winery in Guild also serve food. Use the food menu filter in this guide to narrow to these spots. When is the best time to visit the Blue Ridge wineries from Chattanooga? Spring and early summer are least crowded. Fall foliage from mid-October through November draws the biggest weekend crowds. If you go in fall, arrive before noon. Mercier Orchards runs pick-your-own apple seasons that bring families on fall weekends. Which Chattanooga breweries have live music? Wanderlinger Brewing and Oddstory Brewing both host live music on weekends. Check their social media for current schedules. The Chattanooga live music guide covers a broader list of Southside venues. title: Cloudland Canyon State Park: Hikes, Waterfalls & Caves
description: The big guide to Cloudland Canyon State Park for hiking, waterfalls, caves, mountain biking, camping, disc golf, and nearby restaurants, plus in-depth details on each.
body: ; ; ( })) })} /> This guide covers 19 trails, activities, and dining spots at Cloudland Canyon State Park and nearby. The park sits in Rising Fawn, Georgia, about 35 miles south of Chattanooga. It covers over 3,500 acres on the western edge of Lookout Mountain. Six hiking trails are listed here, from a one-mile overlook walk to a six-mile descent into the gorge. The Waterfalls Trail drops over 600 metal grate stairs to Hemlock Falls and Cherokee Falls. The West Rim Loop has ranked as one of the top hikes in the United States in multiple years. Mountain biking centers on the 5 Points Recreation Area, a few miles east of the main park entrance. Four route options are listed here, from an easy 3-mile loop to an expert 5-mile ride. The park rents bikes at the Visitor Center for $35 half day or $55 full day. The Activity filter separates hiking, mountain biking, and dining. The Difficulty filter narrows to easier or challenging options. The Kids filter surfaces six spots well-suited for families. The park charges a $10 daily parking fee and is open 7am to 10pm year-round. If there is a trail or activity worth adding, send an email . Details change. Confirm before you go. Activity : Hiking Try Me ↓ ← Try Me Mountain Biking Dining Nearby Good for Kids Difficulty : Easier Challenging Location : Main Park 5 Points Area Near Park Hiking at Cloudland Canyon . Six hiking trails are listed here, from one mile to six miles. Three are easier and accessible to most visitors. The West Rim Loop is the signature trail, nearly five miles along the canyon rim with views throughout. The Waterfalls Trail is the hardest and most rewarding — 600-plus metal stairs lead to Hemlock Falls and Cherokee Falls at the bottom of the gorge. Sitton's Gulch is the most remote, following creek valleys through spring wildflowers with far fewer people on the trail. Chattanooga outdoors guide Mountain Biking at 5 Points . The 5 Points Recreation Area sits a few miles east of the main park entrance. The network has 20-plus miles of trail ranging from green to expert. The Cloudland Canyon Connector (CCC) is the main spine of the system, linking all the other trails. Two easier routes and two advanced routes are listed here. The park rents bikes at the Visitor Center for $35 half day or $55 full day. Call ahead to confirm availability. Chattanooga outdoors guide Cloudland Canyon with Kids . Six activities here are well-suited for families with children. The Meadowlands and Overlook trails are both one mile and easy to complete. The fishing pond is stocked with catfish and requires no license. The 18-hole disc golf course is included with park entry. The park also keeps an all-terrain Action Trackchair and EnChroma glasses for visitors with mobility or color-vision needs — ask at the park office to reserve either one. Chattanooga museums and exhibits Eating Near the Park . Three restaurants are within 10 to 15 minutes of the park. Hope House Cafe handles breakfast and lunch. Canyon Grill is the dinner option but is closed Sunday and Monday, so plan your visit day around that. Thatcher's BBQ is the most casual and handles lunch or dinner. Several North Georgia breweries and wineries are also within 30 minutes of the park. Breweries and wineries near Chattanooga The 5 Points Recreation Area has its own parking and trailhead, a few miles east of the main park entrance. Plan to move your car between the two areas if you want to hike and bike on the same trip. Camping books fast in spring and fall. Yurts and cabins sell out first. Reserve a few weeks ahead for peak season weekends. Check the Georgia State Parks site for availability. Several North Georgia breweries and wineries are within 30 minutes of the park. The breweries and wineries guide covers those stops. For more trails and outdoor activities near Chattanooga, the Chattanooga outdoors guide covers 70-plus routes across Lookout Mountain, Raccoon Mountain, and the city greenways. FAQ . Do you need a fishing license at Cloudland Canyon? No license required. The park pond is stocked with channel catfish. Catch and keep runs from the day after Labor Day through the end of November. All other times are catch and release. Fishing in the park's creeks is not allowed. Can you rent bikes at Cloudland Canyon? Yes. The Visitor Center rents mountain bikes for $35 half day or $55 full day. Call ahead to confirm availability before making the drive. Can you bring dogs to Cloudland Canyon? Dogs are welcome on most trails on a leash no longer than 6 feet. The Waterfalls Trail is not recommended for dogs. The 600-plus metal grate stairs can be painful and difficult for them to navigate. When do the cave tours run? Guided wild cave tours of Sitton's Cave run in April, June, July, September, and October. Each tour lasts about 2 to 2.5 hours and costs $45 per person, ages 10 and up. Call 706-657-4050 to book. Experienced cavers can get a permit for Case Cave, which requires ropes and harnesses. What waterfalls are in Cloudland Canyon? The park has two main waterfalls: Hemlock Falls and Cherokee Falls. Both are reached via the Waterfalls Trail, which branches off the West Rim Loop. Flow varies with rainfall and is strongest after a heavy storm. Can you swim at Cloudland Canyon? There is no designated swimming area in the park. The waterfalls and creek pools are not set up for swimming. The fishing pond is stocked for fishing only. Other Guides . Listings span downtown roaster bars, Southside cafe-bakeries, suburban drive-thrus, and mountain neighborhood spots on Signal and Lookout. Chattanooga has built a real independent coffee scene over the past decade. Several local operators roast their own beans on-site. Others source from small regional roasters across the Southeast. The result is more range than most mid-size cities offer. The filters are worth using. Roasts here narrows to cafes with an on-site roasting program. Chattanooga has more independent roasters per capita than most comparable cities. Several sell retail bags at the counter. Goodman, Velo, Mean Mug, and Mad Priest are the easiest spots to leave with beans. Most carry a rotating single-origin alongside their house blends. If you want to try before you buy, ask at the counter. Most roaster cafes will walk you through what's on right now. The guide is updated on a rolling schedule. New openings get added as they are confirmed. Closed or changed spots get flagged out. If a listing is wrong or a good shop is missing, send a note . One email is all it takes to get something reviewed. If coffee starts the day, the sweet treats guide has ideas for what comes after. If the afternoon calls for something stronger, the breweries and wineries guide covers the rest of the metro and day-trip range. FAQ . Which coffee shops in Chattanooga roast their own beans? Goodman, Rembrandt's, Velo, Mad Priest, Mean Mug, Stone Cup, and Frothy Monkey all roast on-site or through their own roasting operations. Most sell retail bags at the counter. Ask what's on at the time of your visit — most rotate single-origins through the year. Where can I work from a coffee shop in Chattanooga? The Camp House in the Innovation District, Cadence Coffee near UTC, Oaks Coffee House in East Brainerd, Wired Coffee Bar in Ooltewah, and Velo Coffee on East Main are the most reliable laptop spots. All have dedicated seating and hours that hold up for a full morning. Use the Work friendly filter to see the full list. Are there drive-through coffee options in Chattanooga? (be) Caffeinated runs three dual-window drive-thru locations: Red Bank on Dayton Blvd, North Shore on Kent Street, and Highland Park on East 3rd. They are a local Chattanooga brand. Use the Drive thru filter to find all three on the map. Where can I get coffee near Lookout Mountain or St. Elmo? Goodman Coffee Roasters has a cafe attached to their roasting facility on St. Elmo Ave. Wayward Pastry Co. is a short walk away on the same street. Canopy Coffee and Wine Bar sits on Scenic Highway on the mountain itself. It is a good stop after the Incline or a Cumberland Trail segment. Which Chattanooga coffee shops have outdoor seating? Rembrandt's has garden seating in Bluff View. Velo and Stone Cup on the North Shore both have patios. The Daily Ration in Normal Park has patio seating that fills up on weekends. Canopy on Lookout Mountain has outdoor seating with mountain views. Use the Outdoor seating filter to see all options at once. Other Guides . One of the most famous landmarks in the Chattanooga area, roughly 2,300 feet above the valley and well known historically for its stunning views and strategic use during the Civil War. It spans both Tennessee and Georgia state lines. In addition to trails like Glen Falls and Guild Hardy, the mountain is frequently visited for attractions like Point Park, Cravens House, Rock City and Ruby Falls. A large Wildlife Management Area northwest of downtown Chattanooga, covering roughly 24,500 acres of rugged Cumberland Plateau terrain. Known for hunting access, long gravel roads that connect to trailheads and overlooks and designated OHV routes. Scenic overlooks along the plateau edge offer big views of the Tennessee River Gorge. Stringers Ridge . 92 acre nature park located in the heart of Chattanooga's city limits. An easy escape from downtown. A lakeside state park northeast of downtown Chattanooga along Chickamauga Lake. In total the park encompasses roughly 350 acres. body: ; ; ( })) })} /> This guide covers 16 restaurants, cafes, and bars in Chattanooga where the view is part of the draw. The listings span Tennessee River waterfront, downtown rooftop bars, Lookout Mountain overlooks, and elevated spots a short drive out. Chattanooga's geography creates several distinct settings. The Tennessee River runs through the city center and narrows into a gorge to the west. Lookout Mountain rises 2,300 feet just south of downtown. Several spots sit directly at water level; others look out over the valley from elevation. The downtown entries are within walking distance of each other. Whitebird and Tony's Pasta are both on Bluff View. Scottie's is on Riverfront Pkwy. Whiskey Thief at The Edwin is a rooftop bar with river views a few blocks north. The Dwell's Matilda Midnight is a few blocks south. Four entries are a 20 to 30 minute drive from downtown. Top of the Rock is in Jasper. Riverdance at River Gorge Ranch is in Guild. Canyon Grill and Auld Alliance at McLemore Resort are on the Georgia side of Lookout Mountain. These work as a destination, not an add-on to a downtown day. The filters are worth using. Water narrows to river and lake views at table level. Mountain covers elevated valley views. Top of the Rock and Riverdance both have on-site breweries. See the breweries and wineries guide for taproom-only options. If there is a spot worth adding, send an email . Hours and seasonal programming change. Confirm before making a special trip. Map View Of The Restaurant Locations Below View : Try Me ↓ ← Try Me Water Rooftop Mountain When : Brunch Lunch Dinner Drinks Outdoor seating Book ahead Neighborhood : Downtown North Shore Lookout Mountain Suck Creek Jasper (~30 min) Guild (~20 min) Rising Fawn (~20 min) Water views . Manufacturers Road (North Shore) and Riverfront Pkwy (downtown) put you closest to the Tennessee River at table level. Suck Creek Road to the west is a quieter creek-to-river setting, farther from downtown. The Riverwalk connects most of the riverfront spots on foot. Tennessee Riverwalk Downtown coffee nearby Downtown rooftops . Several downtown hotels have rooftop bars and terraces overlooking the city, mountains, and river corridor. The Edwin and Dwell are the two main options. Both are weather dependent. Confirm before making either one the centerpiece of a plan. A Sheet for Chattanooga Live Music A Playbill for Chattanooga Performing Arts Lookout Mountain . Lookout Mountain sits roughly 2,300 feet above the valley. A handful of spots near the top or along the scenic highway have that elevation working for them. Canopy Coffee is the most accessible, open into the evening with wine and coffee alongside the view. Lookout Mountain outdoor activities Lookout Mountain coffee Reserve the out-of-city spots for evenings or full days when you can make the drive part of the plan. Top of the Rock has live music on Thursdays. Canyon Grill serves dinner only, Tuesday through Saturday. Auld Alliance books out fast, so plan ahead. Weekday evenings and Sunday brunch tend to work better for downtown spots. Scottie's is walk-in only, so arrive early on weekends. Tony's Pasta and Whitebird both take reservations and fill up on Saturday nights. River Drifters on Suck Creek has dog-friendly outdoor seating and rents kayaks on site. Stone Cup's North Shore patio is a good warm-weather stop before or after the Riverwalk . This guide is updated as new spots open. If a listing has changed or a view-worthy spot is missing, send a note . FAQ . Where are the best waterfront restaurants in Chattanooga? The Boathouse on Riverside Dr (North Shore), Scottie's On The River on Riverfront Pkwy, and Tony's Pasta on Bluff View are the most full-service waterfront dinner options. Stone Cup Cafe on Frazier Ave is primarily a coffee stop with a river-facing patio. River Drifters on Suck Creek Road is a patio bar with creek views and a food menu. Are there rooftop bars in Chattanooga with views? Whiskey Thief at The Edwin Hotel has Tennessee River views and over 100 Tennessee whiskeys on the menu. Matilda Midnight at The Dwell Hotel is a smaller open-air cocktail bar with city skyline views. Both are weather dependent, so confirm before making either one the main plan. Do I need reservations at these restaurants? Auld Alliance at McLemore Resort requires reservations and books out fast. Top of the Rock takes reservations via OpenTable. Tony's Pasta and Canyon Grill both recommend reservations. Scottie's On The River is walk-in only. What restaurants or bars have views on Lookout Mountain? Canopy Coffee and Wine Bar is the most accessible, open from coffee hours into wine and beer. Canyon Grill is dinner only, Tuesday through Saturday, with four-state views from the Georgia ridgeline. Auld Alliance at McLemore Resort is fine dining at the cliff edge, reservations required. Where can I have brunch with a view in Chattanooga? Scottie's On The River runs Sunday brunch from 11am to 3pm, walk-in only. Top of the Rock offers weekend brunch at its Jasper Mountain location. Riverdance at River Gorge Ranch in Guild also has brunch. Lakeshore Grille runs Sunday brunch from 11am to 4pm above Chickamauga Lake. Which of these spots are outside Chattanooga? Four entries in this guide are outside city limits but within about 30 minutes. Canyon Grill is in Rising Fawn, GA, about 20 minutes south. Auld Alliance at McLemore Resort is also in Rising Fawn, about 30 minutes out. Top of the Rock is in Jasper, TN, roughly 30 minutes north. Riverdance at River Gorge Ranch is in Guild, TN, about 25 minutes away. Other Guides . title: Guided Tours in Chattanooga, TN
description: Guide to guided tours and in Chattanooga including ghost tours, food tours, kayaking, and historical experiences.
body: ; ; ( })) })} /> This guide covers 12 guided tours in and around Chattanooga. The options range from city history and ghost tours to outdoor adventures, cave spelunking, and food walks. Nickajack Cave near South Pittsburg holds up to 100,000 gray bats. The Bat Cave Sunset Kayak Tour lets you watch them emerge at dusk. It is one of the more unusual things you can do within an hour of downtown. Nine of the 13 tours depart from or near downtown. Chattanooga Ducks, Rydables, and Ghost Tours all leave from near the riverfront. Several can be combined in a single day without a car. The Outdoor filter surfaces five adventure-based options. The Type filter separates city history from outdoor tours and food experiences. The Day Trip filter shows three options that require a short drive outside of Chattanooga. If there is a tour worth adding, send an email . Details change. Confirm before you go. Type : City & History Outdoor Food & Entertainment Format : Try Me ↓ ← Try Me Good for kids Water tour Walking tour Adventure Location : Downtown Day trip City & History Tours . Five tours in this guide cover Chattanooga's history. The Trolley Tours give the broadest city overview. Ghost Tours move slower and go deeper. Chickamauga adds a 15-minute drive but covers the second most deadly Civil War battle in the country. The Duck Boat and Rydables are lighter on history but cover the same downtown geography. History museums and exhibits Outdoor Tours . Five options here get you outside the city. The Bat Cave Kayak runs on the Tennessee River near South Pittsburg from March through October. Experience Chattanooga runs private hikes across the region's mountain trails. Raccoon Mountain Caverns is 8 miles west and open daily. Lookout Mountain Flight Park is for the person who wants something they will talk about for years. Outdoor adventures guide Cloudland Canyon guide Good for Kids . Four tours here work well for families. The Duck Boat is the most reliably fun option for mixed ages. The Southern Belle has sightseeing and dinner options that fit all ages. Experience Chattanooga's alpaca hike is a popular pick for younger kids. Raccoon Mountain Caverns has a lit-path walking tour for all ages, plus more intense wild cave options for older kids and adults. Kid-friendly exhibits Day Trips . Three tours require a short drive. Nickajack Cave (Bat Cave Kayak) is about 35 miles west in South Pittsburg, TN. Chickamauga Battlefield is 15 minutes south in Fort Oglethorpe, GA. Lookout Mountain Flight Park is 30 minutes in Rising Fawn, GA. The Bat Cave tour runs only March through October, so check the season before planning. Most downtown tours can run on the same day. Book the ones that sell out first: Chattanooga Ducks and Rydables fill up on weekends. Ghost Tours are easier to get into day-of. If you plan an outdoor day trip, the Bat Cave Kayak and Chickamauga Battlefield are both best on weekdays. The Bat Cave tour runs only March through October. For more self-guided outdoor options, see the Chattanooga outdoors guide . FAQ . Are there ghost tours in Chattanooga? Yes. Chattanooga Ghost Tours runs walking tours and ghost hunts downtown. The Murder and Mayhem Haunted History walk covers downtown in 2 hours. The UTC Cemetery Ghost Hunt lasts 1.5 hours and includes ghost hunting equipment. A combined Walk and Hunt tour is also available. Tours run rain or shine for all ages. How much is the Chattanooga Ducks tour? The Chattanooga Ducks tour starts around $36 per person. The tour lasts about one hour and departs from 151 Riverfront Parkway downtown. The Duck drives through downtown streets and then into the Tennessee River. Book ahead on busy weekends as tours sell out. Can you kayak to Nickajack Cave near Chattanooga? Yes. Chattanooga Guided Adventures runs a guided sunset kayak tour to Nickajack Cave from March through early October. Up to 100,000 gray bats emerge from the cave at dusk. The 3-mile route is beginner-friendly with no prior experience needed. Tours start around $77 and meet at Maple View Recreation Area in South Pittsburg, TN. What food tours are available in Chattanooga? Chatt Taste offers three guided food tours: the Downtown Chattanooga Food Tour, the Historic Southside Food Tour (2 hours), and ChattaBrunch (food, art, history, and mimosas). Private tours and events are also available. All are walking tours led by local guides with 5-star ratings. Is Chickamauga Battlefield free to visit? Yes. Chickamauga Battlefield is a National Park and admission is free. Ranger-guided tours run on weekends at 10am and 2pm and last about 90 minutes. The NPS app provides a self-guided driving or walking tour of eight points of interest. The battlefield is in Fort Oglethorpe, GA, about 15 minutes from downtown Chattanooga. How much does hang gliding near Chattanooga cost? Lookout Mountain Flight Park offers tandem hang gliding from Rising Fawn, GA, about 30 minutes from downtown. Discovery flights start around $199 per person. You must be at least 14 years old and under 250 pounds. An ultralight plane tows you to 1,500 or 3,000 feet before you soar on your own. Other Guides . title: Chattanooga Holiday Market
description: The Chattanooga Holiday Market brings 200+ local vendors indoors to the Convention Center across two December weekends in 2026.
body: The Chattanooga Holiday Market moves indoors to the Convention Center for two December weekends. Shop on December 12, 13, 19, and 20, 2026. More than 200 local vendors fill the hall with handmade gifts and holiday food. Browse pottery, custom art, handcrafted jewelry, and local apparel. Find natural bath products, home decorations, and woodworking from area makers. Pick up fresh local food for your holiday table. The market stays warm and dry no matter the weather outside. Admission is free, so bring the whole family. Come early for the best selection before popular items sell out.

title: FlashDrive Rocks You Into 2027
description: FlashDrive plays Top 40 dance hits at the Chattanooga Convention Center for a New Year's Eve party on December 31, 2026.
body: FlashDrive rings in the new year at the Chattanooga Convention Center on December 31, 2026. The band starts at 8:00 PM and plays until the countdown to 2027. FlashDrive is a Chattanooga party band that covers Top 40 dance hits. Their sets span 12 genres and seven decades of music. Dress up, dance, and toast midnight with a live band on stage. Reserved tables seat ten guests and cost $500 early bird or $750 after December 1. Individual tickets run $50 early bird or $75 after December 1. Book your table early because early bird pricing ends November 30.

title: O'Reilly Auto Parts World of Wheels
description: The 59th World of Wheels brings hot rods, classic cars, and custom builds to the Chattanooga Convention Center January 8-10, 2027.
body: World of Wheels returns to the Chattanooga Convention Center for its 59th year. The indoor show fills 110,000 square feet with hot rods, race cars, antique cars, custom imports, and motorcycles. Judges score each vehicle on condition, design, finish, and workmanship. Celebrity guests include Kevin Mack from Count's Kustoms and Courtney Hansen from Overhaulin'. The Golden Riders perform stunts all weekend. Kids race on a free Hot Wheels drag track and meet Star Wars cosplayers. Contests award prizes such as a Harley Davidson motorcycle and an electric bike. Buy tickets early at O'Reilly Auto Parts stores for the lowest price. Passes cover a single day with no re-entry.

title: Ren Faire Pre Party with Oddstory Brewing Co.
description: An all-day Renaissance feast at Oddstory Brewing before the Chattanooga Ren Faire, with steins, turkey legs, and mystery trinket bags.
body: Oddstory Brewing hosts an all-day feast before the Chattanooga Renaissance Faire. Gather your crew for steins, turkey legs, and cocktail specials from noon to 10pm. Mystery trinket bags add to the fun. Oddstory is the official beer of the Ren Faire, so their new can designs pour all weekend. The faire itself runs Saturday and Sunday, November 14 and 15, at Coolidge Park and Renaissance Park. Entry to the pre party is free.

title: A Candlelight Christmas with Erick Baker
description: Emmy-winning folk soul artist Erick Baker performs Christmas classics at Songbirds on December 4, 2026.
body: Erick Baker is an Emmy-winning folk soul singer-songwriter from Knoxville, Tennessee. His sound sits at the meeting point of folk, rock, country, and soul. Critics compare his voice to Ray LaMontagne and Amos Lee. This candlelit show features Christmas classics and his heartfelt songwriting. The set starts at 7:00 PM at Songbirds.

title: Bella Lam & The Boys: A Hometown Christmas
description: Chattanooga country artist Bella Lam headlines a hometown Christmas show at Songbirds on December 19, 2026.
body: Bella Lam is a Chattanooga country artist playing a hometown Christmas show with her band. She just released a holiday single called "Slow As Christmas." The song features five-time CMA Musician of the Year Jenee Fleenor on fiddle. Expect new Christmas material alongside her country catalog. This show benefits the Forgotten Child Fund, a local toy drive. Lam has built a loyal following around Chattanooga, so hometown crowds tend to sing along. The set starts at 7:00 PM at Songbirds. Come ready for a festive, sentimental night rather than a loud one.

title: Belles w/ Johnny Gates
description: Country artist Belles plays Songbirds on November 20, 2026, with Johnny Gates opening the show.
body: Belles is a country singer-songwriter with a strong 2026. She wrote the song "Son of Jolene" and recorded it with Dolly Parton. Her set blends modern country with classic storytelling. Johnny Gates opens the night. The show runs from 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM at Songbirds.

title: Ben Sollee
description: Kentucky cellist and singer-songwriter Ben Sollee brings his alt-Americana sound to Songbirds on November 4, 2026.
body: Ben Sollee is a Kentucky cellist, singer, and songwriter. He built his own alt-Americana style from folk, bluegrass, jazz, and R&B roots. His playing weaves unusual cello techniques with banjo, guitar, and soulful vocals. His 2024 album Long Haul draws on tones from the American and global south. Sollee plays Songbirds on West Main Street. The show starts at 7pm. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Bo Bice
description: American Idol runner-up Bo Bice brings his southern rock voice to Songbirds on September 25.
body: Bo Bice plays Songbirds on Thursday, September 25. He finished runner-up on the fourth season of American Idol in 2005. Since then he has leaned into southern rock, blues, and gritty classic rock. His powerful voice made "Inside Your Heaven" a gold-selling single. The show starts at 7pm. Songbirds is on West Main Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue site for tickets and seating.

title: Bronwyn
description: Two-time IBMA Fiddle Player of the Year Bronwyn Keith-Hynes plays Songbirds on December 12, 2026.
body: Bronwyn Keith-Hynes is a bluegrass fiddler from Charlottesville, Virginia, now based in Nashville. She won IBMA Fiddle Player of the Year in 2021 and 2022. She spent years as the fiddler for Molly Tuttle and Golden Highway. Now she fronts her own band and sings lead. Her 2024 album I Built A World earned a Grammy nomination. Expect fiery fiddle playing and rootsy vocals. The set starts at 7:00 PM at Songbirds.

title: Chatham Rabbits
description: North Carolina folk duo Chatham Rabbits play Songbirds on September 3, touring behind a new album.
body: Chatham Rabbits bring their North Carolina folk to Songbirds on Thursday, September 3. The husband-and-wife duo are out behind a new record that critics have called a masterclass in songwriting. Doors and set start at 7pm - the kind of quiet, close room that suits their harmonies. Check the venue site for tickets. Songbirds is at 35 Station St in downtown Chattanooga.

title: Chatt State Student Film Premiere
description: Chatt State students premiere two short films at Songbirds on November 17, 2026, with music from Habitual Strangers.
body: Chattanooga State students screen two short films at Songbirds. The lineup includes "Blue after Gold" and "Vandycorn." The event celebrates local student filmmakers and their work. Live music from Habitual Strangers rounds out the night. The premiere runs from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM. Admission is free.

title: Chattanooga Horn Authority
description: The eight-piece Chattanooga Horn Authority bring big-band energy to Songbirds on September 5.
body: Chattanooga Horn Authority pack Songbirds with big-band horn-driven rock on Saturday, September 5. The eight-piece local ensemble covers Chicago, Steely Dan, Van Morrison, and Huey Lewis with genuine firepower - their members range from 40 to 70 and have deep roots in the Scenic City's music scene. This is a Chattanooga crowd favorite. Music starts at 7pm. Check the Songbirds site for tickets and details.

title: Clay Street Unit w/ Tobacco Road
description: Denver's Clay Street Unit plays Songbirds on September 13 with Tobacco Road.
body: Clay Street Unit bring their Denver take on bluegrass to Songbirds on Saturday, September 13. The band mix string-band roots with an Americana edge, and the songs open up loud when they play live. Tobacco Road warm up the room first. Doors and set start at 7pm. Songbirds is at 35 Station St in the Choo Choo district. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Copeland
description: Long-running indie band Copeland play Songbirds on September 11 with special guest Jenny Dee.
body: Copeland return to the road and stop at Songbirds on Friday, September 11. Active since 2001 with six albums behind them, the band bring their layered indie rock to the downtown stage. Special guest Jenny Dee opens at 7pm. Copeland formed in Lakeland, Florida and have toured continuously since 2001. Their catalog spans emo-influenced indie pop to cinematic rock. The band returns to Songbirds after prior stops in Chattanooga. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Cuffing Season and Sarah Mootz
description: Blues artist Cuffing Season and singer-songwriter Sarah Mootz share the Songbirds stage on November 10, 2026.
body: Cuffing Season is the stage name of Chandler Monroe, a soul and blues singer-songwriter from southern Mississippi. His sound mixes delta blues with modern soul and R&B. Sarah Mootz is an independent singer-songwriter from Athens, Georgia. She leans on rock and indie influences and honest storytelling. The two artists have recorded together, pairing his deep voice with her lighter tone. They bring both pop-forward and blues sounds to this double bill.

title: Fai Laci
description: Boston quintet Fai Laci bring their cathartic live show to Songbirds on September 22.
body: Boston rock band Fai Laci play Songbirds on Tuesday, September 22 behind their debut album Elephant in the Room, produced by Dan Auerbach of The Black Keys. The five-piece blend punk urgency and glam stomp with the swagger of classic rock - loud and cathartic live. Music starts at 7pm in the intimate downtown room. Check the Songbirds site for tickets.

title: Feng E
description: Taiwanese ukulele prodigy Feng E plays Songbirds on November 1, 2026, with fiery fingerstyle covers and originals.
body: Feng E is a Taiwanese ukulele prodigy born in 2007. He started playing at age five and now draws nearly a million YouTube subscribers. He plays fierce lead lines and driving rhythms on a single ukulele. His sets mix originals with covers of Nirvana, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Jackson. Feng E plays Songbirds on West Main Street. Check the venue site for show date and tickets. Doors and set at 7pm.

title: Fox N' Vead
description: Alternative rock band Fox N' Vead play Songbirds on September 18 with Rob Langdon.
body: Fox N' Vead bring their self-described "crunge" sound to Songbirds on Friday, September 18. The Concord, NC four-piece blend hard-hitting grunge riffs with country and blues roots - outlaw energy filtered through alternative rock. Rob Langdon opens. Music starts at 7pm. Songbirds is at 35 Station St in the Choo Choo district. Doors open at 6pm. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Hannah Wicklund w/ Slow Funeral and Leah Blevins
description: Rock guitarist Hannah Wicklund headlines Songbirds on December 8, 2026, with Slow Funeral and Leah Blevins.
body: Hannah Wicklund is a rock guitarist from Hilton Head Island, South Carolina. She started gigging at age eight and built her sound on classic rock. Her riffs draw on Jimi Hendrix, Fleetwood Mac, and Tom Petty. Expect blistering solos and searing vocals. Slow Funeral and Leah Blevins open the show. The set starts at 7:00 PM at Songbirds.

title: Home Again: A Benefit for TIRRC
description: A benefit concert for TIRRC at Songbirds featuring Kofi Mawuko and the Ogya World Music Band with Mariah Friend on November 5, 2026.
body: This benefit concert supports the Tennessee Immigrant and Refugee Rights Coalition. Kofi Mawuko leads the Ogya World Music Band, a Chattanooga group he founded. Mawuko is a Ghanaian native, and his name for the band means "fire" in the Ewe language. The band blends West African rhythms with reggae, Afrobeat, blues, jazz, and rock. Their live shows feature master drumming, dynamic horns, and vibrant dancing. Mariah Friend joins the bill. Doors and music start at 6:30 PM.

title: Hunter Flynn w/ Peytan Porter
description: Kentucky singer-songwriter Hunter Flynn plays Songbirds on November 28, 2026, with Peytan Porter.
body: Hunter Flynn is a Kentucky-born singer-songwriter and visual artist. His songs carry emotional honesty and deep Appalachian roots. He writes with plain language and quiet detail. Peytan Porter joins him on the bill. The pairing makes this a strong night for folk and Americana fans at Songbirds.

title: IBMA Bluegrass Ramble
description: Songbirds hosts official IBMA Bluegrass Ramble showcases on October 20 and 21 during World of Bluegrass.
body: Songbirds serves as an official venue for the IBMA Bluegrass Ramble. The Ramble runs October 20 and 21 as part of IBMA World of Bluegrass in Chattanooga. Multiple showcase bands play each night across downtown rooms. The 2026 lineup spans 30 official showcase artists, from Missy Raines & Allegheny to The Slocan Ramblers. Doors and music start at 6:30pm. Each set runs short, so acts rotate through the night. Check the venue site for the nightly bill and tickets.

title: J. Roddy Walston
description: Cleveland, Tennessee rocker J. Roddy Walston brings his high-energy piano rock to Songbirds on November 14, 2026.
body: J. Roddy Walston is a rocker from Cleveland, Tennessee. He fuses Southern rock, blues, soul, and funk into loud, high-energy rock and roll. He plays piano like a percussion instrument and pounds the keys hard. His live shows run hot and sweaty. The music starts at 7:00 PM.

title: Jay Buchanan
description: Jay Buchanan brings his commanding, soul-tinged voice to Songbirds on September 19.
body: Jay Buchanan plays Songbirds on Saturday, September 19. Called one of the most commanding voices in modern rock, he pulls deep soul influence into every song. This one starts a little later - doors and set at 8pm. Buchanan fronts Rival Sons and has toured with deep-pocket blues players worldwide. His solo sets strip back the production and focus on voice and guitar. Songbirds is an intimate room that suits that format. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Jed Harrelson w/ the mood swings
description: Nashville soul artist Jed Harrelson plays Songbirds on December 3, 2026, with the mood swings.
body: Jed Harrelson is a Nashville soul singer-songwriter from Texarkana, Arkansas. He blends soul, rock, R&B, and blues with Southern grit. His songs feature smooth guitar tones and raw emotion. He draws on influences like Marcus King and Allen Stone. The mood swings open the show. The set starts at 8:00 PM at Songbirds.

title: John Cowan Trio
description: The John Cowan Trio play Songbirds on September 4, marking 25 years of shared history and musical trust.
body: The John Cowan Trio land at Songbirds on Friday, September 4. Twenty-five years of shared history, musical trust, and genuine friendship show up in every note. Doors and set start at 7pm in the intimate downtown room. John Cowan is a bluegrass bass singer who anchored the New Grass Revival for decades. His trio shows lean on three-part vocal harmony and acoustic interplay. Songbirds is an intimate listening room on West Main Street. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Johnny Balik
description: Chattanooga pop-soul and R&B artist Johnny Balik headlines Songbirds on November 21, 2026.
body: Johnny Balik is a Chattanooga singer-songwriter. He mixes pop-soul with R&B and warm, melodic hooks. His songs have earned more than 50 million streams. He draws over 100,000 monthly listeners on Spotify. This hometown show gives fans a close look at his sound at Songbirds.

title: Joshua Ray Walker w/ Cecilia Castleman
description: Dallas Americana songwriter Joshua Ray Walker plays Songbirds with Cecilia Castleman on October 18.
body: Joshua Ray Walker is a Dallas country and Americana songwriter with a rich, expressive tenor. His songs paint vivid, character-driven stories with dark humor and deep empathy. He has played the Grand Ole Opry and toured across the U.S. and Europe. Cecilia Castleman opens the night. Music starts at 7pm at Songbirds. See the venue site for tickets. Check the Songbirds site for tickets.

title: Karly Hartzman w/ Verity Den
description: Karly Hartzman of Wednesday headlines Songbirds on December 2, 2026, with Verity Den.
body: Karly Hartzman leads the rock band Wednesday. She writes sharp, image-rich songs rooted in Southern life. She has toured internationally and released six albums. Critics praise her lyrics and her raw guitar tone. Verity Den opens the show. The set starts at 8:00 PM at Songbirds.

title: Macartney Reinhardt and Mary Kate Farmer
description: Pop-country singer Macartney Reinhardt shares the bill with Mary Kate Farmer at Songbirds on October 10.
body: Macartney Reinhardt is a pop-country singer and songwriter from Atlanta. She is a relative of jazz guitar legend Django Reinhardt. Her songs mix bright melodies with country storytelling. Mary Kate Farmer shares the bill for this early show. Music starts at 7pm at Songbirds on West Main. See the venue site for tickets. Check the Songbirds site for tickets. Songbirds is on West Main Street.

title: MainX24 Paint & Sip Party
description: A MAINx24 paint and sip party at Songbirds on December 5, 2026, led by Gracie Clark.
body: Gracie Clark leads this paint and sip party during MAINx24. She walks the room through a Christmas painting step by step. All painting supplies are included with your ticket. The event runs at noon on December 5, 2026, so you catch it early in the festival day. MAINx24 is a 24-hour street festival along Main Street in Chattanooga's Southside. Each person needs their own ticket. No painting experience is required. Arrive a few minutes early to pick a seat and set up your canvas.

title: Nik Parr & the Selfless Lovers
description: Austin piano-driven roots rock band Nik Parr & the Selfless Lovers play Songbirds on October 9.
body: Nik Parr & the Selfless Lovers play Songbirds on Friday, October 9. The Austin band delivers high-energy, piano-driven roots rock. Their sound pulls from classic rock, soul, blues, and southern rock. Nik Parr often plays saxophone and piano at the same time on stage. The show starts at 7pm. Songbirds is at 35 Station St in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Nolan Taylor
description: Singer-songwriter Nolan Taylor plays Songbirds on September 10 with Jess Woodland.
body: Nolan Taylor brings his socially conscious songwriting to Songbirds on Thursday, September 10. Jess Woodland opens the night. It is a quiet, close room built for lyrics like these - doors and set at 7pm. Taylor's songwriting covers race, identity, and the American experience with clarity and care. His debut Brave and Strange landed in 2024 and earned strong roots-music praise. Check the Songbirds site for tickets.

title: Pierre Bensusan
description: French acoustic guitar virtuoso Pierre Bensusan brings his DADGAD mastery to Songbirds on September 29.
body: Pierre Bensusan plays Songbirds on Monday, September 29. The French guitarist is known worldwide as a master of the DADGAD tuning. His playing blends Celtic, folk, world music, and chamber jazz into one voice. Fellow guitarists from Mark Knopfler to Pat Metheny have praised his work. The show starts at 7pm. Songbirds is at 35 Station St in the Choo Choo district. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Ron Pope
description: Prolific songwriter Ron Pope plays Songbirds on September 14.
body: Ron Pope plays Songbirds on Monday, September 14. The prolific songwriter has drawn praise from Rolling Stone and Billboard for his heartfelt, road-worn catalog. Doors and music start at 7pm. Pope built his audience independently and has toured the world without label support. His most popular songs were discovered through TV placements. He works best in small listening rooms. Songbirds is on West Main Street. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Rubiks Groove
description: Nashville party band Rubiks Groove brings an 80s, 90s, and 2000s tribute show to Songbirds on October 23.
body: Rubiks Groove plays Songbirds on Friday, October 23. The Nashville band delivers an 80s, 90s, and 2000s tribute party. Their set spans rock to hip hop and mixes live music with costumes, characters, and video. The show works as a full interactive experience for the crowd. Doors and start time show at 7pm. Check the Songbirds site for tickets. Songbirds is on West Main Street.

title: Sloppy Street Tacos & Co.
description: Chattanooga jam band Sloppy Street Tacos plays a New Year's Eve show at Songbirds on December 31, 2026.
body: Sloppy Street Tacos is a Chattanooga funk rock band that improvises hard. They pull from Vulfpeck, Umphrey's McGee, Talking Heads, and the Grateful Dead. Their sets mix funk, rock, jazz, blues, and folk into long jams. The lineup runs guitar, synth, saxophone, drums, and bass. This is a New Year's Eve show, so the music runs past midnight into 2027. A jam band suits the night because the sets stretch out and build. The music starts at 9:00 PM at Songbirds. Pace yourself and plan a ride home for the early hours.

title: SPANKthe80s
description: SPANKthe80s brings its high-energy 1980s tribute show to Songbirds in Chattanooga on November 6, 2026.
body: SPANKthe80s is a tribute band that recreates the sound and style of the 1980s. The group has performed this show since 1999. Their sets pull hits from Michael Jackson, Prince, Bon Jovi, Journey, and more. Expect bold fashion, a bright light show, and nonstop energy. The band bills itself as the nation's premiere 80s tribute act. The show starts at 8:00 PM.

title: Supernova – Oasis Tribute w/ Ryan Oyer
description: Oasis tribute band Supernova brings the Britpop swagger to Songbirds on October 2, with Ryan Oyer opening.
body: Supernova plays Songbirds on Thursday, October 2. The six-piece tribute band recreates the energy and swagger of a live Oasis show. Expect the big Britpop anthems delivered with full intensity. Local favorite Ryan Oyer opens the night. The show starts at 7pm. Oasis announced their reunion tour in 2025 and drew massive attention. Supernova fills the gap for fans who want the songs live. Songbirds is at 35 Station St. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: The Arcadian Wild w/ Addison Agen
description: Nashville indie folk trio The Arcadian Wild play Songbirds with Addison Agen on November 7, 2026.
body: The Arcadian Wild is an indie folk and pop trio from Nashville. The group blends confessional pop, folk, progressive bluegrass, and formal vocal harmony. Members Isaac Horn, Lincoln Mick, and Bailey Warren first sang together in a university choir. Fort Wayne singer-songwriter Addison Agen opens the show. Agen was a finalist on NBC's The Voice at age 16. This stop is part of the Make It Out Alive Tour.

title: The Banshees
description: The Banshees return to Songbirds for an intimate live set on October 16.
body: The Banshees return to Songbirds after past shows at the Main Street room. The band has built a following in Chattanooga's live music scene. Expect a full set in an intimate, listening-focused space. The show starts at 7pm. Check the venue site for tickets and details. Check the Songbirds site for details on set time, tickets, and opener if one is confirmed.

title: The Floating Men - A No Sh!t Rehearsal
description: Nashville rock band The Floating Men play a live rehearsal show at Songbirds on October 30.
body: The Floating Men play Songbirds on Friday, October 30. The Nashville band formed in 1990 around songwriter Jeff Holmes. They built a reputation for rowdy rock shows driven by acoustic instruments. Their sound blends rock, pop, and jazzy detours. This date runs as a live rehearsal set. Music starts at 7:30pm. Check the Songbirds site for tickets. Songbirds is at 35 Station St in the Choo Choo district.

title: The Floating Men
description: The Floating Men bring their Nashville indie rock to Songbirds on October 31, 2026. This show is sold out.
body: The Floating Men formed in Nashville in 1990. Frontman Jeff Holmes leads the band through rock, pop, and jazzy interludes. They stay fully independent and build concept albums for a devoted fanbase known as the Floatilla. This show is sold out. The Floating Men are a Nashville-based band who formed in 1990 around songwriter Jeff Holmes. They blended acoustic instruments with rock energy and built a devoted following called the Floatilla. Their catalog spans concept albums and punchy singles. Check the Songbirds site for details.

title: The Local Honeys w/ Hunter Blalock
description: Kentucky old-time duo The Local Honeys play Songbirds on October 29 with Hunter Blalock.
body: The Local Honeys play Songbirds on Thursday, October 29. The Kentucky duo pairs Linda Jean Stokley on guitar and fiddle with Montana Hobbs on banjo. They root their sound in old-time Appalachian folk and write original songs about mountain life. Hunter Blalock opens the show. Music starts at 7pm. Songbirds is at 35 Station St in the Choo Choo district. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: The Lonesome Wave and Randy Steele Save Christmas
description: The Lonesome Wave and Randy Steele play surf rock and bluegrass holiday songs at Songbirds on December 11, 2026.
body: The Lonesome Wave plays land-locked surf rock from Chattanooga. The band leans on the sound of The Ventures, Duane Eddy, and Booker T and the MGs. For this show they rework holiday songs in that twangy, reverb-heavy style. Randy Steele joins them. Steele is a Chattanooga banjo player and firefighter who won an Independent Music Award for his bluegrass writing. Two local acts split one stage, so you get surf guitar and bluegrass banjo in the same night. The set starts at 7:00 PM at Songbirds. Come early if you want a spot up front.

title: Tommy Prine w/ Delaney Ramsdell
description: Nashville songwriter Tommy Prine plays Songbirds on November 12, 2026, with Delaney Ramsdell.
body: Tommy Prine is a Nashville singer and songwriter. His debut album This Far South moves across folk, country, alt-indie, and rock. His writing draws on loss, love, and growth in his twenties. Delaney Ramsdell opens the night. Doors open before the 7:00 PM show.

title: Triptych EP Release Party
description: Northwest Georgia rock band Triptych celebrates their first EP at Songbirds on December 18, 2026.
body: Triptych is a three-piece rock band from the Northwest Georgia area. This show marks the release of their first EP. The band plays a release party to celebrate the new record. Fans get a first live run through the new songs. The night gives local listeners a chance to back a rising regional act. The set starts at 7:00 PM at Songbirds.

title: Tyler Bryant - Holiday Benefit Concert
description: Two-time Grammy winner Tyler Bryant plays a holiday benefit concert at Songbirds on December 10, 2026.
body: Tyler Bryant is a two-time Grammy-winning producer, songwriter, and guitarist from Honey Grove, Texas. He fronts the Nashville rock band Tyler Bryant and the Shakedown. The group has released six albums and toured with ZZ Top, Aerosmith, and Lynyrd Skynyrd. Bryant won his Grammys for his production work with Larkin Poe and Ruthie Foster. This show is a holiday benefit concert. The set starts at 7:00 PM at Songbirds.

title: Vickie Vaughn
description: Award-winning bassist and vocalist Vickie Vaughn brings her progressive bluegrass to Songbirds on September 26.
body: Vickie Vaughn plays Songbirds on Friday, September 26. She is a Nashville bassist and vocalist who fronts her own progressive bluegrass band. Her sound mixes roots-driven bluegrass with a touch of pop country. She was voted IBMA Bass Player of the Year in 2023 and 2024. The show starts at 7pm. Songbirds is at 35 Station St in the Choo Choo district. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Youth Talent Show
description: Local young performers take the Songbirds stage for a judged talent show on November 19, 2026.
body: Young local performers take the Songbirds stage for a talent show. A judging panel scores each act. The lineup features singers, musicians, and other acts from the community. The show runs from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM. Come support Chattanooga's next generation of talent.

title: National Cheeseburger Day
description: The Tap House celebrates National Cheeseburger Day in downtown Chattanooga on September 18.
body: The Tap House is putting a giant, juicy cheeseburger front and center for National Cheeseburger Day on September 18. Roll through downtown on Broad Street anytime from 11am to 8:30pm and pair it with a craft beer. No cover charge. The Tap House is at 419 Broad St in downtown Chattanooga. They have more than 60 beers on tap. No reservation needed - walk in anytime during open hours.

title: National Drink Beer Day
description: Celebrate National Drink Beer Day at The Tap House in downtown Chattanooga on September 28 with a rotating list of craft brews.
body: National Drink Beer Day lands on September 28, and The Tap House wants you to pick from their many craft brews to celebrate. Head downtown to Broad Street between 11am and 7:30pm. No cover, just a good excuse to try something new on tap. The Tap House is at 419 Broad St in downtown Chattanooga. They rotate 60-plus taps, so there is always something new. Walk in anytime during open hours.

title: National Sandwich Day
description: The Tap House celebrates National Sandwich Day in downtown Chattanooga on November 3.
body: The Tap House is stacking things between bread for National Sandwich Day on November 3. Stop by downtown on Broad Street from 11am and grab a sandwich with a craft beer. No cover charge. The Tap House is at 419 Broad St in downtown Chattanooga. They keep 60-plus taps rotating with local and national craft beers. Walk in anytime during open hours. No reservation needed.

title: 49 Winchester
description: Virginia roots-rock band 49 Winchester plays The Signal on February 11 with Appalachian storytelling and anthemic songs.
body: 49 Winchester is a roots-rock band from Castlewood, Virginia. The six-piece blends Appalachian country, Southern rock, and raw storytelling. Frontman Isaac Gibson writes about small-town life with a weathered, honest voice. Their breakout record "Fortune Favors the Bold" put them on larger stages across the country. Fans can expect songs like "Russell County Line" and "Hillbilly Daydream." The show starts at 8pm with doors at 6:30pm. Tickets are required.

title: All Them Witches
description: Psychedelic hard rock band All Them Witches plays The Signal on October 10.
body: Nashville's All Them Witches return to The Signal on October 10 behind House of Mirrors, their 2026 studio album. The band weaves hard rock, stoner psych, blues, and Southern folk into long, hypnotic sets that build into something serious. This is a new-lineup record - their first with drummer Christian Powers. Music at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave in Chattanooga. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: AVATAR
description: Swedish metal band Avatar brings the Across The Underworld Tour to The Signal on May 24, 2027, with The Barbarians of California.
body: Avatar is a Swedish heavy metal band from Gothenburg. Their sound mixes groove metal riffs with circus-dark theatrics. Frontman Johannes Eckerstrom sings in a sharp, grinning snarl and paints his face like a jester. Live, the band leans hard into costumes, staging, and showmanship. This stop is part of the Across The Underworld Tour. The band booked these headline dates between stadium shows opening for Metallica. A club this size is a rare, close-up setting for them. The Barbarians of California open the night. Doors open at 6pm and the show starts at 7pm. Tickets are required.

title: Babyfxce E
description: Detroit rapper Babyfxce E plays The Signal on March 8 with his deadpan flow and gritty street storytelling.
body: Babyfxce E is a rapper from the east side of Detroit. He raps with a flat, deadpan flow that lands his punchlines hard. His style fits the gritty, bass-heavy Detroit scene. Tracks like "Jamie Lee Curtis" and "Wock Not Juice" built his buzz online. He pairs sharp humor with blunt street storytelling. The show starts at 8pm with doors at 7pm. Tickets are required.

title: Bingo Loco
description: Bingo Loco turns The Signal into a bingo rave with prizes, dance-offs, and confetti on November 21 (21+).
body: Bingo Loco comes to The Signal on November 21. This is bingo turned into a party. Comedian hosts run three games with real prizes between dance-offs, lip-sync battles, confetti showers, and throwback anthems from the DJ. The show has sold out across more than 200 cities worldwide. This event is 21 and up. Doors open at 5:30pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Bowling for Soup
description: Pop-punk institution Bowling for Soup plays The Signal on November 10.
body: Pop-punk institution Bowling for Soup play The Signal on November 10. The Wichita Falls, Texas band has been doing this since 1994 - their "1985" and "Girl All The Bad Guys Want" are permanent fixtures of the genre. Expect singalongs, humor, and 30 years of hooks delivered without apology. Music at 7:30pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Cannons
description: Synth-pop band Cannons brings its dreamy sound to The Signal on October 14.
body: LA synth-pop trio Cannons bring Everything Glows, their fifth album, to The Signal on October 14. Shimmering analog production, glossy guitars, and Michelle Joy's sultry vocals are the calling cards - the band landed on Columbia Records in 2026. They co-headlined a US tour with Bob Moses earlier this year to strong reviews. Show at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Chattanooga Pride: Rainbow Rave
description: The Pride-season electronic dance party Rainbow Rave lights up The Signal on October 9 (18+).
body: The Signal hosts Rainbow Rave on October 9 as part of Chattanooga's Pride season. This is a Pride countdown dance party - electronic music, a full production, and an 18-and-up crowd ready to move. Doors open at 9pm. This one runs late, so pace yourself. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. This is 18 and up. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Christone Kingfish Ingram
description: 21st-century blues guitarist Christone "Kingfish" Ingram plays The Signal on November 12.
body: Christone "Kingfish" Ingram brings his 2025 album Hard Road to The Signal on November 12. The Clarksdale, Mississippi guitarist picked up a guitar at age six and built a modern Delta blues voice that earned two Grammy nominations before he turned 25. His own Red Zero Records released Hard Road as his most personal work yet. Show at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Cigarettes @ Sunset
description: Cigarettes @ Sunset bring their gritty "possum rock" to The Signal on November 6, touring their debut EP Possum Rock.
body: Cigarettes @ Sunset play The Signal on November 6 behind their March 2026 debut EP, Possum Rock. The band from the Appalachian foothills call their sound "possum rock" - gritty blues, indie riffs, and mountain fiddle lines fused into something raw and original. "Pavement," their breakout track, has crossed 5 million Spotify streams. Show at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Clothing Swap: hosted by Swap Don't Shop Chatt
description: A free three-hour clothing swap at The Commons at The Signal. Bring clothes to trade and take home unlimited items at no cost.
body: Swap Don't Shop Chatt hosts a free clothing swap at The Commons at The Signal. Bring clothes you no longer wear and trade them for something new to you. The event runs three hours and includes sections for kids and local makers. Take home as many items as you like at no cost. It is a simple way to refresh your closet and cut down on waste.

title: Corey Kent
description: Country artist Corey Kent brings his heartland rock sound to The Signal on February 25.
body: Corey Kent is a country artist from Frisco, Texas. His single "Wild as Her" hit number one and went triple platinum. He pairs gritty vocals with heartland rock energy. His album Heartland Rock and Roll shapes the current tour. The show starts at 8pm. Tickets are required. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue site to buy tickets.

title: Corey Smith
description: Georgia singer-songwriter Corey Smith plays The Signal on March 12 with Southern rock and honest storytelling.
body: Corey Smith is a singer-songwriter from Jefferson, Georgia. He built a grassroots following by giving away music online and touring hard. His songs mix Southern rock, country, and plainspoken storytelling. A former teacher, he writes with a direct, conversational voice. Fans can expect favorites like "Twenty-One" and "If I Could Do It Again." The show starts at 8pm with doors at 6:30pm. Tickets are required.

title: CupcakKe
description: Rapper CupcakKe headlines an 18+ show at The Signal on October 6.
body: Chicago rapper CupcakKe plays The Signal on October 6 behind The Bakkery, her 2025 album. She brings raw, genre-fluid energy across hip house, hyperpop, and afrobeats - her 2026 Bakkery Tour sold out every North American date. This is a bold, unapologetic live show. 18 and up, show at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: David Cross
description: Comedian David Cross brings his Fake Joy stand-up tour to The Signal on February 3.
body: David Cross is a stand-up comedian and actor. He helped lead the alternative comedy wave of the 1990s. His sets swing from strange, playful bits to sharp political commentary. This show is part of his Fake Joy tour. Doors open at 7pm and the show starts at 8pm. Tickets are required.

title: DEMOLA LIVE!
description: Afrobeats violinist Demola brings his genre-blending live show to The Signal on January 22.
body: Demola is a Nigerian-born violinist and multi-instrumentalist based in Houston, Texas. He fuses classical technique with Afrobeats, hip-hop, R&B, and pop. His viral videos built a following of more than 2 million people. He also plays as the official violinist for R&B group Tony! Toni! Toné!. The show starts at 8pm. Doors open at 6:30pm. Tickets are required. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Dylan Gossett - The Ramblin' Tour 2027
description: Texas Americana artist Dylan Gossett plays The Signal on March 30 as part of The Ramblin' Tour 2027.
body: Dylan Gossett brings The Ramblin' Tour 2027 to The Signal on March 30. The Austin singer-songwriter broke out with his 2x Platinum anthem "Coal." His music blends Americana and Red Dirt country with lyrics rooted in a Southern upbringing. The show supports his sophomore album Ramblin'. Doors open at 6:30pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Electric Avenue - The 80s MTV Experience
description: Electric Avenue brings The 80s MTV Experience to The Signal in Chattanooga, playing accurate tributes to Duran Duran, Wham!, Tears for Fears, and more.
body: Electric Avenue recreates the sound of 1980s MTV with close accuracy. The band plays hits from Duran Duran, Wham!, Tears for Fears, Simple Minds, INXS, and Prince. They formed in 2013 and now tour across the country. Their sound tracks the original recordings so well that record labels once challenged them. This show runs the decade's biggest radio and video hits in one night. Doors open at 6:30 PM.

title: The Emo Night Tour
description: The Emo Night Tour brings an 18+ dance party of emo anthems to The Signal on September 19.
body: The Emo Night Tour lands at The Signal on September 19. DJs spin emo and pop-punk anthems all night long. This show is 18 and up. Doors and show at 8pm. The tour brings emo's biggest hits - My Chemical Romance, Fall Out Boy, Paramore, and more - into one DJ-driven night. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Fool House
description: The '90s tribute party Fool House revives NSYNC, Britney, and Blink-182 at The Signal on October 16.
body: '90s and Y2K tribute act Fool House takes over The Signal on October 16 with a full set of NSYNC, Britney Spears, and Blink-182 throwbacks. This is the full experience - production, choreography, and a room that knows every word. Come dressed for the era. Music at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Garrison Keillor Tonight
description: Garrison Keillor brings his solo storytelling show to The Signal on January 24, 2027, with poems, songs, and a sing-along.
body: Garrison Keillor hosted A Prairie Home Companion for more than forty years. He is known for his slow, dry News from Lake Wobegon monologues. This solo show mixes stories, poems, limericks, and songs. He also leads the room in a sing-along. The set is one man, a microphone, and a long memory. This stop is part of his four-month solo tour across the country. Fans of old-time public radio will feel at home here. Doors open at 5:30pm and the show starts at 7pm. Tickets are required.

title: Greensky Bluegrass
description: Acclaimed bluegrass ensemble Greensky Bluegrass plays The Signal on September 9.
body: Michigan's Greensky Bluegrass headline The Signal on September 9 during their 2026 evening-with tour - two full sets, no opener. The Kalamazoo five-piece play acoustic stomp with the rule-breaking energy of rock and roll, rooted in jam-band tradition but never predictable. Their 2025 anniversary album XXV is a good starting point if you're new to them. Music at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Here Come the Mummies
description: The funk-rock spectacle Here Come the Mummies wraps up The Signal on September 11.
body: Eight bandaged funk-rockers strong, Here Come the Mummies bring their theatrical live spectacle to The Signal on September 11. Music at 8pm. Loud, funky, and very silly in the best way. The mummies have played more than 2,000 shows across the US and never break character. Their identities stay secret even after three decades of touring. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Houndmouth
description: Alternative rock band Houndmouth plays The Signal on September 18.
body: Indiana alt-rockers Houndmouth bring their 2026 album Lordy to The Signal on September 18. The New Albany trio mix vintage country melodics with roots rock and echoes of the blues - a heartland sound with genuine grit. Their fifth album dropped July 10. Show at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: IBMA Bluegrass Live!
description: IBMA Bluegrass Live! brings two nights of bluegrass to The Signal on October 23 and 24.
body: IBMA Bluegrass Live! takes over The Signal for two nights of string band music. Friday, October 23 features Michael Cleveland & Friends with Leftover Salmon. Saturday, October 24 brings Della Mae and Sierra Ferrell to the main room. The lineup mixes hard-driving traditional bluegrass with newgrass and roots songwriting. Buy a single night or a weekend pass. VIP weekend passes are limited to 200 and add priority seating and early entry. Doors open at 6:30pm Friday and 7pm Saturday.

title: Isaiah Rashad
description: Chattanooga-born rapper Isaiah Rashad plays a hometown show at The Signal on November 25.
body: Isaiah Rashad is a Chattanooga-born rapper on Top Dawg Entertainment. He is a founding member of the local collective TheHouse. His music blends laid-back Southern flow with introspective writing. This hometown show marks 10 years of his debut album The Sun's Tirade. The show starts at 8pm. Tickets are required. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: It's A 2000s Party: Chattanooga
description: A throwback dance party spanning 2000s pop, hip-hop, and rock at The Signal on September 4.
body: It's A 2000s Party lands at The Signal on September 4 with a DJ set spanning Y2K pop, hip-hop, and rock. Expect Destiny's Child, Eminem, Fall Out Boy, and everything in between - this is a nostalgia-first dance night built for people who grew up on TRL. Dancing starts at 9pm. This is an 18-and-up event. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Jackson Dean
description: Country rocker Jackson Dean brings his gritty, road-worn sound to The Signal on November 7.
body: Jackson Dean plays The Signal on November 7. The Maryland-born country rocker broke through with the number-one hit "Don't Come Lookin'" from his debut album Greenbroke. His sound leans on twangy slide guitar, rock-edged electric riffs, and a deep, weathered voice. Expect uptempo, freewheeling songs built for a loud room. Doors open at 6:30pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: JD Simo & Ghalia Volt
description: Guitarist JD Simo and blues-rocker Ghalia Volt share the stage at The Signal on September 3.
body: Nashville guitarist JD Simo and Belgian blues-rock force Ghalia Volt share the bill at The Signal on September 3. Simo is a session ace who has played with Jack White and Beyoncé - his own music fuses Motown soul with Woodstock-era guitar fire. Volt's new 2026 album Burn the House Down, which Simo produced, is the spine of the night. Music at 8pm.

title: Kameron Marlowe
description: Country singer Kameron Marlowe plays The Signal on February 4 with his gritty ballads and heartland sound.
body: Kameron Marlowe is a country singer-songwriter from North Carolina signed to Columbia Nashville. His debut single "Giving You Up" built his name and still anchors his live set. He pairs a smoky baritone with heartfelt ballads and gritty country rock. Fans can expect favorites like "Steady Heart" and "Burn 'Em All" alongside newer material. The show starts at 8pm with doors at 6:30pm. Tickets are required.

title: Kawaii Rave
description: Kawaii Rave brings its anime-inspired dance party to The Parlour at The Signal on February 26, 2027. This event is 18+.
body: Kawaii Rave is a touring anime-inspired dance party. DJs spin EDM, K-pop, hyperpop, and big pop anthems all night. The crowd comes in cosplay, and the room fills with bright lights and color. The vibe centers on anime fandom and self-expression. This show takes over The Parlour, the smaller room at The Signal. That means a tight, high-energy dance floor rather than a big hall. This event is 18+, so bring a valid ID. Doors open at 8pm and the party starts at 9pm. Tickets are required.

title: Keith Anderson
description: Country singer-songwriter Keith Anderson performs at The Signal on September 18.
body: Country veteran Keith Anderson plays The Signal on September 18. He co-wrote Garth Brooks and George Jones's "Beer Run," penned Big & Rich's number one "Lost in This Moment," and built a solo career on gold-certified hook-heavy country. His 2008 Top 5 hit "I Still Miss You" still anchors his live sets. Music at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: King's X
description: Progressive rock trio King's X plays The Signal on November 13.
body: King's X plays The Signal on November 13. The trio has recorded together for more than four decades. Their sound fuses heavy progressive rock, soul, and tight three-part harmonies. Guitarist Ty Tabor, bassist Doug Pinnick, and drummer Jerry Gaskill built a devoted following through albums like Gretchen Goes to Nebraska and Dogman. Expect a deep catalog of riffs and layered vocals from a band that shaped the genre. Doors open at 6:30pm and the show runs to 11pm.

title: Kylie Morgan
description: Country artist Kylie Morgan brings her confessional songwriting to The Signal on September 11.
body: Country singer-songwriter Kylie Morgan plays The Signal on September 11. She writes confessional, unguarded songs - her 2025 single "Then You Happened" is one of the rawest breakup ballads in recent country memory. She went independent in 2024 and has been putting her whole self into every performance since. Show at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Lily Rose
description: Atlanta R&B and country artist Lily Rose plays The Signal on October 2.
