body: Atlanta-born Lily Rose plays The Signal on October 2 behind her debut full-length I Know What I Want, released in October 2025. She blends country, pop, and hip-hop into a sound that's entirely her own - sharp and honest, not slick. Her breakout 2020 viral hit "Villain" earned her tours with Luke Bryan, Sam Hunt, and Shania Twain. Show at 8pm.

title: Lupita Infante
description: Mexican-American singer Lupita Infante brings modern música mexicana to The Signal on November 28.
body: Two-time Latin Grammy nominee Lupita Infante plays The Signal on November 28. Her grandparents are Mexican music legends, and she carries that lineage into modern mariachi, norteño, and ranchera. Her 2025 album Las de Infante reimagines 23 of her grandfather Pedro Infante's most iconic songs. Show at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Miss Fiesta Latina 2026
description: A celebration of beauty, culture, and talent in Chattanooga's Latino community at The Signal on September 5.
body: Miss Fiesta Latina 2026 celebrates beauty, talent, and culture from Chattanooga's Latino community at The Signal on September 5. The night features candidates competing across multiple categories in a formal pageant setting. This is a community-anchored event that brings together families and supporters from across the region. Doors at 6pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets and details.

title: Neko Case
description: Acclaimed singer-songwriter Neko Case performs at The Signal on November 6.
body: Neko Case plays The Signal on November 6 in support of Neon Grey Midnight Green, her first self-produced album. She recorded it live with a full band at her Vermont studio - her most direct and urgent record in years. Case brings a country-noir vocal power and cinematic storytelling that few artists can match. Show at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Neon Moon: The Ultimate 90's Country Tribute Band
description: Ring in the new year at The Signal with Neon Moon, a 90's country tribute band playing hits from Garth Brooks, Randy Travis, and Brooks & Dunn.
body: Neon Moon is an all-star tribute band that recreates the sound of 90's country. They play the era's biggest hits from Garth Brooks, Randy Travis, and Brooks & Dunn. The Signal hosts them for a New Year's Eve celebration that runs past midnight. Sing along to the songs that defined the decade and dance into 2027. Doors open at 7:30 PM.

title: NIGHTLITE: The 30+ Party
description: NIGHTLITE: The 30+ Party brings club energy for grown-ups to The Signal on November 14.
body: NIGHTLITE is a dance party built for people over 30. The DJ spins hits from the 80s, 90s, 2000s, and today. You get a packed floor, drinks with friends, and real club energy. The night ends early, so you are home at a reasonable hour. This event is 21 and up. Doors open at 5pm and the show runs from 6pm to 9pm. Tickets are required.

title: Niko Moon
description: Country hitmaker Niko Moon brings his summer anthems to The Signal on October 8.
body: Country artist Niko Moon hits The Signal on October 8 behind his 2026 album ROOTS. He writes feel-good songs rooted in country, R&B, and reggae - his triple-platinum "GOOD TIME" put him on the map after years of writing for Zac Brown. ROOTS pulls him back toward his Southern roots. Show at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Pouya
description: Miami underground rapper Pouya headlines The Signal on December 8.
body: Miami underground rapper Pouya headlines The Signal on December 8 behind 2026's Foreverglades. He helped build the SoundCloud rap underground and his dark, bass-heavy trap style still draws a dedicated crowd. Expect a loud, intense set - this one runs late. Doors at 7:30pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Project Pat
description: Southern hip-hop veteran Project Pat takes The Signal stage on September 25.
body: Memphis hip-hop legend Project Pat takes The Signal stage on September 25. He's the older brother of Juicy J and a foundational figure in Three 6 Mafia's Dirty South movement - his 2001 anthem "Chickenhead" still lands. Paranoia-laced street rap with heavy bass production: this is classic Memphis. Show at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: R&B ONLY LIVE
description: R&B ONLY LIVE brings its DJ-driven R&B dance party to The Signal on December 5. This 18+ event spins classic and modern R&B.
body: R&B ONLY LIVE is a touring dance party from COLORS Worldwide. DJs spin R&B hits from the past and the present all night. The crowd sings and dances instead of watching a single headliner. This is an 18+ event, so bring a valid ID. Doors open at 8pm and the party starts at 9pm. Tickets are required. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: RATBOYS
description: Indie rock duo RATBOYS play new material at The Signal on October 22.
body: Chicago indie rockers RATBOYS bring their sixth album, Singin' to an Empty Chair, to The Signal on October 22. The band blends sauntering, reflective indie rock with a touch of alt-country - distortion-laced but never harsh. Guitarist Dave Sagan and vocalist Julia Steiner have been building this sound since 2010. Show at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Rewind: 2000s Rave
description: Rewind: 2000s Rave spins Y2K hits as edits, remixes, and mashups at The Signal on January 16, 2027. This event is 18+.
body: Rewind: 2000s Rave is a full club night built around Y2K music. DJs rework the biggest 2000s hits as edits, remixes, and mashups. The set leans on songs you already know from the radio and the club. Expect a packed dance floor and nonstop throwback energy. This event is 18+, so bring a valid ID. It shares the night with NIGHTLITE, a party aimed at the 30-and-up crowd earlier in the evening. Doors open at 8pm and the rave starts at 9pm. Tickets are required.

title: Rumours ATL: A Fleetwood Mac Tribute
description: Rumours ATL recreates the sound of Fleetwood Mac at The Signal on January 23 with note-for-note classics.
body: Rumours ATL is an Atlanta tribute band devoted to Fleetwood Mac. The group recreates the classic lineup fronted by Stevie Nicks and Lindsey Buckingham. Their set draws heavily from the "Rumours" album and other hits across the catalog. Expect to hear "Go Your Own Way," "Dreams," "Landslide," and "The Chain." The show starts at 8pm with doors at 6:30pm. Tickets are required.

title: Shake 'Em on Down Tour 2026 feat. Samantha Fish, Cedric Burnside & Daddy Long Legs
description: The Shake 'Em on Down Tour brings Samantha Fish, Cedric Burnside, and Daddy Long Legs to The Signal for a night of blues.
body: The Shake 'Em on Down Tour is a blues caravan curated by guitarist Samantha Fish. She plays fierce, high-energy blues rock and shares the stage with two more strong acts. Cedric Burnside carries the raw North Mississippi hill country blues tradition. Daddy Long Legs mix blues, gospel, and rock into a wild live show. Together the three acts trace the past, present, and future of the blues. Doors open at 6:30 PM.

title: Sister Hazel
description: Florida rock band Sister Hazel brings their harmony-driven sound to The Signal on December 10.
body: Sister Hazel is a Florida rock band with roots in the late 90s. Their harmony-driven single "All for You" became a lasting radio hit. The five-piece mixes rock, folk, and Southern pop. They bring a warm, sing-along live show to The Signal. The show starts at 8pm. Tickets are required. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site to buy tickets.

title: The Brook & The Bluff
description: Four-part-harmony rock band The Brook & The Bluff returns to The Signal on October 5.
body: Birmingham alt-rock band The Brook & The Bluff play The Signal on October 5 behind Werewolf, their 2026 album on Dualtone Records. They build loud, melodic songs on a foundation of choir-like four-part harmonies and swamp-rock guitar - think Petty and Creedence filtered through the modern South. This is their high-voltage touring record. Music at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: The Funeral Portrait
description: Gothic metal band The Funeral Portrait headlines a Halloween-night show at The Signal on October 31.
body: Spend Halloween night at The Signal with Atlanta gothic rock band The Funeral Portrait on October 31. The band draws from My Chemical Romance, Ghost, and Motionless In White - big theatrical anthems built on mythology and emotion. Their 2026 release Live From Suffocate City landed on Better Noise Music. Music at 8pm. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: The Renaissance Orchestra - Black Tie: The Scorpio Experience
description: The Renaissance Orchestra plays a live R&B and hip-hop set at The Parlour at The Signal on November 13.
body: The Renaissance Orchestra is a live collective from Atlanta. They blend hip-hop, R&B, and soul with full live instrumentation. Their Black Tie shows reimagine chart hits as orchestral arrangements. This Scorpio Experience date lands at The Parlour at The Signal. The event is 21 and up. The show starts at 9pm. Doors open at 8pm. Tickets are required. Check The Signal venue site for tickets.

title: The Young Dubliners
description: The Young Dubliners bring Celtic rock to The Signal on February 19 with fiddle-driven energy and Irish anthems.
body: The Young Dubliners are a Celtic rock band with Irish roots and a Los Angeles home base. Frontman Keith Roberts leads a high-energy mix of rock guitars and traditional fiddle. The band has toured for decades and built a loyal live following. Their sound joins driving anthems with Irish folk melodies. Fans can expect a fast, loud show packed with sing-along moments. The show starts at 8pm with doors at 6:30pm. Tickets are required.

title: United We Dance: Halloween Rave
description: United We Dance throws a Halloween rave at The Signal on October 30 with house, techno, and bass.
body: United We Dance throws a Halloween rave at The Signal. DJs spin house, techno, and bass through the night. Costumes fill the floor for the after-dark party. Doors open at 8pm and the music runs late. This show is 18 and up. Tickets are required. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Vincent Mason
description: Country singer-songwriter Vincent Mason plays The Signal in Chattanooga on March 6.
body: Vincent Mason is a country singer-songwriter from Georgia. He pairs plainspoken, sincere lyrics with a light, soulful touch. His sound draws comparisons to Parker McCollum and John Mayer. Mason released his debut album There I Go in late 2025. This show is all ages. Doors open at 7pm and the show starts at 8pm. Tickets are required.

title: Zoso
description: Led Zeppelin tribute Zoso recreates the classics at The Signal on September 26.
body: Led Zeppelin tribute act Zoso recreates the raw energy and musicianship of the originals at The Signal on September 26. Music at 8pm. A must for the classic-rock faithful. Zoso has toured since 1995 and is widely considered the top Led Zeppelin tribute in the US. They recreate the full Zeppelin live experience, from Plant's vocals to Bonham's drum fills. The Signal is at 21 Choo Choo Ave. Check the venue site for tickets.

title: Aquarium Animals & Beloved Pets Ofrenda
description: The Tennessee Aquarium hosts its fourth annual ofrenda from October 27 to November 2, 2026, honoring aquarium animals and beloved pets.
body: The Tennessee Aquarium sets up its fourth annual ofrenda from October 27 to November 2, 2026. An ofrenda is a memorial altar rooted in Day of the Dead tradition. This display honors aquarium animals that have passed and invites guests to remember beloved pets of their own. Staff add photos and small tokens to the altar. You can view the ofrenda during regular hours with standard admission.

title: Aquascarium 2026
description: Aquascarium is the Tennessee Aquarium's family trick-or-treat night with costumed divers, candy, and spooky fun on October 30.
body: Aquascarium is the Tennessee Aquarium's yearly trick-or-treat night. The event brings scaly, spooky, family-friendly fun to the galleries. Themed decorations fill the halls. Costumed SCUBA divers swim in the tanks. Pirates, lemurs, and mad scientists hand out candy and share aquatic facts. Music plays throughout the night. Children must stay with an adult. This event often sells out, so buy tickets early.

title: College Days – Half-Price Admission
description: College Days at the Tennessee Aquarium run September 10–30, 2026, offering half-price admission for college students.
body: College Days bring half-price admission to the Tennessee Aquarium for students. The offer runs September 10–30, 2026. Show a valid college ID at the door to get the discount. Explore both aquarium buildings, from the river to the ocean, at a lower price. It is a good chance for students to see live animals and exhibits on a budget. Details are on the Aquarium's events page.

title: Fall Camp: Changing with the Seasons
description: Changing with the Seasons is the Tennessee Aquarium's fall camp running October 12–21, 2026 - a week of hands-on nature and wildlife exploration for kids.
body: Changing with the Seasons is the Tennessee Aquarium's fall camp for kids, running October 12-21, 2026. The week focuses on seasonal changes in nature and wildlife. Each day covers a different animal or ecosystem. The camp runs full days from 8:30am to 4pm. It is designed for children ages 6 to 12. Tennessee Aquarium camps combine animal encounters, educator-led lessons, and hands-on activities. Registration is required through the aquarium website. Space is limited and sessions fill early. The aquarium is on Broad Street at the downtown Chattanooga riverfront.

title: Fall Camp: Fungi Friends
description: Fungi Friends is the Tennessee Aquarium's single-day fall camp on October 19, 2026 - a hands-on day of learning about fungi, decomposition, and the hidden world of nature.
body: Fungi Friends is a one-day fall camp at the Tennessee Aquarium on October 19, 2026. Kids dig into the world of fungi - decomposition, mycelium, and the role mushrooms play in forest ecosystems. The camp runs from 8:30am to 4pm and is designed for children ages 6 to 12. Tennessee Aquarium camps combine classroom learning with hands-on activities. Registration is required through the aquarium website. Space is limited. The aquarium is on Broad Street at the downtown Chattanooga riverfront. Check the website for the specific age range, cost, and registration deadline.

title: Hispanic Heritage Month at the Aquarium
description: The Tennessee Aquarium marks Hispanic Heritage Month from September 15 to October 15, 2026, with programming that celebrates Latino culture and heritage.
body: The Tennessee Aquarium marks Hispanic Heritage Month from September 15 to October 15. The observance honors the culture, history, and contributions of Latino communities. The Aquarium ties the celebration to its exhibits on rivers and species from across the Americas. Visitors can explore galleries during regular hours throughout the month. Check the Aquarium's events page for any special programs or dates tied to the observance. Admission covers access to the full building.

title: Holiday Cheers (21+)
description: The Tennessee Aquarium hosts Holiday Cheers, a 21+ after-hours party, on November 20, 2026, with spiked drinks and a mac-and-cheese bar.
body: The Tennessee Aquarium opens its River Journey building after hours for Holiday Cheers on November 20, 2026. This party is for guests 21 and older. Tickets include spiked seasonal drinks and a mac-and-cheese bar. You can walk the exhibits among festive decor without the daytime crowds. The Chattanooga Elf waits for Santa alongside guests. Designated driver tickets cost less for those who skip the drinks.

title: Holidays Under the Peaks
description: Holidays Under the Peaks runs November 27 through December 27, 2026, at the Tennessee Aquarium with festive decor, music, and seasonal programming.
body: Holidays Under the Peaks turns the Tennessee Aquarium into a winter wonderland from November 27 through December 27, 2026. The iconic glass peaks glow with candy cane lights above festive decor. An electric eel powers a twinkling holiday tree in one exhibit. Daily seasonal programs include Winter Adaptations at 12:15 pm and Let It Glow at 1:15 pm. The holiday celebration is included with regular Aquarium admission. Families can explore the exhibits amid holiday music and lights.

title: Octo-berfest (21+)
description: Octo-berfest is a 21+ after-hours party at the Tennessee Aquarium that mixes Oktoberfest traditions with a tribute to the octopus.
body: Octo-berfest blends Oktoberfest customs with a tribute to the octopus. This 21+ event runs after hours inside the Ocean Journey building. Guests sip Oktoberfest-style drinks and eat a German pretzel while they tour the galleries. Fall decor fills the space for the night. Bring a valid government-issued photo ID to enter. The event often sells out, so buy tickets in advance.

title: Partner Days
description: Partner Days at the Tennessee Aquarium run September 10–30, 2026, with special admission offers for employees of participating organizations.
body: Partner Days give employees of participating organizations a special deal at the Tennessee Aquarium. The offer runs September 10–30, 2026. Bring a workplace ID or pay stub to claim the discount. It applies to everyone in the paying party. Tickets cover the Tennessee Aquarium and the IMAX 3D Theater documentary films. Check the events page to see if your employer takes part.

title: Penguin Baby Shower
description: The Tennessee Aquarium hosts a Penguin Baby Shower on September 13, 2026, to celebrate two new Gentoo penguin chicks before they get their names.
body: The Tennessee Aquarium is throwing a Penguin Baby Shower for two new Gentoo penguin chicks. The chicks hatched weeks apart in the summer of 2026, on June 25 and July 17. This event celebrates them before they receive their names. A public naming auction opens on September 15, so visitors can bid on naming rights and animal-made art. Come meet the aquarium's newest floofy arrivals.

title: Preschool Classes: Sea Sprouts - Fall 2026
description: Sea Sprouts is the Tennessee Aquarium's fall preschool class series - hands-on learning about aquatic life for young kids, running September through November 2026.
body: Sea Sprouts is the Tennessee Aquarium's fall preschool class series for young kids. Sessions run from September 18 through November 20, 2026, with hands-on activities focused on ocean and river life. The classes are designed for children ages 3 to 5. Each session runs about an hour. The aquarium is on Broad Street at the downtown Chattanooga riverfront. Registration is required through the aquarium website. Each session covers a different aquatic theme. Check the website for cost, session dates, and registration details. This is a popular program - register early to secure your spot.

title: SCUBA Claus Dives
description: SCUBA Claus dives into the Tennessee Aquarium on weekends from November 28 through December 20, 2026, to greet guests from underwater.
body: Saint Nicholas trades his sleigh for scuba gear during Holidays Under the Peaks. SCUBA Claus dives into the River Journey exhibits each weekend from November 28 through December 20, 2026. He waves to guests from underwater at 2:00 pm on Saturdays and Sundays. The dive rotates between different exhibits across the holiday weekends. Kids can watch Santa swim among fish and other aquarium animals. The dives are included with regular Aquarium admission.

title: Sleep in the Deep: Public Overnight
description: Sleep in the Deep is a public overnight at the Tennessee Aquarium on December 11, 2026, for guests ages 6 and older.
body: Sleep in the Deep lets guests spend the night inside the Tennessee Aquarium on December 11, 2026. Guests explore both the River Journey and Ocean Journey buildings after hours with no crowds. The overnight includes a late-night snack and breakfast. You get a behind-the-scenes look at how the aquarium cares for its animals. Guests must be 6 or older, and anyone under 18 needs an adult. Standard tickets cost $75 and VIP tickets cost $95. This date is sold out.

title: Speaker Event – America the Beautiful: Our Natural Wonders 3D
description: The Tennessee Aquarium hosts a speaker event on November 12, 2026, tied to the IMAX film America the Beautiful: Our Natural Wonders 3D.
body: The Tennessee Aquarium pairs a speaker event with the giant-screen film "America the Beautiful: Our Natural Wonders 3D" on November 12, 2026. The IMAX film tours the country's most striking landscapes and national parks. A guest speaker adds context before or after the screening. The program runs at the aquarium's IMAX theater. Check the event link for the start time and ticket price.

title: Tennessee Aquarium Online Auction 2026
description: The Tennessee Aquarium runs its annual fundraising auction online from September 15 to September 22, 2026, with artwork and behind-the-scenes experiences up for bid.
body: The Tennessee Aquarium runs its annual fundraising auction online this fall. Bidding opens at 10 a.m. on September 15 and closes at 10 a.m. on September 22. Aquarium animals painted the artwork up for bid, from penguins to turtles to alligators. Winners can also claim behind-the-scenes experiences and staycation packages. One prize lets you name two Gentoo penguin chicks that hatched this summer. Proceeds support the Aquarium's conservation and education work. Place bids through the Aquarium's events page.

title: The Polar Express 3D in IMAX
description: The Polar Express 3D plays daily in the IMAX theater at the Tennessee Aquarium from November 27 through December 27, 2026.
body: The Polar Express returns in 3D to the Tennessee Aquarium IMAX theater this holiday season. Daily showings run from November 27 through December 27, 2026. The film follows a boy's train ride to the North Pole on Christmas Eve. The giant IMAX screen puts you inside the snowy journey. Staff recommend you wear pajamas and bring a blanket for the show. An IMAX ticket is required to attend.

title: TN River Rescue Clean-Up
description: The Tennessee River Rescue Clean-Up returns October 3, 2026 - a volunteer effort to remove trash from the Tennessee River and its tributaries.
body: Tennessee River Rescue is the longest-running clean-up effort in the Tennessee River basin. Volunteers gather each fall to remove trash from the river and its tributaries. The event spans more than twenty sites across four counties. Freshwater scientists from the Tennessee Aquarium Conservation Institute join the effort. Anyone can sign up to help clean the water and protect local wildlife. Registration details are on the Aquarium's events page.

title: Winter Camp: Snowy Science
description: Snowy Science is a two-day winter camp at the Tennessee Aquarium on January 4 and 5, 2027, for kids ages 5 to 12.
body: Snowy Science is a two-day winter camp at the Tennessee Aquarium for kids ages 5 to 12. Campers run frosty experiments and explore the science behind cold-weather conditions. They also tour the aquarium to find animals with winter adaptations. Each day includes an up-close animal encounter. The camp runs January 4 and 5, 2027, from 9:00 am to 3:30 pm.

title: Winter Camp: Winter Wonders
description: Winter Wonders is the Tennessee Aquarium's holiday-week camp running December 28, 2026 through January 1, 2027, for kids ages 5 to 12.
body: Winter Wonders is a holiday-week camp at the Tennessee Aquarium for kids ages 5 to 12. Campers learn how animals adapt to cold weather and winter environments. The week includes guided tours, winter crafts, and close encounters with ambassador animals. Campers also help with enrichment activities for the aquarium's animals. The camp runs December 28, 2026 through January 1, 2027, from 9:00 am to 3:30 pm each day.

title: America 250: Deconstructing the Bill of Rights
description: Dancers and poets examine the Bill of Rights through movement and spoken word at Barking Legs Theater on December 11.
body: Local artists take apart the Bill of Rights for this America 250 program. Dancer Ann Law leads the movement side of the show. Poets Marcus Patrick-Ellsworth and Christian Collier bring spoken word. Together they read the founding text through dance and verse. The night asks what these rights mean today. The performance starts at 7:00 on Dodds Avenue. Seating is limited, so arrive early.

title: Barking Strings: An Alt-Country Grab Bag
description: Barking Strings returns to Barking Legs Theater with an alt-country grab bag of local musicians on October 12.
body: Barking Strings is a monthly acoustic series at Barking Legs Theater. This night gathers local musicians for an alt-country grab bag. They pull from Ryan Adams, Jason Isbell, Sturgill Simpson, the Jayhawks, and Jackson Browne. The sound stays loose, warm, and rooted in roots rock and country songwriting. There is no cover charge, but the tip jar supports the performers.

title: Barking Strings: Jammin' On the Music of James Taylor
description: Barking Strings celebrates the songs of James Taylor with a monthly acoustic jam at Barking Legs Theater on September 14.
body: Barking Strings is a monthly acoustic collaboration at Barking Legs Theater. This edition celebrates the songs of James Taylor. Musicians from across the Chattanooga area join for an informal set of Taylor's catalog. Songs include Fire and Rain, Carolina in My Mind, and You've Got a Friend. The Barking Strings format encourages participation and collaboration rather than a polished performance. The event takes place at Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. Bring your instrument if you want to sit in.

title: Barking Strings: Jamming with Local Songwriters
description: Barking Strings brings local songwriters together for a monthly acoustic jam at Barking Legs Theater on November 9.
body: Barking Strings is a monthly acoustic collaboration at Barking Legs Theater. Rotating local musicians jam with songwriters Steve Smith and Zach Suede. The format stays loose and open, so sets shift from month to month. There is no cover charge, but a tip jar supports the players. Music runs from 7:30 to 9:30 in the lounge.

title: Ben Stephens Live
description: Chattanooga pianist and songwriter Ben Stephens plays a late-night set at Barking Legs Theater on December 18, 2026.
body: Ben Stephens is a Chattanooga pianist and songwriter. His music mixes funk, psychedelic sounds, and playful lyrics. He draws on the storytelling style of Elton John, Billy Joel, Randy Newman, and Ben Folds. The show starts at 9:00 PM in the lounge at Barking Legs Theater. Cover is $5 at the door. Stephens plays piano-driven songs from his own catalog, including work from his album "Hello World, This Is The Inside Of My Mind." Expect a loose, late-night set built around keys and sharp lyrics.

title: Beneath These Stones: Voices from Pleasant Garden Cemetery
description: Original poetic monologues bring the stories of Pleasant Garden Cemetery to life at Barking Legs Theater on October 18.
body: Original poetic monologues bring the people buried at Pleasant Garden Cemetery back to life. The historic African American cemetery in Chattanooga holds the remains of community members spanning generations. The performers write and deliver original dramatic monologues in first person, voice by voice. The production runs at Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue. Check the Barking Legs website for ticket details and start time. This is a thoughtful, literary performance that blends theater, history, and community memory into one evening. Seating is limited at the intimate 100-seat venue.

title: Crys Matthews
description: Nashville singer-songwriter Crys Matthews brings her socially conscious Americana to Barking Legs Theater on February 11.
body: Crys Matthews is a Nashville singer-songwriter and award-winning lyricist. She blends Country, Americana, Folk, Blues, and Bluegrass into a bold sound. Her lyrics tackle social justice issues with honesty and craft. Her title track Changemakers won Song of the Year at the 2022 International Folk Music Awards. The show runs from 7:30 to 10:00.

title: Cue the Dice: Buckaroo Blues (DnD in Space...Kinda!)
description: Cue the Dice stages Buckaroo Blues, a live sci-fi improv and tabletop show, at Barking Legs Theater on November 15.
body: Cue the Dice blends tabletop roleplaying with live improvised comedy. Buckaroo Blues is part sci-fi adventure and part stage show. Expect bounty hunters, system failures, and plenty of questionable dice rolls. The cast builds the story live, so no two shows play the same. The afternoon session runs from 3:00 to 4:00.

title: Cultural Cross Ties Close Out Party
description: A four-year Sister Cities film program wraps with a full screening at Barking Legs Theater on December 8.
body: This party closes out the four-year Cultural Cross Ties program. The project built creative exchanges with Chattanooga's Sister Cities. Partner cities include Givatayim in Israel, Hamm in Germany, Tono in Japan, and Accra in Ghana. The night screens all the films made through the program. Come see the work and meet the artists behind it. The screening starts at 6:00 on Dodds Avenue.

title: December Monday Night Big Band
description: The Chattanooga Monday Night Big Band plays a swinging Christmas set at Barking Legs Theater on December 7.
body: The Chattanooga Monday Night Big Band returns for a holiday show. Vocalist Paige Denton joins the band for this set. The full horn section swings through Christmas standards and big band classics. These players carry decades of experience on the Barking Legs stage. Expect a warm, festive night of live jazz. Music runs from 7:30 to 9:30 on Dodds Avenue.

title: Dukes Up Presents: Hearts in Harmony
description: A benefit concert at Barking Legs Theater featuring heart transplant recipients and vocalist Jermaine Purifory on September 13.
body: Dukes Up presents a benefit concert built around heart transplant recipients and their stories. The evening features vocal performances, instrumental sets, and personal testimony from transplant recipients. Dukes Up is a Chattanooga-area organization that supports heart transplant awareness and patient resources. The event raises funds and builds community around the cause. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue is an intimate venue well suited to this kind of personal, story-driven evening. Check the venue website for ticket details and the full program lineup. Expect an emotional and uplifting event.

title: Flamy Grant
description: Drag Americana artist Flamy Grant brings her folk and gospel songwriting to Barking Legs Theater on January 22.
body: Flamy Grant is a drag Americana singer and songwriter from Asheville. She blends folk, gospel, and roots into theatrical, personal storytelling. Her debut album topped the iTunes Christian chart in 2023. Randy Steele opens the night on Dodds Avenue. The music runs from 7:30 to 9:30. Tickets are available through Barking Legs.

title: Frankie Gavin: Traditional Irish Fiddle Music
description: Irish fiddle virtuoso Frankie Gavin performs traditional music on the main stage at Barking Legs Theater on November 16.
body: Frankie Gavin plays traditional Irish fiddle on the Barking Legs main stage. Gavin founded the celebrated band De Dannan in 1975 and has been a central figure in Irish traditional music for over 50 years. He plays fiddle and flute and has recorded with artists including Stephane Grappelli and Yehudi Menuhin. His playing sits in the Connaught style of the west of Ireland. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue is an intimate space where traditional Irish music carries with full detail. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time.

title: Haley Richardson & Don Penzien: An Evening of Traditional Irish Music
description: All-Ireland champion fiddler Haley Richardson plays traditional Irish music at Barking Legs Theater on December 10.
body: Fiddler Haley Richardson is a multiple All-Ireland champion. She learned the lilting Sligo style from master Brian Conway and has toured with Riverdance. Guitarist Don Penzien backs her with driving DADGAD accompaniment. The pair have played together since 2017. Expect fast jigs and reels alongside slow, haunting airs. The music runs from 7:30 to 9:30. Buy advance tickets to be sure of a seat.

title: Improv Eve with Sfyria Trio and Chatt-Town Unsound Collective
description: A free-improvising saxophone trio meets an improvised dance collective at Barking Legs Theater on December 13.
body: Sfyria Trio plays pure free improvisation. The band pairs saxophone, bass, and drums into moody, textured sound. They build music from small motifs and shifting timbres. The Chatt-Town Unsound Collective improvises dance alongside the music. Nothing is scored, so every moment unfolds live. The two groups follow a free, dreamlike logic together. Music runs from 7:30 to 9:30. Advance tickets are available.

title: Knackered Ramblers: Mike Compton & Laura Boosinger
description: The Knackered Ramblers bring bluegrass, old-time, and shaped-note hymns to Barking Legs Theater on December 12.
body: The Knackered Ramblers pair mandolinist Mike Compton with singer Laura Boosinger. Their set blends traditional country, old-time, and early bluegrass. Compton is widely regarded as one of the finest traditional mandolinists working today, with a career rooted in Nashville and deep old-time repertoire. Boosinger is an Asheville-based singer and old-time fiddler with a strong connection to Appalachian vocal traditions. Together they present pre-commercial country and folk music in a close, seated listening format. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue is well suited to this kind of traditional acoustic performance. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Liminal Lounge: A Listening Experience
description: Liminal Lounge brings a focused listening experience to Barking Legs Theater on October 16.
body: Liminal Lounge is built for real listening, not background noise. The set fills the Barking Legs room on Dodds Avenue from start to finish without interruption. The format asks the audience to settle in and pay close attention to the music. The artist or artists performing shift with each edition of the event. Check the Barking Legs website for the current lineup and ticket details. The room seats about 100 people in an intimate arrangement. This is a rare format for Chattanooga - a performance environment built entirely around attentive, focused listening.

title: Monday Nite Big Band: Jazz Fest Preview Night
description: The Chattanooga Monday Nite Big Band previews its Chattanooga Jazz Fest set at Barking Legs Theater on October 5.
body: The Chattanooga Monday Nite Big Band previews its set for the Second Annual Chattanooga Jazz Fest. The full ensemble plays before the festival opens. This preview night gives fans a close look at the band before the main event. The Monday Nite Big Band is a Chattanooga institution that has played weekly since the 1970s. The ensemble covers the classic big band repertoire including swing, bebop, and jazz standards. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue is a close, intimate venue for a 17-piece ensemble. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time.

title: Monday Nite Big Band
description: The Monday Nite Big Band plays four decades of big band jazz at Barking Legs Theater on November 2.
body: The Monday Nite Big Band fills the Barking Legs stage on Dodds Avenue. Professional players carry more than forty years of big band jazz. The horn section drives a full, swinging sound through the room. The music runs from 7:30 to 9:30. Tickets are available at the door.

title: New Threads: Spit in Your Face New Works Staged Reading
description: Barking Legs Theater hosts a staged reading of Spit in Your Face, a provocative new work, on October 2.
body: New Threads is a staged reading of new theatrical work at Barking Legs Theater. Spit in Your Face is witty, provocative, and honest. The play asks who gets to tell whose stories and at what cost. A staged reading keeps the focus on the script with a minimal set. The reading starts at 7:00 and runs about an hour. See the theater website for tickets.

title: NUFF: Nooga Underground Film Fest
description: NUFF is Chattanooga's underground film festival at Barking Legs Theater, screening horror, exploitation, and cult cinema across two days.
body: The Nooga Underground Film Fest celebrates counterculture and cult cinema. NUFF screens films you rarely find elsewhere. The lineup leans into horror, exploitation, extreme violence, and crime thrillers. The festival runs across two days with film blocks, filmmaker Q&As, and craft beer. It also folds in special programming such as a comedy show. Doors open at noon each day and screenings continue into the evening.

title: One Hit Wonders
description: Barking Legs Theater presents One Hit Wonders, a night of songs you know, on September 4.
body: One Hit Wonders packs a set with the songs everyone half remembers. The band plays them back to back at Barking Legs on a Friday. The concept is simple and works every time - the room lights up for songs that defined a year and then disappeared. The band covers decades of one-hit wonders from pop, rock, and R&B. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue seats about 100. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. This is an easy, fun night out that works for a wide range of music fans.

title: Oops! All Kings
description: A King of Drag Season 2 premiere viewing plus live drag king performances at Barking Legs Theater on September 20.
body: Oops! All Kings pairs a viewing of the King of Drag Season 2 premiere with live local talent. The night spotlights drag performers and celebrates the season launch. Local drag artists perform before and between viewing segments. The event takes place at Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. This is a community gathering for fans of drag and reality competition television. The format mixes the viewing party atmosphere with live performance, making it more than a simple watch party.

title: Queens for a Cause
description: Queens for a Cause is a drag benefit at Barking Legs Theater on September 24. All proceeds fund surgery for Evelyn.
body: Queens for a Cause is a drag benefit at Barking Legs Theater. Performers take the Dodds Avenue stage to raise money for a Chattanooga nonprofit or community cause. The specific beneficiary changes each edition. Local drag artists perform sets across the evening while the audience shows support through ticket purchases and tips. Barking Legs is an intimate venue of about 100 seats. Check the venue website for the current beneficiary, performing artists, and ticket details. This is one of several community-benefit drag shows that Barking Legs hosts through the year.

title: The Pop-Up Project Presents Razzle Dazzle VIP Reception
description: The Pop-Up Project hosts the Razzle Dazzle VIP reception, a fundraiser with warm food and a bonfire, at Barking Legs Theater on November 19.
body: The Pop-Up Project hosts the Razzle Dazzle VIP reception as a fundraiser. The outdoor garden sets the scene with a bonfire and a cozy atmosphere. Guests enjoy warm food and beverages through the evening. Early bird tickets cost $40 until November 12. The reception runs from 8:30 to 10:30.

title: Reverence | AP
description: Saxophonist Austin Pettit brings his band Reverence to the Wednesday Jazz series at Barking Legs Theater on December 9.
body: Saxophonist Austin Pettit leads his band Reverence for this Wednesday Jazz set. Pettit is a respected name in the Chattanooga jazz scene and plays with several area groups. His band features young players pushing the music forward. The set showcases the next generation taking jazz to a new level. Music runs from 7:30 to 9:30.

title: Rocky Horror Picture Show Accessible Showing
description: Seed Theatre hosts a neurodivergent-friendly Rocky Horror showing with ASL interpretation at Barking Legs on October 29.
body: Seed Theatre stages a neurodivergent-friendly Rocky Horror Picture Show. The team adjusts lighting, sound, and audience expectations to make the experience accessible to sensory-sensitive attendees. The classic 1975 film plays with live shadowcast performance. Audience props are available but participation is never required. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue seats about 100. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. This showing is intended for anyone who wants the full Rocky Horror experience in a lower-stimulation environment. It runs before the Halloween weekend performances.

title: Rocky Horror Picture Show (Saturday Evening)
description: Seed Theatre performs a Saturday evening Rocky Horror shadowcast at Barking Legs Theater on October 24.
body: Seed Theatre returns for a Saturday evening Rocky Horror Picture Show. The cast performs the cult classic live beside the film in full shadowcast style. Audience props bags are sold at the door. This is the evening show - the late show runs later the same night. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue seats about 100. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The Saturday evening show is typically the most family-accessible time slot in the Halloween run. The late show on the same night draws a different, more raucous crowd.

title: Rocky Horror Picture Show (Saturday Late Show)
description: Seed Theatre performs a late-night Rocky Horror shadowcast at Barking Legs Theater on October 24.
body: Seed Theatre closes Saturday with a late-night Rocky Horror Picture Show. The cast shadowcasts the film live in full Broadway-style costumes and choreography. Audience props bags are sold at the door. The late show draws the most participatory crowd of the Halloween run. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue seats about 100. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. This is the rowdiest edition of Seed Theatre's Halloween season - arrive ready to participate. The cast expects and encourages audience interaction throughout the film.

title: Rocky Horror Picture Show (Seed Theatre)
description: Seed Theatre stages a live Rocky Horror Picture Show shadowcast at Barking Legs Theater on October 23.
body: Seed Theatre performs The Rocky Horror Picture Show live beside the film. This Broadway-style shadowcast adds costumes, choreography, and crowd participation to the classic 1975 cult film. Audience props bags are sold at the door. The cast performs every move while the original film plays on screen. This is an early show - the late show on the same night is a separate event. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue seats about 100. Check the venue website for ticket details. This Halloween season run includes multiple performances across the week.

title: Seed: Call Me Ursula
description: Seed Theatre presents Call Me Ursula, a musical portrait of Disney's Sea Witch, at Barking Legs on October 25.
body: Jason B. Schmidt performs Call Me Ursula at Barking Legs Theater. The musical digs into Disney's Sea Witch and her origin story. Schmidt writes and performs this one-person show that reframes the villain from The Little Mermaid. The production combines original songs with monologue and theatrical character work. Seed Theatre produces original and experimental theater at Barking Legs on Dodds Avenue. Check the venue website for ticket details and performance dates. The show runs multiple evenings. It is part of Seed Theatre's ongoing commitment to new and boundary-pushing work in Chattanooga.

title: Seed: Rocky Horror Picture Show (Friday)
description: Seed Theatre performs a Friday Rocky Horror shadowcast at Barking Legs Theater on October 30.
body: Seed Theatre opens Halloween weekend with a Friday Rocky Horror Picture Show. The cast performs the film live in full Broadway shadowcast costumes and choreography. Audience props bags are sold at the door. This is the first of multiple performances across the Halloween weekend. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue seats about 100. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. Friday's show is usually the first to sell out as fans plan their Halloween weekend around the Seed Theatre run.

title: Seed: Rocky Horror Picture Show (Halloween Evening)
description: Seed Theatre performs a Halloween evening Rocky Horror shadowcast at Barking Legs Theater on October 31.
body: Seed Theatre marks Halloween night with a live Rocky Horror Picture Show. The cast shadowcasts the cult classic in full Broadway-style costumes and choreography. Audience props bags are sold at the door. This is the evening performance on Halloween night - a separate late show follows later. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue seats about 100. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. This performance marks the peak of Seed Theatre's Halloween season, which includes multiple Rocky Horror runs across the final week of October.

title: Seed: Rocky Horror Picture Show (Halloween Late Show)
description: Seed Theatre performs a Halloween late-night Rocky Horror shadowcast at Barking Legs Theater on October 31.
body: Seed Theatre closes Halloween with a late-night Rocky Horror Picture Show. The cast performs the film live in full Broadway shadowcast style - costumes, choreography, and crowd interaction. Audience props bags are sold at the door. The late show runs after the earlier evening performance. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue seats about 100. Check the venue website for ticket details. The late show traditionally draws the most enthusiastic audience of the Halloween run. This is the final performance of Seed Theatre's Rocky Horror season.

title: Seed Theatre Benefit Show
description: A drag benefit show hosted by River Abrasax at Barking Legs Theater, raising funds for Seed Theatre on November 15.
body: Seed Theatre hosts a drag benefit show to raise money for its productions. River Abrasax hosts a night of drag performances from local artists. Proceeds go directly to Seed Theatre's production budget for upcoming shows. The company produces original and experimental theater at Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. Seed Theatre has become a consistent force in Chattanooga's independent theater scene. This benefit gives audiences a fun night out while directly supporting new work in the city.

title: Seed Theatre's Cat on a Hot Tin Roof
description: Seed Theatre stages Tennessee Williams' Cat on a Hot Tin Roof at Barking Legs Theater on September 11.
body: Seed Theatre stages Tennessee Williams' Cat on a Hot Tin Roof at Barking Legs. Director Mixy Mixon reads the play through the lens of family silence, desire, and truth-telling. The production features Seed Theatre's core ensemble. Cat on a Hot Tin Roof is a 1955 Pulitzer Prize-winning drama set on a Mississippi plantation during a birthday celebration. The play centers on Brick, Maggie, and Big Daddy as long-buried family tensions explode over one night. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue seats about 100. Check the venue website for ticket details.

title: Stephen Powers Sextet
description: Guitarist Stephen Powers leads his jazz sextet for Wednesday Jazz at Barking Legs Theater on December 15.
body: Guitarist Stephen Powers leads a strong new generation of Chattanooga jazz players. His sextet features saxophonists Grady Dickinson and Matt Roehrich up front. A full rhythm section drives the band behind them. Powers is known for sharp technique and steady growth as a player. The group plays regularly around the city. Music runs from 7:30 to 9:30 on Dodds Avenue. Advance tickets are available.

title: The Monthly Jazz Jam for Pros
description: Professional musicians trade sets with a rotating house trio at the Monthly Jazz Jam at Barking Legs Theater on October 26.
body: The Monthly Jazz Jam brings working pros to the Barking Legs lounge on Dodds Avenue. A rotating house trio anchors the night. Players sit in and swap standards across the set. The music runs from 7:30 to 9:30. Tickets are $10 in advance or $12 at the door.

title: The Oz Noy Trio
description: The Oz Noy Trio headlines a special Wednesday Jazz night at Barking Legs Theater on October 21.
body: Guitarist Oz Noy brings his trio to Barking Legs for a special Wednesday jazz night. His playing bends jazz toward funk and rock, with unusual chord choices and percussive attack. Noy is an Israeli-born New York guitarist who has played with Dave Weckl, Chris Potter, and others in the jazz and fusion world. His studio recordings blend jazz, funk, and blues into a distinctive solo sound. The trio format keeps the focus on his guitar while bass and drums provide the rhythmic foundation. Barking Legs on Dodds Avenue is an intimate space for this kind of guitar-centric jazz. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: The Silent Light presents Live Metal Scoring to Silent Films
description: The Silent Light scores classic silent films with live heavy metal at Barking Legs Theater on October 9.
body: The Silent Light plays live heavy metal beneath two classic silent films. The program pairs Faust with A Page of Madness, two expressionist films from the 1920s. The band performs original metal compositions timed to the films in a live synchronized performance. This is an unusual and genuinely compelling art event at Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue. The combination of early film and live heavy metal creates a contrast that works in a 100-seat intimate venue. Check the Barking Legs website for ticket details and start time.

title: The Thanksgiving Play (Evening)
description: Seed Theatre's evening showing of Larissa FastHorse's satire at Barking Legs Theater on December 5.
body: Seed Theatre stages Larissa FastHorse's sharp satire. FastHorse is the first Native American playwright with one of the most produced plays in America. Four well-meaning white artists try to build a culturally sensitive Thanksgiving play for schoolchildren. Their good intentions fall apart fast. The comedy skewers performative activism and liberal guilt. Doors and seating are limited, so arrive early for this run.

title: The Thanksgiving Play (Matinee)
description: Seed Theatre's afternoon showing of Larissa FastHorse's satire at Barking Legs Theater on December 5.
body: Seed Theatre stages Larissa FastHorse's sharp satire. FastHorse is the first Native American playwright with one of the most produced plays in America. title: Threads: Footnotes
description: Threads: Footnotes premieres a Southern skateboarding video at Barking Legs Theater on October 17. Admission is free.
body: Threads: Footnotes premieres a new skateboarding video at Barking Legs Theater. The film features local skaters from across the Chattanooga area. Footage was shot at parks and street spots in and around the city over the past year. The premiere includes a live event with the filmmakers and skaters present. Barking Legs on Dodds Avenue provides the screening space. Check the Barking Legs website for ticket details and start time. This is a celebration of the local skate community and a document of the streets and parks they use.

title: Wednesday Jazz: Alan Wyatt Quartet
description: The Alan Wyatt Quartet plays the weekly Wednesday Jazz series at Barking Legs Theater on September 2.
body: The Alan Wyatt Quartet returns to the Barking Legs lounge for Wednesday jazz. Settle in near the band on Dodds Avenue for an evening of jazz standards and original compositions. Wyatt is a Chattanooga-based pianist and bandleader who has performed in the region for years. The quartet format builds on the interplay between piano, bass, drums, and a horn or guitar. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue is an intimate jazz venue that seats about 100. Suggested donation at the door. This is a weekly series - arrive early for a table close to the stage.

title: Wednesday Jazz: Bob Stagner & Friends
description: Percussionist Bob Stagner leads a quartet for the Wednesday Jazz series at Barking Legs Theater on November 11.
body: Percussionist Bob Stagner leads a quartet in the Barking Legs lounge for Wednesday jazz. Stagner is a longtime fixture of the Chattanooga music scene. His friends fill out a loose, inventive set on Dodds Avenue. The music runs from 7:30 to 9:30. Tickets are available at the door.

title: Wednesday Jazz: Eric Vaughn Trio
description: High-energy pianist Eric Vaughn brings his trio to Wednesday Jazz at Barking Legs Theater on September 23.
body: Eric Vaughn is a high-energy pianist with a spry, joyful touch at the keys. He leads a trio with bass and drums for this Wednesday Jazz set. His playing blends swinging standards with his own bright compositions. Music runs from 7:30 to 9:30 in the Barking Legs lounge. Tickets are $10 in advance or $12 at the door. Barking Legs Theater is on Dodds Avenue in Chattanooga and seats about 100. The Wednesday Jazz series is a weekly event. Arrive early for a good seat.

title: Wednesday Jazz: Kash Wright Trio
description: Pianist Kash Wright leads his classic jazz trio for the Wednesday Jazz series at Barking Legs Theater on October 28.
body: Pianist Kash Wright leads a classic jazz trio in the Barking Legs lounge. Acoustic bass and drums round out the group. The trio plays standards and originals with an easy, warm feel. Vocalist Rishard joins for the night. The music runs from 7:30 to 9:30. Tickets are $10 in advance or $12 at the door.

title: Wednesday Jazz: Mark Jones Quartet
description: The Mark Jones Quartet plays the weekly Wednesday Jazz series at Barking Legs Theater on October 14.
body: Guitarist Mark Jones leads the quartet for this week's Wednesday Jazz set. He plays alongside Jim Crumble, Tony Tortora, and David Nix in a rotating cast of Chattanooga jazz regulars. Jones is a veteran of the local jazz scene with years of performance at Barking Legs and other regional venues. The quartet covers jazz standards and original compositions in an intimate listening format. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue seats about 100. Suggested donation at the door. Wednesday Jazz runs year-round and is one of the most consistent jazz programs in the city.

title: Wednesday Jazz: Marquis Dotson & Friends
description: Keyboardist Marquis Dotson leads the band for the Wednesday Jazz series at Barking Legs Theater on November 18.
body: Marquis Dotson steps up as band leader for this Wednesday Jazz set. Dotson is a mainstay on keys in the Chattanooga jazz scene. He has anchored Wednesday Jazz at Barking Legs for years and released his album Keybridge in 2017. The performance moves to the lounge for the night. Music runs from 7:30 to 9:30.

title: Wednesday Jazz: Nathan Warner Quartet
description: Trumpeter Nathan Warner leads his quartet for the Wednesday Jazz series at Barking Legs Theater on December 2.
body: Trumpeter Nathan Warner leads his quartet for this Wednesday Jazz set. Warner moved to Chattanooga from New York City and plays with regional symphonies. His range runs from screaming lead lines to tender ballads. The quartet features Shawn Perkinson on guitar, David Schwab on bass, and Matt Turnure on drums. Music runs from 7:30 to 9:30.

title: Wednesday Jazz Special: Josh Couts Quintet
description: The Josh Couts Quintet plays a Wednesday Jazz Special at Barking Legs Theater on September 30.
body: Huntsville guitarist Josh Couts leads his quintet on the Barking Legs stage. Couts teaches jazz at the University of Alabama in Huntsville and performs across the Southeast. The quintet format gives the music room to breathe with interlocking parts across guitar, bass, drums, and horns. This is a special edition of the weekly Wednesday Jazz series. Barking Legs Theater on Dodds Avenue is an intimate venue where jazz sounds close and detailed. Suggested donation at the door. The room holds about 100 people. Arrive early to get a good seat near the stage.

title: 20 Years of Weeks with Lenox Hills
description: 20 Years of Weeks anniversary show at Barrelhouse Ballroom on November 21 with Lenox Hills.
body: 20 Years of Weeks marks the anniversary at Barrelhouse Ballroom with Lenox Hills on the bill. Saturday night show on Long St. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 21+. Lenox Hills is a Chattanooga-area country and Americana band. The band has played local stages for years and built a loyal local following. 20 Years of Weeks is an anniversary event - the specific milestone and context is shared through the venue's social pages. Doors at 7pm. Check the site for the full billing and any support acts scheduled for the evening.

title: 423 Frequency: A House Music Experience
description: 423 Frequency brings a late-night house music set to Barrelhouse Ballroom on November 28.
body: 423 Frequency is a house music night built for the dance floor. The name nods to the Chattanooga area code. DJs run four-on-the-floor sets from deep house to driving grooves. Doors open late at 9pm, so the night runs long. Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday. $15 advance or $20 at the door. 18+.

title: 65 North Pickers with The Great Outdoors
description: 65 North Pickers bring jam-grass to Barrelhouse Ballroom on January 22. Doors at 7pm, 18+.
body: 65 North Pickers are a Kentucky bluegrass quartet with a jam-band streak. They pair fast, clean picking with long improvised runs. Their originals nod to the Grateful Dead and festival-era psychedelia. The band plays Chattanooga often and draws a loyal crowd. The Great Outdoors open the show. Doors at 7pm, music at 8pm on Long St. $20 advance or $25 at the door. 18+. This is a stand-and-dance show, so plan to be on your feet.

title: A Town Hall Show
description: A Town Hall Show plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on September 17.
body: A Town Hall Show lands at Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Thursday night. Doors at 7pm, music at 8pm on Long St. $20 advance or $23 at the door. 18+. A Town Hall is a Nashville rock act known for high-energy performances and sharp songwriting. The band builds anthemic rock songs with layered production and strong hooks. They have toured nationally and released recordings that sit in the modern rock and indie rock space. Barrelhouse Ballroom is a mid-size venue well suited to the band's volume and energy. Check the site for support acts.

title: Back 2 Mac: Fleetwood Mac Tribute
description: Back 2 Mac brings a Fleetwood Mac tribute to Barrelhouse Ballroom on September 11. Doors at 7pm, 18+.
body: Back 2 Mac runs the Fleetwood Mac catalog at Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Friday night in September. Doors at 7pm on Long St. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 21+. The tribute band covers all eras of Fleetwood Mac - the early British blues records, the Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks era, and the late 70s and 80s hits. Expect Rumours, Tusk, Mirage, and more. Back 2 Mac brings the full production including keyboards, multiple vocalists, and the layered guitar arrangements from the studio records. Check the site for final details.

title: Bertha: A Grateful Drag
description: Bertha: A Grateful Drag brings drag and Grateful Dead together at Barrelhouse Ballroom on November 5.
body: Bertha is a drag show built around the Grateful Dead catalog. It's exactly what it sounds like and it works. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St hosts this traveling production that blends drag performance with live Dead music and fan culture. Performers lip sync and dance to iconic songs while the room fills with tie-dye and dancing. The concept originated in the Northeast and has toured nationally. It appeals to Deadheads, drag fans, and anyone who wants a night that is genuinely unusual. Doors at 7pm. Check the site for ticket prices.

title: Black Stone Cherry
description: Black Stone Cherry bring southern hard rock to Barrelhouse Ballroom on November 29. Doors at 7pm, 18+.
body: Black Stone Cherry play southern hard rock built on heavy riffs and blues roots. The Kentucky band pulls from Lynyrd Skynyrd and Led Zeppelin. They bring big rock hooks to Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Sunday. Doors at 7pm, music at 8pm on Long St. $24 advance or $29 at the door. 18+. Barrelhouse Ballroom is on Long Street in downtown Chattanooga. Doors at 7pm. Check the venue site for ticket prices and support acts.

title: Blake Whiten with Slater Nalley
description: Blake Whiten plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on October 10 with Slater Nalley opening.
body: Blake Whiten plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday with Slater Nalley opening. Two acts on Long St - get there for the opener. Whiten is a Nashville-based country and Americana singer-songwriter with a strong, story-driven approach to songwriting. His live show is guitar-forward and rooted in classic country arrangements. Nalley is a Chattanooga-area singer-songwriter who opens for regional and national acts at Barrelhouse. Doors at 7pm on Long St. $22 advance or $27 at the door. Check the venue site for final details.

title: Bob Marley Birthday Bash
description: The Bob Marley Birthday Bash hits Barrelhouse Ballroom on February 5, 2027. A reggae night honoring Bob Marley. 18+.
body: The Bob Marley Birthday Bash lands at Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Friday. The show marks the birthday of reggae icon Bob Marley. Fans gather each February to honor his music and legacy. Expect live reggae and classic Marley songs played through the night. These celebrations pull reggae fans from across the region. The crowd dances and sings along to songs everyone knows. Doors open at 7pm. $15 advance or $20 at the door. 18+.

title: Boot Scootin Boogie Nights
description: Boot Scootin Boogie Nights country dance party at Barrelhouse Ballroom on October 9.
body: Boot Scootin Boogie Nights turns Barrelhouse Ballroom into a country dance floor on a Friday. $20 advance or $25 at the door. 21+. The event features DJ-driven country and line dance music from classic hits to current country chart songs. Instructors lead basic line dances earlier in the evening before the floor opens up. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St has the space and the sound system to handle a full country dance night. Doors at 7pm. Check the venue site for DJs and any special guests on the bill.

title: Brenn! Amateur At Best Tour
description: Brenn! plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on October 3 on the Amateur At Best Tour.
body: Brenn! brings the Amateur At Best Tour to Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday. Pricing TBA - check the website for tickets. 18+. Brenn! is a rising pop-punk and alternative artist with a growing online following. The Amateur At Best Tour marks a new album or EP cycle. Brenn!'s music blends early 2000s pop-punk energy with modern production. Live shows are energetic and fan-focused, with strong crowd interaction. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St is a mid-size venue suited to this kind of high-energy performance. Doors at 7pm. Check the site for ticket prices and support acts.

title: Brock Butler & Dr. Bacon
description: Brock Butler and Dr. Bacon play Barrelhouse Ballroom on September 5. 21+.
body: Brock Butler & Dr. Bacon bring a night of live music to Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Friday. Expect long jams and a loose, improvisational approach to the set. Butler is the frontman of Perpetual Groove, a Georgia jam band with a loyal following. Dr. Bacon is a Chattanooga-area roots and jam band. Together they play off each other in a bill that leans on improvisation and audience energy. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St is an ideal venue for this kind of collaborative evening. Doors at 7pm. Check the site for ticket prices.

title: Carter Faith
description: Carter Faith plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on October 1. Doors at 6:30pm, 21+.
body: Carter Faith opens October at Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Wednesday night. Doors at 6:30pm on Long St. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 18+. Faith is a Tennessee-raised country singer who plays modern country with a classic edge. Her voice sits in a confident, natural range, and her live show leans on acoustic instrumentation. She has released recordings and toured the Southeast. This is a mid-week show suited to fans who prefer a quieter start to the month. Check the venue site for support acts and final details.

title: Creed Fisher with KC Johns
description: Creed Fisher plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on November 20 with KC Johns opening.
body: Creed Fisher plays outlaw country and doesn't soften it for anyone. KC Johns opens. Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Friday. $25 advance or $30 at the door. 21+. Fisher is a Texas outlaw country artist who records independently and tours nationally. His music sits in the red dirt and outlaw country tradition and pulls from artists like Waylon Jennings and David Allan Coe. KC Johns is a Chattanooga-area country act. Doors at 7pm on Long St. Fisher plays to dedicated fans who prefer country that leans hard into the outlaw tradition. Check the venue site for final details.

title: Crimewave: A Darkwave Dance Party
description: Crimewave brings a darkwave and goth dance party to Barrelhouse Ballroom on January 30. Doors at 8pm, 18+.
body: Crimewave is a darkwave dance party built for the goth and post-punk crowd. DJs spin cold synths, drum machines, and heavy bass all night. Expect tracks that pull from darkwave, EBM, and classic goth. The dress code leans black, though all are welcome. Doors open at 8pm and the floor fills later. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St. $15 advance or $20 at the door. 18+. This is a late one, so pace yourself and plan a ride home.

title: Crowe Boys and Gareth
description: Crowe Boys play country-folk with Gareth opening at Barrelhouse Ballroom on February 26.
body: Crowe Boys are brothers Ocie and Wes Crowe, now signed to Universal Music Group Nashville. They blend country, folk, and alternative roots into a warm acoustic sound. Their song "Where Did I Go Wrong" went viral and pulled in a wide new audience. Gareth opens the night. Doors at 6:30pm. Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Friday. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 18+.

title: Departure: A Tribute to Journey
description: Departure plays a full set of Journey arena-rock hits at Barrelhouse Ballroom on December 4.
body: Departure is a national Journey tribute act with more than 15 years on the road. The band recreates the soaring vocals and arena-rock energy of the original. Expect a two-hour set of hits from the 1970s and 1980s. Think "Don't Stop Believin'" and the deep cuts. Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Friday. $22 advance or $25 at the door. 18+.

title: Dizgo
description: Dizgo bring their psychedelic funk to Barrelhouse Ballroom on September 25, a high-energy Friday 18+ show on Long Street.
body: Dizgo at Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Friday. They bring the psychedelic funk and don't let up. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 21+. Dizgo is a Nashville-based psychedelic funk and jam band. Their live shows build long, groove-heavy sets that move from tight funk to open improvisational territory. The band has toured nationally and plays clubs and festivals in the South and Midwest. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St gives them room to build and extend their sets. Doors at 7pm. Check the venue site for support acts and final details.

title: Drivin N Cryin
description: Southern rock institution Drivin N Cryin plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on September 26, a Saturday 21+ show with deep catalog.
body: Drivin N Cryin has been a Southern rock and alternative country institution since the '80s. They play Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday - the room is the right size for a band with this much catalog. $25 advance. 21+. The band formed in Atlanta in 1985. Frontman Kevn Kinney has led the group through decades of Southern rock, folk, and grunge-adjacent material. Their catalog includes albums released on Island Records and others. Live they lean on guitar-heavy arrangements and long sets. Doors at 7pm on Long St. Check the venue site for support acts.

title: El Desmadre
description: El Desmadre live at Barrelhouse Ballroom on October 16. Doors at 8pm, 18+.
body: El Desmadre brings the chaos back to Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Friday night. The name translates to the mayhem, and the event delivers on that promise. El Desmadre is a Chattanooga Latin night with live DJs spinning reggaeton, cumbia, Latin trap, and salsa. The dance floor fills early. The event has built a consistent monthly following on Long St. Doors at 8pm. Ticket prices vary - check the venue site. 18+. El Desmadre runs on the first or second Friday of each month. It is one of the few dedicated Latin music nights in Chattanooga.

title: ETC + Kasvott Chatt
description: ETC plays Barrelhouse Ballroom with Kasvott Chatt on September 12. Doors at 7pm, 18+.
body: ETC teams up with Kasvott Chatt for a Saturday night at Barrelhouse Ballroom in September. Doors at 7pm on Long St. $15 advance or $20 at the door. 18+. ETC is an electronic music act known for energetic live sets. Kasvott Chatt is a Chattanooga electronic and jam-influenced duo with a loyal local following. Together they build a night of live electronic and bass-influenced music on Long St. This is a double bill worth attending for fans of either artist or the broader electronic music community in Chattanooga. Check the site for final details.

title: Frankly Scarlet x Runaway Gin
description: Frankly Scarlet and Runaway Gin share the stage at Barrelhouse Ballroom on February 27, 2027. One honors the Grateful Dead, the other honors Phish. 18+.
body: Two jam band tributes share a bill at Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday. Frankly Scarlet plays the music of the Grateful Dead with loose, improvised takes on songs like Friend of the Devil. Runaway Gin covers Phish and recreates their long, intricate jams with care. Fans of both legends get one dancing night under one roof. Doors at 8pm on Long St. $20 advance or $25 at the door. 18+.

title: Gravedigger's Ball
description: The 5th Annual Gravedigger's Ball hits Barrelhouse Ballroom on October 30 with DJ Scuba Steve and a big costume contest. 18+.
body: The 5th Annual Gravedigger's Ball returns to Barrelhouse Ballroom on Friday, October 30. DJ Scuba Steve spins the night. The costume contest is one of the largest in town. Best couple or group wins $1,000 and best solo wins $500. Entry to the contest is free with a ticket, and sign-ups close at 10:30pm. Doors open at 8pm. Tickets cost $15 in advance or $20 at the door. This is an 18+ event.

title: Greylan James
description: Greylan James plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on December 12. The Nashville country singer and hit songwriter brings a contemporary country set. Doors early, 18+.
body: Greylan James plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday night. He is a Knoxville-raised, Nashville-based country singer and songwriter. James writes in the outlaw and Southern rock-influenced country tradition. His live show leans on guitar and earnest vocals. He has released recordings and built a following in the Tennessee and Southeast country scene. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St is a mid-size venue that suits his sound without losing the intimacy. Doors at 7pm. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 18+. Check the venue site for support acts and final details.

title: Grunge Night: Jeremy Would Let Me Drown
description: Jeremy Would Let Me Drown plays a grunge night at Barrelhouse Ballroom on January 29, 2027. Expect Pearl Jam, Alice in Chains, and Soundgarden. 21+.
body: Jeremy Would Let Me Drown brings a 90s grunge night to Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Friday. The Atlanta band pays tribute to Pearl Jam, Alice in Chains, and Soundgarden. Two singers trade lead vocals to match the styles of Eddie Vedder, Layne Staley, and Chris Cornell. Expect heavy riffs, dark energy, and the sound of an entire decade. Doors at 9pm on Long St. $15 advance or $20 at the door. 21+.

title: GrungeFest
description: GrungeFest revives early 90s grunge at Barrelhouse Ballroom on December 18. Music starts 8pm, 18+.
body: GrungeFest revives the sound of the early 90s at Barrelhouse Ballroom. Local bands cover Nirvana, Soundgarden, Pearl Jam, Alice in Chains, and others from the grunge era. The festival format puts multiple tribute acts on the stage through the evening. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St is a natural venue for high-volume guitar music. The event draws fans of the era who want to hear the songs played faithfully and loud. Doors at 7pm. Check the venue site for the full band lineup, ticket prices, and start time.

title: Halloween Party
description: Barrelhouse Ballroom throws a Halloween costume party with DJs on October 31. Doors at 9pm, 18+.
body: Barrelhouse Ballroom hosts a Halloween costume party on the night of October 31. DJs spin dance music while the room fills with costumes. The party runs late on Long St in downtown Chattanooga. Cash prizes go to the best costumes. Expect a mix of classic Halloween tracks, hip-hop, and electronic dance music from the DJ lineup. Barrelhouse Ballroom has held this annual party for multiple years. Doors at 8pm. 21+. Check the venue site for cover price, costume contest rules, and DJ lineup.

title: Hogslop String Band / Hannah Marie Kelley / Roy Caudill
description: Hogslop String Band bring old-time string music to Barrelhouse Ballroom on January 17. Doors at 6pm, 18+.
body: Hogslop String Band are a Nashville old-time band with seven members. They push old-time past its usual limits. Their sound mixes fiddle and banjo with rock, folk, and psychedelic streaks. The live show runs on stamina and sweat, and it often turns into a square dance. Hannah Marie Kelley and Roy Caudill open the night. Doors at 6pm, music at 7pm on Long St. $20 advance or $25 at the door. 18+. Come ready to dance near the stage, not sit still.

title: Holy Locust + Johanna Rose & The Dreamboats
description: Holy Locust and Johanna Rose & The Dreamboats play Barrelhouse Ballroom on December 18. Folk punk meets New Orleans jazz. 18+.
body: Holy Locust headlines Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Friday night. The five-piece acoustic band blends folk punk, gothic country, and Americana into something that sits outside easy category. Johanna Rose & The Dreamboats open. Rose is a Chattanooga-based Americana artist known for detailed, emotionally charged songwriting. This double bill brings two distinct styles of roots music to Long St. Doors at 7pm on Long St. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 18+. Check the venue site for final ticket details and start time.

title: IBMA Bluegrass Ramble
description: The IBMA Bluegrass Ramble brings juried showcase artists to Barrelhouse Ballroom on October 20 and 21 during World of Bluegrass.
body: The IBMA Bluegrass Ramble brings juried showcase artists to Barrelhouse Ballroom. It runs as part of IBMA World of Bluegrass in downtown Chattanooga. Judges pick the acts through a competitive application. The showcases spotlight rising and established bluegrass bands. Barrelhouse is one of several official Ramble venues this year. The Ramble format spreads across multiple downtown locations over several nights. Artists use the exposure to connect with labels, booking agents, and fans. Check the venue site for the nightly lineup and tickets.

title: IBMA World of Bluegrass 2026
description: Barrelhouse Ballroom hosts late-night bluegrass sets during IBMA World of Bluegrass weekend, starting October 23.
body: IBMA World of Bluegrass fills downtown Chattanooga with bluegrass in late October. Barrelhouse Ballroom hosts late-night sets during the festival weekend. Players and fans gather after the main stage shows for more music. The room stays open late for jams and showcase acts. Music starts around 11pm on Long St. Check the venue site for the lineup and cover. The festival draws thousands of bluegrass fans and industry professionals to Chattanooga. Barrelhouse is one of several official late-night venues. Expect a mix of established names and emerging acts on the stage.

title: Jason Scott & The High Heat x Marfa
description: Jason Scott & The High Heat plays Barrelhouse Ballroom with Marfa on September 19.
body: Jason Scott & The High Heat teams up with Marfa at Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday. Two bands worth showing up for. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 21+. Jason Scott & The High Heat is a Nashville-based roots rock and country act. Marfa is a Chattanooga-area band that blends indie rock and Americana. The pairing works well together and draws from overlapping audiences. Doors at 7pm on Long St. This is a Saturday night double bill that keeps the energy high across both sets. Check the venue site for final details.

title: John Morgan with Erin Kinsey
description: Country artist John Morgan plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on December 3 with Erin Kinsey opening. Doors 7pm, show 8pm, 18+.
body: John Morgan headlines Barrelhouse Ballroom on Thursday, December 3. The North Carolina singer blends bluegrass roots with modern country and rock. He co-wrote 16 songs with Jason Aldean and scored a 1 with his own single "Friends Like That." Texas artist Erin Kinsey opens. She is known for viral hits like "Just Drive" and "I Ain't Crazy." Doors open at 7pm and the show starts at 8pm. Tickets cost $25 in advance or $28 at the door. This is an 18+ show.

title: Kaitlin Butts: The Hello, HonkyTonk Tour
description: Kaitlin Butts brings the Hello, Honky Tonk Tour to Barrelhouse Ballroom on February 6, 2027. Classic country storytelling. 18+.
body: Kaitlin Butts plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday night. The Tulsa singer-songwriter tours behind her fourth album, Hello, Honky Tonk. Her style mixes classic country with humor and storytelling. She draws on Merle Haggard, Roger Miller, the Chicks, and Miranda Lambert. The album plays out like a musical set inside a honky tonk bar. Each song gives a character its moment in the spotlight. Doors open at 6:30pm. $20 advance or $25 at the door. 18+.

title: Keller Williams
description: Keller Williams brings his one-man live-looping jam set to Barrelhouse Ballroom on April 16. Doors at 7pm, 18+.
body: Keller Williams is a one-man jam band who builds full songs live. He layers acoustic guitar, bass, and vocals with looping pedals in real time. Nothing is prerecorded, so each loop stacks in front of the crowd. His sound blends bluegrass, funk, reggae, and groovy electronica. He takes requests and leans on call-and-response. Doors at 7pm, music at 8pm on Long St. $30 advance or $35 at the door. 18+. Get there early for a spot near the stage to watch the looping up close.

title: Kota the Friend
description: Kota the Friend live at Barrelhouse Ballroom on September 10. Doors at 8pm, 21+.
body: Brooklyn rapper and producer Kota the Friend plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Thursday night in September. He's been on a consistent run of releases since 2018. Kota builds self-produced rap with mellow, jazz-influenced beats and introspective lyrics. His album Everything series has earned him a large independent following. He tours consistently and plays mid-size listening room venues. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St seats several hundred and gives the show an intimate feel. Doors at 7pm, show at 8pm. Check the site for ticket prices and any support acts.

title: Locals Only: Clockwise
