description: Clockwise headlines the Locals Only night at Barrelhouse Ballroom on December 10. Doors 6pm, show 7pm, 18+.
body: Clockwise headlines the Locals Only night at Barrelhouse Ballroom on December 10. The Chattanooga band plays heavy music that blends deathcore, metal, and grunge. Doors open at 6pm and the show starts at 7pm. Tickets run $12 in advance or $15 at the door. 18+.

title: Lucero
description: Memphis country-punk band Lucero play Barrelhouse Ballroom on October 17, a Saturday 18+ show from a 25-year institution.
body: Lucero has been making Southern rock and country-punk out of Memphis for 25 years. They play Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday - the room suits the band's size and sound. The band has released over ten albums, most recently on Liberty and Lament Records. Their music pulls from punk, country, Americana, and Southern rock into a sound that is entirely their own. Frontman Ben Nichols writes plainspoken songs about loss, drinking, and the South. Doors at 7pm on Long St. $25 advance or $30 at the door. Check the site for support acts.

title: Madelyn Tallent with Camden Smith
description: Madelyn Tallent plays Barrelhouse Ballroom with Camden Smith on September 18. Doors at 7pm, 18+.
body: Madelyn Tallent headlines Barrelhouse Ballroom with Camden Smith opening on a Thursday in September. Doors at 7pm on Long St. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 18+. Tallent is a Chattanooga singer-songwriter with a strong voice and an Americana and folk-influenced sound. Smith is a Chattanooga-area guitarist and singer-songwriter who has opened for regional and national acts at Barrelhouse. This is a local double bill that keeps the room warm on a weeknight. Check the venue site for final details.

title: Magolia and Johnson Electric Co.
description: Magnolia and Johnson Electric Co. play Barrelhouse Ballroom on April 10, 2027. Doors 7pm, 18+.
body: Magnolia and Johnson Electric Co. bring their Americana rock to Barrelhouse Ballroom on April 10, 2027. The group pairs Will Johnson of Centro-matic with surviving members of Magnolia Electric Co. Their sets honor the songs of the late Jason Molina, mixing heavy rock with dark country. Doors at 7pm. Tickets run $25 in advance or $30 at the door. 18+.

title: MAINx24 at Barrelhouse Ballroom
description: Barrelhouse Ballroom joins MAINx24 on December 5. The Southside street festival runs noon to midnight on Long St.
body: MAINx24 is a 24-hour neighborhood festival on Chattanooga's Southside. Neighbors and merchants run it every December. Barrelhouse Ballroom hosts a full day of live music during the celebration. The venue stays open from noon to midnight. The wider festival adds a parade, open studios, a chili cook-off, and late-night dance parties. The whole event is free and family-friendly. Barrelhouse sits on Long St, a short walk from the Main Street action. Expect crowds and street parking that fills up fast, so arrive early.

title: Momentum NYE: Casey Club, TWOPERCENT, Saidimeant, Solnox, UP TEN
description: Momentum NYE brings a five-DJ electronic lineup to Barrelhouse Ballroom on December 31. Doors and show at 9pm, 18+.
body: Momentum NYE rings in 2027 at Barrelhouse Ballroom on Thursday, December 31. Five DJs share the bill: Casey Club, TWOPERCENT, Saidimeant, Solnox, and UP TEN. The night runs on high-energy electronic dance sets across the room. Doors and music both start at 9pm. Tickets cost $40 in advance or $45 at the door. This is an 18+ event. Plan to count down to midnight on the dance floor.

title: Night Moves
description: Night Moves bring their dreamy Minneapolis indie sound to Barrelhouse Ballroom on November 1, a Sunday 18+ show.
body: Night Moves brings their dreamy Minneapolis indie sound to Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Sunday. Doors at 7pm, show at 8pm on Long St. $20 advance or $23 at the door. 18+. The band formed in Minneapolis and builds slow-burning indie rock with synthesizers, reverb-heavy guitars, and breathy vocals. They have released albums on Domino Records. Critics compare them to artists like Real Estate and Whitney for their warm, unhurried approach to rock songwriting. The Sunday show suits their sound - easy and atmospheric rather than aggressive.

title: OmCat, Freedom Junction, Tin Roof Cats ft. Sugarlegg
description: OmCat, Freedom Junction, and Tin Roof Cats play Barrelhouse Ballroom on January 24, 2027. Jam and Grateful Dead tribute. 18+.
body: Three acts share the bill at Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Sunday. OmCat is a Nashville jam group formed in 2024. The band fuses many genres and improvises on stage. Three lead singers trade vocals, and their motto is "all music proposed is fair game." Tin Roof Cats plays the Grateful Dead catalog with high energy, featuring Sugarlegg. Freedom Junction fills out the lineup. Doors open at 6pm. $15 advance or $20 at the door. 18+.

title: Pass The Aux
description: Pass The Aux hands the playlist to the crowd at Barrelhouse Ballroom on October 2. Party starts 10pm, 21+.
body: Pass The Aux hands the playlist to the crowd. Anyone can queue a song and pack the floor with their pick. Expect a fast rotation of genres as the room takes over the music. This format runs at Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St. No cover or low door price makes it an accessible weeknight option. The night attracts a mix of regulars and new faces who want to hear something different from a programmed setlist. Doors at 7pm. Check the venue site for dates, start time, and any entry charge.

title: Pigeons Playing Ping Pong
description: Jam band Pigeons Playing Ping Pong plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on October 11.
body: Pigeons Playing Ping Pong brings their high-energy funk and jam sound to Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Sunday. They play long sets built on tight rhythmic grooves and extended improvisational sections. The band formed in Baltimore and has toured nationally for over a decade. Fans call themselves Flock members and follow the band across multiple nights. Their studio albums chart on the jam band charts. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St gives them room to stretch out. Doors at 7pm, show at 8pm. Check the venue site for ticket prices and support acts.

title: Post Animal: Maybe You Have To Tour
description: Post Animal plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on November 7 on the Maybe You Have To Tour.
body: Post Animal brings their psych-rock to Barrelhouse Ballroom on the Maybe You Have To Tour. Saturday night on Long St, doors at 7pm. The Chicago band blends heavy psychedelic guitar with driving rhythms and pop hooks. They have released albums on Polyvinyl Records and toured nationally. The band's members include Wyatt Shears, who also plays with The Garden. Post Animal's live show leans on volume and atmosphere. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 18+. Check the site for the support act and final details.

title: Pynk Beard
description: Pynk Beard plays a Thursday show at Barrelhouse Ballroom on October 8, a mid-week 21+ concert on Long Street.
body: Pynk Beard at Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Thursday. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 21+. Good mid-week show for those who keep late hours. Pynk Beard is a pop and dance artist known for high-energy live performances. His shows combine theatrical production with upbeat crowd interaction. He has built a following in the LGBTQ+ and dance music communities. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St is a natural fit for his brand of fun, inclusive, floor-filling sets. Doors at 7pm. Check the venue site for support acts and final lineup details.

title: REMakes
description: REMakes play an early R.E.M. tribute set at Barrelhouse Ballroom on November 13. Doors at 7pm, 21+.
body: REMakes recreate the early R.E.M. catalog with a faithful sound and energy. The Georgia tribute band has played this material for years. Their setlist pulls from Murmur, Reckoning, and Fables of the Reconstruction - the IRS Records years before R.E.M. became stadium-sized. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St seats several hundred and gives the show an intimate feel suited to this era of R.E.M.'s catalog. Doors at 7pm. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 18+. Check the venue site for support acts and final ticket details.

title: Saxsquatch
description: Saxsquatch brings the masked-sax show to Barrelhouse Ballroom on September 27. Doors at 7pm, 21+.
body: Saxsquatch - the sasquatch in a suit with a saxophone - lands at Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday night in September. The character-driven performance blends comedy, spectacle, and genuine saxophone playing into one wild act. Saxsquatch performs at clubs and festivals across the country and has built a loyal following online and in person. His shows are crowd-pleasing, energetic, and impossible to describe to someone who hasn't seen one. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St gives the act room to roam. Doors at 7pm. Check the site for ticket prices and support acts.

title: Shadowgrass
description: Shadowgrass live at Barrelhouse Ballroom on December 5. Doors at 8pm, 18+.
body: Shadowgrass closes out the year at Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday night in December. Doors at 8pm on Long St. $25 advance or $30 at the door. 21+. Shadowgrass is a progressive bluegrass and jam band from the Chattanooga area. Their sound blends traditional bluegrass instrumentation with rock energy and improvisational sections. The band has built a consistent following in the Southeast. A year-end show at Barrelhouse is a tradition for the band and their fans. Check the venue site for support acts and final ticket details.

title: Sicard Hollow with Omcat
description: Sicard Hollow plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on November 6 with Omcat opening.
body: Sicard Hollow brings their bluegrass-rooted jam sound to Barrelhouse Ballroom with Omcat opening. Friday night on Long St. Sicard Hollow is an Asheville, North Carolina jam band that blends bluegrass, folk, and rock into extended improvisational sets. They have toured the Southeast and built a following in the festival and listening room circuit. Omcat is a Chattanooga-area opener. Doors at 7pm. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 21+. Check the venue site for the final ticket details and start time.

title: Sippy
description: Bass producer Sippy brings her heavy dubstep set to Barrelhouse Ballroom on April 17. Doors at 9pm, 18+.
body: Sippy is a Sydney-born bass producer now based in Los Angeles. She is known for fearless sound design and heavy, stage-commanding sets. Her music hits hard with dubstep and riddim and gritty bass. She has played Lost Lands, Bonnaroo, and Red Rocks, and she has remixed Zeds Dead and Marshmello. Her 2025 album Scars in Stereo marked her debut full-length. Doors at 9pm on Long St. 18+. Check the venue site for ticket prices and set times. Bring earplugs, since the low end runs loud.

title: SoDown with Blossm, Valleria, Jawnra
description: SoDown brings live electronic music to Barrelhouse Ballroom on September 4, with Blossm, Valleria, and Jawnra. Doors at 8pm, 18+.
body: SoDown headlines Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Friday night in September. Blossm, Valleria, and Jawnra open the bill. Doors at 8pm and the show starts at 9pm. Expect bass-heavy live electronic sets. $25 advance or $30 at the door. 18+. SoDown is a Denver-based producer and multi-instrumentalist who blends bass music with funk and soul. His live performances incorporate saxophone, keys, and live production. Blossm and Valleria are electronic artists known for melodic bass sets. Jawnra adds another layer of live electronic energy to the opening run.

title: Sundy Best
description: Eastern Kentucky country-folk duo Sundy Best play Barrelhouse Ballroom on December 18, a Friday 18+ show of back-porch stomp and soul.
body: Sundy Best is a country-folk duo from Prestonsburg in eastern Kentucky. Nick Jamerson and Kris Bentley build a stomping back-porch sound from acoustic guitar, cajón, and tight vocal harmony. They mix Appalachian folk, bluegrass, rock, and soul. The Kentucky Music Hall of Fame named them to its Class of 2026. This is a Friday 18+ show. Doors open at 8:00pm. Tickets run $25 in advance.

title: The Band Feel with Parrotfish
description: The Band Feel plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on January 23, 2027 with Parrotfish opening. Folk-rock and retro soul. 18+.
body: The Band Feel plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday night. The group mixes folk-rock and retro soul. Their classic rock sound sits between Led Zeppelin and The Black Crowes. Their debut LP, What of Now, came out in August 2026. Parrotfish opens the night. The Nashville quartet slides between alternative rock, pop-punk, reggae, and funk. They lean on funky riffs and three-part harmonies. Doors open at 7pm. $20 advance or $25 at the door. 18+.

title: The Broken Hearts: Tribute to Tom Petty and The Heartbreakers
description: The Broken Hearts play a full Tom Petty set at Barrelhouse Ballroom on March 26.
body: The Broken Hearts are a national Tom Petty tribute band from Gainesville, Florida. Former Petty and Mudcrutch bassist Charlie Souza started the group in 2017. The set runs through the classics like "American Girl," "Free Fallin'," and "Refugee." The band aims to match the sound and feel of a real Heartbreakers show. Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Friday. $20 advance or $25 at the door. 18+.

title: The Heavy Heavy with The Point
description: The Heavy Heavy play Barrelhouse Ballroom with The Point on November 14. Doors at 8pm, 18+.
body: The Heavy Heavy are a Brighton, UK band who play a warm blend of psychedelic rock, blues, and sunshine pop. Their sound pulls from California 70s rock and British folk-rock. The Point is a Chattanooga-area opener. The Heavy Heavy have released recordings on independent labels and toured Europe and the United States. Their live show leans on jangly guitars, organ, and harmonies. Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St is a good-sized room for this kind of atmospheric rock. Doors at 7pm. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 18+. Check the site for final details.

title: The Jeremy McComb Honky-Tonk Circus Tour
description: Jeremy McComb brings the Honky-Tonk Circus Tour to Barrelhouse Ballroom on November 12.
body: Jeremy McComb's Honky-Tonk Circus Tour rolls into Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Thursday. Country and Western with some showmanship thrown in. McComb is a Nashville-based country artist who has toured with major acts and appeared on major country radio. His live show blends traditional honky-tonk with high-energy stage presence. The Honky-Tonk Circus Tour name signals a show built for movement and fun. Doors at 7pm on Long St. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 18+. Check the venue site for support acts and final details.

title: The Stolen Faces
description: The Stolen Faces bring their Grateful Dead tribute to Barrelhouse Ballroom on November 27. Doors at 8pm, 21+.
body: The Stolen Faces are a Nashville band that has played the music of the Grateful Dead since 2014. They cover the Dead's deep catalog with the loose, soulful feel of a seasoned jam band. Expect long jams and a dancing crowd on this Friday after Thanksgiving. Doors at 8pm on Long St. $15 advance or $20 at the door. 21+.

title: Tucker Underwood with Madelyn Tallent and Tyler Garrett
description: Chattanooga country artist Tucker Underwood plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on September 18 with Madelyn Tallent and Tyler Garrett. Doors 8pm, 18+.
body: Tucker Underwood is a Chattanooga country artist and multi-instrumentalist. His sound blends modern country, country rock, and Southern Americana. Madelyn Tallent and Tyler Garrett open the bill. Tallent is a Chattanooga singer-songwriter known for strong vocals and heartfelt storytelling. Garrett is a Chattanooga-area guitarist and songwriter. The three acts make this a strong local country bill at Barrelhouse Ballroom on Long St. Doors at 7pm. $22 advance or $27 at the door. 18+. Check the venue site for final ticket details.

title: Velcro Pygmies
description: Velcro Pygmies bring their 80s hair-rock show to Barrelhouse Ballroom on December 26. Doors 7pm, 18+.
body: Velcro Pygmies play loud, loose 80s hair rock at Barrelhouse Ballroom on December 26. The Louisville band formed in 1990 and leans on big guitars, Van Halen energy, and stage theatrics. Expect a party set the night after Christmas. Doors at 7pm. Tickets run $22 in advance or $25 at the door. 18+.

title: Wolph
description: Wolph brings Southern and psychedelic rock to Barrelhouse Ballroom on October 29. Doors 7pm, show 8pm, 18+.
body: Wolph plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on Thursday, October 29. The Virginia band mixes classic rock, blues, Southern rock, and psychedelic rock into a loose, jam-heavy set. Their sound leans on long guitar runs and steady groove. Doors open at 7pm and the show starts at 8pm. Tickets cost $15 in advance or $20 at the door. This is an 18+ show.

title: Youth Fountain
description: Youth Fountain plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on February 7, 2027. The Vancouver pop punk band brings big hooks and raw emo lyrics. 18+.
body: Youth Fountain plays Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday night. The Vancouver band works in pop punk and emo. Singer Tyler Zanon writes raw, personal songs with big, anthemic hooks. Their sound sits near melodic hardcore but keeps moving past it. Albums like Letters to Our Former Selves charted on the alternative lists. $20 advance or $25 at the door. 18+.

title: Zach John King: Get to Drinkin' Tour
description: Zach John King brings his Get to Drinkin' Tour to Barrelhouse Ballroom on April 24, 2027. The Sony Nashville artist blends country with indie-rock. 18+.
body: Zach John King headlines the Get to Drinkin' Tour at Barrelhouse Ballroom on a Saturday. The Sony Music Nashville artist mixes modern country with an indie-pop pulse. His single Get to Drinkin' climbed the country charts and named this tour. King moved to Nashville in 2022 and has opened for Morgan Wallen and Luke Bryan. Doors at 8pm on Long St. $25 advance or $30 at the door. 18+.

title: Bessie Smith Legacy Gala 2026
description: The Bessie Smith Legacy Gala 2026 raises funds for the cultural center on November 14 at The Westin Chattanooga.
body: The Bessie Smith Legacy Gala is the center's yearly fundraiser. It honors the legacy of blues singer Bessie Smith and supports the center's programs. Guests enjoy an evening of dinner, music, and awards. The 2026 gala takes place at The Westin Chattanooga on Pine Street. Doors open at 6pm. Buy tickets through the center's website. The center is on Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard in Chattanooga. Check the BSCC website for ticket details and the specific program lineup.

title: Community Day: Featuring Art Contest Exhibit Opening and Free Museum Admission
description: Community Day at the Bessie Smith Cultural Center brings free museum admission and an art contest exhibit opening on February 6.
body: Community Day opens the center's doors for free. The day features the opening of the annual art contest exhibit. Local artists display their work across the galleries. Free museum admission means the whole collection is accessible to anyone who comes through the door. The Bessie Smith Cultural Center is on Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard in Chattanooga. The center holds exhibits, artifacts, and programs dedicated to African American history and culture. Check the BSCC website for the schedule of activities and the art contest exhibit opening time.

title: NPHC Lip Sync Showdown: Battle of the Greeks
description: Chattanooga's Black Greek-letter organizations face off in a lip sync battle at the Bessie Smith Cultural Center on February 4.
body: The NPHC Lip Sync Showdown pits Chattanooga's Black Greek-letter organizations against each other. Members of the Divine Nine perform choreographed lip sync routines. The crowd cheers on the strolls, steps, and stage antics. The battle runs from 6pm to 8pm at the center. Buy tickets through the Bessie Smith Cultural Center website. The Bessie Smith Cultural Center is on Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard in Chattanooga. Check the BSCC website for ticket details and the competing organizations.

title: Reel Conversations: TILL Movie Night
description: The Bessie Smith Cultural Center screens the film TILL with guided discussion on February 11.
body: Reel Conversations screens the film TILL, the story of Mamie Till-Mobley and her son Emmett. The movie night pairs the screening with a guided discussion. Guest panelists lead the conversation after the film. TILL was released in 2022 and directed by Chinonye Chukwu. It tells the story of Mamie Till-Mobley's fight for justice after her son Emmett was murdered in Mississippi in 1955. The Bessie Smith Cultural Center is on Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard in Chattanooga. Check the BSCC website for ticket details.

title: Voices That Shaped the Story: A Night of Black Journalism
description: The Bessie Smith Cultural Center celebrates Black journalism with writers and reporters on February 18.
body: Voices That Shaped the Story celebrates Black journalism. The night gathers writers and reporters to share their work and history. Panelists trace how Black journalists documented their communities and shaped national narratives. The Bessie Smith Cultural Center is on Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard in Chattanooga. The center serves as the city's primary institution dedicated to African American history and culture. Check the BSCC website for ticket details and start time. This is a panel and discussion format event that runs about two hours.

title: Chattanooga Boat Show 2027
description: The Chattanooga Boat Show returns to the Convention Center February 4-7, 2027 with hundreds of boats from local dealers and area vendors.
body: The Chattanooga Boat Show returns to the Convention Center over four days in February. Local dealers fill the floor with hundreds of boats. Walk the aisles and compare pontoons, fishing rigs, and ski boats in one place. Area vendors round out the show with gear and accessories. The show opens Thursday afternoon and runs through Sunday. A single day ticket costs $15. A weekend pass covers all four days for $25. Kids 6 to 12 get in for $5, and children under 5 are free. A free TWRA safety class runs Saturday at 9am. Anyone born after 1989 needs the Type 600 permit, and this class covers it. Parking is available at the Convention Center.

title: Joggers & Lagers
description: Free 5K run every Tuesday at 6pm from Chattanooga Brewing Co., with extended happy hour discounts for runners.
body: Lace up for a free 5K that steps off from Chattanooga Brewing every Tuesday at 6pm. Run it hard or walk it easy, then collect the reward: a dollar off pints and half-price appetizers. Chattanooga Brewing is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. The 5K route runs through the downtown area and takes about 30 minutes at a comfortable pace. No registration required - show up and join the group. The post-run discount makes staying for a pint an easy decision. Check the brewery social pages for any changes to the weekly schedule.

title: Magic the Gathering Meet Up
description: Unofficial Magic the Gathering meet up every Tuesday from 5-9pm at Chattanooga Brewing Co., with half-price apps and $4 pints.
body: Bring a deck to Chattanooga Brewing every Tuesday from 5 to 9pm and find a table for an unofficial Magic the Gathering meet up. Half price appetizers and $4 pints run the whole night. Grind a format or learn the ropes, either way it is an easy weeknight hang on Chestnut St. Chattanooga Brewing is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. The meet-up is free to join - you just need a deck and your own beverages.

title: Open Mic Night with Jack Endelouz
description: Open mic night hosted by Jack Endelouz every Thursday at Chattanooga Brewing Co. Sign-up at 6:30pm, music at 7pm.
body: Thursday is open mic night at Chattanooga Brewing, hosted by Jack Endelouz. Sign up starts at 6:30pm and the music kicks off at 7. Bring an instrument, a few songs, or just a set of ears. The room stays friendly to first timers and regulars alike, so there is no wrong way to show up. Chattanooga Brewing is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. No ticket required to sign up or watch.

title: Trivia with Barry
description: Free trivia night with Barry every Wednesday at 7pm at Chattanooga Brewing Co., with beer specials and half-price wings.
body: Wednesday nights belong to Barry at Chattanooga Brewing on Chestnut St. Trivia runs 7 to 9pm and points carry over week to week, so a steady crew builds a real edge. Beer specials and half price wings keep the table happy, and the top scorers walk out with prizes. Free to play. Chattanooga Brewing is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. No ticket required. Walk in and find a team of up to six.

title: Chattanooga Cars and Coffee - November 2026
description: Free monthly car show at Chattanooga State Campus. The November show is the final event of the 2026 season, running 8am to noon.
body: The November show closes out the 2026 Chattanooga Cars and Coffee season. It runs 8am to noon on the 3rd Sunday at Chattanooga State. All makes and models are welcome. Chattanooga Cars and Coffee meets monthly at Chattanooga State Community College on Amnicola Highway. The show draws collectors and enthusiasts from across Chattanooga and the surrounding region. No ticket required. Free to attend. Coffee is available on site. November typically draws a strong turnout as regulars make their last appearance before the winter break. Check the event social pages for any special guests or prizes.

title: Chattanooga Cars and Coffee - October 2026
description: Free monthly car show at Chattanooga State Campus. Classic and custom vehicles gather the 3rd Sunday of each month from 8am to noon.
body: Chattanooga Cars and Coffee meets on the 3rd Sunday of each month at Chattanooga State. The October show runs 8am to noon. All makes, models, and eras are welcome. The event draws collectors and enthusiasts from across Chattanooga and the surrounding region. Free to attend. No ticket required. Coffee is available on site. October is one of the most popular months for the show as the fall weather brings out the community and the light is good for photos. Check the event social pages for any special categories or guest appearances.

title: Chattanooga Cars and Coffee
description: Chattanooga Cars and Coffee is a free monthly car show at Chattanooga State on the 3rd Sunday of each month, March through November, from 8am to noon.
body: Chattanooga Cars and Coffee meets at Chattanooga State on the 3rd Sunday of each month from March through November. Hours run 8am to noon. The show is free and open to the public. Enthusiasts bring everything from daily drivers to show cars. Each month often has a loose theme. Past focuses have included Italian marques, BMW M cars, JDM imports, and American muscle. The lot at 4501 Amnicola Hwy fills up early, so arriving before 9am gets you the best view of the lineup.

title: Chattanooga Christmas Village Holiday Market
description: The Chattanooga Christmas Village Holiday Market at Camp Jordan Arena in East Ridge runs three days with 140-plus vendors, free Santa photos, and character meet-and-greets.
body: More than 140 vendors fill Camp Jordan Arena for three days of indoor holiday shopping. Friday runs 2pm to 7pm, Saturday 10am to 5pm, and Sunday 10am to 4pm. Admission is $8. Kids 12 and under get in free. Photo ops with Santa, the Grinch, and Cindy Lou Who are included at no extra charge. Camp Jordan Arena is at 323 Camp Jordan Pkwy in East Ridge, about 10 minutes from downtown Chattanooga via I-24 East.

title: Chattanooga Comic Con
description: Chattanooga Comic Con fills the Convention Center for two days each November. Expect a vendor hall, gaming hall, cosplay competition, celebrity guests, and panels covering comics, anime, and sci-fi.
body: Chattanooga Comic Con takes over the Convention Center for two days each November. The vendor hall runs comics, collectibles, and artist tables. The gaming hall stays open late on Saturday for board games and console play. Cosplay competitions run both days with categories for all ages. Tickets run $20 to $50 depending on day and access level. Kids 12 and under get in free. The event is cash only at the door, but an ATM is on site. Weekend passes and single-day tickets are available at chattanoogacomiccon.com.

title: Chattanooga Lookouts Home Games
description: Chattanooga Lookouts home games at Erlanger Park in the South Broad District. Southern League baseball in a new 8,032-seat ballpark.
body: The Chattanooga Lookouts play Southern League baseball at Erlanger Park. The ballpark opened in April 2026 in the South Broad District. It seats 8,032 fans. The Lookouts are a Double-A affiliate of the Cincinnati Reds. Erlanger Park is on Broad Street in the South Broad neighborhood. The stadium includes grass berm seating, club sections, and standard reserved seats. Check the Lookouts website for the full home schedule, ticket prices, and parking. Games typically start at 7:15pm on weeknights and 6:15pm on Saturdays. Sunday games start at 2:05pm. Kids and families are welcome.

title: Market at Erlanger Medical Mall
description: The Chattanooga Market at Erlanger Medical Mall every Wednesday, 10:30am–1:30pm in Lobby A. Fresh produce, local art, and live music. Free admission.
body: The Chattanooga Market runs at Erlanger Medical Mall every Wednesday from 10:30am to 1:30pm. Find it in Lobby A. Fresh produce, local art, and live music in a hospital setting. The Erlanger Market location serves patients, staff, and visitors who may not be able to reach the larger Saturday market. The selection includes local vendors with seasonal produce, prepared foods, and handmade goods. No ticket required. The Erlanger Medical Mall is on Citico Street in Chattanooga. Check the Chattanooga Market website for the current vendor list and any changes to the weekly schedule.

title: Chattanooga Market - River Market
description: The Chattanooga Market at Tennessee Aquarium Plaza every Saturday. Fresh produce, local art, live music, and food vendors on the downtown riverfront. Free admission.
body: The Chattanooga Market sets up at the Tennessee Aquarium Plaza every Saturday from 10am to 5pm. Fresh produce, local vendors, art, and live music on the downtown waterfront. The Chattanooga Market is one of the largest weekly markets in the region. It runs every Saturday from May through November at the aquarium plaza on Broad Street. Local farmers, food makers, and artisans set up each week. No ticket required. The waterfront location makes for an easy combination with a river walk or visit to other downtown attractions. Check the market website for the current vendor list.

title: Chattanooga New Year's Eve Celebration
description: Chattanooga's free New Year's Eve celebration returns to Coolidge Park on December 31. Expect a Kids Zone, live music on the Main Stage from 6pm, food vendors, and midnight fireworks over the Tennessee River.
body: Coolidge Park hosts Chattanooga's free New Year's Eve celebration on December 31. The park sits on the North Shore riverfront, across the Tennessee River from downtown. Family Fun Zones and a Kids Stage open in the afternoon. A Kid's Countdown runs near 5:55pm for families with young children who will not make midnight. The Main Stage brings live music from 6pm until the ball drops. Food and beverage vendors from around the city line the park. At midnight the crowd counts down together and fireworks light up the river. The City of Chattanooga hosts the event each year, and admission is free.

title: 25th Annual Chattanooga Oktoberfest
description: The 25th Annual Chattanooga Oktoberfest brings two days of live Oompah music, craft beer, Bavarian food, and family activities to First Horizon Pavilion.
body: Chattanooga's longest-running Oktoberfest lands at First Horizon Pavilion for two days. Live Oompah music plays under the main tent all weekend. The Biergarten pours from local, regional, and international breweries. Saturday runs 10am to 8pm and Sunday runs 11am to 5pm. Contests include brat toss and stein hoisting. Kids get face painting and balloon animals. Free admission, card-only payments for food and beer.

title: Chattanooga Pride Parade & Festival
description: Chattanooga Pride brings a parade and free outdoor festival to the downtown riverfront each October. Expect live music, drag performances, vendors, food, and family activities.
body: Chattanooga Pride takes over Ross's Landing on the downtown riverfront each October for a free all-day parade and festival. The parade steps off in the morning and winds through downtown before the festival opens at noon. Live music, drag performances, vendors, food stalls, and informational booths run through the evening. The event is free and family friendly. Full schedule and entertainment lineup are posted at chattanoogapride.com as the date approaches.

title: Chattanooga Renaissance Faire
description: The Chattanooga Renaissance Faire runs two days at Coolidge Park and Renaissance Park. Expect three stages of live entertainment, combat arenas, artisan demos, and roaming costumed performers.
body: Two days of medieval shenanigans spread across Coolidge Park and Renaissance Park each November. Three stages run live performances all weekend. Combat arenas host staged fights and demos between roving performers. Artisan booths show traditional crafts being made. Add-on ticketed experiences include a King's and Queen's Feast, Royal Tea Service, Tea with the Fairies, and hands on workshops in stained glass and entomology. General admission and add-on tickets are sold separately at chattrenfaire.com.

title: Come From Away
description: Come From Away runs September 11-27, 2026 on the Main Stage at the Chattanooga Theatre Centre.
body: Thirty-eight planes get grounded in a small Newfoundland town on 9/11. The people of Gander take in thousands of stranded strangers. They answer fear with food and kindness. Chattanooga Theatre Centre stages Come From Away as a full musical production. The Tony Award-winning show has a cast of twelve who play multiple roles. CTC is a community theater on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. Check the website for the full run, ticket prices, and showtimes. The show runs about 100 minutes without an intermission. It is one of the most emotionally affecting musicals of the past decade.

title: Duck for President
description: Duck for President runs May 8-16, 2027 in the Circle Theatre at the Chattanooga Theatre Centre.
body: A farm duck gets tired of chores and wins the farm election. Then he sets his sights on the White House. He learns that running things takes real work. Chattanooga Theatre Centre stages Duck for President as part of its youth or family programming. CTC is a community theater on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. This short, light-hearted show works well for young audiences and school groups. Check the CTC website for the full run, ticket prices, and showtimes. The show runs about 60 minutes and includes audience interaction. It is based on the popular children's book series by Doreen Cronin.

title: Harry Connick Jr.'s The Happy Elf
description: Harry Connick Jr.'s The Happy Elf runs December 4-20, 2026 on the Main Stage at the Chattanooga Theatre Centre.
body: Eubie the elf spreads Christmas cheer, and Harry Connick Jr. sets it all to jazz. The songs swing while the story stays warm and simple. It works as a holiday show for all ages. Chattanooga Theatre Centre stages this musical at the end of the year. CTC is a community theater on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. The show includes live music and a full cast. Check the CTC website for the full run, ticket prices, and showtimes. The Happy Elf runs about 90 minutes and is family-friendly. Good choice for a holiday outing with kids or grandchildren.

title: Schoolhouse Rock Live!
description: Schoolhouse Rock Live! runs February 13-21, 2027 on the Main Stage at the Chattanooga Theatre Centre.
body: The 1970s cartoon songs jump from screen to stage. You will hear the tunes that taught grammar, math, and history. The cast keeps it bright, quick, and fun. Chattanooga Theatre Centre stages Schoolhouse Rock Live! as a family-friendly production. CTC is a community theater on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. The show recreates the beloved Schoolhouse Rock segments with live singers and dancers. Check the CTC website for the full run, ticket prices, and showtimes. This production appeals to adults who grew up with the cartoons and to children discovering the songs for the first time.

title: See Rock City
description: See Rock City runs November 6-22, 2026 in the Circle Theatre at the Chattanooga Theatre Centre.
body: May and Raleigh build a marriage while World War II pulls at the seams. They face loss and hard choices side by side. This tender sequel drama lives in a specific moment in Southern history. Chattanooga Theatre Centre stages See Rock City as part of its season. CTC is a community theater on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. The play is set in the North Georgia and Chattanooga area, which gives local audiences a particular connection to the material. Check the CTC website for the full run, ticket prices, and showtimes.

title: Shakespeare's Julius Caesar
description: Shakespeare's Julius Caesar runs March 12-21, 2027 on the Main Stage at the Chattanooga Theatre Centre.
body: Power, betrayal, and a knife in the Senate. Conspirators cut down Caesar, and Rome slides into civil war. Mark Antony's funeral speech turns the crowd. Chattanooga Theatre Centre stages Shakespeare's Julius Caesar as part of its season. CTC is a community theater on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. The cast includes community members and trained actors. Performances run multiple evenings and weekends. Check the CTC website for the full run, ticket prices, and showtimes. The theater seats several hundred. Julius Caesar runs about two and a half hours with an intermission.

title: The Complete History of America (abridged)
description: The Complete History of America (abridged) runs April 2-18, 2027 in the Circle Theatre.
body: Six hundred years of American history, sprinted through in about 90 minutes. The pace never lets up and the jokes come fast. It is a gleeful romp that trusts the audience to keep up. Chattanooga Theatre Centre stages this condensed comic history as part of its season. CTC is a community theater on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. The show features a small cast moving through sketches at high speed. Check the CTC website for the full run, ticket prices, and showtimes. This show works for a wide audience and plays well for groups.

title: The Cost of Justice
description: The Cost of Justice, a staged reading, runs February 5-6, 2027 at the Chattanooga Theatre Centre.
body: The Martin family loses someone they love, then fights for justice. Grief and the courtroom pull them in two directions at once. This new drama weighs both. Chattanooga Theatre Centre stages The Cost of Justice as part of its season. CTC is a community theater on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. The play examines justice, loss, and community through a family's experience with the legal system. Check the CTC website for the full run, ticket prices, and showtimes. New American dramas at community theaters are a rarer program choice - this one is worth attention.

title: The Entire American Revolution (In 40 Minutes or Less!)
description: The Entire American Revolution (In 40 Minutes or Less!) runs September 26 - October 4, 2026 in the Circle Theatre.
body: Two centuries of rebellion, crammed into 40 minutes flat. The cast tears from the Boston Tea Party straight to Yorktown. Nobody stops to catch a breath. Chattanooga Theatre Centre stages this condensed comic history show as part of its youth or family programming. CTC is a community theater on Brainerd Road. The fast format works well for school groups and families with younger audiences. Check the CTC website for the full run, ticket prices, and showtimes. This show pairs well with the also-short Complete History of America Abridged running in the same season.

title: West Side Story
description: West Side Story runs July 16 - August 1, 2027 on the Main Stage at the Chattanooga Theatre Centre.
body: Two young lovers meet across a bitter street rivalry in New York. Leonard Bernstein's score carries the heartbreak, with a book by Arthur Laurents. The dancing does the rest. Chattanooga Theatre Centre stages West Side Story as a full musical production. CTC is a community theater on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. The show requires a large cast and live music to do properly. Check the CTC website for the full run, ticket prices, and showtimes. West Side Story runs about two and a half hours with an intermission. This is one of the great American musicals.

title: You Can't Take It With You
description: You Can't Take It With You runs April 30 - May 16, 2027 on the Main Stage at the Chattanooga Theatre Centre.
body: Grandpa Vanderhof runs a house full of happy oddballs. Trouble lands when his granddaughter falls for her buttoned-up boss. Two very different families collide. This Pulitzer Prize-winning comedy by George S. Kaufman and Moss Hart is one of the most performed plays in American theater. Chattanooga Theatre Centre stages You Can't Take It With You as part of its season. CTC is a community theater on Brainerd Road. Check the website for the full run, ticket prices, and showtimes. The play runs about two and a half hours with an intermission.

title: Big Band's Best!
description: The Chattanooga Symphony performs classic swing and big band arrangements on February 13 at the Tivoli Theatre.
body: Big band arrangements fill the Tivoli for Valentine's weekend. The program pulls from the swing era: Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Glenn Miller, and others. The CSO's brass and rhythm sections drive the arrangements in a pops concert format. The Tivoli Theatre is a restored 1921 venue on Broad Street that seats about 1,700. Big Band's Best is an annual Valentine's season tradition. Check the CSO website for ticket prices and seating. Doors open 30 minutes before curtain. The Tivoli's acoustics and intimate scale make it a natural home for this kind of program.

title: Cirque de la Symphonie
description: World-class acrobats and aerialists perform live with the Chattanooga Symphony on April 10 at the Tivoli Theatre.
body: Aerialists, acrobats, and contortionists perform live with the orchestra at this Pops show. The Cirque de la Symphonie touring production coordinates circus performance with live orchestral music. The acts perform above and around the stage while the CSO plays. This is not a typical concert format. The combination of live acrobatics and live orchestra is visually and musically impressive. Check the CSO website for ticket prices and seating. The Pops series tends to draw wider audiences than the Classics series. Memorial Auditorium seats about 2,000 on McCallie Avenue.

title: CYS Fall Concert
description: The Chattanooga Youth Symphony presents its fall concert on November 2 at Memorial Auditorium.
body: Students from across the region perform full orchestral works at Memorial Auditorium. The Chattanooga Youth Symphony trains young musicians in a professional orchestral setting. The fall concert is the ensemble's first full performance of the season. The program typically includes one large orchestral work and several smaller pieces. The orchestra is conducted by professional musicians. Admission is free or low cost. Check the CYS website for the program and any ticket requirements. Memorial Auditorium is on McCallie Avenue and seats about 2,000. This is a free or low-cost alternative to the professional CSO season.

title: CYS Side-by-Side
description: Chattanooga Youth Symphony students perform alongside professional CSO musicians on May 3 at the Tivoli Theatre.
body: Youth Symphony students perform side by side with professional CSO musicians at the Tivoli. Each student shares a music stand and a part with a CSO player. The program is both a performance and a mentorship experience. The CYS Side-by-Side concert is one of the highlights of the youth orchestra season. The program typically features a substantial orchestral work. Admission is free or low cost. Check the CSO and CYS websites for program details and any ticket requirements. The Tivoli Theatre is on Broad Street and seats about 1,700.

title: CYS Winter Concert
description: The Chattanooga Youth Symphony presents its winter concert on February 8 at the Tivoli Theatre.
body: Students from across the region perform full orchestral works at the Tivoli. The winter program covers pieces the ensemble has prepared through the fall semester. The Chattanooga Youth Symphony trains young musicians from across the region in a professional orchestral setting. The winter concert marks the midpoint of the season. Admission is free or low cost. Check the CYS website for the program and any ticket requirements. The Tivoli Theatre is on Broad Street and seats about 1,700. This is a good opportunity to hear the next generation of Chattanooga musicians.

title: Handel's Messiah
description: The Chattanooga Symphony and chorus perform Handel's Messiah on December 5 at Memorial Auditorium.
body: The CSO and full chorus perform Handel's Messiah, including the Hallelujah chorus. The oratorio runs about two and a half hours with an intermission. Messiah was first performed in Dublin in 1742. The Hallelujah chorus traditionally prompts the audience to stand. The December 5 performance runs at 7:30 PM at Memorial Auditorium. Check the CSO website for ticket prices and seating. Memorial Auditorium is on McCallie Avenue and seats about 2,000. The CSO performs Messiah annually as part of the holiday season programming.

title: Handel's Messiah
description: The Chattanooga Symphony and chorus perform Handel's Messiah on December 6 at Memorial Auditorium.
body: The CSO and full chorus perform Handel's Messiah, including the Hallelujah chorus. The oratorio runs about two and a half hours with an intermission. This is the second performance, following the December 5 show. The matinee runs at 3:00 PM on Sunday. Check the CSO website for ticket prices and seating. Memorial Auditorium on McCallie Avenue seats about 2,000. The Sunday matinee is a good option for those who prefer afternoon programming. The Hallelujah chorus traditionally prompts the audience to stand.

title: Home for the Holidays
description: The Chattanooga Symphony's annual holiday pops concert at Memorial Auditorium on December 19.
body: The CSO's holiday pops show brings carols, film music, and seasonal orchestral favorites to Memorial Auditorium. The program is the orchestra's end-of-year send-off for the community. A matinee performance follows December 20 at 3:00 PM. This is the evening performance on December 19. The program includes audience sing-alongs, holiday readings, and a full orchestral program of seasonal music. Check the CSO website for ticket prices and seating. Memorial Auditorium on McCallie Avenue seats about 2,000. This is one of the most popular shows in the CSO season.

title: Home for the Holidays
description: The Chattanooga Symphony's annual holiday pops concert at Memorial Auditorium on December 20.
body: The CSO's holiday pops show brings carols, film music, and seasonal orchestral favorites to Memorial Auditorium. The program is the orchestra's end-of-year send-off for the community. This is the Sunday matinee at 3:00 PM, following the Saturday evening performance. The program includes audience sing-alongs, holiday readings, and a full orchestral program of seasonal music. Check the CSO website for ticket prices and seating. Memorial Auditorium on McCallie Avenue seats about 2,000. This matinee is a popular option for families and those who prefer afternoon concerts.

title: Mozart & Mahler: A World of Wonder
description: The CSO closes its Classics Series with Mozart and Mahler on April 29 at the Tivoli Theatre.
body: The season's final Classics concert pairs Mozart and Mahler on the same program. Mozart's tight, clear writing sets up a contrast with Mahler's vast, emotional orchestration. Mahler's works typically require large forces and run 60 to 90 minutes. The pairing is musically and intellectually interesting. Check the CSO website for the specific works and any guest soloists on the program. Concerts take place at the Tivoli Theatre on Broad Street. The Tivoli seats about 1,700. Doors open 30 minutes before curtain. This is the closing concert of the CSO Classics season.

title: Mozart's Musical Conversations
description: The CSO's Front Row series explores Mozart's chamber and orchestral writing on January 23 at Memorial Auditorium.
body: The Front Row series puts the audience a few feet from the players. This program covers Mozart's writing, with performers explaining musical decisions and structure between pieces. Front Row concerts combine live performance with informal commentary from the musicians. The audience asks questions and the players respond. This format turns a concert into a conversation about how music works. Check the CSO website for ticket details and the specific program. Front Row concerts take place at the Tivoli Theatre on Broad Street. The series runs several times through the season.

title: Music in the Wild: Peter and the Wolf
description: The Chattanooga Symphony performs Prokofiev's Peter and the Wolf outdoors at Reflection Riding on October 4.
body: The CSO performs Prokofiev's Peter and the Wolf outdoors at Reflection Riding. Before the main concert, musicians pop up along the trail introducing each instrument and character from the story. The piece was composed in 1936 for children and assigns each character a specific instrument - the duck is an oboe, the wolf is horns. The outdoor format puts the audience in the landscape while the music plays. Check the CSO and Reflection Riding websites for ticket details. This event is family-friendly. Bring a blanket or low chair for the main performance.

title: Rachmaninoff Piano Concerto No. 2
description: The Chattanooga Symphony performs Rachmaninoff's Second Piano Concerto on November 19 at Memorial Auditorium.
body: Rachmaninoff's Second opens with solo piano chords before the full orchestra enters. The lyrical second movement has appeared in dozens of films and recordings. The concerto is one of the most performed in the standard repertoire. This CSO Classics concert pairs the concerto with another orchestral work. Check the CSO website for the full program, soloist, and ticket details. Concerts take place at the Tivoli Theatre on Broad Street. The Tivoli seats about 1,700 and is one of the best-sounding rooms in the region for large orchestral works.

title: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back in Concert
description: The Chattanooga Symphony performs John Williams' live score while The Empire Strikes Back plays on screen, November 7.
body: The CSO performs John Williams' score live while the film plays on screen. The Empire Strikes Back introduced the Imperial March and the Cloud City theme. The CSO plays the full orchestral score in sync with the film at Memorial Auditorium. This format is called a live-to-picture concert. The orchestra plays in the pit while the film runs above. John Williams' score for The Empire Strikes Back is considered one of the greatest in film history. Check the CSO website for ticket prices and seating. Memorial Auditorium seats about 2,000 on McCallie Avenue.

title: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back in Concert
description: The Chattanooga Symphony performs John Williams' live score while The Empire Strikes Back plays on screen, November 8.
body: The CSO performs John Williams' score live while the film plays on screen. The Empire Strikes Back introduced the Imperial March and the Cloud City theme. This is the second of two performances, following the Friday show. The CSO plays the full orchestral score in sync with the film at Memorial Auditorium. Live-to-picture concerts allow audiences to experience a beloved film with live orchestral accompaniment. Check the CSO website for ticket prices and seating. Memorial Auditorium seats about 2,000 on McCallie Avenue.

title: Tchaikovsky Symphony No. 4
description: The CSO marks its return to the restored Tivoli Theatre with Tchaikovsky's Fourth Symphony on February 18.
body: The CSO plays its first Tivoli concert this season with Tchaikovsky's Fourth Symphony. The work opens with a fate motif, then moves through three more movements of increasing urgency and power. The finale is one of the loudest endings in the standard repertoire. The CSO Classics series brings professional orchestral programming to the Tivoli Theatre on Broad Street. Check the CSO website for the full program, any guest soloists, and ticket details. The Tivoli seats about 1,700. Doors open 30 minutes before curtain.

title: Voices Unbroken feat. The CSO Chorus
description: The CSO Chorus takes center stage in Voices Unbroken on March 20 at the Tivoli Theatre.
body: The CSO Chorus leads this Front Row program, performing choral works drawn from traditions of struggle and survival. The Front Row series puts the audience close to the performers in an intimate chamber setting. The program for Voices Unbroken covers spirituals, protest songs, freedom songs, and other works connected to the history of resilience. This is the Friday performance. A second performance follows on Saturday, March 21. Check the CSO website for ticket details. Front Row concerts take place at the Tivoli Theatre on Broad Street.

title: Voices Unbroken feat. The CSO Chorus
description: The CSO Chorus takes center stage in Voices Unbroken on March 21 at the Tivoli Theatre.
body: The CSO Chorus leads this Front Row program, performing choral works drawn from traditions of struggle and survival. The Front Row series puts the audience close to the performers. The program for Voices Unbroken covers spirituals, protest songs, freedom songs, and other works connected to the history of resilience. This is the Saturday performance, following the Friday show. Check the CSO website for ticket details. Front Row concerts take place at the Tivoli Theatre on Broad Street. The Saturday show is the final performance of this program.

title: American Grappling Federation
description: The American Grappling Federation holds a jiu-jitsu and grappling tournament at the Chattanooga Convention Center on September 19, 2026.
body: The American Grappling Federation brings a jiu-jitsu and submission grappling tournament to the Convention Center on September 19. Competitors face off across gi and no-gi brackets. Come to watch the matches or sign up to compete. Check the AGF website for divisions, registration, and the day's schedule. The AGF runs tournaments across the Southeast and national circuit. The Convention Center is at 1 Carter Plaza in downtown Chattanooga. Spectator admission is typically low cost or free. The day runs from early morning through the afternoon as bracket rounds are completed.

title: Chattanooga Comic Con
description: Chattanooga Comic Con returns to the Chattanooga Convention Center on November 7 and 8, 2026 with celebrity guests, cosplay, and gaming.
body: Chattanooga Comic Con fills the Convention Center on November 7 and 8, 2026. This is the fifth year of the show. The weekend brings comics, celebrity guests, content creators, and cosplay contests. A large vendor hall sells art, toys, and collectibles. Panels and workshops run both days. The gaming hall holds tabletop and console rooms. Saturday runs 10 AM to 6 PM, with the gaming hall open until 10 PM. Sunday runs 11 AM to 5 PM. Single-day and weekend passes are on sale online.

title: Chattanooga Kidney Foundation - Dare to Dance
description: The Chattanooga Kidney Foundation hosts its Dare to Dance fundraiser at the Chattanooga Convention Center on October 3, 2026.
body: Dare to Dance is the Chattanooga Kidney Foundation's yearly fundraiser at the Convention Center on October 3. Local dancers take the floor to raise money for kidney patients and their families. Expect performances, an evening program, and a good cause behind it all. Check the Chattanooga Kidney Foundation website for tickets and table details. The Chattanooga Kidney Foundation provides support and resources to kidney patients and their families in the region. This annual event is the foundation's primary fundraiser.

title: SouthPaw Promotions
description: SouthPaw Promotions brings a professional boxing card to the Chattanooga Convention Center on October 29, 2026.
body: SouthPaw Promotions stages a professional boxing card at the Convention Center on October 29. The company runs fight nights across the Southeast and works out of Chattanooga. Expect several bouts across weight classes on the ticket. Local fighters share the card with regional talent. Check the SouthPaw Promotions website for the full fight lineup, ticket prices, and doors time. Ringside and general seating sell separately.

title: Steve Gonsalves Live: A Life with Ghosts
description: Ghost Hunters veteran Steve Gonsalves brings his live show A Life with Ghosts to the Chattanooga Convention Center on September 10.
body: Steve Gonsalves from Ghost Hunters brings his live show to the Chattanooga Convention Center on September 10. He shares stories from years of paranormal investigation on the long-running television series. Gonsalves has appeared on Ghost Hunters since its debut in 2004. The live show covers his experiences, unexplained events, and what it is actually like to investigate haunted locations. The Convention Center is at 1 Carter Plaza in downtown Chattanooga. Check the Convention Center website for ticket details. This is an evening event with audience Q&A.

title: Tennessee Tow Show
description: The Tennessee Tow Show fills the Chattanooga Convention Center with towing equipment, demos, and training from October 15 to 17, 2026.
body: The Tennessee Tow Show returns to the Convention Center from October 15 to 17. This industry event fills the whole hall with towing and recovery equipment. About 100 vendors sell products, gear, and services. Training classes run Thursday and Friday. Exhibits open Friday and Saturday. The weekend also holds a Hall of Fame ceremony and a Wall of the Fallen tribute. Admission to the exhibits is free, but you need an attendee badge to enter.

title: The Pink Bride Show
description: The Pink Bride Show returns to the Chattanooga Convention Center on September 6, 2026, connecting engaged couples with local wedding vendors.
body: Photographers, caterers, florists, venues, and every other vendor you need for a wedding, all in one room at the Convention Center on September 6 from noon to 4pm. General admission is free. VIP bundle available at checkout if you want the extras. Find the vendor lineup at thepinkbride.com. The Pink Bride Show tours multiple cities and brings regional wedding vendors together in one place. The Chattanooga edition connects engaged couples planning their wedding with local and regional vendors. The Convention Center is at 1 Carter Plaza in downtown Chattanooga.

title: 100 Dinner: Fall Seating
description: A multi-course seasonal farm dinner with local chefs at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: The fall seating of Crabtree's 100 Dinner Series lands at the Evelyn Center. Local chefs build a multi-course meal around seasonal, farm-grown ingredients. Between courses, staff share the story of the farm's food-access and education work. Seats are limited and tickets sell fast, so book early through the farm's site. Check the Crabtree Farms website for cost and registration. The event is ticketed and space is limited. The Evelyn Center is on the Crabtree Farms property on Jersey Pike.

title: All About Herbal Shrubs
description: Hands-on herbal shrub workshop at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms teaches you how to make herbal shrubs from scratch. A shrub blends herbs, fruit, and vinegar into a concentrated tonic. People have used these drinks as time-honored wellness remedies for generations. The workshop covers ingredients, method, and flavor. The session runs from 6:00pm to 7:30pm. Tickets cost $39.19 and include materials. Register early because this class has limited space.

title: Beginner Dot Mandalas: Ornaments
description: Beginner dot mandala ornament painting class at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms hosts a beginner dot mandala class. You learn to paint ornaments using simple dotting tools. The instructor teaches patterns, designs, and color choices step by step. No art experience is needed to join. The class runs from 6:00pm to 7:30pm on the farm. Tickets cost $39.19 and supplies are included. You take your finished ornament home. Register early because the class fills fast.

title: Canning for Beginners
description: Free beginner canning class at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga, in partnership with Gaining Ground.
body: Crabtree Farms and Gaining Ground teach the basics of home canning. This class opens a three-part autumn food preservation series. Students learn safe methods for canning fruits and vegetables. The class runs from 12:00pm to 2:00pm. Admission is free, but space fills quickly. Register in advance to reserve a spot. Beginners will leave ready to can at home. Check the Crabtree Farms website for registration and cost. All equipment and ingredients are provided at the farm on Jersey Pike in Chattanooga.

title: Community Book Club: Braiding Sweetgrass
description: Free book club at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga discussing Braiding Sweetgrass.
body: Crabtree Farms hosts its monthly community book club. This session covers "Braiding Sweetgrass: Indigenous Wisdom, Scientific Knowledge and the Teachings of Plants." Readers discuss food, land, sustainability, health, and community. The group meets from 5:30pm to 7:30pm on the farm. Admission is free and open to everyone. Bring your own copy of the book. Arrive early to settle in before the talk.

title: Community Book Club: The Accidental Ecosystem
description: Free book club at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga discussing The Accidental Ecosystem.
body: Crabtree Farms hosts this monthly community book club. This session covers "The Accidental Ecosystem: People and Wildlife in American Cities." Readers discuss urban wildlife, sustainability, and community themes. The group meets from 5:30pm to 7:30pm on the farm. Admission is free and open to everyone. Bring your own copy of the book. Arrive early to settle in before the talk.

title: Community Book Club: The Seed Keeper
description: Free book club at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga discussing The Seed Keeper.
body: Crabtree Farms hosts its monthly community book club. This session covers "The Seed Keeper: A Novel" by Diane Wilson. Readers discuss food, land, sustainability, health, and community. The group meets from 5:30pm to 7:30pm on the farm. Admission is free and open to everyone. Bring your own copy of the book. Arrive early to settle in before the talk. Check the Crabtree Farms website for registration and cost. The book club is free or low cost and open to anyone who has read the book.

title: Fall Plant Sale and Pollinator Festival
description: Crabtree Farms hosts its Fall Plant Sale and Pollinator Festival over three days in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms runs this three-day fall tradition from September 25 to 27. Shoppers browse native plants, pollinator-friendly flowers, and cool-season vegetables. Staff and volunteers answer gardening questions on site. The festival mixes plant shopping with community activities and pollinator education. Hours run from 9:00am on Friday through 3:00pm on Sunday. Bring a wagon for hauling your finds. The plant sale is free to attend. Plants are priced individually. Crabtree Farms is on Jersey Pike in Chattanooga. Check the website for specific hours and the full vendor and demonstrator schedule.

title: Community Book Club: The Home Place
description: Free monthly book club at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga discussing food, land, and community.
body: Crabtree Farms and Wild Ones host this monthly book club. This session covers "The Home Place." Readers talk about food, land, sustainability, health, and community. The group meets in a relaxed setting on the farm. Bring your own copy and your thoughts. Admission is free, so arrive early to find a seat. Check the Crabtree Farms website for registration and cost. The book club is free or low cost and open to anyone who has read the book.

title: Fall Into Your Best Spring Garden
description: Fall garden preparation class at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms teaches you how to prepare your garden before winter. The class covers the steps that set up a strong spring season. Students learn soil care, bed cleanup, and smart timing. These tasks make a real difference once the weather warms. The class runs from 10:00am to 12:00pm. Tickets cost $30. Register early to reserve your spot in the class.

title: Fall Plant & Seed Swap
description: Free community plant and seed swap at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms hosts a community plant and seed swap. Bring any extra seeds or plants you have to share with others. The event includes demonstrations on seed saving with real examples. You can trade your surplus and learn how to collect and store seeds. The swap runs from 5:00pm to 7:00pm. Admission is free and open to all gardeners. Come to meet other growers and build your garden.

title: Field to Feast: Fall Harvest Dinner
description: Crabtree Farms hosts an intimate fall harvest dinner with a seasonal menu in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms serves a multi-course dinner built from the fall harvest. Chefs cook with produce grown on the farm and from local partners. The evening runs from 6:00pm to 9:00pm in an outdoor farm setting. Tickets cost $225 per person. Seats are limited for this intimate dinner, so book ahead. The meal supports the farm's education programs. The event is ticketed and space is limited. Check the Crabtree Farms website for registration, cost, and the specific chef lineup.

title: Holiday Cooking with Your Fall Harvest
description: Free holiday cooking class at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga, with Gaining Ground.
body: Crabtree Farms and Gaining Ground teach holiday cooking with fall produce. This class is part of the autumn food preservation series at the farm. Students learn to turn seasonal harvests into festive dishes. The session shows simple ways to cook and store fall vegetables. The class runs from 12:00pm to 2:00pm. Admission is free, but space fills quickly. Register in advance to reserve a spot.

title: Make and Take: Medicinal Mushrooms
description: Hands-on medicinal mushroom workshop at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms leads an introductory workshop on medicinal mushrooms. The class covers common species and their health benefits. Attendees make a simple mushroom remedy to take home. The session runs from 6:00pm to 8:00pm. Tickets cost $35 and include all materials. No experience is needed. Space is limited, so register in advance to hold your spot. Check the Crabtree Farms website for registration and cost. This is a hands-on session at the farm on Jersey Pike. All materials are provided.

title: Make & Take: Winter Wellness, Syrups, Oxymels and Fire Cider
description: Hands-on herbal remedy workshop at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms leads a hands-on workshop on winter herbal remedies. Students explore syrups, oxymels, and fire cider for immune support. The class explains how each remedy works and how to make it. Every participant crafts a remedy to take home. The session runs from 6:00pm to 8:00pm. Tickets cost $35 and include materials. Register early because make-and-take classes fill fast.

title: Making Gingerbread Cookies with Sourdough
description: Beginner-friendly sourdough gingerbread cookie class at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms teaches a beginner-friendly baking class. Students bake gingerbread cookies using sourdough discard. The class covers mixing, rolling, and decorating by hand. The session runs from 6:00pm to 8:00pm on the farm. Tickets cost $71.21 and include all ingredients. You take your cookies home at the end. Register early because baking classes fill fast.

title: Meet the Microorganisms
description: Microscope workshop exploring soil biology at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Second run of the microscope workshop if August filled up. Same hands-on look at what lives in healthy soil - with the fall season giving the samples a different character than summer. Crabtree Farms leads this workshop in their learning space on Jersey Pike. Participants use microscopes to view live microorganisms from soil samples. No science background required. The class covers what healthy soil needs and why microbial life matters for growing food. Register through the Crabtree Farms website. Space is limited. Check the site for the specific cost and start time.

title: Nature as Teacher: A Mindfulness Practice
description: Free nature-based mindfulness meditation session at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms hosts a monthly mindfulness meditation group. The practice uses the farm landscape as a focus for attention. A facilitator guides the session through simple, nature-based exercises. The group meets from 10:00am to 11:00am. Admission is free and open to all skill levels. Wear comfortable clothes and shoes for walking outdoors. No meditation experience is required. The session is free or low cost. Check the Crabtree Farms website for registration and the specific monthly date. No prior meditation experience is required.

title: Plant Identification and Foraging
description: Guided foraging and plant identification walk at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: A guided walk through the farm property covering foraging fundamentals and plant ID. Good for beginners who want to learn what's edible and what isn't. Crabtree Farms leads this walk on Jersey Pike with a knowledgeable guide who points out edible plants, common look-alikes, and safe harvesting practices. No experience is needed. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water. Register through the Crabtree Farms website. Space is limited. Check the site for the specific cost and start time. The walk covers two to three hours and ends at the farm.

title: Pressed Flower Art: Beauty in the Everyday
description: Pressed flower art workshop at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms hosts a relaxing art workshop. Students arrange pressed flowers and natural materials into finished pieces. The class invites you to slow down and notice small beauty in nature. The session runs from 6:00pm to 7:30pm on the farm. Tickets cost $39.19 and include all supplies. You take your artwork home at the end. Register early because workshops fill fast.

title: Pruning for Greatness 101
description: Learn hands-on pruning at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga. Shape trees for strong growth and master tools, timing, and cuts. Noon to 3pm, $35.
body: Crabtree Farms leads a hands-on pruning workshop that goes beyond the basics. Students learn how to shape plants and trees for strong growth. The class covers tools, timing, and proper cuts. Good pruning keeps plants healthy and productive year after year. The class runs from 12:00pm to 3:00pm. Tickets cost $35. Register early to reserve your place in the class.

title: Snowy Cabin Acrylic Painting
description: Paint a snowy cabin scene in acrylics at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga. All skill levels welcome. 6pm to 8pm, $53.07.
body: Crabtree Farms hosts a guided acrylic painting class with a cozy winter theme. You will paint a snowy cabin scene step by step. The instructor walks the whole room through each stage. Beginners and advanced painters are both welcome. No experience is needed to finish a canvas you can take home. The class runs from 6:00pm to 8:00pm. Tickets cost $53.07. This evening class pairs well with a relaxed night out. Arrive a few minutes early to settle in and claim a good seat. Register ahead, since hands-on art classes at the farm fill up fast.

title: Sourdough Bagels
description: Hands-on sourdough bagel baking workshop at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree's baking workshops fill fast. This one covers sourdough bagel technique from scratch - mixing, shaping, boiling, baking. Beginners welcome, experienced bakers will still find it worth the trip. Crabtree Farms runs this class in their learning kitchen on Jersey Pike. Students work with live sourdough starter and leave with fresh bagels they made themselves. All ingredients and equipment are provided. Register through the Crabtree Farms website. Space is limited. Check the site for the specific cost and start time. The workshop runs about three to four hours.

title: The Art of Kombucha Brewing
description: Hands-on kombucha brewing class at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms leads an interactive class on brewing kombucha at home. The session covers the fermentation process and the drink's probiotic benefits. Students learn how to start and maintain their own brew. The class runs from 6:00pm to 8:00pm. Tickets cost $35 and include materials. No prior experience is needed. Register early to secure your place in the class. Check the Crabtree Farms website for registration and cost. The class is at the farm on Jersey Pike. All materials are provided.

title: The Extraordinary Caterpillar Film Screening
description: Free film screening of The Extraordinary Caterpillar at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms screens "The Extraordinary Caterpillar" with the Wild Ones Tennessee Valley Chapter. The film explores insect life cycles and the role of native plants. The screening runs from 6:00pm to 7:30pm. A short discussion follows the film. Admission is free and open to all ages. Seating is first come, first served, so plan to arrive early. Crabtree Farms is on Jersey Pike in Chattanooga. Check the website for registration and cost. The Wild Ones Tennessee Valley Chapter focuses on native plant and habitat conservation.

title: The Simple Art of Sourdough
description: Hands-on sourdough baking class at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree Farms teaches sourdough baking from the ground up. The class covers starter care, mixing, shaping, and baking. Students work with dough by hand throughout the session. The class runs from 12:00pm to 2:00pm. Tickets cost $40 and include materials. Beginners are welcome, and experienced bakers will pick up new tips. Register early because baking classes fill fast. Check the Crabtree Farms website for registration and cost. All materials and ingredients are provided at the farm on Jersey Pike in Chattanooga.

title: A Drunken Night Out
description: A Drunken Night Out brings a loose, late-night comedy show to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: A Drunken Night Out brings a loose, party-style comedy show to The Comedy Catch. Comics lean into the late-night energy for an unfiltered set of jokes. The show is rated R, so leave the kids at home. Grab a drink and settle in downtown at 29 Station Street. Plan a ride home and make a full night of it with friends.

title: A Very Merry Night of Magic and Comedy
description: Award-winning magicians Lance Johnson and Lawrence James bring a holiday comedy magic show to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Magicians Lance Johnson and Lawrence James team up for a holiday comedy magic show. The two performers bring more than 60 years of combined experience to the stage. Their act mixes sleight of hand with laughs and Christmas cheer. They have played comedy clubs, college campuses, and Fortune 500 events across the country. This show is clean and works for a family night out. It starts at 7:00 PM at 29 Station Street.

title: Adult Bingo
description: Adult Bingo mixes stand-up laughs with a rowdy game night at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Adult Bingo turns The Comedy Catch into a rowdy game night with prizes and plenty of laughs. Expect a raunchy spin on the classic bingo card, hosted with comedy between rounds. The show starts at 7:00 PM and is rated R. Gather your friends for a grown-up night out downtown at 29 Station Street and play for the win. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue website for ticket details and the monthly bingo schedule.

title: Alex Velluto
description: Clean comic Alex Velluto brings his sharp observational stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Alex Velluto headlines a clean comedy night at The Comedy Catch. The Salt Lake City comic is known for sharp observational jokes and a tidy delivery. He has recorded three Dry Bar Comedy specials and toured more than 100 cities. Nate Bargatze picked him to perform on the series The Showcase. This show is clean, so it works for a wide crowd. Doors open downtown at 29 Station Street.

title: AV and Friends
description: Dalton native AV hosts a hometown comedy showcase with national talent at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: AV hosts a hometown comedy showcase at The Comedy Catch. The Dalton, Georgia native calls the club home and brings serious talent along. The lineup pulls some of the funniest comics from Atlanta and beyond. Expect big personalities, sharp jokes, and nonstop laughs. This show starts at 6:00 PM on Sunday. It is rated R, so plan an adult night out downtown at 29 Station Street.

title: "Big Irish" Jay Hollingsworth
description: "Big Irish" Jay Hollingsworth brings charmingly brutal stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Big Irish Jay Hollingsworth headlines two nights at The Comedy Catch. The comic came up in Boston, where readers once named him the city's best comedy export. His charmingly brutal style has drawn more than 100 million online views. His debut special Green Monster streams on Amazon Prime. Shows run Tuesday and Wednesday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show carries an adult rating.

title: Billy Sorrells
description: Chattanooga-born comedian Billy Sorrells returns home for a special engagement at The Comedy Catch.
body: Billy Sorrells plays a special engagement at The Comedy Catch. He was born in Chattanooga and grew up in Houston. Sorrells built a following on Wild 'N Out and BET Comic View. He also went viral online with his Peaches character. This one-night show starts at 7:00 PM. The show is rated R, so leave the kids at home and come for an adult evening of stand-up.

title: Billy Wayne Davis
description: Tennessee comic Billy Wayne Davis brings his small-town stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Billy Wayne Davis headlines a special engagement at The Comedy Catch. The comic grew up in Crossville, Tennessee, and built his act on small-town stories. He has appeared on Last Comic Standing and WTF with Marc Maron. He toured with Ralphie May and opened for Sturgill Simpson. His album Testify arrived in 2022. This show is rated R, so plan an adult night out downtown at 29 Station Street.

title: Brent Terhune
description: Viral satirist Brent Terhune brings his stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Brent Terhune headlines The Comedy Catch. The Indianapolis comic built 65 million-plus views with his satirical online character. Variety named him one of its 10 Comics to Watch for 2020. He has written daily topical jokes for the syndicated Bob and Tom Show for over a decade. His style gets called a blue-collar take on The Colbert Report. Shows run Friday and Saturday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show is rated R.

title: Carmen Lagala
