description: Vermont-raised comic Carmen Lagala brings her smart, dark stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Carmen Lagala headlines a special engagement at The Comedy Catch. The New York comic grew up in small-town Vermont and plays that charm against smart, dark jokes. She made her network debut on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert in 2018. Her special Sweet Batch has passed 300,000 views online. Shows run Saturday and Sunday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show is rated R, so plan an adult night out.

title: Chris Cope
description: Dry Bar Comedy star Chris Cope brings his touring stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Chris Cope headlines The Comedy Catch. The Florida-raised, Los Angeles-based comic started in 2003 and tours nationally. His Dry Bar special Babyface has passed six million views. He has appeared on Jimmy Kimmel Live, Tosh.0, and The Conan O'Brien Show. He also won the 2015 Big Sky Comedy Festival. Shows run Friday and Saturday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show is rated R, so plan an adult night out downtown.

title: Chris Higgins
description: Comedian Chris Higgins performs two nights of stand-up at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Chris Higgins plays two nights at The Comedy Catch. You can grab the 7:00 PM or 9:15 PM show on either date. His comedy is rated R, so expect an adult crowd and mature material. Higgins has performed at clubs and festivals nationally and appeared on regional comedy circuits. His stand-up draws on personal experience and sharp observational writing. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue website for ticket prices. Each show runs about 75 minutes. Doors open 30 minutes before showtime.

title: Chris Munch
description: Character comic Chris Munch brings his clean stand-up and viral personas to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Chris Munch headlines a special engagement at The Comedy Catch. The actor and comic has performed for live crowds and cameras for more than 20 years. He created viral characters like Pastor Bobby and Chad that have drawn millions of views online. His clean style works for nearly any room. He blends personal stories with sharp takes on everyday life. Find the show downtown at 29 Station Street.

title: Chris Porter
description: Last Comic Standing finalist Chris Porter brings his caustic stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Chris Porter brings raw, caustic stand-up to The Comedy Catch for a special engagement. The Kansas City comic was a finalist on Last Comic Standing and a regular on The Bob & Tom Show. He works clean of props and gimmicks, drawing hard laughs from everyday life. Shows run Friday at 7:00 PM and Saturday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. Rated R, so come ready for an adult night out.

title: Claude Stuart
description: Comedian Claude Stuart performs two nights of stand-up at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Two nights of adult stand-up from Claude Stuart hit The Comedy Catch. Shows run at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM on both dates. Plan a grown-up night out downtown. Stuart is a veteran stand-up comedian with years of touring experience across clubs nationally. His material is adult-rated and leans on experience, observation, and character work. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue website for ticket prices. Doors open 30 minutes before showtime. Each show runs about 75 minutes.

title: Cody Smith
description: Pharmacist-turned-comedian Cody Smith brings his wordplay and observational stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Cody Smith headlines The Comedy Catch. Comedic Cody left pharmacy to chase comedy and now tours the world. He has more than seven million combined followers and over a billion streams online. His laid-back act leans on clever wordplay and sharp takes on adult life. He is known for his partnership with Skrewball Peanut Butter Whiskey. This show starts at 7:00 PM on Thursday. It is rated R, so plan an adult night out downtown.

title: Conor Janda
description: New York comic Conor Janda brings his sharp personal stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Conor Janda headlines The Comedy Catch. The Philadelphia native and New York transplant writes sharp, personal jokes. His set covers a stay-at-home dad, an all-boys Catholic school, and getting sober. A Just for Laughs New Face, he has appeared on Comedy Central and in Kevin Hart's Funny AF on Netflix. He also co-created the web series Boys Club. This show starts at 6:00 PM on Sunday. It is rated R and LGBTQ-friendly.

title: Dale Jones
description: High-energy comic Dale Jones brings his rapid-fire physical stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Dale Jones headlines a special engagement at The Comedy Catch. The Atlanta comic runs a machine-gun delivery packed with animated faces and physical bits. He trained at Second City and appeared on Last Comic Standing. His album I'm Not Well hit the top three on iTunes. Shows run Saturday and Sunday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show is rated for adults, so plan a night out downtown.

title: Damon Darling
description: Viral crowd-work comic Damon Darling brings his down-to-earth stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Damon Darling headlines The Comedy Catch. The Ohio comic built a huge online following with crowd-work clips and his Got a Dollar series. He has more than 2.7 million TikTok followers and hundreds of millions of video views. His comedy runs observational and down-to-earth, with stories from his oil-rig days. He started stand-up during his sobriety journey. Shows run Thursday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show is rated for adults.

title: David Jolly
description: Kill Tony favorite David Jolly brings his raw, fearless stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: David Jolly headlines The Comedy Catch. The Florida comic built a following through the Kill Tony podcast. He calls himself America's Favorite Uncle and leans on warm, relatable storytelling. His set runs raw and fearless, with unfiltered stories and sharp wit. He speaks openly about his sobriety on stage and online. This show starts at 7:00 PM on Thursday. It is rated for adults, so plan a night out downtown at 29 Station Street.

title: DJ Sandhu
description: Sacramento comic DJ Sandhu brings absurd observational stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: DJ Sandhu headlines two nights at The Comedy Catch. The Sacramento comic mixes absurd observations with sharp takes on culture, travel, and family. He has performed at the Edinburgh Fringe and toured dozens of cities each year. He has also shared stages with Russell Peters and Theo Von. Shows run Tuesday and Wednesday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show carries an adult rating.

title: Dustin Nickerson
description: Clean comic Dustin Nickerson brings his family-focused stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Dustin Nickerson headlines a special engagement at The Comedy Catch. The Seattle-area comic built his name on clean, observational jokes about marriage, parenting, and aging. He married young and raised three kids, and that chaos drives his act. He has performed on The Tonight Show and in the Netflix Is a Joke Festival. Shows run Saturday and Sunday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show is rated PG-13.

title: Elizabeth Brunot
description: Comedian Elizabeth Brunot headlines a special engagement at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Elizabeth Brunot headlines a special engagement at The Comedy Catch. Her stand-up brings bold, honest jokes and strong stage presence to the room. The show starts at 6:00 PM and is an adult set. Make plans for an early evening of laughs downtown at 29 Station Street and get there ahead of showtime for a good seat. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue website for ticket prices and show times.

title: Emo Phillips
description: Cult stand-up legend Emo Phillips brings his surreal one-liners and childlike delivery to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Emo Phillips headlines The Comedy Catch. The Chicago-born comic became a cult figure in the 1980s with surreal, offbeat one-liners. His act uses a wandering falsetto and a confused, childlike delivery. Critics have likened his style to Pee-wee Herman mixed with Steven Wright. He slips dark twists into innocent setups when the crowd least expects it. This show starts at 7:00 PM on Wednesday. It is rated for adults, so plan a night out downtown.

title: Funny Over 50
description: Funny Over 50 brings clean comedy built for an older crowd to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Funny Over 50 brings clean comedy built for an older crowd to The Comedy Catch. Comics work jokes about aging, family, and the small stuff of daily life. The show is clean, so it fits a wide range of guests. It starts early at 5:00 PM, so plan dinner downtown nearby. Find the room at 29 Station Street and share an afternoon of easy laughs.

title: Gareth Reynolds
description: The Dollop co-host Gareth Reynolds brings his stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Gareth Reynolds headlines The Comedy Catch. The Milwaukee comic co-hosts the hit history podcast The Dollop, which pulls millions of downloads each month. His debut album Riddled With Disease hit number one on the Billboard comedy chart. He has written for or appeared on New Girl, Arrested Development, and You're the Worst. He also co-hosts We're Here to Help with Jake Johnson. This show starts at 7:00 PM on Thursday. It is rated for adults.

title: Graeson McGaha
description: Comedian Graeson McGaha performs a special engagement at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga. This show is sold out.
body: Graeson McGaha headlines a special engagement at The Comedy Catch, and this one is sold out. Watch the venue page for any seats they release. The set is rated R. McGaha is a Chattanooga-area comedian who has built a following through local and regional performances. His material draws on Southern life and personal experience. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. The sold-out status reflects strong local demand. Check the venue website for any released or returned tickets closer to the show date.

title: Greg Morton
description: America's Got Talent impressionist Greg Morton brings his rapid-fire voices and clean comedy to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Greg Morton headlines The Comedy Catch. The Canadian-born impressionist and voice actor reached the semifinals on America's Got Talent. His act blends rapid-fire voices, pop-culture satire, and storytelling. He has voiced more than 20 cartoons and played Just for Laughs four times. He has shared stages with Dave Chappelle and Chris Rock. Shows run Friday and Saturday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This is a clean show that works for the whole family.

title: Holiday Friendsgiving 2025
description: Holiday Friendsgiving brings an LGBTQ comedy celebration to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Holiday Friendsgiving brings an LGBTQ comedy celebration to The Comedy Catch. The afternoon show gathers comics and friends for a seasonal party built around laughs. The event starts early at 2:00 PM, so plan the rest of your day around it. This show is rated R, so leave the kids at home. Find the room downtown at 29 Station Street and raise a toast with the crowd.

title: Home for the Holidays with Karen Mills
description: UTC basketball legend and touring comic Karen Mills brings a holiday stand-up show to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Karen Mills headlines a holiday show at The Comedy Catch. The touring comic has more than 30 years on stage and played the Grand Ole Opry. She was an All-American basketball player at UTC, and her jersey hangs retired. Her honest, relatable jokes cover aging, menopause, and daily life. A cancer survivor, she tours with Leanne Morgan and appears in the Netflix series Leanne. This show starts at 6:00 PM on Sunday. It is rated PG-13.

title: Hot Fudge Comedy
description: Hot Fudge Comedy delivers a lineup of stand-up comics at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Hot Fudge Comedy puts a rotating lineup of stand-up comics on the stage at The Comedy Catch. Each comic works a short set, so the night moves fast and covers many styles. The show is rated R, so leave the kids at home. Doors open downtown at 29 Station Street. Grab a drink and settle in for a full night of laughs.

title: Improv Comedy Night
description: Improv Comedy Night brings fast, unscripted sketch comedy to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Improv Comedy Night fills the stage at The Comedy Catch with fast, unscripted comedy. Performers build scenes and jokes from audience suggestions in the moment. No two shows play out the same way. The format rewards quick thinking and bold choices. This show starts at 7:00 PM. The show carries an adult rating, so plan a night out downtown at 29 Station Street.

title: Janet Williams – The Tennessee Tramp
description: Southern comedian Janet Williams, The Tennessee Tramp, brings her stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Janet Williams, known as The Tennessee Tramp, brings her Southern stand-up to The Comedy Catch. Her act is packed with down-home stories and sharp jokes about small-town life. The show starts at 7:00 PM and is rated R. Come out for a fun adult night downtown at 29 Station Street and settle in for a comic who knows her crowd.

title: Jeremy Alder
description: North Carolina comic Jeremy Alder brings faith-shaped stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Jeremy Alder plays a special engagement at The Comedy Catch. The North Carolina comic grew up homeschooled by missionary parents and once worked as a preacher. He now mines that upbringing for sharp, thoughtful jokes. His Dry Bar special Purity Pants has drawn millions of views. He has opened for Tom Papa and Demetri Martin. This show starts at 7:00 PM and is rated PG-13.

title: Jodi White
description: Comedian Jodi White performs two nights of stand-up at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Jodi White brings two nights of stand-up to The Comedy Catch. Her act leans on candid, relatable takes that keep the room laughing. Shows run at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM on both nights. Rated R, so leave the kids at home. Pick your show time and get to 29 Station Street early for a good seat. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue website for ticket prices and show times.

title: Jonnie W
description: Clean comedy headliner Jonnie W performs at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga. This show is sold out.
body: Clean, family-friendly jokes are Jonnie W's calling card at The Comedy Catch. This show is sold out, so check the venue for released seats. Doors open 30 minutes before the 7:00 PM show. Jonnie W is a Nashville-based comedian known for clean stand-up that works across age groups. He has toured nationally and appeared on television. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the website for any returned tickets. This is a rare sold-out engagement at the venue and demand remains high for any released seats.

title: Jordan Conley
description: America's Got Talent comedian Jordan Conley brings his high-energy stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Jordan Conley headlines The Comedy Catch. He is a stand-up comedian from Garden Grove, California. He won the Wildcard spot on Season 17 of America's Got Talent and reached the semifinals. Simon Cowell gave his set a standing ovation. His comedy covers movies, superheroes, theme parks, and married life. He brings high energy and a rapid-fire delivery to the stage. Shows run Friday and Saturday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show is rated PG-18.

title: Josh Sneed
description: Comedy Central comic Josh Sneed brings his clean observational stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Josh Sneed headlines The Comedy Catch. The Cincinnati comic left a job at Procter and Gamble to chase stand-up. He has a Comedy Central Presents special and a Last Comic Standing run. His clean, relatable act draws on life as a husband and father. He is one of the most-played comics on Sirius XM and hosts the Detention podcast. Shows run Friday and Saturday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show is rated PG-13.

title: Kasaun Wilson
description: Emmy-nominated writer and comedian Kasaun Wilson brings his storytelling stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Kasaun Wilson headlines The Comedy Catch. He is a comedian and writer who earned Emmy and WGA nominations for The Problem with Jon Stewart. Rolling Stone recognized his work on that show. He began comedy at Howard University and has since played the Apollo Theater and Netflix Is a Joke. His stand-up blends sharp storytelling with honest observation. He has also appeared on Last Comic Standing and Laff Tracks. Shows run Friday and Saturday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show is rated PG-18.

title: Lookout Comedy Festival with Alex Kumin
description: NYC comic Alex Kumin headlines a Lookout Comedy Festival show at The Comedy Catch.
body: Alex Kumin headlines a Lookout Comedy Festival show at The Comedy Catch. The New York comic came up through Chicago and Boston before settling in the city. She writes bold, sharp stand-up about gender and social life. She is a regular at the Comedy Cellar and topped a 2025 comics-to-watch list. Shows run at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. The show is rated R.

title: Lookout Comedy Festival with Daniel Dellano
description: Atlanta comic Daniel Dellanno headlines a Lookout Comedy Festival show at The Comedy Catch.
body: Daniel Dellanno headlines a Lookout Comedy Festival show at The Comedy Catch. The Atlanta comic started stand-up at age 18 and made his Netflix debut on Kevin Hart's Funny AF. His style blends quick wit with honest jokes about dating and city life. He has also played the Comedy Store in Los Angeles. This show starts at 7:00 PM. The show is rated R.

title: Lookout Comedy Festival with Jimmy Sowell
description: Chattanooga comic Jimmy Sowell headlines a Lookout Comedy Festival show at The Comedy Catch.
body: Jimmy Sowell headlines a Lookout Comedy Festival show at The Comedy Catch. Sowell is a Chattanooga comic known online as NERDORK. His viral pullover sketches have drawn hundreds of millions of views across social media. He pairs silly energy with adult stoner humor and nearly a decade of stand-up experience. This show starts at 7:00 PM. The show is rated R, so come ready for an adult set.

title: Lookout Comedy Festival with Ryan Goodcase
description: Deadpan comic Ryan Goodcase headlines a Lookout Comedy Festival show at The Comedy Catch.
body: Ryan Goodcase headlines a Lookout Comedy Festival show at The Comedy Catch. Goodcase writes tight jokes and delivers them with dry, deadpan calm. He became the youngest winner of the World Series of Comedy in 2019. He later won the San Francisco International Comedy Competition. A festival clip of his set drew tens of millions of views. Shows run at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. The show is rated R.

title: Luke Null
description: Former SNL cast member Luke Null brings his musical comedy to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Luke Null headlines The Comedy Catch. The Cincinnati comic was a cast member on Saturday Night Live for its 43rd season. He builds his act around a guitar, pairing witty jokes with catchy songs. He trained in improv at the iO Theater in Chicago before SNL. His special Pretty Songs, Dirty Words came out in 2025. This show starts at 7:00 PM on Thursday. It is rated R, so plan an adult night out.

title: Mario Adrion
description: Comedian and content creator Mario Adrion brings a special engagement to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Mario Adrion brings his stage show to The Comedy Catch for a special engagement. The former model turned comedian and content creator is known for his big online following and playful, high-energy set. Shows run at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM on both nights. Rated R, so plan an adult night out downtown at 29 Station Street. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue website for ticket prices and show times.

title: Mario Tory
description: Atlanta comic Mario Tory brings his quick storytelling and crowd-savvy timing to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Mario Tory headlines The Comedy Catch. The Atlanta comic is known for quick storytelling and crowd-savvy timing. He was the first comedian featured on Kevin Hart's Hart of the City on Comedy Central. Hart then produced his half-hour special for The Next Level. He has also performed on 50 Cent's BET show 50 Central. This show starts at 7:00 PM on Saturday. It is rated R, so plan an adult night out downtown.

title: Matthew Broussard
description: Tonight Show and Conan comic Matthew Broussard brings his clever stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Matthew Broussard headlines The Comedy Catch. The Atlanta-raised comic studied applied math at Rice before stand-up. He has performed on The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon and Conan. He also filmed a Comedy Central Half Hour and competed in Roast Battle. His set digs into personal stories plus sidebars on grammar and statistics. Shows run Friday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM, Saturday at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM. This show is rated for adults.

title: Michael Longfellow
description: Former SNL cast member Michael Longfellow performs two nights of stand-up at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Michael Longfellow brings his dry, sharp stand-up to The Comedy Catch for two nights. The former Saturday Night Live cast member earned comparisons to Norm Macdonald for his deadpan delivery. Shows run at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM on both nights. Rated R, so plan a grown-up night out downtown at 29 Station Street. Pick your time and get there early.

title: Michael Palascak
description: Clean comedian Michael Palascak headlines a special engagement at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Michael Palascak headlines a special engagement of clean comedy at The Comedy Catch. He is known for tight, family-friendly sets and appearances on late-night TV. The show starts at 7:00 PM and works for a wide crowd. Bring the whole group for a fun night out downtown at 29 Station Street and enjoy laughs everyone can share. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue website for ticket prices and show times.

title: Moody Molavi
description: Iranian-American comic Moody Molavi brings high-energy storytelling to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Moody Molavi headlines a high-energy night at The Comedy Catch. The Tennessee-based comic grew up as an Iranian Southern Baptist and mines that mashup for laughs. He calls himself a blend of kebabs and grits. His Dry Bar special Remove Before Flight has passed 10 million views. His act runs on animated storytelling and family stories. This show is rated PG-13. Find the room downtown at 29 Station Street.

title: Mr. Showtime David Scott
description: Guinness World Record holder Mr. Showtime David Scott brings his high-energy stand-up and music finale to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: David Scott headlines The Comedy Catch as Mr. Showtime. The New York native holds the Guinness World Record for the longest solo stand-up set at 40 hours and 8 minutes. His act channels Rat Pack style and pure stage energy. The finale runs the crowd through four decades of music. He has appeared on HBO and Comedy Central. Shows run Friday and Saturday, with 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM sets on Friday. This show is rated for adults.

title: Musical Monday
description: Musical Monday blends live music and comedy on the stage at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Musical Monday mixes live music and comedy on one stage at The Comedy Catch. Performers blend songs and jokes for a relaxed, offbeat night out. The show starts early at 6:00 PM, so plan dinner downtown first. This show carries an adult rating. Find the room at 29 Station Street and settle in for something different from a standard stand-up set.

title: New Year's Eve with Nick Murphy
description: Austin comic Nick Murphy headlines New Year's Eve at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Nick Murphy headlines New Year's Eve at The Comedy Catch. The Atlanta-raised, Austin-based comic made his debut on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. Netflix picked him for its 2025 Introducing showcase after sets at major festivals. He credits his stage skill to years of observation and hard work. Ring in the new year with two shows at 7:00 PM and 10:00 PM. This show is rated R, so plan an adult night out.

title: Nick Murphy
description: Tonight Show comic Nick Murphy brings his observational stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Nick Murphy headlines a weekend run at The Comedy Catch. The Atlanta-raised, Austin-based comic made his debut on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. Netflix selected him for its 2025 Introducing showcase after sets at the Netflix Is A Joke and Moontower festivals. His observational comedy draws on years of watching and writing. Shows run Friday and Saturday, with 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM sets on Saturday. This show is rated for adults.

title: Now You See Us Comedy Tour
description: Kill Tony Golden Ticket winners Mason Bird, Chris Silio, and JJ Alexander bring the Now You See Us Comedy Tour to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: The Now You See Us Comedy Tour comes to The Comedy Catch. The show features Mason Bird, Chris Silio, and JJ Alexander. All three earned Golden Tickets on the Kill Tony podcast. Chris Silio is a blind comic from Miami known for brutally honest jokes. The night brings outrageous stories, sharp observations, and unpredictable humor. This show starts at 7:00 PM on Thursday. It is rated R, so plan an adult night out downtown.

title: Open Mic Night
description: Open Mic Night brings up-and-coming stand-up comics to the stage at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Open Mic Night puts fresh comics on the stage at The Comedy Catch. New acts test jokes and work on their sets in front of a live crowd. Shows are rated R, so leave the kids at home. Grab a seat downtown at 29 Station Street and cheer on the next wave of local talent. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. No ticket required to attend Open Mic Night.

title: Patrick Garrity
description: Touring comic Patrick Garrity brings wild characters and impressions to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Patrick Garrity headlines a special engagement at The Comedy Catch. The comic runs a nonstop road schedule he calls the Neverending Tour. He packs his act with wild characters, sharp impressions, and off-the-wall stories. Fans sign his white touring car after every show. His material draws on the military, Irish culture, and life as the youngest sibling. This show is rated R, so plan an adult night out.

title: Rob Coleman
description: Cleveland comic Rob Coleman brings clean, clever stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Rob Coleman headlines two nights at The Comedy Catch. The Cleveland comic has worked the stage for more than a decade. He won the 2025 World Series of Comedy. Coleman keeps his material clean and clever, which lets him play clubs, colleges, and churches alike. Shows run Friday and Saturday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. Come downtown to 29 Station Street for the show.

title: Rocky Dale Davis
description: Alabama comic Rocky Dale Davis brings his viral storytelling stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Rocky Dale Davis headlines The Comedy Catch. The Brookwood, Alabama native has racked up over 500 million views online. He has appeared on NBC's Bring the Funny and Comedy Central's Hart of the City. He jokes about his redneck family, his Brooklyn neighbors, and sober dating. He has opened for Bert Kreischer and Tom Segura. Shows run Wednesday and Thursday at 7:00 PM. This show is rated R, so plan an adult night out downtown.

title: Salty Mom Comedy Tour
description: The Salty Mom Comedy Tour brings a night of stand-up about motherhood and marriage to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: The Salty Mom Comedy Tour rolls into The Comedy Catch for one night only. Expect honest, unfiltered jokes about motherhood, marriage, and everyday chaos. The show runs at 7:00 PM and is rated PG-18. Round up your friends for a well-earned night out downtown at 29 Station Street and laugh through the parts of parenting nobody warns you about. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue website for ticket prices and show times.

title: Sarah Rose Hyland
description: Second City and Comedy Store comic Sarah Rose Hyland brings her character-driven stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Sarah Rose Hyland headlines The Comedy Catch. The Louisville native started at Second City Chicago before moving to Los Angeles. She trained at UCB and The Groundlings and now performs at the Comedy Store. She landed series-regular roles on MTV's Punk'd and Fox's MADtv. She has opened for Margaret Cho and Bobby Lee. This show starts at 7:00 PM on Thursday. It is rated R, so plan an adult night out downtown.

title: Sean Patton
description: New Orleans comic Sean Patton brings his restless stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Sean Patton headlines a special engagement at The Comedy Catch. The New Orleans comic built his name in New York with restless, physical storytelling. He has twice performed on Conan and released the Peacock special Number One. He also stars on the FX series English Teacher. Shows run Monday and Tuesday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show is rated R, so plan an adult night out.

title: Shapel Lacey
description: Comedy Store regular Shapel Lacey brings his honest, high-energy stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Shapel Lacey headlines The Comedy Catch. The Mesa, Arizona native is a paid regular at the world-famous Comedy Store. A former competitive cheerleader and punk rocker, he turns personal chaos into comedy. His material runs sharp, honest, and unexpectedly heartwarming. He made the 2026 Netflix shortlist and performs alongside Bill Burr and Matt Rife. Shows run Friday and Saturday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show is rated R, so plan an adult night out.

title: Shayne Smith
description: Heavily tattooed storyteller Shayne Smith brings his offbeat stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Shayne Smith headlines The Comedy Catch. The Utah-raised comic is one of the most tattooed performers in comedy. His act blends sharp storytelling with an offbeat, self-aware sense of humor. His special Prison for Wizards has passed 32 million views online. He also sings for the band Painted Devils. Shows run Friday and Saturday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This is a clean show that works for a night out downtown.

title: Steven Rogers
description: Clean comic and Brian Regan opener Steven Rogers brings his observational stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Steven Rogers headlines The Comedy Catch. The Syracuse native and New York comic made his TV debut on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert. He opens for Brian Regan in theaters across the country. His act blends wit, vulnerability, and observational jokes about everyday life. His album Before He Was Super hit number one on iTunes. Shows run Friday through Sunday. This is a clean show that works for a family night out.

title: Ted Barton
description: Comedian Ted Barton performs two nights of stand-up at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Ted Barton takes the stage for two nights of stand-up at The Comedy Catch. His set mixes sharp storytelling with quick crowd work for a lively room. Shows run Monday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM, then Tuesday at 6:00 PM. Rated PG-18, so plan a grown-up night out downtown at 29 Station Street. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue website for ticket prices. Each show runs about 75 minutes.

title: The Love & Marriage Game with Bad Santa
description: Bad Santa hosts a live couples game show at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga, where pairs compete for prizes.
body: Bad Santa hosts a live couples game show at The Comedy Catch. Pairs answer questions to test how well they know each other. Couples battle other teams for a shot at the stage and a prize. The late show starts at 10:00 PM on Saturday. This is an audience-driven night, so bring your partner and play along. This show is rated R, so plan an adult night out downtown.

title: Tony Tone
description: Def Comedy Jam veteran Tony Tone brings his impressions and real-life humor to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Tony Tone headlines The Comedy Catch. He is a veteran comedian and actor who has performed since 1990. He appeared on HBO's Def Comedy Jam, BET's Comic View, and Comics Unleashed. From 2006 to 2013 he served as Ringmaster for the UniverSoul Circus. His act mixes sharp impressions with stories about family and everyday life. He has shared the stage with Dave Chappelle, Steve Harvey, and Chris Rock. Shows run Friday and Saturday at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM. This show is rated R.

title: Winston Hodges
description: Touring comic Winston Hodges brings high-energy Southern stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Winston Hodges plays a special engagement at The Comedy Catch. The comic grew up in Richmond, Virginia and now tours full time from Washington, D.C. His high-energy sets mix Southern charm with edgy, pointed jokes about race and religion. He reached the top six on Kevin Hart's Funny AF for Netflix. This show starts at 7:00 PM and is rated R.

title: Chattanooga Market at Creature Comforts Beer Garden
description: The Chattanooga Market sets up every Thursday at the Creature Comforts Beer Garden in the Foundries District, next to Erlanger Park.
body: Beer and local goods every Thursday evening. The Chattanooga Market sets up inside The Shed at the Creature Comforts Beer Garden. The Shed sits in the Foundries District, next to Erlanger Park and the Tennessee Riverwalk. Vendors bring produce, handmade goods, and local products from 4 to 8 PM. Cold beer pours from the shipping crate bar the whole time. No ticket, no cover.

title: UGA vs. Georgia Tech Watch Party
description: Watch the UGA vs. Georgia Tech rivalry game at Creature Comforts Beer Garden in Chattanooga. The venue pours the official craft beer of the Dawgs for the occasion.
body: UGA and Georgia Tech have played every year since 1897. The rivalry draws strong Dawgs support in Chattanooga. Creature Comforts is pouring the official craft beer of the Dawgs for this watch party. The Beer Garden is a good spot to watch with people who actually care about the result. The event runs 3 pm to 11 pm. Hours depend on the actual kickoff time. Check the venue's social pages before game day for any updates. The Beer Garden sits at Foundry Plaza, an open-air space in the Foundries District next to Erlanger Park. Parking in the Foundry District fills fast on busy nights. The 21st Street garage nearby is a solid backup option.

title: Bluegrass Week
description: Bluegrass Week at the Creative Discovery Museum starts October 18 with music-themed activities in the galleries from 10am to 5pm.
body: Bluegrass Week fills the Creative Discovery Museum with music starting October 18, from 10am to 5pm. The museum's renovated music area shows off instruments and sounds from different cultures. Kids pick, strum, and learn where bluegrass comes from across the week. Hands-on activities run all day. This event is for members. The Creative Discovery Museum is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the CDM website for admission pricing. Members receive a discount.

title: Cheers to the New Year
description: Creative Discovery Museum throws a family New Year's party with evening play on December 30.
body: Cheers to the New Year is the museum's family New Year's party. Kids get to ring in the celebration a night early on December 30. The evening runs the museum after hours for two hours of play. Tickets cost $22, and members pay just $10. This event works well for families who want to toast the new year but still get the kids to bed. Buy tickets ahead of time, since holiday evenings fill up fast. Park on Chestnut Street or in a nearby downtown garage.

title: Chef in Residence
description: Chef in Residence at the Creative Discovery Museum runs Saturdays from November 7 to January 2 with Dr. Luronda Jennings in the kitchen.
body: Chef in Residence brings hands-on cooking to the Creative Discovery Museum on Saturdays. Dr. Luronda Jennings leads the sessions from 1:30 to 2:30pm. The program runs from November 7 through January 2. Kids learn simple kitchen skills and explore how food is made. Each Saturday offers a fresh activity in the museum's Culinary Corner. Museum admission covers the program, so no separate ticket is needed. The Creative Discovery Museum is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the CDM website for the full Saturday schedule.

title: Club Discovery
description: Club Discovery at the Creative Discovery Museum is a Tuesday evening respite program for children of all abilities in kindergarten through 5th grade.
body: Club Discovery is a Tuesday evening respite program at the Creative Discovery Museum. It welcomes children of all abilities in kindergarten through 5th grade. The next session runs November 17 from 5:30 to 7:30pm. Trained volunteers guide the group through a predictable routine of play and activities. Kids make friends, spark curiosity, and explore the museum together. Each night includes snacks and plenty of peer interaction. The cost is $25 per session. The Creative Discovery Museum is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga.

title: Community Night
description: Community Night at the Creative Discovery Museum on October 6 lets members explore the galleries after hours from 5:30 to 8pm.
body: Explore the Creative Discovery Museum after hours at Community Night on October 6, from 5:30 to 8pm. Members get the run of the galleries, the inventor's workshop, and the hands-on exhibits across four floors. The evening gives families a quieter window to play and build together. Bring your membership card to get in. The Creative Discovery Museum is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the CDM website for member pricing and any registration requirements.

title: Countdown to FUN
description: Celebrate a year of play at Creative Discovery Museum with a daytime New Year's Eve countdown on December 31.
body: Countdown to FUN celebrates a full year of play on New Year's Eve. The museum runs its normal daytime hours with a festive countdown. This daytime party suits young kids who cannot stay up until midnight. Families get to mark the new year early and still make it home for naps. Museum admission covers the day's activities. Come in the morning for the calmest exhibits before the afternoon crowd. Parking is easiest before 11 AM on Chestnut Street.

title: Creative Perk
description: Creative Perk at the Creative Discovery Museum on October 17 celebrates coffeehouse culture with themed activities from 9am to 5pm.
body: Creative Perk brings coffeehouse culture to the Creative Discovery Museum on October 17, from 9am to 5pm. The day pairs the museum's hands-on exhibits with activities themed around cafes and the drinks families love. Kids explore the galleries while parents enjoy the cozy twist. This event is for members, so bring your card. The Creative Discovery Museum is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the CDM website for admission pricing and any special programming during the day.

title: Drink & Discover: Camp Fear
description: Drink & Discover: Camp Fear turns the Creative Discovery Museum into a 21+ after-hours mystery on October 23 from 7 to 10pm.
body: Adults become campers for one night at Drink & Discover: Camp Fear on October 23. This 21+ after-hours event runs from 7 to 10pm at the Creative Discovery Museum. Solve a mystery inspired by classic 1980s summer camp adventures while you play games and work puzzles. General admission is $35 and includes one drink ticket. Bring valid ID for entry.

title: Jingle Bell Member Morning
description: CDM members get an early holiday morning of play before the museum opens to the public on December 13.
body: Jingle Bell Member Morning gives CDM members the museum before the public arrives. Families celebrate the holiday season with a festive morning of play. The early start means shorter lines and quieter exhibits for young kids. This event is free, but only current members can attend. Bring your membership card to check in at the door. The 8:30 AM start makes this a good fit for early-rising toddlers. Grab coffee nearby first, since the morning ends at 10 AM.

title: KIDCON
description: KIDCON at the Creative Discovery Museum on September 18 is a superhero-themed family night for members from 6 to 8pm.
body: Suit up for KIDCON at the Creative Discovery Museum on September 18, from 6 to 8pm. The whole family can dress as their favorite superheroes for a night of games, crafts, and heroic fun. KIDCON is an extended hours event at the CDM on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Members receive a discount on admission. The event runs the museum as a convention-themed experience with stations and activities across the building. Check the CDM website for ticket details. Costumes are encouraged and many families come in full superhero gear.

title: Member Evening - Snow Night
description: Member Evening - Snow Night opens the Winter Playland exhibit at the Creative Discovery Museum on November 9 from 6 to 8pm.
body: Snow Night opens the Winter Playland exhibit at the Creative Discovery Museum. The new exhibit shows how people play in cold weather. Kids try ice climbing, ice skating, and snowman decorating at hands-on stations. The museum serves hot chocolate throughout the evening. The night ends with the first indoor snowfall and a Frosty the Snowman dance party. This event is for members only, and you must register in advance.

title: Member Morning
description: Member Morning at the Creative Discovery Museum on November 22 gives members early access to the galleries before general admission opens.
body: Member Morning gives Creative Discovery Museum members early access to the galleries. The next one runs November 22 from 9 to 10am. Members explore the hands-on exhibits before the museum opens to general admission guests. The quiet hour lets families play and build without the usual crowds. This perk is free for members, so bring your card. The Creative Discovery Museum is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the CDM website for the full schedule of member mornings and other member benefits.

title: Monster Bash
description: Monster Bash at the Creative Discovery Museum on October 9 is a spooky-not-scary family night for members from 6 to 9pm.
body: Get in on the spooky-not-scary fun at Monster Bash on October 9, from 6 to 9pm. The Creative Discovery Museum fills with Halloween games and hands-on activities. Monster Bash is designed for young children - the scares are minimal and the focus is on play and creativity. The museum is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the CDM website for ticket prices. Members receive a discount. The event runs with extended hours compared to regular admission. Costumes are welcome and encouraged. Expect craft stations, themed games, and character appearances through the evening.

title: National Park City PLAY Street
description: National Park City PLAY Street at the Creative Discovery Museum on September 26 is a free block party celebrating outdoor recreation in Chattanooga.
body: Head to the Creative Discovery Museum on September 26 for the National Park City PLAY Street, a free block party from 9am to 3pm. The museum teams up with Chattanooga National Park City to celebrate outdoor play and recreation. Expect hands-on activities, games, and ways to explore the outdoors right in the heart of downtown. Everyone is welcome, and admission is free.

title: Preschool Adventure: Snow Fun
description: Preschoolers explore winter with hands-on play and pretend snow at Creative Discovery Museum on December 12.
body: Preschool Adventure: Snow Fun turns the museum into a winter playground for young children. Kids explore the season through hands-on activities and creative play. They make a little pretend snow and dig into sensory discoveries. The program suits toddlers and preschoolers who learn best by touching and doing. This event runs all day, so you can come when it fits your child's nap schedule. Museum admission covers the activities. Arrive early on a weekend to find parking near the Chestnut Street entrance.

title: Preschool Adventure: Superheroes!
description: Preschool Adventure: Superheroes! at the Creative Discovery Museum runs September 12 from 9 to 11am. A morning of superhero fun made for little kids.
body: The Creative Discovery Museum hosts a superhero morning for preschoolers on September 12, from 9 to 11am. Little kids can play, explore, and pretend to save the day. The event is free for members. Non-member admission applies at the standard rate for the museum on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. The preschool adventure format uses the museum's existing play areas alongside themed programming. Costumes are welcome. Check the CDM website for registration and any special requirements for the event. These morning programs fill quickly for the preschool age group.

title: Sensory Night
description: Sensory Night at the Creative Discovery Museum on December 4 gives children with sensory sensitivities a calm, low-sensory evening in the galleries.
body: Sensory Night gives children with sensory sensitivities a calm way to explore the Creative Discovery Museum. The museum runs this evening on December 4 from 5:30 to 8pm. Staff dim the overhead announcements and reduce food smells and other strong sensory inputs. Guests can check out headphones at Guest Relations. Admission is free, but you must register in advance. The museum caps attendance at 200 visitors to keep the space quiet and comfortable.

title: STEAM Week
description: STEAM Week at the Creative Discovery Museum celebrates the Tennessee STEAM Festival with hands-on science and art activities from October 10.
body: STEAM Week kicks off October 10 as the Creative Discovery Museum joins the Tennessee STEAM Festival. The museum fills with hands-on activities across science, technology, engineering, art, and math. Kids build, experiment, and test ideas in the inventor's workshop and across the galleries. The festival runs statewide through late October. This event is for members. The Creative Discovery Museum is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the CDM website for admission pricing. Members receive a discount during the festival week.

title: Turquoise Trail
description: Turquoise Trail is an inclusive, low-sensory trick-or-treat night at the Creative Discovery Museum on October 26 from 6 to 7:30pm.
body: Turquoise Trail is an inclusive trick-or-treat night at the Creative Discovery Museum on October 26, from 6 to 7:30pm. The event uses reduced sensory stimulation - lower lights, lower sound levels, and a quieter environment for children who find standard Halloween events overwhelming. The museum is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the CDM website for ticket details. Costumes are welcome. Turquoise Trail is designed to give sensory-sensitive kids and families a Halloween experience that works for them. The event typically sells out - register early through the museum website.

title: Chattanooga Hungry Turkey
description: The Chattanooga Hungry Turkey is a post-Thanksgiving road race on the CTC calendar with registration through RaceRoster.
body: The Chattanooga Hungry Turkey runs the Saturday after Thanksgiving, two days after the Fitness Central Turkey Trot. It gives runners back-to-back holiday race options without leaving the region. Registration is through RaceRoster. The November timing means cold morning temperatures, so dress in layers and expect a crowd of post-holiday runners. The CTC handles timing and certification. Check the CTC calendar for distance, start location, and current registration fees.

title: Circle Endurance Event 3, 6, 12, 24 Hour
description: The Circle Endurance Event gives runners a choice of 3, 6, 12, or 24-hour timed formats on a looped course. Run as many miles as you can before time runs out.
body: Pick your suffering: 3, 6, 12, or 24 hours on a looped course, covering as many miles as you can before time runs out. The format rewards patience over pace. There are no place finishes based on distance covered. You set your own target and adjust on the fly. Volunteers can sign up through UltraSignUp if you want to support without racing. Check the CTC calendar for course location and start time.

title: Fitness Central Turkey Trot 2026
description: The Fitness Central Turkey Trot is a Chattanooga Thanksgiving morning road race sponsored by the Chattanooga Track Club.
body: Thanksgiving morning in Chattanooga means road racing before the turkey hits the table. The Fitness Central Turkey Trot is a CTC-sponsored event with chip timing and a certified course. The club has run events like this for decades and the logistics are well organized. These races fill up fast in November. Check the CTC calendar for distance, start time, and registration link.

title: 48th Annual Habitat For Humanity Hogpen Hillclimb 18k & Cool River Tubing 5k
description: The 48th annual Hogpen Hillclimb offers an 18k trail race with serious elevation gain alongside a 5k option, with proceeds benefiting Habitat for Humanity.
body: Now in its 48th year, the Hogpen Hillclimb is one of the oldest races on the Chattanooga calendar. The 18k course carries significant elevation gain. A 5k Cool River Tubing option gives less-experienced runners a way in. Proceeds benefit Habitat for Humanity. January conditions mean cold mornings and potentially icy trails. The charity connection and long history make this one a fixture for local runners. Check the CTC calendar for start location and registration.

title: 2026 Little Debbie Christmas Tree Cake Run
description: The Little Debbie Christmas Tree Cake Run is a holiday-themed road race in Ooltewah, TN with a fun snack tie-in and a festive December atmosphere.
body: A holiday race in Ooltewah with one of the better names on the local calendar. The Little Debbie tie-in brings a festive crowd and costumes are common. The December date and playful theme make it a popular pick for runners who want something seasonal. It sits in the middle of a busy stretch of CTC races. Check the CTC calendar for distance, start time, and registration link.

title: Nightmare on Nashville Street 5K and Fun Run
description: The Nightmare on Nashville Street 5K and Fun Run is a Halloween-themed race along Nashville Street in Chattanooga with costumes encouraged.
body: Nashville Street in Chattanooga gets a Halloween takeover for this 5K and Fun Run in late October. Costumes are standard. The race draws as many runners in monster suits as it does people going for a PR. A Fun Run option opens it up to kids and casual participants. The route along Nashville Street keeps things mostly flat. Check the CTC calendar for start time and registration.

title: Run Santa Run Chattanooga
description: Run Santa Run Chattanooga is a holiday-themed road race in December where costumes are encouraged and the festive atmosphere is part of the draw.
body: Santa suits, elf hats, and reindeer antlers are standard gear for this one. Run Santa Run Chattanooga is a holiday costume race that draws competitive runners and first-timers in equal measure. It is part of the broader Run Santa Run series with events in cities across the country. The December date and festive atmosphere make it one of the more social races on the CTC calendar. Check the CTC website for distance, start location, and registration.

title: Trail of Tears 5 Miler
description: The Trail of Tears 5 Miler is a 5-mile road race on the CTC calendar in December.
body: Five miles sits between a 5K and a 10K, which makes the Trail of Tears 5 Miler a solid mid-December workout for runners building through the holidays. The CTC handles chip timing and course certification. The race falls the same weekend as Christmas at the Choo-Choo, so downtown parking can be tighter than usual. Check the CTC calendar for start location and current registration fees.

title: The Wauhatchie Trail Race
description: The Wauhatchie Trail Race is a trail run in the Wauhatchie area near Lookout Mountain with registration through UltraSignUp.
body: The Wauhatchie Trail Race heads into the valley near Lookout Mountain on wooded single-track with uneven terrain. February conditions can run from firm to muddy depending on recent rain. Trail shoes are worth the investment for this course. Registration is through UltraSignUp. The race draws a mix of Chattanooga trail regulars and runners from across the region. Check the CTC calendar or UltraSignUp for distance options and current fees.

title: Live Trivia Tuesday at Feed Tavern & Table Co.
description: Weekly Tuesday live trivia at Feed Tavern & Table Co. on the Southside. Host Izzy runs questions from 7:30pm with $4 pints and half-price house wine.
body: Izzy hosts trivia every Tuesday at 7:30pm inside the Tavern at Feed Tavern & Table Co. on the Southside. Teams compete across multiple rounds of general knowledge, pop culture, and themed questions. Feed Tavern & Table Co. is a Southside Chattanooga restaurant and bar. No ticket required. Walk in and form a team. Table size limits vary - check the social pages. The kitchen serves food through the trivia session. The Tavern is the indoor bar section of the restaurant. Check the Feed social pages for any changes to the weekly schedule or any special themed trivia nights.

title: Thursday Patio Live Music at Feed Tavern & Table Co.
description: Weekly Thursday live local music on the patio at Feed Tavern & Table Co. on the Southside. Local artists perform from 6:30pm with $8 cocktail specials.
body: Local musicians play live on the patio every Thursday starting at 6:30pm at Feed Tavern & Table Co. Artists rotate weekly and the current lineup posts on the venue social pages. Feed Tavern & Table Co. is a Southside Chattanooga restaurant and bar. The patio provides outdoor seating during the warmer months. No cover charge for patio music nights. Walk in and find a seat. The kitchen serves food through the evening. Check the Feed social pages for the weekly artist announcement and any changes to the schedule.

title: Wednesday Bingo at Feed Tavern & Table Co.
description: Weekly Wednesday bingo night at Feed Tavern & Table Co. on the Southside. Host Izzy calls cards from 7pm with Whiskey Wednesday cocktail specials running all night.
body: Izzy calls bingo every Wednesday at 7pm at Feed Tavern & Table Co. on the Southside. Cards start at 7pm and games run through the evening. Whiskey Wednesday specials are on. Feed Tavern & Table Co. is a Southside Chattanooga restaurant and bar. The bingo night is a weekly community event that draws regulars and newcomers. No ticket required - walk in and buy cards at the door. The Whiskey Wednesday specials give you something to sip while you wait for your numbers. Check the Feed social pages for any changes to the weekly schedule.

title: 3 Sisters Bluegrass Festival
description: The 3 Sisters Bluegrass Festival returns to Ross's Landing in Chattanooga on October 2-3, 2026. Free admission, local and national bluegrass acts on the Tennessee River.
body: Free bluegrass on the riverfront, two days, rain or shine. Chattanooga Presents books local, regional, and national acts every fall at Ross's Landing. Rhonda Vincent is confirmed for 2026. Lawn chairs and blankets welcome. No outside food, drink, or coolers. Vendors on site with food, beer, and wine. Leashed dogs OK. Free electric shuttle runs until 11pm. Downtown hotels are a short walk if you're making a weekend of it.

title: Chattanooga Motorcar Festival
description: The Chattanooga Motorcar Festival takes over the downtown riverfront for a weekend of vintage racing, Concours d'Elegance, and car culture. Debuted 2019, returning Fall 2026.
body: Vintage racing on track, a Concours d'Elegance drawing entries from across the country, automobile displays, and concerts on the downtown riverfront. The festival debuted in 2019 and ran every fall until a postponement in 2025. The 2024 Best in Show went to a 1935 Swallow Sidecar SS1. Returning Fall 2026. Specific dates haven't been announced yet. Check chattanoogamotorcar.com for updates.

title: Ketner's Mill Country Arts Fair
description: Ketner's Mill Country Arts Fair returns October 3-4, 2026 in Whitwell, TN. 48th annual fair at the historic 1824 grist mill - 150+ artisans, sorghum demos, bluegrass, wagon rides, and southern fair food in the Sequatchie Valley.
body: An 1824 water-powered grist mill in the Sequatchie Valley, about 45 minutes from Chattanooga, hosts this every October. Over 150 juried artisans sell paintings, pottery, woodworking, jewelry, and folk art. Sorghum molasses gets made on site with mule-powered equipment. Wagon and canoe rides run on the Sequatchie River, the Marion County 4-H brings a petting zoo, and live bluegrass, country, and gospel plays all weekend. $8 cash at the gate, kids 8 and under free. All admission goes toward preserving the mill. Saturday 9am–6pm, Sunday 10am–5:30pm. Free parking, leashed dogs welcome.

title: MAINx24
description: MAINx24 is a 24-hour street festival on the Chattanooga Southside every first Saturday of December. 120+ events including the parade, Chili Cook-Off, Adult Big Wheel Races, and concerts on Main Street.
body: Main Street on the Southside goes car-free for 24 hours every first Saturday of December. What started as a handful of events has grown to 120+: parade (voted best in Chattanooga three years running), live music across multiple stages, art installations, food, and community events from midnight to midnight. MAINx24 is Chattanooga's signature end-of-year community event. The South Broad Main Street corridor closes to cars from midnight Saturday to midnight Sunday. Free to attend. Check the MAINx24 website for the full event map, participating businesses, and entertainment schedule. Reflection Riding participates as a community partner.

title: Wine Over Water
description: Wine Over Water returns October 10, 2026 at Renaissance Park in Chattanooga. 30th anniversary of the region's premier wine tasting event - curated pours, food by Whitebird's Chef Amanda Clayton, and live music. 21+ only.
body: Thirty years of wine on the Tennessee River. Curated tastings with a commemorative glass, small bites and food pairings by Chef Amanda Clayton of Whitebird, charcuterie, pulled pork, live music from Ben van Winkle and The Figments, and roaming performances by the Chattanooga Circus Collective. The 2026 edition moves from the Walnut Street Bridge to Renaissance Park, between the Walnut Street and Market Street Bridges, while the bridge is under renovation. Same riverfront setting, different footprint. 21+ only, tickets through Eventbrite, nonrefundable but transferable. Presented by Preserve Chattanooga, platinum sponsor Food City.

title: Adventure Days at Chattanooga Zoo
description: Chattanooga Zoo teams up with the Chattanooga Public Library four times a year. Library card holders age 18 and under get free zoo admission, plus story time and hands-on activities all day.
body: Four times a year, the Chattanooga Zoo opens free to library cardholders age 18 and under. Bring your Chattanooga Public Library card to the ticket booth. Library staff run hands-on activities all day. A librarian leads story time at 11am and again at noon. Adults without a library card pay standard zoo rates. Gates open at 9am. The zoo sits inside Warner Park off North Holtzclaw Avenue.

title: Asian Lantern Festival at Chattanooga Zoo
description: Hundreds of illuminated hand-crafted lanterns fill the Chattanooga Zoo grounds each night from November 18 through January 23. Displays up to 16 feet tall feature tigers, polar bears, red pandas, and elephants across nearly 50 scenes.
body: Hundreds of hand-crafted illuminated lanterns line the zoo grounds each night through late January. Displays reach up to 16 feet tall and cover wildlife including tigers, polar bears, red pandas, and elephants. Nearly 50 distinct scenes are spread across the zoo. Some installations include interactive elements like swings and seesaws. Indoor habitats will be closed and most resident animals won't be visible during the festival. Tickets run $23.50 for adults and $17.50 for children ages 3-12. Zoo members pay $19 for adults and $14 for kids. The festival runs Wednesday through Sunday, 5:30 to 9:30pm.

title: Conservation Awareness Days at Chattanooga Zoo
description: Chattanooga Zoo runs Conservation Awareness Days to celebrate SAFE programs and wildlife conservation. Expect keeper chats, animal enrichment, info stations, and arts and crafts from 11am to 3pm.
body: The zoo marks wildlife conservation milestones with extra programming across the grounds. Conservation Awareness Days celebrate SAFE initiatives. SAFE stands for Saving Animals From Extinction. Each event runs from 11am to 3pm. Zoo keepers add extra talks on featured animals. Find information stations, themed animal enrichment, and arts and crafts at each stop. Everything is included with standard admission. Arrive by 11am to catch the first keeper chat.

title: Sunday Patio Music
description: Free live music on the patio every Sunday from 1 to 4pm at Five Wits Brewing Company, featuring local Chattanooga musicians.
body: Sundays slow down on the Five Wits patio on Long Street. Local musicians play from 1 to 4pm while the taps stay busy. Claim a table outside, bring a friend, and settle in. Five Wits Brewing is a craft brewery on Long Street in downtown Chattanooga. The Sunday patio music is a free event - walk in and find a spot. Acts rotate weekly and cover acoustic rock, folk, country, and Americana. Check the Five Wits social pages for the weekly artist and any changes to the schedule. The patio is covered and stays comfortable in most weather.

title: Trivia Night at Five Wits
description: Free trivia night every Thursday at 7pm at Five Wits Brewing Company, hosted by Chatt Trivia with prizes for the top three teams.
body: Thursday nights mean trivia at Five Wits on Long Street. Chatt Trivia hosts from 7 to 9pm. Answer well and your team lands in the top three for prizes. Grab a pint and find a table. Five Wits Brewing is a craft brewery on Long Street in downtown Chattanooga. No ticket required - walk in and form a team. The trivia format covers general knowledge, pop culture, sports, and current events. Check the Five Wits social pages for any themed trivia nights or changes to the weekly schedule.

title: Fall Festival at Flat Top Mountain Farm
description: Fall festival weekends at Flat Top Mountain Farm in Soddy-Daisy, TN - pumpkin patch, hayrides, corn maze, and mountain views.
body: Flat Top runs fall weekends through September and October - pumpkin patch, hayrides with views out to the Smoky Mountains, a corn maze, flower fields, food trucks, and live music most weekends. Flat Top Mountain Farm is near Ooltewah, Tennessee, east of Chattanooga. Admission is charged - check the Flat Top website for pricing and any timed entry requirements. The farm sits at an elevation that provides clear views toward the Smokies on clear days. Bring comfortable clothes and shoes you can walk in. Fall weekends draw large crowds - arrive early to beat the lines.

title: Harvest Hustle 5K
description: Off-road 5K through Flat Top Mountain Farm in Soddy-Daisy, TN on September 27.
body: Off-road 5K through the farm fields at Flat Top Mountain, with the sunflower fields and mountain views as the backdrop. The course runs past grazing horses and over the farm's natural terrain. Flat Top Mountain Farm is near Ooltewah, Tennessee, east of Chattanooga. Registration is required through the Flat Top website or a third-party running registration platform. Entry fees include a post-race gathering at the farm. This is a scenic and distinctive 5K course with elevation changes throughout. Check the Flat Top website for registration details, start time, and parking information.

title: Cocktail Class at Gate 11 Distillery
description: Weekly Thursday cocktail class at Gate 11 Distillery, where instructor Savanna guides guests through two seasonal cocktails using Gate 11 spirits. 21+.
body: Learn to mix two seasonal cocktails at Gate 11 every Thursday. Instructor Savanna walks the class through each pour and technique. You use Gate 11 spirits made in house. The class runs from 6 to 8pm and costs $30. You must be 21 or older to take part. Leave with recipes you can shake at home. Gate 11 Distillery is on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. The distillery makes spirits on-site. Check the Gate 11 website for cost and reservation details.

title: Distillery Divas and Drag Bingo at Gate 11
description: Weekly Saturday Distillery Divas and Drag Bingo at Gate 11 Distillery, hosted by Anastasia L'amour with bingo at 8pm and the main show at 9pm. 18+.
body: Saturday nights bring drag and bingo to Gate 11. Anastasia L'amour hosts the Distillery Divas. Bingo cards hit the tables at 8pm and the main show follows at 9pm. Gate 11 Distillery is on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. The distillery makes spirits on-site and uses them in its cocktails. Distillery Divas and Drag Bingo is a recurring Saturday night event. Check the Gate 11 website for ticket details. The event combines the game of bingo with live drag performance for an evening that keeps everyone at the table. Adult-rated content.

title: E.IGHT at the GATE Comedy Showcase
description: Monthly free comedy showcase at Gate 11 Distillery on the last Sunday, hosted by Alex Hutchinson with eight performers each night.
body: Eight comics take the stage at Gate 11 on the last Sunday of each month. Alex Hutchinson emcees the E.IGHT at the GATE showcase. Each performer gets a set, so the styles shift fast all night. The show runs from 7:30 to 10pm and costs nothing to watch. Order a craft cocktail and settle in. Local comedy fans fill the room.

title: Jest in Time Comedy Improv at Gate 11 Distillery
description: Weekly Tuesday comedy improv competition at Gate 11 Distillery, hosted by Shellyta Chatman with signups at 7:30pm and the show at 8pm.
body: Tuesday nights turn into a comedy showdown at Gate 11. Shellyta Chatman hosts Jest in Time, an improv competition that runs on audience calls. Signups open at 7:30pm and the show starts at 8pm. Performers build scenes on the spot from your suggestions. Grab a cocktail and heckle in good fun. The crowd helps pick who wins. Gate 11 Distillery is on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. Check the Gate 11 website for entry fee and start time.

title: Monday Blues Jam at Gate 11 Distillery
description: Free weekly Monday Blues Jam at Gate 11 Distillery, hosted by Robin Baker with Yattie Westfield and open sit-in slots for local musicians.
body: Blues fills the room at Gate 11 every Monday. Robin Baker and Yattie Westfield lead the jam from 7:30 to 10pm. Local players sit in and trade solos all night. The distillery pours craft spirits at the bar while you listen. Bring an instrument or just a good ear. Play starts at 7:30pm and the night runs loose. Gate 11 Distillery is on Brainerd Road in Chattanooga. The Monday blues jam is a free or low-cost weekly event. Check social pages for any changes.

title: Wednesday Trivia at Hair of the Dog Pub
body: Wednesday trivia runs every week at Hair of the Dog Pub on Market Street. Not Rocket Science Trivia hosts the night starting at 7pm. The pub is 21 and up with darts, pool, dog-friendly outdoor seating, and a full bar.

title: Autumn in Watercolor: Plein Air Workshop
description: Plein air watercolor workshop at Happy Valley Farms in Rossville, GA with nationally acclaimed watercolorist Alan Shuptrine.
body: Paint the countryside with nationally acclaimed watercolorist Alan Shuptrine. The workshop runs five hours with live demonstrations and personal instruction on capturing fall landscapes in watercolor. Shuptrine is a Chattanooga-based painter known for large-scale, highly detailed watercolor works. His paintings of the Appalachian region have been published and exhibited nationally. Happy Valley Farms provides the setting. Register through Happy Valley Farms. Check the site for cost and the specific date. All skill levels are welcome but participants should bring their own watercolor supplies if they have them.

title: Barbecue & Bourbon Dinner
description: Farm-to-table four-course dinner at Happy Valley Farms in Rossville, GA with pitmaster Chris Prieto, bourbon cocktails, and live music.
body: Four courses with award-winning pitmaster Chris Prieto - smoked brisket, farm-sourced sides, specialty bourbon cocktails, and live music against the sunflower fields. Happy Valley Farms hosts this dinner on its property. Prieto is known for his work in competition barbecue and farm-to-table barbecue cooking. The dinner format pairs his food with bourbon pairings selected for each course. Live music plays during the meal. Register through Happy Valley Farms. Check the site for cost and the specific date. Space is limited.

title: Boots and Buckles Line Dance Classes
description: Country and contemporary line dance class at Harrison Center every Monday evening.
body: Line dancing at Harrison Center every Monday evening, 6 to 9 PM in the Multi Purpose Room. The class covers country and contemporary styles. Beginners start with foundational steps while returning students tackle more complex routines. No partner is needed. Harrison Center is on Dodds Avenue in Chattanooga and runs a broad schedule of programs for seniors and adults. Check the website for cost and registration. Comfortable shoes with a smooth sole work best for line dancing. The Monday night class has built a consistent group of regular attendees.

title: Buddha Vandana and Dhamma Sermon
description: Buddhist prayer recitation and dharma teaching open to the public at Harrison Center.
body: A Buddhist prayer recitation and dhamma sermon at Harrison Center on September 26. The session runs about 90 minutes in the Multi Purpose Room. It is a free, community-oriented religious program open to anyone interested in Buddhist teaching and practice. The dhamma sermon covers Buddhist philosophy and practical application. Harrison Center is on Dodds Avenue in Chattanooga and regularly hosts community events across a range of spiritual and cultural traditions. No prior knowledge of Buddhism is required to attend. Check the Harrison Center website for the start time and any registration details.

title: Computer Basics Course
description: Three-session beginner computer course at Harrison Center building foundational digital skills.
body: Three evenings of computer training at Harrison Center, September 16 through 18. Sessions run from 5 to 8 PM in Classroom 1. The course is built for adults with little or no computer experience. Topics include navigating the desktop, using a web browser, email basics, and file management. Harrison Center is on Dodds Avenue in Chattanooga and serves the senior and adult community. Register through the center. Check the Harrison Center website for the cost and any prerequisite. The small class size allows the instructor to give individualized attention to each participant.

title: Fit4 Exercise Classes
description: Low-impact fitness class for women at Harrison Center combining aerobics, weights, and pilates stretching.
body: Aerobics, light weights, and Pilates stretching for women of all ages at Harrison Center. The class meets Monday afternoons in the Multi Purpose Room on Dodds Avenue. The format is low-impact and suits beginners and those returning to exercise after time away. Harrison Center serves the senior and adult community with affordable fitness programming. Check the website for the specific class time and any enrollment cost. The class runs through the semester and is led by a certified instructor. Bring comfortable clothes and a water bottle. Light hand weights are available at the center.

title: Kit & Kaboodle Krafting
description: Casual paper crafting session at Harrison Center for card making, journaling, and memory keeping.
body: Harrison Center hosts a casual paper crafting session on October 20. Crafters gather to work on projects together in the library classroom. You practice card making, scrapbooking, or any paper-based project of your choice. Some supplies are shared. Bring your own materials if you have specific projects in mind. Harrison Center is on Dodds Avenue in Chattanooga and serves the senior community with classes and programs. Check the website for the specific time and any entry fee. Kit & Kaboodle Krafting is a relaxed, social crafting event suited to all skill levels.

title: Medicare Educational Seminar
description: Free Medicare education seminar at Harrison Center covering benefit options and enrollment.
body: Harrison Center hosts a free Medicare education seminar on October 1. A licensed presenter explains how to compare plans and maximize your benefits. The session covers Medicare Part A, B, C, and D, along with supplement and Advantage plan options. This is not a sales presentation. No obligation to purchase anything. Harrison Center is on Dodds Avenue in Chattanooga and regularly hosts free educational programming for seniors and adults. Check the website for the start time and registration details. Attendees often bring specific questions about their own coverage and situations.

title: Paper Pixies - Stamp.N.Chat
description: Paper crafting class at Harrison Center with instruction from Stamp.N.Chat30. All materials included.
body: Stamp.N.Chat30 leads a paper crafting class at Harrison Center on October 8. Vicki Sewell is an Independent Stampin' Up! demonstrator. All materials are provided for this hands-on session. Participants learn basic stamping techniques and leave with finished cards or projects. No prior crafting experience is needed. Harrison Center is on Dodds Avenue in Chattanooga. Check the website for cost and registration. The class runs about two hours in the library classroom. Stampin' Up! uses rubber stamps, ink, and paper craft supplies to create greeting cards and other paper goods.

title: Seams Hard, Sew Easy
description: Adult sewing class at Harrison Center open to beginners and experienced sewers alike.
body: Sewing classes for adults at Harrison Center, meeting Tuesdays and Thursdays in Classroom 2. The sessions cover hand and machine sewing basics. Seniors are especially welcome. All skill levels fit in. No prior experience needed. Harrison Center is on Dodds Avenue in Chattanooga and serves the senior community with classes, programs, and events. The sewing class runs across multiple sessions in a semester format. Check the Harrison Center website for the full schedule, enrollment details, and any materials fee. The center provides sewing machines for students who do not own one.

title: Senior Acrylic Painting Classes
description: Weekly acrylic painting class for seniors at Harrison Center every Wednesday morning.
body: Acrylic painting for seniors every Wednesday morning at Harrison Center. The class covers basic techniques in Classroom 9. No prior experience is needed. Each week the instructor introduces new skills - color mixing, brush work, composition, and subject matter. Students develop individual projects at their own pace. Harrison Center is on Dodds Avenue in Chattanooga. Check the website for the specific class time and any materials fee. The class runs through the semester and builds toward a small showcase of student work. All materials are available at the center.

title: Seniors Dance
description: Monthly senior dance at Harrison Center featuring The Country Connection Band.
body: The Country Connection Band plays the senior dance at Harrison Center on September 19. The set covers classic country, waltz, cha-cha, line dance, and ballroom styles. Harrison Center hosts monthly dances as part of its senior programming. The dances draw regulars who come for the music, the company, and the chance to move. Harrison Center is on Dodds Avenue in Chattanooga. Check the website for admission details and start time. The dances typically run a few hours in the afternoon. All skill levels and dance backgrounds are welcome.

title: The Raqetts
description: Halloween charity dance event at Harrison Center benefiting McKamey Animal Center.
body: The Raqetts stage a Halloween charity dance event at Harrison Center on October 24. The party runs all afternoon and evening in the auditorium. All proceeds go to McKamey Animal Center as donations. Guests can dress in costume and support local animal rescue. The long window lets attendees drop in at any time. Harrison Center is on Dodds Avenue in Chattanooga and serves the senior community. Check the Harrison Center website for ticket details.

title: USA Dance Choo Choo Chapter
description: Monthly social ballroom dance hosted by the USA Dance Choo Choo Chapter at Harrison Center.
body: The USA Dance Choo Choo Chapter runs its monthly social ballroom dance at Harrison Center on October 9. The evening pairs a group lesson with open social dancing. USA Dance is a national nonprofit organization that promotes partner dancing across the country. The Choo Choo Chapter serves the Chattanooga area. Dances include waltz, foxtrot, swing, cha-cha, and others in the ballroom canon. Harrison Center is on Dodds Avenue. Check the USA Dance Choo Choo Chapter website for ticket details and start time. No partner is required - partners are shared among the attendees.

title: Bella and The Boys
description: Bella and The Boys play Hi-Fi Clyde's with high-energy country on September 18.
body: High energy country runs the night on Main Street. Bella Lam leads the band. She grew up in Tennessee and studied music at UTC. The set mixes modern and classic country with strong vocals and a tight band behind her. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred and has a dedicated dance floor. Bella and The Boys are a Chattanooga-area act with a growing regional following. Good Friday or Saturday night option for country fans.

title: Bettin' On The Mule
description: Northwest Georgia southern rock band Bettin' On The Mule plays Hi-Fi Clyde's on December 4.
body: Southern rock meets classic rock and country in this set. Bettin' On The Mule formed in 2017 in Rockmart, Georgia. Jacob Wilson leads the group and writes most of its songs. The band calls its blend hometown rock. They have won the Smiley's Georgia Music Showcase twice. Doors are 21 and up. Cover is $10.

title: Chattanooga Horn Authority
description: Eight-piece classic rock horn band Chattanooga Horn Authority plays Hi-Fi Clyde's on December 18.
body: Big brass rock fills the room. Chattanooga Horn Authority is an eight-piece local band. The group plays horn-driven covers of Chicago, Blood Sweat & Tears, Steely Dan, and Huey Lewis. The members bring decades of stage experience. Late crowds pack the floor for these sets. Doors are 21 and up. Cover is $10.

title: Cuatro Cinco: Ugly Christmas Sweater Party
