description: Chattanooga rapper Cuatro Cinco headlines an ugly Christmas sweater party at Hi-Fi Clyde's on December 12.
body: Hip hop drives this holiday party. Cuatro Cinco is a Chattanooga rapper known for upbeat, positive tracks. He won the 2025 Road to Nightfall contest and headlined that series. Wear your ugliest Christmas sweater for the theme. Expect a loud, high energy set. Doors are 21 and up. Cover is $10.

title: Doubleshotz
description: Chattanooga classic-rock cover band Doubleshotz plays Hi-Fi Clyde's on October 16.
body: Classic rock and blues covers carry the night. Doubleshotz plays a deep catalog. The set pulls from Stevie Ray Vaughan, Led Zeppelin, Eric Clapton, and others in the classic rock and blues tradition. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred people. Doubleshotz is a Chattanooga-area cover band known for faithful, high-energy renditions of classic material. Weekend nights at Hi-Fi Clyde's are well suited to this kind of catalog-driven set.

title: Forbidden Hwy
description: Regional Southern rock band Forbidden Hwy plays Hi-Fi Clyde's on October 23.
body: Guitar-driven riffs and a road-worn twang set the tone. Forbidden Hwy plays Southern and country rock. Expect familiar rock and country songs with a Southern edge. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred people and has a dedicated dance floor in front of the stage. Forbidden Hwy is a Chattanooga-area band that has played local venues and regional stages. Weekend nights at Hi-Fi Clyde's on Main Street suit this kind of guitar-driven set.

title: Fresh Mind
description: Fresh Mind brings reggae-rock fusion to Hi-Fi Clyde's on September 25.
body: Reggae rhythms, rock, jazz, and blues all share one set. Fresh Mind comes from the greater Chattanooga area. Frontman James Snider was born in Jamaica and brings the reggae tradition into the band's sound. The group has performed across the region and recorded multiple sets. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred people and has a dedicated dance floor in front of the stage.

title: Paul Childers Band
description: Nashville guitarist Paul Childers returns to Hi-Fi Clyde's on November 25.
body: Pop, R&B, and soul mix with blues rock leads. Paul Childers returns to Hi-Fi Clyde's with his band. His grooves lean on a Motown feel. He plays as a Solo act and with his full band. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred people. This November show is a return engagement from earlier in the year. Childers is a Nashville-based guitarist who brings a strong set of original soul and blues rock material to the stage.

title: Paul Childers Band
description: Nashville soul-funk guitarist Paul Childers plays Hi-Fi Clyde's on October 2.
body: Soul, funk, and blues rock guitar drive this Nashville set. Paul Childers sings, writes, and plays lead. His grooves lean on a Motown feel. He is a Southern guitarist and songwriter who has toured nationally and recorded in Nashville studios. His live band brings the full horn and rhythm section behind his guitar work. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred people with a dedicated dance floor in front of the stage.

title: Sloppy Street Tacos
description: Chattanooga funk-rock band Sloppy Street Tacos plays a Halloween show at Hi-Fi Clyde's.
body: Improvised jams and funk rock energy fill this Halloween set. Sloppy Street Tacos comes from Chattanooga. Vulfpeck and the Grateful Dead shape their sound. The band plays funk, rock, and jam material in long, improvisational sets. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The Halloween show may include costumes and themed programming. The room holds a few hundred people with a dedicated dance floor. This is a good late October option for fans of groove-heavy live music.

title: Sol Parade
description: Chattanooga funk and groove rock band Sol Parade plays Hi-Fi Clyde's on November 27.
body: Soft funk grooves meet hard-hitting riffs. Sol Parade comes from Chattanooga. Their songs build on steady grooves and layered guitars. The set shifts between tight funk arrangements and heavier guitar passages. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred people with a dedicated dance floor. Sol Parade is a Chattanooga-area band with a following in the local music scene. Weekend nights on Main Street suit this kind of groove-driven live rock performance.

title: Stacey Blanton Band
description: Georgia country artist Stacey Blanton plays Hi-Fi Clyde's on October 9.
body: Modern country and classic rock fill this loud, upbeat set. Stacey Blanton is a Georgia artist. The Georgia Country Awards named him 2025 Artist of the Year. His live show combines original material with strong stage energy. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred people with a dedicated dance floor. Blanton brings the energy of a touring artist who has earned regional recognition through consistent performance.

title: The Band Chickamauga
description: North Georgia country group The Band Chickamauga plays Hi-Fi Clyde's on November 13.
body: Traditional country runs the night. The Band Chickamauga comes from Chickamauga, Georgia. The lineup features Morgan Conway, Brownie Hamilton, and Brandon Thomas. Their sound sits in the classic honky-tonk and traditional country tradition. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred people. This is a Friday or Saturday night show for fans of real, old-school country music without modern pop production.

title: The Essentials
description: Chattanooga cover band The Essentials plays Hi-Fi Clyde's on November 6.
body: Classic rock, grunge, Southern rock, and blues fill the set. The Essentials play Chattanooga stages. Readers of the Times Free Press voted them Best of Chattanooga. The band covers a wide range of classic rock material with strong musicianship. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred people. The Essentials have played the local circuit for years and built a consistent following among Chattanooga rock fans.

title: The Hard Luck Band
description: North Georgia rock band Hard Luck plays Hi-Fi Clyde's on November 25.
body: Classic rock and roll runs the night. Hard Luck comes from North Georgia. The band leans on dual guitar harmonies, boogie woogie piano, and a thick rhythm section. Raspy vocals lead the sound. This show lands the night before Thanksgiving. Doors are 21 and up. Cover is $10.

title: Throttle 21
description: Throttle 21 plays classic rock covers at Hi-Fi Clyde's on January 30.
body: Throttle 21 is a Chattanooga power trio. The band plays rock covers from the 70s, 80s, and 90s. Their set pulls from artists like Bryan Adams and Michael Jackson, running hits from multiple genres. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred people and has a dedicated dance floor in front of the stage. This is a high-energy night well suited for a weekend crowd that wants to hear songs they already know.

title: Tucker Underwood Band
description: Chattanooga country artist Tucker Underwood plays Hi-Fi Clyde's on October 30.
body: Modern country and Southern roots shape this set. Tucker Underwood grew up in the South and lives in Chattanooga. Melody and storytelling lead his songs. He plays guitar and writes original material that sits at the intersection of modern country and Americana. The Tucker Underwood Band includes a full band backing him. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred people. Underwood also headlines Barrelhouse Ballroom and plays across the Chattanooga regional circuit.

title: Tucker Underwood
description: Chattanooga country artist Tucker Underwood plays Hi-Fi Clyde's on December 11.
body: Tucker Underwood plays modern country with a Southern rock edge. He lives in Chattanooga and writes songs built on melody and storytelling. His sound draws comparisons to Luke Combs, Koe Wetzel, and HARDY. His songs cover chasing a dream, heartbreak, and Friday nights. Hits 96 named him a rising country act on its Proximity Playlist. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in the South Broad District. This show is 21 and up with a $10 cover. Doors and start time are listed on the venue website.

title: Zech Dallas Band
description: The Zech Dallas Band brings 90s-leaning country to Hi-Fi Clyde's on November 20.
body: A 90s country feel runs through this set. Zechariah Dallas calls Georgia home and writes honest, story-driven songs. He has shared stages with Jackson Dean and other rising country acts. His sound blends traditional production with modern performance energy. Hi-Fi Clyde's is a live music venue on Main Street in Chattanooga's South Broad District. Check the venue website for ticket details and start time. The room holds a few hundred people with a dedicated dance floor. This is a weekend night country show for fans who prefer the classic era of the format.

title: Hutton & Smith Bike Night
description: Bike Night every Tuesday starting at 6pm at Hutton & Smith Brewing Co. on the Southside. Ride in, grab a $3 pint, and hang with the local cycling crowd. Dogs welcome, 21+.
body: Bike Night at Hutton and Smith every Tuesday starting at 6pm. Cyclists roll in, $3 pints are on, and the patio fills up with riders from across the Southside. Discuss routes, talk gear, or just enjoy the beer. Hutton and Smith Brewing is on Williams Street in the Southside neighborhood of Chattanooga. Bike Night draws road cyclists, mountain bikers, and commuters. No ticket required. Walk in with your bike and claim a patio table. The $3 pint special runs through the night. Check the Hutton and Smith social pages for any changes to the weekly schedule.

title: Hutton & Smith Thursday Trivia
description: Free trivia every Thursday at 7pm at Hutton & Smith Brewing Co. on the Southside. Dogs welcome, 21+.
body: Free trivia every Thursday night at 7pm at Hutton and Smith Brewing on the Southside. Bring a crew, grab a pint, and see what you know. Questions run across categories. Hutton and Smith Brewing is on Williams Street in the Southside neighborhood of Chattanooga. The trivia night is free and runs about two hours. No ticket required. Walk in and form a team of up to six. The brewery pours its own craft beers alongside seasonal and limited releases. Check the Hutton and Smith social pages for any themed trivia nights or special events on the weekly schedule.

title: Art After Dark
description: Art After Dark gives teens after-hours art-making at the Downtown Chattanooga Library on October 10.
body: Art After Dark gives teens ages 12 to 18 after-hours access to the Downtown Chattanooga Library on October 10. The night pairs art-making with snacks and a relaxed social atmosphere. The Hunter Museum co-presents this event. Art supplies and materials are provided. The Downtown Chattanooga Library is on Broad Street. This is a free event for teens. No registration is required. The evening is designed to give young people a creative and social outlet in a welcoming space. Check the Hunter Museum or Chattanooga Public Library websites for the specific start time and program details.

title: Art Chatt: Freedom for Sale
description: A free SOBI Connect program at the Hunter Museum on November 5, with dance, music, poetry, and hands-on art responding to Free as they want to be.
body: SOBI Connect, a local creative collective, leads this evening program at the Hunter Museum. The program responds to the exhibition Free as they want to be: Artists Committed to Memory. Dancers, musicians, and poets perform throughout the night. You also make your own art and talk about the show's themes. The event runs from 6 to 8 PM as part of Throwback Thursday. Admission is free.

title: Art+Issues: Free as they want to be Healing Circle
description: This Art+Issues healing circle invites Black men to honest conversation and reflection at the Hunter Museum on December 10.
body: This Art+Issues healing circle invites Black men to a space for honest conversation and reflection on December 10. Anthony M. Wiley Jr. of Welcome to Today leads the gathering. The session draws on the exhibition "Free as they want to be: Artists Committed to Memory." Participants explore freedom, identity, and healing. The program runs from 6 PM to 7 PM and admission is free.

title: Art Wise: Deborah Willis, Ph.D.
description: Dr. Deborah Willis speaks at the Hunter Museum on October 22 about African American photography and the Free As They Want To Be exhibition.
body: Dr. Deborah Willis speaks at the Hunter Museum on October 22 as part of the Art Wise series. She is a MacArthur Fellow and chairs the Department of Photography and Imaging at New York University. She ranks among the nation's leading historians of African American photography. Her talk draws on the exhibition Free As They Want To Be: Artists Committed To Memory. This event is free and open to all.

title: Art Wise: U.S. 250th
description: Art Wise: U.S. 250th is a guided art talk at the Hunter Museum on September 10 marking the nation's 250th year.
body: Art Wise: U.S. 250th takes a closer look at American art on September 10 as the country nears its 250th year. A guide walks you through the work and shares the history behind the pieces. The Hunter Museum holds a significant collection of American art spanning the 18th century to the present. Art Wise programs are designed to be accessible for people with no prior art history background. Check the Hunter Museum website for cost and registration. The museum is on the bluff above the Tennessee River on Bluff View in Chattanooga.

title: Artful Yoga with J Alexander
description: Artful Yoga pairs a guided yoga practice with art at the Hunter Museum on October 18, led by J Alexander.
body: Artful Yoga pairs a guided yoga practice with the art of the Hunter Museum on October 18. J Alexander leads this month's session. The ongoing series connects the museum's collection with local and visiting instructors. All experience levels are welcome. You must bring your own yoga mat. Your $5 donation supports the museum's educational programs. The Hunter Museum is on the bluff above the Tennessee River on Bluff View. Check the museum website for cost and registration.

title: Artful Yoga
description: Artful Yoga pairs an art-inspired yoga practice with the Hunter Museum galleries on November 22, led by Sarah Maginniss.
body: Artful Yoga pairs an art-inspired yoga practice with the Hunter Museum on November 22. Sarah Maginniss leads this session. The practice welcomes yogis of all skill levels. You must bring your own mat. Your $5 donation supports the museum's educational programs. The series connects the museum's collection with a guided movement practice.

title: Black Professionals @ the Hunter
description: Black Professionals @ the Hunter gathers area professionals for culture and connection on October 5.
body: This bimonthly gathering brings area Black professionals together for community, culture, and connection on October 5. The October event honors BettyeLynn Smith and features live performances, food, and time to network. Guests can view the exhibition Free as they want to be and take part in a new career development session led by Unum and the Urban League. An after-hours social follows the main program.

title: Crafts and Coffee
description: An adult art-making afternoon with complimentary coffee or tea at the Hunter Museum on November 6.
body: Crafts and Coffee gives adults ages 18 and up an afternoon of art-making and conversation on November 6. Makers create a hands-on craft while they sip complimentary coffee or tea. The relaxed setting pairs creative work with easy social time in the museum. EBT cardholders enter for free. The program runs from 2 to 4 PM on the first Friday of the month.

title: Crafts & Coffee
description: Crafts & Coffee is a relaxed morning of art making at the Hunter Museum on September 4.
body: Crafts & Coffee gives you a slow morning at the Hunter Museum on September 4. Grab a hot cup, sit down at a table, and make something small with your hands. It is a low-pressure creative morning. The Hunter Museum is on the bluff above the Tennessee River on Bluff View. Crafts & Coffee runs periodically as part of the museum's community programming. Supplies are provided. No art experience is required. Check the Hunter Museum website for cost and registration. The museum is open to the public and admission fees may apply for access to the galleries.

title: Fall Break Camp 2026
description: A five-day art camp for kids ages 6 to 12 at the Hunter Museum over fall break, October 12 to 16.
body: Kids ages 6 to 12 spend fall break making art at the Hunter, October 12 to 16. Each of the five days brings a new project, from sculpture and textiles to prints. Campers explore the museum collection and draw ideas from the current exhibitions. The museum supplies all art materials and snacks. Pack a nut-free lunch and a water bottle each day. Check the museum site for daily times and how to register.

title: Fragments of Becoming: Memory, Loss, and Discovery
description: Fragments of Becoming brings artist Karla Bivens and designer Vee Rhodes to the Hunter Museum on December 3.
body: Fragments of Becoming runs at the Hunter Museum on December 3 from 6 to 7 PM. Artist Karla Bivens and designer Vee Rhodes lead this program. They explore how people and communities hold memory, identity, absence, and belonging. The work shows how we save, break, and rebuild our memories over time. The program responds to the exhibition Free as they want to be: Artists Committed to Memory. Admission is free and open to all.

title: Free as they want to be: Artists Committed to Memory Opening
description: The opening reception for Free as they want to be runs at the Hunter Museum on October 1.
body: This reception opens a traveling exhibition at the Hunter Museum on October 1. The show gathers contemporary artists who use archival material to link history, memory, and freedom. It takes its title from James Baldwin's line that people are as free as they want to be. The evening runs as part of the museum's Throwback Thursday series and welcomes the general public.

title: Layering Meaning in Black Identity with Photographer Woodson Carpenter
description: Photographer Woodson Carpenter leads a hands-on workshop on Black identity at the Hunter Museum on October 8.
body: Photographer and poet Woodson Carpenter leads this hands-on workshop on October 8. It opens with a guided walkthrough of the exhibition Free as they want to be. Each guest brings a personal photograph to swap with another attendee, then responds with paint, pencil, poetry, or prose. Everyone leaves with a piece of collaborative art, and no advance registration is required.

title: Made for You and Me (Hecho Para Ti y Para Mí)
description: A bilingual family art program in Spanish and English at the Hunter Museum on September 24.
body: This program runs in both Spanish and English on September 24. Families look at art together and then make something with their own hands. The Spanish title, Hecho Para Ti y Para Mí, tells you the museum wants every visitor to feel at home. Bring the kids and share the gallery in the language you speak best. Check the museum site for the time and how to sign up.

title: Make and Move Monday
description: Make and Move Monday pairs art projects with movement for families at the Hunter Museum on September 7.
body: Make and Move Monday mixes hands-on art with a little bit of moving around on September 7. Kids build something at the table, then get up and shake out the wiggles. The Hunter Museum hosts this family-friendly Monday program. It is designed for young children with adult accompaniment. Art supplies are provided. The museum is on the bluff above the Tennessee River on Bluff View. Check the Hunter Museum website for cost, registration, and age recommendations. The Make and Move format alternates between seated art activities and movement exercises to keep young participants engaged.

title: Make and Move
description: Make and Move pairs a gallery visit, an art project, and movement for young families at the Hunter Museum on November 2.
body: Make and Move is a monthly program for preschool and homeschool families on November 2. Each session blends a gallery experience, a hands-on art activity, and dance or movement. Kids build something at the table, then get up and move their bodies. One adult joins each family for free, and total family cost stays at or below $25. It runs from 1 to 2 PM.

title: Meyer, Marshall, Meyer
description: A String Theory chamber concert at the Hunter Museum on January 26, featuring Edgar Meyer, George Meyer, and Mike Marshall.
body: String Theory brings three string players to the Hunter Museum on January 26 at 6:30pm. Bassist Edgar Meyer performs with his son George Meyer and mandolin master Mike Marshall. The trio blends classical, bluegrass, and folk in one evening. Their sound crosses genre lines with ease. The concert takes place inside the museum, part of the String Theory chamber music season. Seats are limited for this intimate setting. Check the String Theory or Hunter Museum site for ticket prices and how to buy. Arrive early to find your seat before the music starts.

title: Plants for Healing and the Art of Saya Woolfalk at Crabtree Farms
description: An off-site event on healing plants and the art of Saya Woolfalk at Crabtree Farms on September 5.
body: This one leaves the bluff and heads to Crabtree Farms on September 5. The day links healing plants in the ground to the art of Saya Woolfalk. Spend it outdoors with your hands in the dirt, connecting the garden back to the gallery. Check the museum site for timing and how to sign up. Check the Hunter Museum website for cost and registration. This program runs as an off-site event and requires separate registration from standard museum admission.

title: STEM School Presents
description: STEM School students present their takes on the Hunter Museum collection on October 8.
body: Students from STEM School share their own readings of works in the Hunter's East Wing galleries on October 8. The evening spotlights how young creative and technical minds see the museum collection. Teachers, friends, and families attend free after checking in at Guest Services. The program centers on student presentations rather than a general museum tour. The Hunter Museum is on Bluff View in Chattanooga. Check the museum website for admission details and start time.

title: Style in Free as they want to be
description: An in-gallery fashion show celebrating Black style, set inside the Free as they want to be exhibition at the Hunter Museum on October 29.
body: Chery Jordan and the Runway Rebels bring a fashion show into the galleries on October 29. Models walk a runway that celebrates Black style and creative expression. Music and dance fill the space alongside the looks. The show ties into the exhibition Free as they want to be: Artists Committed to Memory, which traces identity and cultural memory through art. Regular museum admission applies.

title: Sunday Studio
description: Sunday Studio brings drop-in art activities for kids and families to the Hunter Museum on October 4.
body: Sunday Studio fills the Hunter Museum with drop-in art activities on October 4. Kids and families work through hands-on projects led by museum staff, the Downtown Public Library, and the Houston Museum. The program celebrates the new exhibition Free as they want to be and marks the reopening of the Walnut Street Bridge. Outdoor activities run alongside the indoor tables.

title: Throwback Thursday and Saya Woolfalk: A Musical Experience
description: A musical experience tied to the Saya Woolfalk exhibition at the Hunter Museum on September 3.
body: The Hunter turns Throwback Thursday into a music night on September 3. Live sound fills the galleries and ties into the Saya Woolfalk exhibition. Wander with the music as your guide. The Saya Woolfalk exhibition features large-scale installations that blend identity, mythology, and science. Throwback Thursday is a recurring Hunter Museum program that invites visitors into the galleries in a social, after-hours format. Check the Hunter Museum website for admission details and start time. The museum is on the bluff above the Tennessee River on Bluff View in Chattanooga.

title: Throwback Thursday and SOBI Connects
description: Free evening hours at the Hunter Museum on November 5, with a SOBI Connects program responding to the Free as they want to be exhibition.
body: The Hunter opens its doors for free on November 5 from 4 to 8 PM. Visitors explore the permanent collection and the exhibition Free as they want to be: Artists Committed to Memory. SOBI, a collective of local Black creatives, leads a collaborative art program that responds to the show. The Art Bridges Foundation Access for All program sponsors the free admission. Drop in anytime during the evening.

title: Throwback Thursday
description: Throwback Thursday gives free evening access to the Hunter Museum collection and current exhibitions on December 3.
body: Throwback Thursday opens the Hunter Museum for free on December 3 from 4 PM to 8 PM. Visitors can explore the permanent collection at no charge. The current exhibition "Free as they want to be: Artists Committed to Memory" is also open. Cheryl Finley, Ph.D., and Deborah Willis, Ph.D., curated that show. The Art Bridges Foundation supports this program through its Access for All initiative.

title: Vision + Verse: Posing as Past
description: Vision + Verse: Posing as Past brings live performance to the Hunter Museum on November 19.
body: Vision + Verse: Posing as Past runs at the Hunter Museum on November 19 from 6 to 7 PM. Local performers respond to art through dance, poetry, voice, and music. The program connects to the exhibition Free as they want to be: Artists Committed to Memory. Each piece asks how we picture the past and who gets to pose within it. Admission is free and open to everyone.

title: Vision + Verse: Pride, Prejudice, and Black Queer Identity
description: Vision + Verse marks Chattanooga Pride Week with performances at the Hunter Museum on October 15.
body: Vision + Verse marks Chattanooga Pride Week at the Hunter Museum on October 15. Marcus Ellsworth, River Abraxas, Janelle Jezebelle, and other local Black creatives lead performances and discussion. The program ties to the exhibition Free as they want to be, now on view at the museum. It suits anyone who wants to explore Black queer identity through art and open conversation.

title: Winter Break Camp 2026
description: A week-long winter art camp for kids at the Hunter Museum, December 28 to 31.
body: Rising 1st through 6th graders spend winter break making art at the Hunter, December 28 to 31. Campers work with a wide range of art materials and tools across the week. Each day includes hands-on projects and guided walks through the galleries and sculpture garden. Kids draw ideas from the museum collection of American art. Camp runs 9am to 4pm each day. Non-members pay $300 for the week. Passport-level members and above pay $240. Check the museum site for lunch rules and how to register.

title: Wreaths and Art at Walden Peak Farm
description: Wreaths and Art at Walden Peak Farm is an off-site art and craft outing hosted by the Hunter Museum on September 19.
body: Wreaths and Art at Walden Peak Farm takes the museum outdoors on September 19. Spend the day making a wreath and looking at art on the farm. It is a hands-on trip into the countryside. Walden Peak Farm is an agricultural property in the Chattanooga region. The Hunter Museum brings art interpretation to this off-site location. All wreath-making materials are provided. Check the Hunter Museum website for cost and registration. This is a full-day program that combines craft, art appreciation, and a visit to a working farm.

title: Improv Chattanooga Monthly Comedy Show
description: Improv Chattanooga performs their free monthly comedy show at the Chattanooga Public Library downtown branch. Open to all ages.
body: Improv Chattanooga performs their free monthly comedy show at the Chattanooga Public Library's downtown branch. The troupe builds scenes entirely from audience suggestions. No two shows are the same. The Downtown Chattanooga Library is on Broad Street. This is a free, all-ages show that runs about an hour. No ticket required. Improv Chattanooga has performed in Chattanooga for years and runs classes and workshops alongside their monthly public shows. The library format makes it accessible to anyone who wants to see live comedy without a cover charge. Check their social pages for the specific date each month.

title: Improv Chattanooga Presents a Hall-Marquee Christmas Special
description: Improv Chattanooga performs a Hallmark-style improvised holiday romance at the Historic Mars Theatre in LaFayette. All scenes built from audience suggestions.
body: Improv Chattanooga spoofs the Hallmark holiday movie at the Historic Mars Theatre in LaFayette. The troupe builds a full improvised romance from audience suggestions. Expect small-town charm, a snowbound meet-cute, and the usual seasonal tropes played for laughs. Every scene is made up on the spot, so no two shows match. The show starts at 8pm and runs about 90 minutes. Tickets are $14.10 at the door or online.

title: Improv Comedy Show at The Chattery
description: Improv Chattanooga curates a night of improvised comedy at The Chattery. Performers from across the Chattanooga area build scenes from audience ideas. Ages 18 and up.
body: Improv Chattanooga curates a night of improvised comedy at The Chattery. Performers from across the Chattanooga area take the stage. Every scene is built on the spot from audience suggestions, so no two shows repeat. Doors open at 7:00pm and the show starts at 7:30pm. This show is for ages 18 and up. Tickets are $17.85 in advance or at the door.

title: Improvised Holiday Romance
description: Improv Chattanooga builds a full Hallmark-style holiday romance from audience suggestions at the Chattanooga Theatre Centre. One improvised show, all made up on the spot.
body: Improv Chattanooga spoofs the holiday romance movie at the Chattanooga Theatre Centre. The troupe builds a full improvised love story from audience suggestions. Expect a small town, an unexpected romance, and a holiday miracle or two. The show plays as equal parts homage and takedown of the genre. Every scene is made up on the spot, so no two nights are alike. Doors and seating start before the 7:30pm curtain. Tickets begin at $11 online or at the door.

title: Improv Chattanooga Monthly Open House
description: Improv Chattanooga hosts a free monthly open house at the Downtown Library. Adults can drop in to watch, try improv, or just observe. No experience needed.
body: Improv Chattanooga holds a free open house on the first Monday of every month at the Downtown Library. Adults of any age can drop in to watch scenes, participate in warm-up games, or try improv for the first time. No experience or registration is required. The event runs from 6:30 to 8:30 PM. The Downtown Chattanooga Library is on Broad Street. The open house is free and no registration is required. Improv Chattanooga also runs classes and workshops throughout the year.

title: So Funny It's Scary
description: Improv Chattanooga brings a Halloween-themed improv show to The Comedy Catch. All scenes built from live audience suggestions. 18+.
body: Improv Chattanooga brings their Halloween show to The Comedy Catch. The troupe performs a horror-themed set built entirely from audience suggestions. Every scene has a Halloween twist, and nothing is scripted. The Comedy Catch is on Chestnut Street in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue website for ticket details. Improv Chattanooga performs original long-form and short-form improv. The Halloween show is a crowd-favorite annual event. The show is PG-13 to adult-rated depending on audience suggestions. It runs about 90 minutes. Good option for a Halloween week night out.

title: Stand-Up vs. Improv: Lookout Comedy Festival
description: Improv Chattanooga faces off against stand-up comics at Barlery for Night 4 of the 2026 Lookout Comedy Festival.
body: Improv Chattanooga squares off against stand-up comics in a live face-off at Barlery. General seating is first come, first served. Tickets are $10 online. Barlery is a Chattanooga bar that hosts festival events. Check the Lookout Comedy Festival website for ticket details.

title: Daily Programs

body: John A. Patten Community Center runs daily programs at 3202 Kellys Ferry Rd. The center is open Monday through Friday from 11:30am to 8pm. Saturday hours are noon to 4pm. Her sound blends Texas country roots with powerful, soulful vocals. Bella Lam and the Boys open the night. Admission and parking are free for all ages. Family activities start at 4:00 PM. Doors open at 6:00 PM. Bring a chair and enjoy the lake.

title: Captain Mike & The Shipwrecked
description: Captain Mike & The Shipwrecked bring a Jimmy Buffett tribute to Lakeside Live at Chester Frost Park. James Snider opens. Free admission.
body: Captain Mike & The Shipwrecked play a Jimmy Buffett tribute set at Chester Frost Park. The nine-piece band covers Coral Reefer hits, deep cuts, and seafaring stories. James Snider with Fresh Mind opens the night. Admission and parking are free for all ages. Family activities start at 4:00 PM. Doors open at 6:00 PM. Bring a lawn chair or blanket and sit by the lake.

title: Rubiks Groove

body: Rubiks Groove deliver a high-energy 80s and 90s dance party at Chester Frost Park. The band covers dance, rock, pop, and rap hits from the era. Costumed characters lead an interactive, over-the-top show. Admission and parking are free for all ages. Family activities start at 4:00 PM. Doors open at 6:00 PM. Pack a lawn chair or blanket and dance by the lake.

body: Alex Kumin headlined Comedy Central Standup, NBC's "That Clip Show: Holiday Edition," and the Don't Tell Comedy series. Time Out named her a Comics to Watch pick. Check the festival website for ticket details, venue location, and the full festival schedule.

Dellanno performs at clubs and festivals nationally. His style combines storytelling with sharp crowd work. This show is part of the Lookout Comedy Festival, which runs multiple nights across Chattanooga venues in October. title: Don't Tell Comedy

title: Drunk/High/Sober

Cherry St. Tavern hosts this performance. Check the Lookout Comedy Festival website for ticket details and the full festival lineup. The show runs late and is adult-rated.

title: Kyle Kinane: JJ's Bohemia 20th Anniversary Night

body: Kyle Kinane closes the festival with the second of two 20th anniversary shows at JJ's Bohemia. He tells long, dark stories with dry wit. Kinane is considered one of the best working storytellers in stand-up. JJ's Bohemia is a Chattanooga venue celebrating its 20th year with this two-night comedy series as part of the Lookout Comedy Festival. Check the festival website for ticket details.

title: Nerdork feat. Jimmy Sowell

body: Jimmy Sowell goes by Nerdork on stage. His "pullover" sketches pulled hundreds of millions of views on TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube. He brings sharp, dry storytelling to this Lookout Comedy Festival set. Sowell performs at clubs and theaters nationally and has built a large social media following. This show is part of the annual Lookout Comedy Festival, which runs multiple nights across Chattanooga venues. Check the festival website for ticket details and the specific venue for this performance.

title: One-Minute Lightning Round

body: Festival comics each get exactly one minute on stage. The clock is unforgiving and there are no extensions. It runs at 11pm at Cherry St. Tavern, right after the Drunk/High/Sober show. Admission is free. This format puts maximum pressure on each comedian to get to the punchline fast. It is part of the Lookout Comedy Festival late-night programming. title: Shane Torres: JJ's Bohemia 20th Anniversary Night

body: Shane Torres headlines the opening show of the Lookout Comedy Festival's JJ's Bohemia series. He's a New York comic best known for a deadpan Conan bit defending Nickelback. Torres performs at clubs and festivals nationally and has appeared on major late-night programs. His style is dry and precise with a deadpan delivery. title: Lookout Wild Film Festival

title: Ashley McBryde: Into the Wild

title: Black Jacket Symphony: Michael Jackson's Thriller
description: Black Jacket Symphony performs Michael Jackson's Thriller album in its entirety at the Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Auditorium.
body: Black Jacket Symphony performs classic albums live on stage, note for note. The Thriller show re-creates Michael Jackson's 1982 record from first track to last. A live band of eight or more musicians plays every part while the visuals and production match the album's era. After the album portion, the show expands into Michael Jackson hits from the full catalog. Memorial Auditorium seats about 2,000 on McCallie Avenue. Check the venue website for ticket prices. Black Jacket Symphony produces this show alongside other album tribute productions throughout the year.

title: Gabriel Iglesias: The 1976 Tour
description: Stand-up comedian Gabriel Iglesias plays the Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Auditorium in Chattanooga on The 1976 Tour.

title: John Mulaney: Mister Whatever
description: Stand-up comedian John Mulaney brings his Mister Whatever tour to the Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Auditorium in Chattanooga.
body: John Mulaney is a stand-up comedian and former Saturday Night Live writer. He builds long-form stories about everyday situations with precise, observational writing. title: Lindsey Stirling: The Snow Waltz Tour
description: Lindsey Stirling plays her annual holiday show at the Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Auditorium in Chattanooga.

The Snow Waltz Tour is her annual holiday show with original material and seasonal arrangements. Stirling built her following through viral YouTube videos that blended violin performance with cinematic visuals. She has sold millions of records and toured globally. Memorial Auditorium seats about 2,000 on McCallie Avenue. Check the venue website for ticket prices. The concert runs about two hours. title: Nutcracker! Magical Christmas Ballet
description: The Nutcracker! Magical Christmas Ballet brings its holiday tour to the Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Auditorium in Chattanooga.
body: The Nutcracker! Magical Christmas Ballet is a touring holiday production built for families. The show pairs classical ballet with large puppets, soaring birds, and grand stage sets. Dancers from ballet companies around the world perform the full story. Choreographer Viktor Davydiuk directs this North American tour. body: BINGO every Monday at 6:30pm at Oddstory Brewing on Campbell St. Cold beer, free to play, and a crowd that takes the numbers surprisingly seriously. Good way to start the week. title: Oddstory Pub Trivia

body: Pub trivia twice a week at Oddstory on Campbell St, every Tuesday and Thursday at 7:30pm. Grab a pint and bring a crew with a hodgepodge of knowledge. title: 1st Farmers Market of 2027
description: The Ooltewah Farmers Market returns to its regular Thursday schedule on January 7, 2027 after a short holiday break.
body: The Ooltewah Farmers Market reopens for the new year on January 7. The market took a short break over the holidays. It now resumes its regular Thursday afternoon schedule. Winter hours run from 3pm to 5pm. Vendors bring cold-weather produce, preserved goods, meats, eggs, and baked items. The market sits at Ooltewah Nursery on Main Street, east of Chattanooga. This first market of the year is a good time to restock after the holidays. Parking is on site and free. Bring cash for the smaller farm stands. Check the market social pages for the January vendor lineup.

title: Blacksmithing Demonstration
description: Watch local blacksmith John Buff of Refining Fire Forge give a live metalworking demo at the Ooltewah Farmers Market.
body: Raw metal goes in, finished ironwork comes out. John Buff has been forging custom ironwork and knives at Refining Fire Forge in Ooltewah since 2006. He'll work at the anvil during the market so you can watch the whole process. The Ooltewah Farmers Market runs every Thursday afternoon on Hunter Road in Ooltewah. The demonstration is a free market day addition. No separate ticket required. The market runs from 3 to 6pm on Thursdays. Watch Buff shape hot metal with hammer and tong while shopping the regular Thursday vendor lineup.

title: Christmastime at the Market 2026
description: The Ooltewah Farmers Market fills December Thursdays with Christmas foods and local arts and crafts at Ooltewah Nursery.
body: The Ooltewah Farmers Market turns festive through December. Vendors bring Christmas foods, baked goods, and seasonal treats for your holiday table. Local makers set up arts and crafts shows alongside the usual farm stands. The market runs every Thursday afternoon on winter hours. Gates are open from 3pm to 5pm. The market sits at Ooltewah Nursery on Main Street, east of Chattanooga. Shop for handmade gifts and stock up on fresh ingredients in one trip. Parking is on site and free. Bring cash, as some small vendors do not take cards. Check the market social pages for the full December date list and guest vendors.

title: Farmers Market Begins Winter Hours
description: The Ooltewah Farmers Market switches to winter hours on November 5, closing at 5pm each Thursday through March.
body: Starting November 5, the Ooltewah Farmers Market shifts to winter hours. The market closes at 5pm each Thursday instead of the usual 6pm. Hours return to 3-6pm in spring. The Ooltewah Farmers Market runs every Thursday afternoon on Hunter Road in Ooltewah, Tennessee, east of Chattanooga. The winter hour shift reflects shorter daylight as the season changes. The vendor lineup continues through the winter months with seasonal produce and preserved goods. Check the Ooltewah Farmers Market social pages for any additional changes to the schedule during the fall and winter transition.

title: Honey Bee Day
description: The Tennessee Valley Beekeepers Association visits the Ooltewah Farmers Market for a day focused on bees, honey, and local beekeeping.
body: Local beekeepers take over a corner of the market for the day. The Tennessee Valley Beekeepers Association is based in Hamilton County and runs a mentorship program for new beekeepers. They bring displays, honey samples, and education about bee biology, hive management, and local pollinator health. The Ooltewah Farmers Market runs every Thursday afternoon on Hunter Road in Ooltewah. No separate ticket required. The market is free to attend. Check the Ooltewah Farmers Market social pages for the specific time and any special programming scheduled alongside the beekeepers.

title: Thanksgiving Farmers Market
description: A special Tuesday market at Ooltewah Nursery the week of Thanksgiving, stocked with farm-fresh local foods for your holiday table.
body: The market normally runs on Thursdays. Thanksgiving week is the exception. Vendors bring farm fresh meats, produce, pies, breads, and dairy timed for holiday cooking. The market has been running since 2013 and features more than 35 local farms. This is the only Tuesday market all year. Free to attend. The market is free to attend. No ticket required. Check the market social pages for the specific start time and vendor list for the holiday week.

title: Adult Archery: Aim Your Game
description: An indoor archery class for adults at the Philip Grymes Outdoor Chattanooga Center focused on improving aim.
body: Adult Archery: Aim Your Game is an indoor class for grown-up archers. It meets at the Philip Grymes Outdoor Chattanooga Center in Coolidge Park. Instructors help you sharpen stance, aim, and a smooth release. All equipment is provided, so you do not need your own bow. The class welcomes both new shooters and those wanting to improve. Groups stay small for direct coaching. Wear closed-toe shoes and clothing you can move in. Register through Outdoor Chattanooga, since spots fill quickly. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Adult Archery
description: An indoor archery class for adults at the Philip Grymes Outdoor Chattanooga Center in Coolidge Park.
body: Adult Archery is an indoor class built for grown-up archers. It meets at the Philip Grymes Outdoor Chattanooga Center in Coolidge Park. Instructors cover safety, form, and aiming at indoor targets. All equipment is provided, so you do not need your own bow. The class suits both first-time and returning adult shooters. Staff give hands-on coaching in a small group setting. Wear closed-toe shoes and clothes you can move in freely. Register through Outdoor Chattanooga, since spots are limited. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Appalachian Conservation Institute: Learn, Explore, & Hike
description: The Appalachian Conservation Institute leads a guided hike at Little Sequatchie Cove, a protected natural area with conservation education along the trail.
body: The Appalachian Conservation Institute leads this guided hike at Little Sequatchie Cove, a privately held natural area in the Sequatchie Valley. The hike covers about four miles and focuses on forest ecology, land conservation, and the natural history of the cove. The event is free. Outdoor Chattanooga co-presents. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Bring water, hiking boots, and layers. The drive to Little Sequatchie Cove takes about an hour from downtown Chattanooga. This is a rare opportunity to access a privately held conservation site with expert guides leading the way.

title: Beaver Moon Night Hike
description: A guided evening hike under the full Beaver Moon, led in partnership with the Tennessee Aquarium.
body: This guided hike explores the trails by the light of the full Beaver Moon. Outdoor Chattanooga leads the walk with the Tennessee Aquarium. Experts share facts about nocturnal wildlife and local ecosystems. They also explain the meaning behind the Beaver Moon. The program suits adults who want to experience nature at night. Bring water and dress for cool evening weather. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Beginner Hike w/ Rooted Paths
description: Rooted Paths leads a flat, beginner-friendly hike along Big Soddy Creek Gulf on a wide gravel trail suitable for all skill levels.
body: Rooted Paths leads this relaxed hike along Big Soddy Creek Gulf. The route follows a flat, wide gravel trail that works well for new hikers. Guides cover trail basics and introduce participants to the geology and plant life of the area. Outdoor Chattanooga co-presents this event. The hike is free and open to adults. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water. Big Soddy Creek Gulf is in Soddy-Daisy, about 20 minutes north of downtown Chattanooga. The area features a gorge carved by the creek through sedimentary rock.

title: Bike the Boardwalk
description: Outdoor Chattanooga leads a guided 8-mile ride along the South Chickamauga Creek Greenway. The flat, paved route is ideal for casual and beginner cyclists.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga leads this guided 8-mile out-and-back ride on the South Chickamauga Creek Greenway. The trail is paved and flat, making it accessible for most fitness levels. Bikes are provided. The group rides together at a conversational pace. Guides point out natural features along the creek. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Bring water and wear comfortable clothes. The ride starts at Outdoor Chattanooga in Coolidge Park. The South Chickamauga Creek Greenway connects multiple Chattanooga neighborhoods and is one of the most popular cycling routes in the city.

title: Birding by Kayak
description: A guided kayak tour at Hiwassee Wildlife Refuge to view migrating Sandhill Cranes and American White Pelicans.
body: This guided kayak tour explores Hiwassee Wildlife Refuge near Birchwood. Paddlers circle Hiwassee Island to view migrating Sandhill Cranes and American White Pelicans. The early morning trip offers the best chances to see and hear the birds. Outdoor Chattanooga provides all kayak gear and a guide. The tour suits ages 16 and up. Previous kayak experience helps in the colder season but is not required. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Bushcraft Basics: Outdoor Skills for Self-Reliance
description: A hands-on class covering essential wilderness skills and self-reliance in the outdoors with Outdoor Chattanooga.
body: Bushcraft Basics teaches the core skills that build confidence outdoors. The hands-on class covers fire craft, shelter ideas, and basic tool use. Students practice each skill with guidance from Outdoor Chattanooga staff. The goal is simple self-reliance in a backcountry setting. The session suits beginners who want a solid foundation. No prior experience is needed to take part. Dress for the weather and bring water and a snack. Register through Outdoor Chattanooga, since the class size stays small. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Bushcraft Series: Outdoor Camp Cooking - A Taste of Thanksgiving
description: A bushcraft class on campfire cooking with holiday-themed meals in the Outdoor Chattanooga series.
body: This class teaches campfire cooking with a holiday theme. Students learn to prepare Thanksgiving-style meals over an open fire. The program covers safe and efficient ways to cook outdoors. Instructors show techniques for wood fire, charcoal, and camp stove cooking. The class fits people who want practical outdoor skills. No cooking experience is required to join. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Chattanooga Bike Club Monthly Meeting
description: The Chattanooga Bike Club meets the third Monday of each month at Outdoor Chattanooga in Coolidge Park to plan group rides and welcome new cyclists.
body: The Chattanooga Bike Club holds its monthly meeting the third Monday of each month at Outdoor Chattanooga in Coolidge Park. Members plan upcoming group rides, share route recommendations, and welcome cyclists of all skill levels. The club focuses on recreational riding around the Chattanooga region. No membership is required to attend a meeting. Meetings are free and open to the public.

title: Chattanooga Grotto Meeting
description: The Chattanooga Grotto caving club meets the first Monday of each month at Outdoor Chattanooga in Coolidge Park. Newcomers are always welcome.
body: The Chattanooga Grotto is a local caving club that meets the first Monday of each month at Outdoor Chattanooga in Coolidge Park. Members share trip reports, plan upcoming cave visits, and discuss gear. No caving experience is needed to attend. The meeting is free and open to anyone curious about underground exploration. The Grotto is affiliated with the National Speleological Society.

title: Fall Colors Hike: Shakerag Hollow
description: Outdoor Chattanooga leads a guided hike through Shakerag Hollow at Sewanee, one of the most vibrant fall color locations in the Southeast.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga leads this guided hike through Shakerag Hollow at Sewanee, Tennessee. The trail follows a creek through old-growth forest known for exceptional fall color. The hollow is on the campus of the University of the South. The route covers about four miles round trip at a moderate pace. Guides identify trees and explain the geology of the Cumberland Plateau. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Bring water, hiking boots, and layers for changing temperatures. The drive to Sewanee takes about 45 minutes from downtown Chattanooga.

title: Fall Family Canoe
description: Outdoor Chattanooga leads a relaxed family paddle on North Chickamauga Creek. The flat water is beginner-friendly and all canoes and gear are provided.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga leads this relaxed family canoe trip on North Chickamauga Creek. The flat water is ideal for beginners and young paddlers. All equipment is provided. Guides instruct basic paddling strokes and help families navigate the creek. The trip covers a few miles at an easy pace. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Children must be old enough to wear a life jacket correctly. Bring water, sunscreen, and clothes that can get wet. North Chickamauga Creek is a clean, calm waterway that cuts through the northern suburbs of Chattanooga.

title: Full Moon Kayak: Hunter's Moon
description: Paddle Chickamauga Lake by moonlight on this guided evening kayak timed for the Hunter's Moon. Guides lead the group around the lake islands as the moon rises.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga hosts this guided evening paddle timed for the Hunter's Moon on Chickamauga Lake. Participants watch the moon rise over the water while paddling a calm stretch of the lake. All equipment is provided. No prior kayaking experience is required. The paddle runs about two hours at a relaxed pace. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Space is limited. Bring layers and clothes that can get wet. The paddle launches from a site on Chickamauga Lake. Full Moon Kayak events sell out quickly - book your spot as soon as registration opens.

title: Guided Hike at Little Cedar Mountain at Nickajack
description: A guided moderate 4-mile hike on the TVA trail at Little Cedar Mountain near Nickajack Lake.
body: This guided hike covers about 4 miles on the TVA trail at Little Cedar Mountain. The trail borders Nickajack Lake and offers water views. The ground can be uneven with rocks and roots. The route rates as moderate, so hikers need good footwear. A guide leads the group and shares details about the area. Bring water and dress for the weather. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: History by Bike: Chickamauga Battlefield
description: Outdoor Chattanooga leads a free guided bicycle tour through Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park. Instructors provide historical context at key Civil War positions.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga leads this free bicycle tour through Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park. Guides stop at key positions and monuments to explain the two-day battle of September 1863, the bloodiest battle of the Western theater. The route covers about 10 miles on paved park roads. Bikes are provided. No prior cycling fitness is required. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Bring water and dress for the weather. The park is 10 miles south of downtown Chattanooga. The tour runs about three hours total.

title: History by Kayak: Chief Dragging Canoe
description: Paddle the Tennessee River Gorge on a guided kayak tour focused on Chief Dragging Canoe and the Cherokee history of the river corridor.
body: This guided paddle through the Tennessee River Gorge traces the life and history of Chief Dragging Canoe, a Cherokee leader who resisted colonial expansion in the 18th century. Outdoor Chattanooga leads this free kayak tour from Ross's Landing. Guides interpret the history along the waterfront and gorge. All equipment is provided. The paddle runs about two hours at a relaxed pace. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. No prior kayaking experience is required. The tour is free but space is limited. Bring water, sunscreen, and clothes that can get wet.

title: History by Kayak: Downtown Chattanooga
description: Paddle the downtown Chattanooga waterfront on a beginner-friendly guided kayak tour. Guides cover the city's industrial history and riverfront transformation from the water.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga leads this guided paddle along the downtown waterfront at Ross's Landing. Guides trace the city's industrial and military history while the group paddles the Tennessee River shoreline. All equipment is provided. No prior kayaking experience is required. The tour runs about two hours at a relaxed pace. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Space is limited. Bring water, sunscreen, and clothes that can get wet. The tour departs from Ross's Landing and covers the downtown waterfront from the river. This is a popular introductory tour for visitors and longtime residents alike.

title: History by Kayak: Patton Island
description: Paddle to Patton Island on a free guided kayak tour led by National Park educators. The route covers Civil War history tied to Tennessee River crossings.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga and the Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park co-lead this free guided kayak tour to Patton Island in the Tennessee River. Guides explain the island's Civil War history during the paddle. All equipment is provided. No prior paddling experience is required. The tour runs about two hours at a relaxed pace. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Space is limited. Bring water, sunscreen, and clothes that can get wet. The launch point is at Ross's Landing downtown. This is one of Outdoor Chattanooga's most popular history-by-water programs.

title: History Walk at South Chickamauga Creek Greenway
description: A guided 2-mile history walk along South Chickamauga Creek Greenway with historian Greg Grant.
body: Historian Greg Grant leads this easy 2-mile walk along South Chickamauga Creek Greenway. The route passes five Civil War-era railroad bridges. Grant explains how these railroads shaped the war and Chattanooga's growth as a transportation hub. The walk blends outdoor exercise with local history. Bring comfortable walking shoes and water. A shuttle supports the route. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Intro to Mountain Biking: FUNdamentals
description: Outdoor Chattanooga's FUNdamentals class teaches new riders balance, braking, and bike control in a controlled field environment.
body: This FUNdamentals class introduces new riders to mountain biking in a controlled field environment. Instructors cover balance, braking, shifting gears, and cornering before guiding the group onto a beginner trail. Bikes and helmets are provided by Outdoor Chattanooga. No prior mountain biking experience is needed. The class runs about two hours at Enterprise South Nature Park. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Space is limited and sessions fill quickly. Bring water and wear closed-toe shoes. This class is the foundation for the Trail Quest program and other beginner cycling events.

title: Learn and Play Disc Golf
description: Try disc golf for the first time with Outdoor Chattanooga. Instructors cover grip, stance, and throwing technique before leading a short beginner-friendly round.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga runs this beginner disc golf session at a local Chattanooga course. Instructors cover grip, stance, and throwing form before the group plays a few holes together. Equipment is provided for participants who do not own discs. The session runs about two hours. No prior disc golf experience is needed. The class introduces the sport in a relaxed, low-pressure format. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Bring water and wear comfortable shoes. The course used for this session varies - check the registration page for the specific location.

title: Learn to Mountain Bike: FUNdamentals
description: Outdoor Chattanooga runs an evening beginner mountain biking class on a grass field at Coolidge Park. Loaner bikes and helmets are available.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga's beginner mountain biking class uses progressive drills on a flat grass field. Instructors cover braking technique, body position, and turning fundamentals before riders move to a beginner trail loop. Bikes and helmets are provided. The class runs about two hours. No prior mountain biking experience is needed. This session meets at Enterprise South Nature Park. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Space fills fast - book early. Bring water and wear closed-toe shoes. The skills covered transfer directly to any trail in the region.

title: Learn to Mountain Bike: FUNdamentals
description: Outdoor Chattanooga teaches beginner mountain bike skills through progressive drills on a flat grass field at Coolidge Park. Bikes and helmets available to borrow.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga's beginner mountain biking class runs progressive drills on a flat grass field. Instructors focus on body position, braking, and turning before guiding the group to a beginner trail loop. Bikes and helmets are provided. No prior experience is needed. This October 20 session runs about two hours at Enterprise South Nature Park. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Space is limited - register early. Bring water and closed-toe shoes. This is the third of four FUNdamentals sessions offered in October as part of the fall beginner mountain biking series.

title: Learn to Mountain Bike: FUNdamentals
description: A late-October beginner mountain biking class from Outdoor Chattanooga. The session covers core skills on a grass field with loaner bikes and helmets available.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga's beginner mountain biking series continues through late October. This session uses a progressive drill format on a flat grass field, then transitions to a beginner trail loop. Bikes and helmets are provided. Instructors focus on body position, braking, and turning control. No prior experience is required. This late October session is one of the final opportunities in the fall program. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Space is limited. Bring water and closed-toe shoes. Enterprise South Nature Park is about 15 minutes from downtown Chattanooga.

title: Learn to Mountain Bike: FUNdamentals
description: Outdoor Chattanooga teaches beginner mountain biking skills on a controlled grass field at Coolidge Park. Loaner bikes and helmets are available.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga's beginner mountain biking class covers core skills on a flat grass field. Instructors use progressive drills to teach body position, braking, and balance before guiding riders onto a beginner trail. Bikes and helmets are provided. No prior experience is required. This October 6 session runs about two hours at Enterprise South Nature Park. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. The class is part of a recurring beginner series that runs through fall. Space is limited. Bring water and closed-toe shoes.

title: Learn to Ride a Bike: Holiday Edition
description: A single-session holiday bike class for adults and children learning to ride or refreshing rusty skills.
body: This holiday edition of Learn to Ride a Bike runs over winter break. The class helps adults and children ride a bicycle in one session. Instructors start with balance and work up to pedaling and steering. Bikes are provided in several sizes, so you can come empty-handed. No experience is assumed, and the class builds from zero. The session takes place on flat, open ground. Two time slots run that day at 10:30 AM and 12:00 PM. Wear comfortable clothes and closed-toe shoes, and register early. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Learn to Ride a Bike
description: Outdoor Chattanooga offers a single-session bike riding class for adults and children who are learning for the first time or want a refresher.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga's bike riding class is for adults and children who have never learned or want a refresher. Instructors start with balance and work up to pedaling and steering on flat ground. Bikes are provided in multiple sizes. No experience is assumed - the class builds from zero. The session runs about 90 minutes. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Bring comfortable clothes and closed-toe shoes. The class takes place in a flat, open area. This is one of Outdoor Chattanooga's most inclusive programs and fills quickly. Book your spot as soon as registration opens.

title: National Take a Hike Day: Guided Hike at Walden's Ridge
description: A guided hike at Walden's Ridge Park near Red Bank to mark National Take a Hike Day.
body: This guided hike marks National Take a Hike Day. The group walks the trails at Walden's Ridge Park, a 200-acre park near Red Bank. A guide leads the route and points out features along the way. The hike suits people who want a relaxed morning outdoors. Bring water and wear sturdy shoes. The pace stays comfortable for most fitness levels. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: National Take a Hike Day
description: Celebrate National Take a Hike Day with a hike led by the Director of Outdoor Chattanooga.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga marks National Take a Hike Day with a group hike led by the organization's Director. The outing celebrates the region's trails and the simple reward of time outside. The trail location is set closer to the date. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water for the walk. Check the Outdoor Chattanooga website for the meeting spot and start time.

title: ODDtober Night Hike w/ Tennessee Aquarium
description: Outdoor Chattanooga and the Tennessee Aquarium lead a guided after-dark nature walk exploring nocturnal ecology and wildlife in the Chattanooga area.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga and the Tennessee Aquarium co-lead this guided night hike. A naturalist walks the group through nocturnal animal behavior and helps participants spot owls, bats, and insects active after dark. The hike covers a local trail at an easy pace. Flashlights or headlamps are recommended. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. The specific trail is shared in the registration confirmation. The event is part of the annual ODDtober series. It is free or low cost. This is a popular fall program - register early. The hike works well for families with older children.

title: Sierra Club Meeting - Cherokee Chapter of TN
description: The Cherokee Chapter of the Tennessee Sierra Club holds its monthly meeting at Outdoor Chattanooga to plan outings and discuss conservation. Open to the public.
body: The Cherokee Chapter of the Tennessee Sierra Club meets monthly at Outdoor Chattanooga in Coolidge Park. Members plan upcoming outings, discuss local conservation issues, and hear from guest speakers on environmental topics. The meeting is free and open to the public. No membership is required to attend. The chapter organizes regular hikes, paddles, and advocacy efforts in the Chattanooga region. Meetings typically run about 90 minutes. Check the Cherokee Chapter's website for the specific agenda and any scheduled speakers. New members and curious newcomers are welcome.

title: Silver Adventures: Art in the Outdoors - Plein Air
description: Outdoor Chattanooga's Silver Adventures program hosts a plein air painting session at Coolidge Park for adults 60 and older. No formal art training needed.
body: Silver Adventures is Outdoor Chattanooga's program for adults 60 and older. This plein air session invites participants to sketch or paint outdoors at a local natural area. Supplies are provided. No prior art experience is needed. The session is relaxed and focused on the experience of making something in nature. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. The specific site is shared in the registration confirmation. The Silver Adventures program runs monthly throughout the year with activities tailored to older adults who want to stay active outdoors.

title: Silver Adventures: History by Bike
description: A free guided bicycle ride for adults 50 and older through historic downtown Chickamauga, Georgia.
body: This free program serves adults 50 and older. Riders follow a guide through downtown Chickamauga on bicycles. The route covers local history at an easy pace. Outdoor Chattanooga provides bikes and helmets. The ride suits people who want gentle exercise and local stories. Previous cycling experience helps but is not required. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Silver Adventures: Winter Waterfall Hike – Blowing Wind Falls
description: A guided winter hike for adults 50 and up to Blowing Wind Falls on the Ritchie Hollow Trail near Chattanooga.
body: Silver Adventures serves adults aged 50 and above. This winter trip visits Blowing Wind Falls, a 30-foot cascade in the Tennessee River Gorge. Hikers follow the Ritchie Hollow Trail, which climbs through mature hardwood forest. The route passes creek crossings and historic moonshine stills. Winter brings stronger water flow over the falls. The hike runs about 2.8 miles round trip with steady elevation gain. An Outdoor Chattanooga guide leads the group at a steady pace. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water and a snack. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Toddler Treks: Renaissance Park
description: A parent and child nature program at Renaissance Park that explores how plants and animals adapt to winter.
body: Toddler Treks brings young children and their grownups outdoors at Renaissance Park. This session looks at winter adaptations in local plants and animals. Guides lead short walks, simple games, and hands-on nature play. The program builds early curiosity about the natural world. It suits toddlers and preschool-age children with a parent or caregiver. The pace stays slow and the trails stay flat. Dress for cool weather and wear shoes that can get muddy. Space is limited, so register early through Outdoor Chattanooga. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Toddler Treks: South Chatt
description: A guided nature walk for toddlers and their caregivers in South Chattanooga.
body: This program pairs young children with a parent or caregiver for a short nature walk. Guides lead easy activities that help toddlers explore the outdoors. The walk moves at a slow pace built for small legs. Children learn about plants, bugs, and the sights along the trail. The program builds early comfort with nature and outdoor play. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Toddler Treks: Sterchi Farm
description: Toddler Treks visits Sterchi Farm for a short nature walk and hands-on outdoor exploration. Designed for children ages 1-5 with a parent or caregiver.
body: Toddler Treks is Outdoor Chattanooga's nature series for families with young children. This session visits Sterchi Farm for a guided walk suited to small legs and short attention spans. Staff lead the group through the farm property, introducing basic animal and plant identification along the way. The event is free or low cost. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Children must be accompanied by an adult. Bring snacks, water, and comfortable clothes. Sterchi Farm is located in the North Chattanooga area. The Toddler Treks series runs monthly and features different outdoor sites across the region.

title: Trail Quest: Intro to Mountain Biking
description: Trail Quest is Outdoor Chattanooga's beginner mountain biking program. Classes start on a grass field and build toward light trail riding over multiple sessions.
body: Trail Quest is Outdoor Chattanooga's multi-session beginner mountain biking program. Classes begin on a grass field where instructors teach balance, braking, and turning before moving to packed dirt trails. This October 11 session is part of the ongoing fall program at Enterprise South Nature Park. Bikes and helmets are provided. No prior experience is needed. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Space fills quickly. Bring water and closed-toe shoes. The program builds rider confidence across multiple sessions and prepares participants for independent trail use in the park.

title: Trail Quest: Intro to Mountain Biking
description: Trail Quest is Outdoor Chattanooga's beginner mountain biking program. Saturday sessions build field fundamentals and prepare riders for light trail riding.
body: Trail Quest is Outdoor Chattanooga's recurring beginner mountain biking program running through the fall. This Saturday session at Enterprise South Nature Park starts on a grass field and moves to a beginner trail loop. Bikes and helmets are provided. Instructors teach balance, braking, and body position from the start. No prior experience is needed. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. The program is part of a multi-session series that builds riding skills over time. Space fills fast. Bring water and closed-toe shoes.

title: Trail Quest: Intro to Mountain Biking
description: Trail Quest is Outdoor Chattanooga's beginner mountain biking program. Classes start on a grass field and build toward light trail riding.
body: Trail Quest is Outdoor Chattanooga's beginner mountain biking program. Classes start on a grass field where instructors teach balance, braking, and turning before moving to packed dirt trails. The program is designed for people with little or no mountain biking experience. Outdoor Chattanooga provides bikes and helmets. The program runs at Enterprise South Nature Park. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. Space is limited and sessions fill early. Bring water and closed-toe shoes. The full multi-week program builds to independent trail riding.

title: Try Archery!
description: A free indoor archery class at the Philip Grymes Outdoor Chattanooga Center in Coolidge Park for new archers.
body: Try Archery is a free indoor class for people new to the sport. It runs at the Philip Grymes Outdoor Chattanooga Center in Coolidge Park. Instructors cover safety, stance, and how to aim and release. All equipment is provided, so no gear is needed. The class welcomes beginners of all ages and skill levels. Staff keep groups small for hands-on help. Wear closed-toe shoes and clothing you can move in. This session fills fast, so sign up as soon as registration opens. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Under the Wolf Moon: Red Wolves & Mindful Trails
description: A guided winter program pairing a mindful trail walk with lessons about red wolves under the January Wolf Moon.
body: This winter program ties the January full moon to a guided trail walk. The January moon is known as the Wolf Moon, named for howling wolves in winter. The outing pairs a mindful walk with lessons about red wolves. Guides share facts about this rare and endangered species. The slow pace gives time to notice the quiet winter landscape. The program suits adults and older children who enjoy nature walks. Dress warmly and wear sturdy shoes for the trail. Register through Outdoor Chattanooga ahead of time. Registration opens three weeks prior and closes two days before the event.

title: Volunteer Info Session
description: Outdoor Chattanooga hosts a volunteer info session at its Coolidge Park center. Staff explain how to get involved with upcoming outdoor programs.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga hosts this info session for new and returning volunteers. Staff walk through upcoming volunteer opportunities and explain how to sign up. Roles range from supporting paddle trips to helping with guided hikes and community events. The session is free and runs at the Coolidge Park center. New volunteers learn what each role involves before they commit. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website.

title: Volunteer Orientation
description: Outdoor Chattanooga's volunteer orientation covers how to get involved with outdoor programs at Coolidge Park. Attendance is required before joining any volunteer crew.
body: Outdoor Chattanooga runs this orientation for anyone interested in volunteering with their programs. Staff walk through the types of volunteer roles available, the commitment expected, and how to sign up for specific events. The orientation takes about an hour at the Outdoor Chattanooga facility in Coolidge Park. Volunteers support everything from cleanup events to instructional programs. No outdoor experience is required for most roles. Register through the Outdoor Chattanooga website. This is a free orientation open to adults. It is the required first step before participating as a volunteer on any Outdoor Chattanooga event.

title: Winter Workshop: Fizz & Ferment: A Kombucha Workshop
description: A hands-on fermentation workshop with Matt Cone of Chattanooga Culture covering kombucha and lacto-fermented foods.
body: This hands-on workshop introduces the basics of home fermentation. Matt Cone of Chattanooga Culture leads the session. You will learn how to brew kombucha using simple, traditional methods. The class also covers lacto-fermented foods you can make at home. Cone shares the steps, tools, and tips for safe fermenting. The workshop suits beginners who want to start brewing their own drinks.
