description: Jason Lyles plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Saturday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: Jason Lyles is a Chattanooga singer-songwriter. He blends powerpop, Americana, and roots rock. His sound mixes The Cars pop hooks with Jason Isbell twang. Strong vocals and rhythmic acoustic guitar drive his set. He also slips in 80s pop and 90s alt-rock covers. The show starts at 7:30 PM by the river. Puckett's runs music every Friday and Saturday. The door stays free and tips go to the players.

title: Jessamyn Rains
description: Jessamyn Rains plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Saturday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: Jessamyn Rains plays Puckett's this Saturday. She is a Chattanooga singer-songwriter who calls her style folk impressionism. Her writing draws on Joni Mitchell, Sara Watkins, and John Denver. She sings, plays, and layers quiet, atmospheric songs. The set starts at 7:30 PM by the river. Puckett's charges no cover, so bring cash for the tip jar. No separate ticket required. Walk in or book a table through the Puckett's website on Aquarium Way in downtown Chattanooga.

title: Jimmy Galloway
description: Jimmy Galloway plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Friday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: Jimmy Galloway is a multi-instrumentalist who moves easily between acoustic and electric music. He draws on Celtic, folk, and jazz styles across a single set. The show starts at 7:30 PM. Puckett's sits on Aquarium Way, near the water. Order supper and stay for the music. No cover runs at the door. Tips feed the band. No separate ticket required. Walk in or book a table through the Puckett's website on Aquarium Way in downtown Chattanooga.

title: Josh Driver & Kylan Rodgers
description: Josh Driver & Kylan Rodgers plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Saturday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: Josh Driver and Kylan Rodgers split the stage at Puckett's on Saturday. Their set starts at 7:30 PM by the river. Puckett's serves Southern food and hosts live music on the weekends on Aquarium Way. Driver is a Chattanooga singer-songwriter who tells honest stories through acoustic folk and country. Rodgers is a Chattanooga-area guitarist and vocalist. The two artists share an audience and play well together as an evening bill. The room is casual and the stage is close to the tables. No separate ticket required - walk in and find a seat.

title: Josh Driver
description: Josh Driver plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Saturday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: Josh Driver takes the Puckett's stage this Saturday. He is a Chattanooga singer-songwriter who tells honest stories through his songs. His sound pulls from rock and country legends. He plays a solo set starting at 7:30 PM near the riverfront. Puckett's serves dinner all night. The door stays free, so bring cash for the tip jar. No separate ticket required. Walk in or book a table through the Puckett's website on Aquarium Way in downtown Chattanooga.

title: Justin & Tab
description: Justin & Tab plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Saturday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: Justin and Tab trade songs at Puckett's on Saturday. Music starts at 7:30 PM, two blocks from the Tennessee Aquarium. Great Southern food runs all night. Justin and Tab are a Chattanooga-area acoustic duo who cover classic rock, pop, and country favorites. Their easy, conversational style fits the restaurant setting well. The room stays full through the last song. Puckett's is on Aquarium Way in downtown Chattanooga. No separate ticket required - walk in and find a table or book a reservation through the Puckett's website.

title: Lucie Tiger
description: Lucie Tiger plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Saturday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: Lucie Tiger plays a Saturday set at Puckett's downtown. Music starts at 7:30 PM. The restaurant sits on Aquarium Way near the river. Tiger is a Chattanooga-area singer-songwriter who blends pop, folk, and Americana into an intimate acoustic style. Her sets feature original material and carefully chosen covers. The restaurant serves Southern food through the whole evening. Puckett's is on Aquarium Way in downtown Chattanooga, two blocks from the Tennessee Aquarium. No separate ticket required. Walk in and find a table or book through the Puckett's website.

title: Nettie & the Delta Boy
description: Nettie & the Delta Boy plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Friday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: Nettie and the Delta Boy bring roots music to Puckett's on Friday. The set opens at 7:30 PM. The restaurant sits on Aquarium Way downtown. Nettie and the Delta Boy are a Chattanooga-area duo who blend folk, blues, and country into a warm acoustic sound. Their sets mix originals with well-chosen covers. The restaurant serves Southern food through the evening. Puckett's is on Aquarium Way, steps from the Tennessee Aquarium. No separate ticket required. Walk in and find a table or book a reservation through the Puckett's website.

title: Pan-O-Ram Club
description: Pan-O-Ram Club plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Saturday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: Pan-O-Ram Club takes Puckett's on Saturday night. The set begins at 7:30 PM, two blocks from the aquarium. The kitchen serves Southern food all evening. Pan-O-Ram Club is a Chattanooga-area band that plays acoustic and electric pop, rock, and country. The group has played Chattanooga stages for years. Their sets move between original material and crowd-friendly covers. Puckett's is on Aquarium Way in downtown Chattanooga. No separate ticket required. Walk in and find a table or book a reservation through the Puckett's website.

title: Richard Daigle
description: Richard Daigle plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Saturday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: Saturday night at Puckett's carries a full live set. Richard Daigle plays at 7:30 PM downtown. The weekend crowd gathers early on Aquarium Way. Daigle is a Chattanooga-area musician who covers classic rock, country, and acoustic pop. His sets work well in a seated restaurant setting. The room stays relaxed but engaged. Puckett's serves Southern comfort food through the evening on Aquarium Way, two blocks from the Tennessee Aquarium. No separate ticket required. Walk in and find a table or book through the Puckett's website.

title: The Briars
description: The Briars plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Saturday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: The Briars fill Puckett's with live music on Saturday night. Music starts at 7:30 PM downtown. The weekend crowd packs the tables early on Aquarium Way. The Briars are a Chattanooga-area roots and Americana band known for high energy live performances. Their sets draw from country, bluegrass, and folk-rock. The restaurant serves Southern comfort food through the whole set. Puckett's is two blocks from the Tennessee Aquarium. No separate ticket required. Walk in or book a table through the Puckett's website. The room stays full through the last song.

title: The Tennessee Warblers
description: The Tennessee Warblers plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Friday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: The Tennessee Warblers land at Puckett's on Friday night. Their set starts at 7:30 PM by the river. Puckett's serves Southern food through the whole evening. The Tennessee Warblers are a Chattanooga-area roots and Americana duo known for vocal harmonies and acoustic instrumentation. Their sets draw from folk, bluegrass, and original Americana. The restaurant is on Aquarium Way in downtown Chattanooga, steps from the Tennessee Aquarium. No separate ticket required - walk in and find a table or book a reservation through the Puckett's website.

title: Tigris
description: Tigris plays live at Puckett's Restaurant in downtown Chattanooga on Friday. The show starts at 7:30 PM with no cover.
body: Tigris is a Chattanooga singer-songwriter with a fast-paced, bluesy sound. Folk and country artists shape the bouncy, upbeat songs. The set opens at 7:30 PM. Puckett's sits on Aquarium Way, steps from the water. Order supper and stay for the show. No cover runs at the door. Tips feed the band. No separate ticket required. Walk in or book a table through the Puckett's website on Aquarium Way in downtown Chattanooga.

title: A Night of Poems, Songs, and Conversation with Laura Candler and Alva Leigh
description: Sewanee poet Laura Candler and Chattanooga singer-songwriter Alva Leigh share original work in an intimate evening of poems, songs, and conversation at the Reading Room.
body: Two Chattanooga artists share a stage for an evening of original work. Laura Candler reads from Common Name, her 2026 Poets Corner Chapbook Contest winner, with poems published in Gulf Coast, SWING, and Variant Literature. Alva Leigh plays songs from Wilderness, her album about motherhood and identity made after years performing in London with Lewis and Leigh. The conversation between sets is part of the format. The Reading Room fits around 40 people. Get there early.

title: Ambient Night
description: Ambient Night at the Reading Room features slow, texture-driven music in an intimate bookshop-bar setting in Chattanooga.
body: Slow, texture-driven music fills the Reading Room once a month for Ambient Night. The format shifts. Some evenings bring a solo performer playing live drones, loops, or slow instrumentals. Other nights lean toward curated listening sets. The room is small and warmly lit, with used books on the walls. Music and bookshelves work well together. Doors open at 7pm, music at 7:30.

title: Eastgate Library Presents Book Chatt Evenings - Drawing Room Comedies Genre Talk
description: Eastgate Library leads a genre discussion on drawing room comedies at the Reading Room in Chattanooga.
body: Eastgate Library brings its Book Chatt Evenings series to the Reading Room for a talk on drawing room comedies. The genre covers witty, dialogue driven fiction and theater set in upper class domestic spaces. Oscar Wilde and Noel Coward wrote the best known examples. The session is conversational and open to everyone. No prior reading is required. Come with thoughts on the form or just come curious. Free, about 90 minutes.

title: Reading Room Thanksgiving Potluck
description: The Reading Room hosts a Thanksgiving potluck the day before the holiday, open to all.
body: The Reading Room is hosting a Thanksgiving potluck the day before the holiday. Bring a dish to share with neighbors and regulars. The bar will be open. It is a low key afternoon with no agenda. The shop has a gift for this kind of gathering: good books nearby, drinks at the bar, and no pressure to leave early. You do not need to bring a dish to attend.

title: Sip with the Stars and the Barnard Astrological Society
description: The Barnard Astronomical Society hosts a casual evening of stargazing conversation at the Reading Room bar in Chattanooga.
body: Chattanooga's amateur astronomy club takes over the bar for an evening. The Barnard Astronomical Society normally meets at UTC's Clarence T. Jones Observatory near Brainerd Road. At the Reading Room, the format goes casual. Expect conversations about recent sky observations, upcoming celestial events, and the basics of backyard astronomy. No telescope or prior experience is needed. Free and open to newcomers and longtime stargazers alike.

title: Small Business Saturday & Scavenger Hunt in the Stacks
description: The Reading Room celebrates Small Business Saturday with a scavenger hunt through its used book collection in Chattanooga.
body: Small Business Saturday falls on November 28, the first Saturday after Thanksgiving. The Reading Room celebrates with a scavenger hunt through its used book stacks. Players search for titles matching a list of clues. It is a low pressure, all ages activity. The shop carries fiction, nonfiction, and local interest books. You will likely walk out with something you were not looking for. Stop in, hunt for some titles, and support a local bookshop.

title: Holidays at Ruby Falls
description: Holidays at Ruby Falls runs November 27 through December 24 on Lookout Mountain. The cave waterfall tours keep running through the season alongside holiday lights, a Forest of Wishes, and Santa visits on select days.
body: The cave waterfall tours keep running through the holiday season at Ruby Falls. Outside, the castle and plaza fill with lights and decorations. Visitors can add a handwritten wish to the Forest of Wishes. Santa visits on select days. The Castle Cafe stays open for food, local craft beer, and hot cocoa by the fireplace. Cave adventure tickets ($19.95 to $42.95) are required for the underground waterfall tour and must be bought online. The plaza, castle, and cafe are free to visit without a ticket. Book ahead as availability fills up during peak weekends.

title: Autumn Equinox Event for Members
description: A members-only evening at Reflection Riding to mark the autumn equinox with native plants, tea, and yoga.
body: Members gather to mark the turn of the season. The evening brings native plant activities, herbal teas, and a guided yoga session on the grounds of Reflection Riding. This annual event is for current members of the arboretum and nature center. It runs at dusk on the fall equinox. Staff lead participants through the garden and forest with seasonal interpretive content. The yoga session is gentle and suited to all experience levels. Bring a mat and layers. Check the Reflection Riding website for event details and member sign-up. Not yet a member - membership starts at a low annual fee.

title: Campfire Concert: Barefoot Nellie
description: An outdoor evening concert at Reflection Riding featuring Barefoot Nellie.
body: Spread a blanket and settle in for live music under the open sky. Barefoot Nellie plays as the sun drops behind the ridge at Reflection Riding. Barefoot Nellie is a Southern folk and roots music project known for warm harmonies and acoustic arrangements. The campfire concert series runs outdoors at the nature center on Garden Road. Admission is charged - check the Reflection Riding website for ticket details. Food and drinks are available on site. Bring layers for the evening temperatures. The nature center grounds provide a natural amphitheater setting with the forest as the backdrop.

title: Campfire Concert: Donna the Buffalo
description: An outdoor evening concert at Reflection Riding featuring Donna the Buffalo.
body: Donna the Buffalo brings their roots sound to the grounds. Spread a blanket and enjoy live music as the evening cools. Food and drinks available on site. Donna the Buffalo is a New York-based roots, reggae, and rock band that has toured nationally for over 30 years. They are known for danceable rhythms, positive lyrics, and a loyal fan community called the Herd. The campfire concert series at Reflection Riding runs outdoors on the nature center grounds. Admission is charged - check the website for ticket details. The nature center is on Garden Road near Lookout Mountain.

title: Campfire Concert: Jon Stickley Trio
description: An outdoor evening concert at Reflection Riding featuring the Jon Stickley Trio.
body: The Jon Stickley Trio plays fast, sharp acoustic music under the open sky. Bring a chair and settle in for the evening. Jon Stickley is an Asheville-based flatpick guitarist who leads a trio with violin and drums. Their music blends bluegrass, jazz, and world music at high speed. They have toured nationally and played major acoustic music festivals. The campfire concert series at Reflection Riding runs outdoors on the nature center grounds. Admission is charged - check the website for ticket details. Food and drinks are available on site. The nature center is on Garden Road.

title: Campfire Concert: Kasvot Chätt
description: An outdoor evening concert at Reflection Riding featuring Kasvot Chätt.
body: Close out the concert season with Kasvot Chätt. Bring a blanket and enjoy live music in the cool night air. Food and drinks available on site. Kasvot Chätt is a Chattanooga-based electronic and experimental music duo. Their sound blends ambient textures with live instrumentation and electronic production. The campfire concert series at Reflection Riding runs outdoors on the grounds of the nature center. Admission is charged - check the Reflection Riding website for ticket details. The nature center is on Garden Road near the base of Lookout Mountain.

title: Campfire Concert: Yarn
description: An outdoor evening concert at Reflection Riding featuring the band Yarn.
body: Bring a chair and enjoy live music in the open air. Yarn plays deep into the evening on the grounds at Reflection Riding. Yarn is an Americana and roots band from the Northeast with a loyal touring following. They blend acoustic instruments with folk and rock influences and are known for energetic, fan-driven live shows. The campfire concert series runs outdoors at the Reflection Riding nature center on Garden Road. Admission is charged - check the website for ticket details. Food and drinks are available. Bring layers for the evening temperatures.

title: Crabtree Farms Fall Plant Sale
description: A weekend fall plant sale at Reflection Riding with native plants from Crabtree Farms.
body: Stock up on native plants for the fall planting season. Crabtree Farms brings a big selection across the whole weekend. Shoppers find perennials, shrubs, and grasses suited to the Chattanooga region at the Reflection Riding fall plant sale. Staff from both organizations help you match plants to your site conditions and sun exposure. The plant sale runs at Reflection Riding Arboretum on Garden Road. Admission to the grounds is free. Plants are priced individually. Fall is an ideal time to plant in the Southeast - root systems establish before winter without the stress of summer heat.

title: Fall Celebration Event for Members
description: A members-only fall celebration at Reflection Riding with nature crafts, herbal tea, and guided sunset yoga.
body: Reflection Riding invites its members to mark the season at this fall celebration. The day blends hands-on nature crafts with warm herbal tea. A guided sunset yoga session closes the hours on the grounds. This event is open to members only, so renew or sign up before you come.

title: Free Tree ReLeaf
description: A free tree giveaway at Reflection Riding, with up to two trees per household.
body: Pick up free trees to plant in your own yard. City residents can take home up to two trees per household. Staff help you choose the right species for your site conditions. Reflection Riding hosts this giveaway as part of its urban reforestation efforts. Trees are native species suited to the Chattanooga region. Supplies are limited and distributed on a first-come basis. Check the Reflection Riding website for the species available and pickup details. The nature center is on Garden Road at the base of Lookout Mountain. This event typically runs one morning and ends when supplies are gone.

title: Give Back Night at Oddstory Central
description: A fundraising night for Reflection Riding at Oddstory Brewing's Central taproom.
body: Grab a beer and put it toward a good cause. Oddstory's Central taproom hosts the night and gives back a share of sales to Reflection Riding Arboretum and Nature Center. The nature center relies on fundraising and community support to maintain its trails, wildlife habitats, and educational programs. This is a low-key evening out that benefits a Chattanooga institution. Oddstory Central is on McCallie Avenue. No ticket required - just show up and order a pint. The give-back percentage is noted on the Reflection Riding website.

title: Green|Spaces Lunch and Learn
description: A midday session at Reflection Riding about its mission and sustainability work, with Green|Spaces.
body: Bring your lunch and learn how Reflection Riding cares for its land. Staff share the site's mission and the daily work behind maintaining the arboretum, wildlife habitats, and educational programs. Green|Spaces leads this midday session on sustainable land stewardship. The event is free or low cost. Check the Reflection Riding website for registration details. The nature center is located on Garden Road at the base of Lookout Mountain. This is a good event for anyone curious about native plant conservation, wildlife corridors, or the practical work of running a nature center in an urban setting.

title: Hard of Hearing Night: Owl Odyssey
description: An evening Owl Odyssey program at Reflection Riding with ASL interpretation, open to all.
body: This evening owl program includes ASL interpretation and welcomes everyone. Learn how barn owls hunt in the dark and raise their young in the hollow trees of Reflection Riding. Staff bring live owls to the program. The ASL interpreter makes the content fully accessible to deaf and hard-of-hearing visitors. The event is free for members and low cost for non-members. Check the Reflection Riding website for ticket details and program start time. The nature center is on Garden Road at the base of Lookout Mountain. Barn owls are resident at the center and are part of their wildlife education program.

title: Hard of Hearing Night: Winged Wisdom
description: An evening birds-of-prey program at Reflection Riding with ASL interpretation, open to all.
body: This evening program covers local birds of prey and includes ASL interpretation. Everyone is welcome to attend. You learn about the owls, hawks, and falcons that live in and around Reflection Riding Arboretum and Nature Center. Staff bring live birds to the program. The ASL interpreter makes the content fully accessible to deaf and hard-of-hearing visitors. The event is free for members and low cost for non-members. Check the Reflection Riding website for ticket details and program start time. The nature center is on Garden Road in Chattanooga near the base of Lookout Mountain.

title: Healing with Nature with The Chattery
description: A guided outdoor wellness session at Reflection Riding, presented with The Chattery.
body: Step outside and let the pace drop. This session with The Chattery uses the trails and gardens to settle the mind and body. The Chattery is a Chattanooga-based lifelong learning organization that offers workshops and classes across a wide range of topics. This program pairs gentle movement on the Reflection Riding trails with mindfulness practices. The session runs about 90 minutes. Check the Chattery website for registration and pricing. The nature center is on Garden Road near Lookout Mountain. No outdoor fitness level is required. Comfortable walking shoes are all you need.

title: Introduction to Hula with The Chattery
description: A one-hour intro to Hawaiian hula dance at Reflection Riding, presented with The Chattery.
body: Learn the basics of hula in one easy hour. This friendly class with The Chattery covers simple steps and the stories behind the dance. The Chattery is a Chattanooga-based lifelong learning organization offering workshops across a range of topics. This outdoor class takes place at Reflection Riding Arboretum on Garden Road. No dance experience is required. The session runs about 60 minutes. Check the Chattery website for registration and pricing. Wear comfortable clothes and shoes you can move in. The class is held on the grounds of the nature center, with the garden and forest as the backdrop.

title: MAINx24 Chili Championship
description: A chili cook-off during MAINx24 that raises money for Reflection Riding.
body: Taste chili and pick a winner at this MAINx24 cook-off on East Main Street. Cooks go head to head while you sample the pots and vote. The MAINx24 Chili Championship is part of the annual MAINx24 event that closes Main Street to cars for 24 hours. Reflection Riding participates in the event as a community partner. Admission to the chili championship varies - check the MAINx24 website for details. East Main Street fills with food, music, and activities across the full 24-hour window. The chili competition runs during daylight hours.

title: Master Gardener Series: Amazing Grasses
description: A Master Gardener talk at Reflection Riding on low-maintenance native grasses.
body: Native grasses add texture and ask for almost no care. This talk covers which grasses grow well here and how to use them in a home garden. The presenter is a Hamilton County Master Gardener Extension Volunteer. The Master Gardener Series runs periodically at Reflection Riding and covers practical gardening topics relevant to the region. Admission is free or low cost. Check the Reflection Riding website for registration and start time. The nature center is on Garden Road near Lookout Mountain. Attendees often bring questions from their own gardens.

title: Music in the Wild
description: An outdoor performance at Reflection Riding inspired by "Peter and the Wolf," with the Chattanooga Symphony & Opera.
body: The Chattanooga Symphony & Opera brings music straight into the woods. The program draws on "Peter and the Wolf" and fits Prokofiev's score to the natural setting of Reflection Riding. Musicians pop up along the trail before the main outdoor performance. The event is family-friendly and free for Reflection Riding members. Non-member tickets are available on the Reflection Riding website. This is part of the CSO's outdoor programming series. The nature center is on Garden Road near Lookout Mountain. Wear comfortable shoes and bring a blanket or low-back chair for the main performance.

title: Nursery Workshop: Propagation Intensive
description: A hands-on plant propagation workshop with the nursery team at Reflection Riding.
body: Learn how to grow new plants from cuttings and seed. The nursery team shows you the same methods they use every day. You leave with propagated cuttings to grow at home. This workshop runs at the Reflection Riding nursery on Garden Road. Space is limited and registration is required through the Reflection Riding website. The session covers stem cuttings, division, and direct seeding for native plants. All materials are provided. The nursery grows native species used in the arboretum and sold at plant sales. This is a hands-on session suited to gardeners of any experience level.

title: Oli Kai Trail Race
description: A timed trail running event at Reflection Riding with 3, 6, and 9-hour options on a 2.1-mile loop.
body: Run as far as your legs will carry you on a 2.1 mile forest loop. Pick the 3, 6, or 9 hour option and set your own pace. The Oli Kai Trail Race takes place on the trail system at Reflection Riding Arboretum and Nature Center on Garden Road. The format allows solo runners and teams. Registration is required through the Reflection Riding website. Entry fees benefit the nature center. The event honors Oli Kai, a beloved member of the Reflection Riding community. Bring water, trail shoes, and something to eat between loops. The trails wind through forest and open ground.

title: Oli Via Half Marathon and 4.5-Mile Trail Race
description: A trail race day at Reflection Riding offering a half marathon and a 4.5-mile course.
body: Choose the half marathon or the shorter 4.5 mile course. Both routes run through the trails and open ground at Reflection Riding Arboretum and Nature Center on Garden Road. Entry fees benefit the nature center. Registration is required through the Reflection Riding website. This event honors the memory of Oli Via, a beloved member of the Reflection Riding community. Bring trail shoes and water. The trails wind through forest and cross open meadow sections. The race draws runners from across the Chattanooga region. Post-race food and beverages are provided for participants.

title: Owl Odyssey
description: An hour with the barn owls of Reflection Riding, the ghosts of the night woods.
body: Meet the barn owls of Reflection Riding and learn why people call them the ghosts of the night woods. A guide explains how these birds hunt in near silence and find prey by sound alone. The nature center keeps barn owls as animal ambassadors because they cannot return to the wild. You watch one up close during the hour. The event is free for members and low cost for non-members. Check the Reflection Riding website for ticket details. The nature center is on Garden Road at the base of Lookout Mountain.

title: PBS Kids Day
description: A free morning of kid-friendly activities at Reflection Riding, hosted with WTCI PBS.
body: Reflection Riding teams up with WTCI PBS for a morning built for young kids. The two hours mix outdoor play with hands-on learning across the grounds. Families can meet familiar PBS characters and explore nature together. The event runs free and suits early elementary ages and younger.

title: Project ReWild
description: A hands-on volunteer workshop at Reflection Riding to remove invasive plants and restore native habitat.
body: Help restore native habitat at this hands-on volunteer workshop. Staff teach you how to spot common invasive plants and pull them the right way. You then plant native species that feed and shelter local wildlife. Take the skills home and rewild your own yard. Volunteers earn a discount in the native plant nursery. The workshop repeats on Saturdays through December.

title: Spirits and Sustainability with Green|Spaces
description: An evening at Reflection Riding on its mission and sustainability work, with light refreshments.
body: Learn how Reflection Riding protects native land and wildlife. Green|Spaces leads the talk over light refreshments. You leave knowing more about what it takes to run a working arboretum and nature center inside a city. Green|Spaces is a Chattanooga nonprofit focused on sustainable building and land stewardship. The evening combines conversation about environmental issues with a tour of the Reflection Riding property. Admission is free or low cost. Check the Reflection Riding website for registration and start time. The nature center is on Garden Road near the base of Lookout Mountain.

title: Tails, Trails, and Ales
description: A dog-friendly trail race day at Reflection Riding, presented by Mountain View Ford.
body: Bring your dog and hit the trails together. This race day lets you run with your four-legged friend across the grounds of Reflection Riding. The event pairs trail running with a post-race beer from a local brewery. Dogs run leashed alongside their owners. Entry fees benefit the nature center. Distances vary - check the Reflection Riding website for race options and registration. Trail shoes and water for both you and your dog are essential. The nature center trails wind through forest and open ground on Garden Road near Lookout Mountain.

title: Tennessee River Rescue
description: A morning waterway cleanup at Reflection Riding as part of the Tennessee River Rescue.
body: Join the yearly cleanup that keeps local waterways clear of trash. Volunteers gather at Reflection Riding to work a stretch of the Tennessee River and nearby waterways. The event provides bags, gloves, and water. No experience needed. Volunteers have removed thousands of pounds of trash in past years. Register through the Reflection Riding website. This is a free volunteer event open to adults and families with older children. The event runs a few hours in the morning. It is part of a larger Tennessee River cleanup effort coordinated across multiple sites along the river.

title: The Battle of Lookout Mountain 163rd Anniversary
description: A guided anniversary hike across Reflection Riding with historian Jim Ogden, marking the Battle Above the Clouds.
body: Local historian Jim Ogden leads a guided hike across Reflection Riding to mark the 163rd anniversary of the Battle of Lookout Mountain. People call this fight the Battle Above the Clouds. The roughly two-mile walk covers the same ground where the Union Army crossed Lookout Creek and assaulted the mountain in 1863. Ogden explains the key moments of one of the most important campaigns of the Civil War. The land is now permanently protected through a conservation easement with the American Battlefield Trust. Expect uneven terrain and about two and a half hours on the trail. Check the Reflection Riding website for ticket details.

title: Under the Wolf Moon: Red Wolves and Mindful Trails
description: Meet the resident red wolves and walk a mindful trail at Reflection Riding during the Wolf Moon.
body: Walk the trails under the January Wolf Moon. City of Chattanooga Parks and Outdoors leads this program with a Reflection Riding naturalist. You meet the resident red wolves and hear their conservation story. Red wolves are critically endangered, and the nature center breeds them for release. A slow, mindful walk follows along scenic trails. The pace helps you start the year with a clear, calm mind.

title: White Duck Taco Giveback Night
description: Dine at White Duck Taco Shop and a share of sales supports Reflection Riding.
body: Eat tacos and help the land. White Duck Taco Shop hosts this giveback night and sends a share of sales to Reflection Riding Arboretum and Nature Center. White Duck Taco has locations in Chattanooga including the Southside and North Shore. Any qualifying purchase during the event window counts. This is a casual night out that doubles as a fundraiser for the nature center. No ticket required - just show up and order. Check the Reflection Riding website for which White Duck Taco location is participating and the hours of the giveback window.

title: Wild Ones Plant Sale
description: A native plant sale at Reflection Riding featuring selections from the Wild Ones group.
body: Find native plants that feed local birds and pollinators. The Wild Ones group brings a strong selection to this one-day sale at Reflection Riding. Wild Ones is a national native plant society with a Tennessee Valley chapter. Their plant sales focus on locally appropriate species that support biodiversity. Staff help you choose plants for your specific conditions. The sale takes place at Reflection Riding Arboretum on Garden Road. Admission to the grounds is free. Plants are priced individually. Fall is an excellent time to plant native perennials and shrubs in the Chattanooga region.

title: Wild Wonders: A Close Encounter with Native Animals
description: A guided tour of the Native Animal Area at Reflection Riding to meet the resident animal ambassadors.
body: Tour the Native Animal Area and meet the resident animal ambassadors of East Tennessee. The nature center cares for red wolves, a bobcat, owls, hawks, and a sandhill crane. These animals cannot survive in the wild, so they help staff teach visitors. A guide explains the role each species plays in the local ecosystem. The event also runs on Saturday with two time slots.

title: Winged Wisdom: Understanding Birds of Prey
description: A morning program on the birds of prey at Reflection Riding and their role in the local ecosystem.
body: Learn why birds of prey matter to the woods and fields around Chattanooga. A guide covers the hawks, owls, and vultures that live at the nature center as animal ambassadors. You hear how each bird hunts and how it keeps rodent numbers in check. The talk shows why healthy raptor populations signal a healthy ecosystem. Staff bring a bird out for a close look.

title: Woodland Walk
description: A guided tree identification walk through the woods at Reflection Riding.
body: Walk the woods with a guide and learn to name the trees around you. Staff point out leaves, bark, and shape so you can tell a white oak from a red oak, or a beech from a hornbeam. The Woodland Walk runs on the trail system at Reflection Riding Arboretum and Nature Center on Garden Road. The event is free for members and low cost for non-members. Check the website for registration and start time. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water. The walk moves at a relaxed pace suited to all fitness levels. It runs about 90 minutes to two hours.

title: Enchanted Garden of Lights
description: Rock City's Enchanted Garden of Lights runs nightly from mid-November through December 31 on Lookout Mountain. Millions of lights transform the gardens into a walkable holiday experience.
body: Millions of lights cover the trails and formations at Rock City Gardens each winter. The route winds through Rock City's rock formations and scenic overlooks, all lit up after dark. It runs nightly from mid-November through December 31. Tickets are required and available at seerockcity.com. The gardens sit on Lookout Mountain just across the Georgia state line, about 20 minutes from downtown Chattanooga.

title: Baking with Freshly Milled Grains
description: Afternoon baking workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm on milling and baking with fresh wheat from Neidlovs Bakery.
body: Erik Zilen of Neidlovs Bakery walks through milling and baking with freshly milled wheat. Three and a half hours on a Saturday afternoon - good intro if you have never worked with home-milled flour. Sequatchie Cove Farm is in Sequatchie Valley, Tennessee, about an hour from Chattanooga. The workshop covers grain selection, milling technique, and the differences between fresh-milled and commercial flour in bread making. All equipment and ingredients are provided. Register through the Sequatchie Cove website. Check the site for cost.

title: Beeswax Candle Making
description: Hand-dipped beeswax candle workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm through the Cumberland Folk School - make taper candles for the holidays.
body: The Cumberland Folk School runs this hands-on class at the farm. You dip tapers in warm beeswax, building each candle layer by layer. Beeswax burns clean and smells faintly of honey. The finished pairs make good holiday gifts for teachers, hosts, and family. No experience is needed, and the farm supplies the wax and tools. Space is limited, so sign up through the farm events page before the class fills.

title: Fermenting the Harvest with Sandor Katz
description: Full-day fermentation workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm with fermentation revivalist Sandor Katz.
body: Sandor Katz literally wrote the book on fermentation. This is a full-day hands-on session at Sequatchie Cove - kraut, kimchi, and other techniques demystified by the author of The Art of Fermentation. Katz is one of the foremost educators in the fermentation revival movement. His books are used as references by home fermenters and professional chefs worldwide. Sequatchie Cove Farm is in Sequatchie Valley, Tennessee, about an hour from Chattanooga. Register through the Sequatchie Cove website. This workshop fills fast - book as soon as registration opens. Check the site for cost.

title: Making a Galette
description: Half-day workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm on rough puff pastry and rustic galettes with Mallory Grimm Tubbs.
body: Learn rough puff pastry and how to shape and fill a galette with Mallory Grimm Tubbs. Four hours, hands-on, you leave with something to eat. Good timing for fall produce. Sequatchie Cove Farm is in Sequatchie Valley, Tennessee, about an hour from Chattanooga. The farm hosts workshops and classes in a rural setting. This is a baking workshop focused on a specific technique. All ingredients and tools are provided. Register through the Sequatchie Cove website. Check the site for cost and the specific date. Skill level: beginner to intermediate bakers welcome.

title: Knitting for Beginners: Washcloths
description: Beginner knitting workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm with Tracy Knutson - learn basic stitches by making a small washcloth.
body: Tracy Knutson teaches the basics of knitting through one small, useful project - a washcloth or dishcloth. You learn to cast on, knit, and bind off, and you leave with something finished. Sequatchie Cove Farm is in Sequatchie Valley, Tennessee, about an hour from Chattanooga. The farm hosts craft and skill workshops alongside agricultural classes. All materials are provided. No prior knitting experience is needed. Register through the Sequatchie Cove website. Check the site for cost and start time. The class runs about three hours and is well suited to complete beginners.

title: Linoleum Block Prints
description: Block printing workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm with Laurel York - carve a linoleum block and pull your own prints.
body: Laurel York walks you through carving a design into linoleum and pulling your own block prints. You learn how to transfer a design, carve it safely, and ink and print on paper or fabric. Sequatchie Cove Farm is in Sequatchie Valley, Tennessee, about an hour from Chattanooga. The farm hosts craft and art workshops alongside agricultural and food classes. All materials are provided. Register through the Sequatchie Cove website. No prior printmaking experience is needed. Check the site for cost and the specific start time. The workshop runs about four hours.

title: October Fundraiser Event
description: Evening fundraiser at Sequatchie Cove Farm with live music from Stones River Reelers, a farm-to-table dinner, and a silent auction.
body: Sequatchie Cove Farm hosts a casual evening to support its move to nonprofit status. Stones River Reelers play live old-time string music while you eat. The farm serves a farm-to-table dinner outdoors. A silent auction of handmade crafts raises money for the nonprofit application. Bring family and blankets for seating on the grass. BYOB is welcome. The rain date is Saturday, October 24. Adult tickets cover ages 12 and up, and children under 2 enter free.

title: Scandinavian Star Ornaments
description: Scandinavian star ornament workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm through the Cumberland Folk School - weave folded paper stars for the holidays.
body: The Cumberland Folk School teaches this Nordic holiday craft at the farm. You weave folded paper strips into three-dimensional woven stars. The technique comes from a long Scandinavian winter tradition. Each finished star hangs on a tree or in a window. The class suits beginners, and the folk school brings the paper and shows every fold. This session was listed as sold out, so check the farm events page for openings or a waitlist.

title: CHOCOLAT - 2nd Annual
description: The second annual CHOCOLAT market at the Chattanooga Choo Choo brings together chocolate artisans and confectionery vendors for a day of tastings and a vendor competition.
body: The second annual CHOCOLAT market at the Choo-Choo brings together chocolate artisans and confectionery vendors for a full day of tastings and a vendor competition. Expect handcrafted truffles, bonbons, and chocolate goods from regional makers. Hours run Saturday 10am to 5pm. Free admission.

title: Christkindlmarkt Coolidge - Weekend 1
description: Shop the Market At brings a European-style holiday market to Coolidge Park for two days of artisan gifts, festive food, and riverside lights.
body: Local artisans line Coolidge Park's riverside walkways with handcrafted gifts and seasonal goods. Food vendors serve hot drinks and festive dishes alongside the shopping. Hours are Saturday 10am to 7pm and Sunday 11am to 6pm. Free admission. This is the first of two back-to-back weekends at Coolidge Park before the holiday markets shift to other venues.

title: Christkindlmarkt Coolidge - Weekend 2
description: The second weekend of Christkindlmarkt Coolidge returns to Coolidge Park on Thanksgiving weekend with new artisan vendors and a European-inspired holiday market.
body: New artisan vendors join the second Christkindlmarkt Coolidge weekend, filling the riverside park with handcrafted gifts and seasonal decor. Hours are Saturday 10am to 7pm and Sunday 11am to 6pm. Free admission. Thanksgiving weekend traffic on the North Shore can be heavy. Plan parking before you go.

title: Christmas at Dolly's Tennessean Travel Stop
description: Shop the Market At heads to Dolly's Tennessean Travel Stop in Cornersville, TN for a holiday market with artisan vendors and Tennessee holiday charm.
body: Shop the Market At brings artisan vendors and holiday shopping to Dolly's Tennessean Travel Stop in Cornersville over a December weekend. Hours have not been announced; check the events page for updated times closer to December. Cornersville is roughly 2.5 hours from Chattanooga. Confirm details before making the drive.

title: Christmas at the Choo-Choo - Weekend 1
description: Shop the Market At transforms the Chattanooga Choo Choo grounds into a holiday market for two weekends in December with artisan vendors, live music, and seasonal gifts.
body: Local artisan vendors set up across the Choo-Choo's outdoor grounds for the first of two December holiday market weekends. Handcrafted gifts and seasonal goods fill the historic hotel's spaces while live holiday music plays throughout the day. Hours are Saturday 10am to 6pm and Sunday 10am to 4pm. Free admission.

title: Christmas at the Choo-Choo - Weekend 2
description: The second weekend of Christmas at the Choo-Choo brings artisan vendors, seasonal beverages, and festive live music back to the Chattanooga Choo Choo grounds.
body: Artisan vendors return to the Choo-Choo grounds for the second December weekend with handcrafted gifts, seasonal beverages, and festive live music. Hours are Saturday 10am to 6pm and Sunday 10am to 4pm. Free admission. This weekend runs the same day as Christmas in the Country on December 12. Both are free.

title: Christmas in the Country
description: McDonald Farm in Sale Creek hosts a one-day rural holiday market with artisan vendors and handcrafted gifts set against a country backdrop.
body: McDonald Farm in Sale Creek hosts a one-day rural holiday market with artisan vendors and handcrafted gifts spread across the farm property. The country setting offers a quieter alternative to the urban market events. Hours run Saturday 10am to 4pm. Free admission. Sale Creek is about 25 miles north of downtown Chattanooga via US-27 North.

title: Crawfish Festival
description: The Crawfish Festival at Crawfish Springs in Chickamauga, GA is a full-day Southern celebration with fresh boiled crawfish, live music, cold drinks, and artisan vendors.
body: Fresh boiled crawfish, live music, cold drinks, and artisan vendors fill the day at Crawfish Springs in Chickamauga. Hours run from 11am to 7pm. Admission details have not been announced; check the events page for updates. Chickamauga is about 25 miles south of downtown Chattanooga via US-27 South.

title: Down Home Days - 53rd Annual
description: The 53rd annual Down Home Days in historic downtown Chickamauga, GA features 100-plus makers, two live music stages, and a kid zone in one of the region's longest-running festivals.
body: More than 100 makers and artisan vendors fill historic downtown Chickamauga for the 53rd annual Down Home Days. Two live music stages and a kid zone round out the day. Hours run Saturday 11am to 8pm. Free admission. Chickamauga is about 25 miles south of Chattanooga via US-27 South. The scale here is bigger than most markets in the organizer's lineup.

title: Georgia Vintage & Makers Market
description: The Georgia Vintage and Makers Market at Lakewood 400 in Cumming, GA runs three days and combines vintage antiques, handmade goods, and artisan products.
body: Lakewood 400 in Cumming, GA hosts a three-day smorgasbord of vintage antiques, estate items, and handmade artisan goods. Hours are Friday 9am to 5pm, Saturday 9am to 6pm, and Sunday 10am to 5pm. Cumming is about 90 miles from Chattanooga. Admission details have not been announced.

title: Last Minute Market
description: The Last Minute Market at The Commons in Collegedale is the final holiday shopping event of the 2026 season with artisan vendors, homemade treats, and live music.
body: Artisan vendors close out the 2026 holiday season at The Commons in Collegedale with handcrafted gifts, homemade treats, and locally made goods. Live music plays throughout both days. Hours are Saturday 11am to 5pm and Sunday 12pm to 5pm. Free admission. The Commons is at 4950 Swinyar Dr, about 20 miles east of downtown Chattanooga.

title: Mardi Gras at WanderLinger
description: Shop the Market At brings a New Orleans-style Mardi Gras celebration to the Chattanooga Choo Choo Gardens with a brass band, King Cake, Cajun food, and an artisan marketplace.
body: A live brass band kicks off this New Orleans-style Mardi Gras afternoon at the Choo-Choo Gardens. Vendors serve King Cake and Cajun food alongside an artisan marketplace. Hours run Saturday 2pm to 9pm. Admission details have not been announced; check the events page for ticket info closer to February.

title: Mother's Day Gala - 5th Annual
description: The fifth annual Mother's Day Gala at the Chattanooga Choo Choo is a curated art and craft market with fresh flowers, gourmet chocolates, and handcrafted jewelry for the holiday weekend.
body: The fifth annual Mother's Day Gala at the Choo-Choo puts fresh flowers, gourmet chocolates, and handcrafted jewelry in one place for the holiday weekend. Hours run Saturday 10am to 5pm. Free admission. Mother's Day falls on May 10, 2027, two days after the market.

title: Mystical March - 5th Annual
description: The fifth annual Mystical March at the Chattanooga Choo Choo is a St. Patrick's Day-themed spring market with handmade goods, local produce, and a hidden-leprechaun hunt.
body: Mystical March hits the Chattanooga Choo-Choo for a fifth year with a St. Patrick's Day theme and a hidden leprechaun hunt across the market grounds. Vendors sell handmade goods and local produce. Hours run Saturday 10am to 5pm. Free admission. The event lands two weeks before St. Patrick's Day and draws strong family turnout.

title: Shop the Market at the Choo Choo - 2nd Annual
description: The second annual Shop the Market at the Choo Choo brings a classic artisan and food market with live entertainment to the historic Chattanooga Choo Choo.
body: Local vendors return to the Choo-Choo grounds for the second year with handmade goods, fresh food products, and live entertainment. The event follows the core market format Shop the Market At runs year-round. Hours are Saturday 10am to 5pm. Free admission. The Choo-Choo is at 1400 Market St in downtown Chattanooga.

title: Springtime in Chattanooga - 4th Annual
description: The fourth annual Springtime in Chattanooga at Coolidge Park features a Paris-inspired spring market with handcrafted goods, an Eiffel Tower photo opportunity, and floral displays.
body: Coolidge Park gets a Paris treatment for the fourth annual Springtime in Chattanooga. Vendors offer handcrafted goods and local products while an Eiffel Tower photo setup and floral displays fill the park. Hours run Saturday 10am to 5pm. Free admission. The park is on the North Shore at 1600 River St, walkable from downtown via the Walnut Street Bridge.

title: Swamp Monster Festival - Inaugural
description: The inaugural Swamp Monster Festival at Chester Frost Park in Hixson celebrates river folklore with family activities, a catfish tournament, and artisan vendors.
body: Chester Frost Park on Chickamauga Lake hosts the inaugural Swamp Monster Festival, a family day built around river folklore. A catfish tournament runs alongside artisan vendors and activities tied to the swamp monster theme. Hours run Saturday 1pm to 9pm. Admission details have not been announced; check the events page for updates.

title: Twilight Firefly Market
description: The Twilight Firefly Market at the Chattanooga Choo Choo is an evening market with twinkling lights, local makers, and live music starting at 5pm on a Saturday in June.
body: The Choo-Choo lights up for an evening market with twinkling lights, local makers, and live music starting at 5pm. The night-time format sets it apart from every other event in this lineup. Hours run Saturday 5pm to 10pm. Free admission. June is firefly season in the Tennessee Valley.

title: Twilight Jewelry Market - 2nd Annual
description: The second annual Twilight Jewelry Market at the Chattanooga Choo Choo Gardens focuses entirely on handcrafted jewelry from regional artisans with live music throughout the day.
body: Regional artisans fill the Choo-Choo Gardens with handcrafted rings, necklaces, bracelets, and earrings for the second annual Twilight Jewelry Market. Live music plays throughout. Hours run Saturday 10am to 5pm. Free admission. This is one of the more focused markets in the lineup, built around a single craft rather than a general artisan mix.

title: Soldiers & Sailors Memorial Auditorium
description: Touring concerts, comedy, and family shows at the 1924 Soldiers & Sailors Memorial Auditorium on McCallie Avenue.
body: A 1924 memorial auditorium on McCallie Avenue seating around 2,000. Named for Hamilton County's World War I veterans. Hosts Broadway tours, classic rock, country, comedy, and other large live events. The building is a registered historic landmark in Chattanooga. The main hall has a traditional horseshoe balcony layout and strong acoustics for large productions. Parking is available in the surrounding McCallie Avenue area. Check the venue website for the current event calendar. The auditorium is managed by the City of Chattanooga. It has hosted major acts and touring productions for 100 years.

title: Chattanooga Horn Authority
description: Chattanooga Horn Authority plays Songbirds on September 5 at 7pm downtown.
body: The Chattanooga Horn Authority packs a big-band brass punch into Songbirds on September 5 at 7pm. Local players, tight charts, and a whole lot of horn on the Westside. The Chattanooga Horn Authority is a local brass ensemble that plays jazz, soul, and big band arrangements. Their sets combine original charts with reimagined classics. Songbirds is a small listening room on the North Shore that seats about 100. The venue is an intimate space that suits both acoustic solo acts and small ensembles. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Copeland w/ Jenny Dee
description: Copeland plays Songbirds on September 11 with special guest Jenny Dee.
body: Copeland brings their Florida rock to Songbirds on September 11 at 7pm, with special guest Jenny Dee. The band has played together since 2001 and has six albums. Copeland plays indie rock and emo-influenced music built on piano, guitar, and Aaron Marsh's tenor voice. They have toured nationally and internationally and built a devoted following over 20 years. Jenny Dee is a Chattanooga-area singer-songwriter. Songbirds is a small listening room on the North Shore. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: John Cowan Trio
description: John Cowan Trio plays Songbirds on September 4 at 7pm in downtown Chattanooga.
body: John Cowan - the New Grass Revival voice - brings his trio to Songbirds on September 4 at 7pm. Decades of high-lonesome harmony and bluegrass fire in a room small enough to feel it. Cowan was the bassist and vocalist for New Grass Revival from the band's formation in 1971. He has toured and recorded with Doobie Brothers, Tony Rice, and others in the acoustic music world. His voice is one of the most distinctive in bluegrass. Songbirds is a small listening room on the North Shore. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Nolan Taylor w/ Jess Woodland
description: Nolan Taylor plays Songbirds on September 10 with Jess Woodland opening.
body: Nolan Taylor plays Songbirds on September 10 at 7pm, with Jess Woodland opening. His songs put a voice to people who often go unheard. The room stays small, so the show feels personal. Taylor is a Nashville singer-songwriter whose Americana and folk music draws on direct, plainspoken storytelling. His songs address working-class themes with emotional honesty. Jess Woodland is a Chattanooga-area singer-songwriter who has opened at Songbirds multiple times. Songbirds is a small listening room on the North Shore. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: St. Elmo Luminaria Festival
description: The St. Elmo Luminaria Festival lights up the Virginia Ave Greenway in Historic St. Elmo each third Saturday of December. Expect luminaries, live music, a makers market, and food trucks.
venue: Virginia Ave Greenway, Historic St. Elmo
body: Paper luminarias line the Virginia Ave Greenway as Historic St. Elmo lights up for its annual December stroll. Volunteers and local businesses build and place hundreds of candle-lit bags along the route each year. Live music, a makers market, and food trucks fill out the evening. The event is free to attend. Luminary kits are available to purchase so your household can light a section of the route. Proceeds support a local nonprofit chosen by the St. Elmo community each year.

title: Movie Night
description: Free movie night every Friday at 7pm at TailGate Brewery on Market St in Chattanooga.
body: Friday nights, TailGate Brewery on Market St puts a movie on the big screen at 7pm. Grab a fresh pint from the taproom. Find a seat and settle in. The show runs about two hours. TailGate Brewery is a Nashville-based craft brewery with a taproom on Market Street in the Southside neighborhood of Chattanooga. The movie selection rotates weekly and is announced on social media. No ticket required - walk in and order a beer. The taproom pours TailGate's core lineup and seasonal releases. Check the social pages for the weekly film announcement.

title: Trivia Night
description: Free trivia night every Thursday at 7pm at TailGate Brewery on Market St in Chattanooga.
body: Thursday nights belong to trivia at TailGate Brewery on Market St. Questions kick off at 7pm. Round up a team or grab a seat with strangers. Order a fresh pint and work through the rounds together. TailGate Brewery is a Nashville-based craft brewery with a taproom on Market Street in the Southside neighborhood of Chattanooga. The trivia format covers general knowledge, pop culture, sports, and current events across multiple rounds. No ticket required - walk in and join a table. Check the TailGate social pages for any themed trivia nights or changes to the schedule.

title: Christkindlmarkt
description: Christkindlmarkt brings a European-inspired holiday market to The Commons in Collegedale on November 7-8, 2026, with artisan gifts, festive food, and Glühwein.
body: Christkindlmarkt returns to The Commons in Collegedale for a two-day holiday market. The event draws on European Christmas market traditions. Vendors sell artisan gifts and festive food across the outdoor plazas. Warm Glühwein and twinkling lights set the Old-World mood. The market runs Saturday from 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM. It reopens Sunday from 11:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Admission is free. Bring cash and arrive early, since the plaza fills up on weekend afternoons.

title: Last Minute Market
description: The Last Minute Market at The Commons in Collegedale runs December 19-20, 2026, with artisan gifts, festive treats, and live music for holiday shoppers.
body: The Last Minute Market gives holiday shoppers a final chance to buy local gifts before Christmas. Vendors fill The Commons with artisan goods and festive treats. Live music plays through the market. Shoppers can find handmade presents and stocking stuffers in one stop. The market opens Saturday from 11:00 AM to 5:00 PM. It runs again Sunday from 12:00 PM to 5:00 PM. Admission is free. The date falls days before Christmas, so plan for a busy crowd.

title: Board Game Night at The Greenhouse Barrel + Taproom
description: Free weekly Thursday Board Game Night at The Greenhouse Barrel + Taproom in Chattanooga, with tabletop games and Oddstory craft beer from 6pm.
body: Thursday nights fill The Greenhouse with board games. Play kicks off at 6pm. Pull something from the shelf of tabletop games or bring your own. Oddstory pours craft beer at the taproom bar while you strategize. The Greenhouse Barrel + Taproom is a craft beer taproom in Chattanooga associated with Oddstory Brewing. Board game nights draw a mix of regulars and new faces. No ticket required - walk in and find a table. This is a free weekly event beyond the cost of your drinks. Check The Greenhouse social pages for any updates to the weekly schedule.

title: Drink & Draw with Jessica Schulman at The Greenhouse Barrel + Taproom
description: Monthly Drink & Draw with artist Jessica Schulman at The Greenhouse Barrel + Taproom, a guided Sunday drawing session with craft beer at 2pm.
body: Once a month, Drink & Draw sets up at The Greenhouse. Artist Jessica Schulman leads the Sunday session at 2pm. You sketch and draw while Oddstory pours craft beer. The Greenhouse Barrel + Taproom is a craft beer taproom in Chattanooga associated with Oddstory Brewing. Drink & Draw is an open-format drawing session - bring your own supplies or use what is provided. No experience is needed. Check The Greenhouse social pages for the specific monthly date and any registration requirements. The session runs about two hours.

title: Pub Trivia at The Greenhouse Barrel + Taproom
description: Free weekly Tuesday Pub Trivia at The Greenhouse Barrel + Taproom in Chattanooga, with craft beer and team rounds starting at 7:30pm.
body: Tuesday nights at The Greenhouse mean trivia. Teams settle in at 7:30pm and work through several rounds. Oddstory pours craft beer at the taproom bar while you argue over answers. The top teams walk away with bragging rights and small prizes. Round up a few friends and name your team. The taproom sits at 336 E M.L. King Blvd. The Greenhouse is associated with Oddstory Brewing. No ticket required. Walk in and find a table. The trivia night is free beyond the cost of your drinks.

title: Sip 'N Snip Collage Night at The Greenhouse Barrel + Taproom
description: Weekly Wednesday Sip 'N Snip Collage Night at The Greenhouse Barrel + Taproom, where you make collage art over craft beer starting at 4pm.
body: Wednesday afternoons turn into collage hour at The Greenhouse. Snipping starts at 4pm. You cut, paste, and layer paper into your own collage. Oddstory beer stays cold and the taproom keeps the doors open. The Greenhouse Barrel + Taproom is a taproom and event space in Chattanooga associated with Oddstory Brewing. The collage format is casual and social - bring magazines, printed photos, or found materials. No artistic experience is needed. Check The Greenhouse social pages for any changes to the weekly schedule. This is a free event beyond the cost of your drinks.

title: A Beautiful Noise: The Neil Diamond Musical
description: A Beautiful Noise is a Broadway jukebox musical telling the life story of Neil Diamond, running five performances at the Tivoli Theatre.
body: A Beautiful Noise is a Broadway musical telling the life story of Neil Diamond. It features his most beloved songs including Sweet Caroline, Cherry Cherry, and I Am... I Said. The show uses a creative structure where Diamond tells his story through a therapy session. A Beautiful Noise ran on Broadway and now tours nationally. The Tivoli Theatre is on Broad Street and seats about 1,700. Check the venue website for ticket prices and showtimes. This is a jukebox musical built for fans of Diamond's catalog across multiple generations.

title: Beetlejuice the Musical
description: Beetlejuice the Musical is a Tony-nominated Broadway show based on Tim Burton's 1988 film, playing five performances at the Tivoli Theatre.
body: Beetlejuice is a Tony-nominated Broadway musical based on Tim Burton's 1988 film. It follows Lydia Deetz and a mischievous ghost in a dark comedic story filled with physical comedy and sharp songs. The show ran 587 performances on Broadway before its national tour. The Tivoli Theatre is on Broad Street and seats about 1,700. Check the venue website for ticket prices and showtimes. The show runs about two and a half hours. It is PG-13 rated. The music and design lean into the quirky, macabre tone of the original film.

title: Ben Folds Five On Tour
description: Alternative rock trio Ben Folds Five perform live at the Tivoli Theatre in Chattanooga.
body: Ben Folds Five is a piano-driven alternative rock trio. The band pairs Ben Folds on piano and vocals with bass and drums. Their sound leans on sharp melodies and witty, honest lyrics. The group is known for hits such as Brick and Song for the Dumped. This tour brings the trio back to the stage together for a full live set.

title: Ben Rector & Friends
description: Singer-songwriter Ben Rector performs live at the Tivoli Theatre in Chattanooga.
body: Ben Rector is a Nashville singer, songwriter, and producer. He writes warm, melodic, piano-driven pop. His songs draw on James Taylor and Paul McCartney. His album Brand New reached the top ten on the Billboard 200. Many of his songs center on the piano with full orchestral backing. This show features guests joining him on stage for the night. The set starts at 7:30 PM. The Tivoli has strong acoustics for a quieter, piano-forward show, so the balcony offers a clear view and sound.

title: Billy Strings
description: Grammy-winning progressive bluegrass artist Billy Strings plays two nights at the Tivoli Theatre in Chattanooga.
body: Billy Strings plays progressive bluegrass with speed, precision, and a psychedelic edge. He won the Grammy for Best Bluegrass Album in 2021 and built one of the most devoted fan bases in the genre. His live shows are long and improvisational. Strings grew up in Michigan and relocated to Nashville. His guitar playing draws from Doc Watson and Tony Rice while moving into territory no traditional bluegrass player has covered. The Tivoli Theatre on Broad Street seats about 1,700. Check the venue website for ticket prices. This show will sell out.

title: Brad Williams: The Big & Small Tour
description: Stand-up comedian Brad Williams brings The Big & Small Tour to the Tivoli Theatre in Chattanooga.
body: Brad Williams is a stand-up comedian known for his high-energy delivery. He turns his own life and experiences into sharp, fast jokes. The Big & Small Tour features new material from the road. Williams has released several comedy specials and hosts his own podcast. He has toured clubs and theaters across the country. His confident, crowd-working style keeps the room engaged all night.

title: Cirque Alice
description: Cirque Alice brings a full-scale circus production based on Alice in Wonderland to the Tivoli Theatre in Chattanooga.
body: Cirque Alice is a circus production based on Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland. The show features international acrobats, aerialists, and contortionists performing against a Wonderland visual world. The production combines physical performance with narrative elements drawn from Carroll's story. The Tivoli Theatre on Broad Street seats about 1,700. Check the venue website for ticket prices and showtimes. The show runs about 90 minutes. It is family-friendly and works well for children who enjoy circus performance. The Tivoli's stage accommodates the aerial rigging required for aerialist acts.

title: Disney's Beauty and the Beast
description: Disney's Beauty and the Beast brings the animated film to a live Broadway stage for eight performances at the Tivoli Theatre.
body: Disney's Beauty and the Beast is a Broadway production based on the animated film. The show features the full score including Be Our Guest and the title song, performed live. Chattanooga Theatre Centre or a touring company stages this at the Tivoli Theatre on Broad Street. The Tivoli is a restored 1921 venue that seats about 1,700. Check the Tivoli website for ticket prices and showtimes. The production runs about two and a half hours with an intermission. This is family-friendly programming suited to children and adults who grew up with the film.

title: Drew & Ellie Holcomb: Rain or Shine Tour
description: Drew and Ellie Holcomb bring their Rain or Shine Tour to the Tivoli Theatre in Chattanooga for a night of folk and Americana.
body: Drew and Ellie Holcomb are a married folk and Americana duo from Tennessee. The Rain or Shine Tour brings them together on one stage. Drew leads the band Drew Holcomb and the Neighbors. Ellie writes and performs her own songs with warm, acoustic roots. Expect tight harmonies, story-driven lyrics, and a mix of solo and shared songs across the set.

title: Dusty Slay: The Neighborhood Guy Tour
description: Stand-up comedian Dusty Slay brings The Neighborhood Guy Tour to the Tivoli Theatre in Chattanooga.
body: Dusty Slay is a stand-up comedian from the South. He is known for his laid-back delivery and down-to-earth stories. His signature greeting is a cheerful "we're having a good time." The Neighborhood Guy Tour features new material about everyday life. Slay has appeared on The Tonight Show and released specials on major platforms. His clean, relatable style draws a wide crowd.

title: Jersey Boys
description: Jersey Boys is the Tony Award-winning Broadway musical about Frankie Valli and the Four Seasons, running eight performances at the Tivoli Theatre.
body: Jersey Boys is the Tony Award-winning Broadway musical about Frankie Valli and the Four Seasons. It follows their rise from the streets of New Jersey to international fame. The show includes hits like Big Girls Don't Cry, Walk Like a Man, and Can't Take My Eyes Off You. It runs eight performances from August 11 through 15. The Tivoli Theatre is on Broad Street and seats about 1,700. Check the venue website for ticket prices. The show runs about two and a half hours with an intermission.

title: John Cleese
description: Monty Python legend John Cleese appears at the Tivoli Theatre for a screening of Monty Python and the Holy Grail followed by a live Q&A.
body: John Cleese is a founding member of Monty Python. This event marks 50 years of Monty Python and the Holy Grail. The night opens with a screening of the film. Cleese then takes the stage for a live question and answer session. He shares stories from his comedy career and responds to the audience. Fans of British comedy will find plenty to enjoy.

title: Josh Turner: 25th Anniversary Tour
description: Country singer Josh Turner brings his 25th Anniversary Tour to the Tivoli Theatre in Chattanooga.
body: Josh Turner sings neotraditional country with a deep bass-baritone voice. His sound stays rooted in classic honky-tonk and gospel. He is known for number-one hits such as Your Man, Long Black Train, and Why Don't We Just Dance. This tour marks 25 years of his career on stage. Turner plays the songs that made him a country radio staple. The Tivoli seats fewer than 1,800 people, so every seat feels close to the stage. Doors open before the 7:30 PM show, so arrive early to find downtown parking.

title: Justin Willman
description: Magician and comedian Justin Willman brings his live magic and comedy show to the Tivoli Theatre in Chattanooga.
body: Justin Willman mixes sleight-of-hand magic with stand-up comedy. He is the host and creator of the Netflix series Magic for Humans. His live show pulls audience members on stage for interactive tricks. Willman builds each bit around a punchline, then lands the trick as the payoff. The style stays casual and conversational throughout the night.

title: Mannheim Steamroller Christmas
description: Mannheim Steamroller brings its Christmas tour to Chattanooga, presented by the Tivoli Theatre Foundation.
body: Mannheim Steamroller performs its long-running Christmas tour, led by founder and composer Chip Davis. The group plays a neo-classical take on holiday carols and original songs. The sound mixes orchestral arrangements with modern electronic elements. This stop takes place on December 17 at 7:30 PM. The Tivoli Theatre Foundation presents the show. Check the Tivoli website for ticket details and seating.

title: Michael Blaustein: Bad Bad Boy
description: Stand-up comedian Michael Blaustein brings his Bad Bad Boy tour to the Tivoli Theatre in Chattanooga.
body: Michael Blaustein is a stand-up comedian and podcast host. He hosts the Stiff Socks podcast with fellow comic Trevor Wallace. His comedy leans on blunt observations and self-deprecating stories. The Bad Bad Boy tour features new stand-up material. Blaustein built a large following through viral clips and club tours. His quick, candid style keeps the pace fast throughout the set.

title: Nate Jackson: Miracle Baby Tour
description: Comedian Nate Jackson brings his Miracle Baby Tour to the Tivoli Theatre in Chattanooga.
body: Nate Jackson is a fast-rising stand-up comedian. His style mixes sharp crowd work, quick improvisation, and relatable storytelling. He built a huge following on TikTok with more than 4.5 million fans. His Netflix special Super Funny debuted at number three on the platform. His past tours sold out about 90 percent of their shows. This stop is one night only, so tickets move fast. The show starts at 7:00 PM. Crowd work means no two nights are the same, so a front section seat puts you in reach of the jokes.
