body: The UTC Mocs women's basketball team hosts Radford at McKenzie Arena. Radford plays in the Big South Conference out of Radford, Virginia. This mid-December game is part of a stretch of home matchups before the holiday break. McKenzie Arena is on the UTC campus on McCallie Avenue. Tipoff is at 5pm. Tickets are available through gomocs.com or the arena box office.

title: UTC Mocs Women's Basketball vs Samford
description: UTC Mocs women's basketball hosts Samford at McKenzie Arena on December 29.
body: The UTC Mocs women's basketball team hosts Samford at McKenzie Arena. Samford competes in the Southern Conference out of Birmingham, Alabama. This late-December home game falls during winter break but SoCon matchups carry conference standing weight. McKenzie Arena is on the UTC campus on McCallie Avenue. Tipoff is at 6pm. Tickets are available through gomocs.com or the arena box office.

title: UTC Mocs Women's Basketball vs Tennessee State
description: UTC Mocs women's basketball hosts Tennessee State at McKenzie Arena on December 18.
body: The UTC Mocs women's basketball team hosts Tennessee State at McKenzie Arena. Tennessee State plays in the SWAC out of Nashville. The two in-state programs do not meet every season, making this a notable non-conference matchup. McKenzie Arena seats around 11,000 on the UTC campus on McCallie Avenue. Tipoff is at 6pm. Tickets are available at gomocs.com or through the arena box office.

title: UTC Mocs Women's Basketball vs Tennessee Tech
description: UTC Mocs women's basketball hosts Tennessee Tech at McKenzie Arena on February 6.
body: The UTC Mocs women's basketball team hosts Tennessee Tech at McKenzie Arena. Tennessee Tech plays in the ASUN Conference out of Cookeville, Tennessee. These in-state programs do not share a conference but the matchup draws fans from across the region. McKenzie Arena seats around 11,000 on the UTC campus on McCallie Avenue. Tipoff is at 2pm. Tickets are available at gomocs.com or through the arena box office.

title: UTC Mocs Women's Basketball vs UNC Greensboro
description: UTC Mocs women's basketball hosts UNC Greensboro at McKenzie Arena on January 16.
body: The UTC Mocs women's basketball team hosts UNC Greensboro at McKenzie Arena. UNCG plays in the Southern Conference out of Greensboro, North Carolina. Weekend afternoon games at McKenzie Arena draw a mix of students and local fans. The arena is on the UTC campus on McCallie Avenue and seats around 11,000. Tipoff is at 2pm. Tickets are available through gomocs.com or the arena box office.

title: UTC Mocs Women's Basketball vs Western Carolina
description: UTC Mocs women's basketball hosts Western Carolina at McKenzie Arena on January 23.
body: The UTC Mocs women's basketball team hosts Western Carolina at McKenzie Arena. Western Carolina is based in Cullowhee, North Carolina and competes in the Southern Conference. Conference standings tighten through January and each home win matters. McKenzie Arena is on the UTC campus on McCallie Avenue and seats around 11,000. Tipoff is at 2pm. Tickets are available at gomocs.com or through the arena box office.

title: UTC Mocs Women's Basketball vs Wofford
description: UTC Mocs women's basketball hosts Wofford at McKenzie Arena on February 23.
body: The UTC Mocs women's basketball team hosts Wofford at McKenzie Arena. Wofford plays in the Southern Conference out of Spartanburg, South Carolina. This late-February game comes near the end of the regular season, when every conference win affects tournament seeding. McKenzie Arena is on the UTC campus on McCallie Avenue and seats around 11,000. Tipoff is at 6pm. Tickets are available at gomocs.com or through the arena box office.

title: UTC Mocs Wrestling: Southern Scuffle
description: Chattanooga hosts the Southern Scuffle wrestling tournament at McKenzie Arena on January 2 and 3.
body: The Mocs host the Southern Scuffle at McKenzie Arena over two days. The event draws nationally ranked Division I wrestling programs from across the country. Mat action starts at 9am on Saturday, January 2. Medal matches run at 3pm on Sunday, January 3. Many of the nation's top wrestlers compete across all weight classes. McKenzie Arena sits on the UTC campus on McCallie Avenue. Buy tickets at the arena box office or through gomocs.com. Arrive early for parking, since the two-day tournament runs long sessions.

title: UTC Mocs Wrestling vs Bellarmine
description: UTC Mocs wrestling hosts Bellarmine in a Southern Conference dual at Maclellan Gym on February 21.
body: The Mocs host Bellarmine in a Southern Conference dual at Maclellan Gym. The Knights wrestle out of Louisville, Kentucky. This Sunday dual closes the regular season at home. Senior wrestlers often get recognized at the final home match of the year. The result carries weight for conference tournament seeding. Maclellan Gym sits on the UTC campus on McCallie Avenue and gives fans a close view of the mat. Buy tickets at the door or through gomocs.com. Check gomocs.com to confirm the start time before you go.

title: UTC Mocs Wrestling vs Campbell
description: UTC Mocs wrestling hosts Campbell in a Southern Conference dual at Maclellan Gym on February 13.
body: The Mocs host Campbell in a Southern Conference dual at Maclellan Gym. The Fighting Camels wrestle out of Buies Creek, North Carolina. The dual starts at 7pm on Saturday night. This match closes a home weekend that opens with VMI on Friday. Campbell is a strong SoCon program and the result shapes conference seeding. Maclellan Gym sits on the UTC campus on McCallie Avenue. Buy tickets at the door or through gomocs.com. The gym seats fewer fans than the arena, so arrive early for a good spot.

title: UTC Mocs Wrestling vs Gardner-Webb
description: UTC Mocs wrestling hosts Gardner-Webb in a Southern Conference dual at Maclellan Gym on January 29.
body: The Mocs host Gardner-Webb in a Southern Conference dual at Maclellan Gym. The Runnin' Bulldogs wrestle out of Boiling Springs, North Carolina. The dual starts at 7pm on Friday night. SoCon duals count toward conference standing and seeding for the league tournament. Maclellan Gym gives fans a close view of the action on the UTC campus on McCallie Avenue. Buy tickets at the door or through gomocs.com. The gym is smaller than the arena, so seats fill fast for conference matchups.

title: UTC Mocs Wrestling vs VMI
description: UTC Mocs wrestling hosts VMI in a Southern Conference dual at Maclellan Gym on February 12.
body: The Mocs host VMI in a Southern Conference dual at Maclellan Gym. The Keydets wrestle out of Lexington, Virginia. The dual starts at 7pm on Friday night. This match opens a home weekend that also features Campbell the next day. SoCon duals carry direct standing and seeding stakes late in the season. Maclellan Gym sits on the UTC campus on McCallie Avenue and puts fans right on top of the mat. Buy tickets at the door or through gomocs.com. Come early to get a seat for the conference dual.

title: The Walker Theatre
description: Touring concerts, comedy, and live events at The Walker Theatre, a restored 1921 venue on Broad Street.
body: A restored 1921 theater on Broad Street seating around 1,700. Hosts touring concerts, comedy, and live events. The Walker Theatre is one of the premier mid-size venues in Chattanooga. The building underwent a full restoration and reopened as a modern concert and event venue while preserving its historic interior details. The main floor and balcony provide good sightlines from most seats. Parking is available in nearby garages and lots on Broad Street. Check the venue website for the current event calendar. The Walker Theatre books national touring acts across music, comedy, and special events.

title: Beast Feast
description: Chef Carolyn smokes a whole hog, lamb ribs, frog legs, and sausage at WanderLinger Brewing on October 3. Mud wrestling and live music run all day.
body: Chef Carolyn fires up the smoker at WanderLinger on October 3. She smokes an entire hog, plus lamb ribs, frog legs, and smoked sausage. The feast starts at 1pm and the food keeps coming. Mud wrestling adds to the spectacle through the afternoon. Live music plays all day and into the night. Pour a fresh beer on Station Street and stay for the whole event.

title: Brina Palencia
description: Voice actress and performer Brina Palencia takes the stage at WanderLinger Brewing on November 7.
body: Brina Palencia is a voice actress known for anime roles, including Chopper in One Piece. She also performs as a singer and songwriter. This show brings her music to WanderLinger on the Choo Choo property in downtown Chattanooga. Palencia has performed at anime conventions and music venues nationally. Her music draws from pop, folk, and theatrical styles. WanderLinger is a craft brewery with a stage. Check the venue for ticket details and start time. This is a crossover event that attracts both anime fans and general live music audiences.

title: Dead Cover Office
description: Dead Cover Office plays Grateful Dead classics at WanderLinger Brewing on November 7 at 6pm. No cover, all ages, in Chattanooga's Southside.
body: Dead Cover Office brings the Grateful Dead songbook to WanderLinger on November 7 from 6 to 9pm. Expect fan favorites and plenty of improvisational jams. Dead Cover Office is a Chattanooga-area band dedicated to the Dead catalog. Their sets pull from the full breadth of the Grateful Dead discography - early psychedelic material, country-influenced songs, and the extended jam pieces from the band's touring years. WanderLinger is a craft brewery on the Choo Choo property in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue for ticket details and start time.

title: Four DJs Go Head to Head
description: Four DJs compete head to head at WanderLinger Brewing on October 18. Your live votes pick who earns direct support for Heritage.
body: Four DJs battle head to head at WanderLinger on October 18. Your live votes decide the winner. The champion earns direct support for Heritage at the October 9 warehouse party. A best-dressed baseball contest runs alongside the sets. Expect surprise giveaways through the night. Doors open at 8pm and the music starts at 9. The first 25 tickets cost $10.

title: Halloween Vintage Bazaar
description: The Halloween Vintage Bazaar brings local vendors and vintage finds to the Choo Choo Gardens on October 31.
body: The Halloween Vintage Bazaar brings local vendors to the Choo Choo Gardens next to WanderLinger. Shop vintage clothing, handmade goods, and one-of-a-kind Halloween items. The outdoor setting at the Choo Choo property gives the event a festive atmosphere. No ticket required to browse. WanderLinger pours craft beer nearby. Check the WanderLinger social pages for vendor details and event hours. Costumes are welcome. The bazaar draws sellers and shoppers from across Chattanooga. This is a good option for finding unique Halloween pieces or early holiday gifts from local makers.

title: Karaoke
description: Free karaoke night at WanderLinger Brewing on September 5 at 7:30pm. Grab a mic and a beer on Chattanooga's Station Street.
body: Karaoke comes to WanderLinger on September 5 from 7:30 to 10:30pm. Pick the song you sing best and take the mic with your friends. There is no cover, and WanderLinger pours craft beer through the evening. The craft brewery is on the Choo Choo property in downtown Chattanooga. Karaoke here is casual and fun - the room is set up for participation over performance. All skill levels welcome. Check the WanderLinger social pages for any updates to the karaoke schedule. This is a weekly or regular event - check the page for recurring dates.

title: MAINx24 & 5th Annual Highland Games
description: WanderLinger hosts its 5th Annual Highland Games during MAINx24 on December 5. Stein holding, Highland challenges, and live music from 6pm.
body: WanderLinger runs its 5th Annual Highland Games on December 5 during MAINx24. The festival takes over Chattanooga's Southside for 24 hours, and this is the brewery's corner of it. The day features games and challenges for everyone, including the popular Stein Holding Competition. Live music starts at 6pm. The Bohannons play from 6 to 8pm, bringing their heavy Southern rock built from punk, metal, and country roots. The Chattanooga band has toured for more than 20 years. Danimal & Friends take over from 9pm to 1am. Admission is free, so arrive early if you want a spot near the stage.

title: Malört for the Mutts: Drink for a Good Cause
description: Malört for the Mutts runs December 18 to 20 at WanderLinger. Every Malört shot sends $1 to McKamey Animal Center in Chattanooga.
body: WanderLinger raises money for local animals from December 18 to 20. For every shot of Malört sold, the brewery donates $1 to McKamey Animal Center. The center cares for homeless dogs and cats across Chattanooga. Malört is a bitter Chicago liqueur with a reputation for strong reactions. That is the point. Order a shot, pull a face, and help a shelter animal. There is no cover charge. Stop in across all three days on Station Street in the Southside.

title: Metal Show
description: PLVNET, TEMPUS, and OVERSIGHT bring a loud metal night to WanderLinger Brewing on September 26. Doors at 9:30pm, $10 cover.
body: Three heavy acts take over WanderLinger on September 26. PLVNET, TEMPUS, and OVERSIGHT play live, trading riffs and running the room loud late into the night. All three are Chattanooga-area metal and hard rock acts. WanderLinger is a craft brewery on the Choo Choo property in downtown Chattanooga. The venue hosts regular live music events across genres. Check the venue for ticket details and start time. This is a local metal bill that draws the Chattanooga heavy music community together. Expect loud, guitar-driven sets from all three acts across the evening.

title: Nightmare on 80's Street
description: Hair Force One plays 80s hair metal at WanderLinger Brewing on Halloween night. Costume party runs from 10pm to 1am in Chattanooga's Southside.
body: Hair Force One takes over WanderLinger on Halloween night with a tribute to 80s hair metal. The five-piece band rips through head-banging hits from Van Halen, AC/DC, and the rest of the big-hair era. Wear a costume and join the party from 10pm to 1am. Cover is $10 at the door. WanderLinger is a craft brewery on the Choo Choo property in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue for ticket details and start time.

title: Nooga Vintage Bazaar
description: The Nooga Vintage Bazaar brings vintage clothing, goods, and a DJ to WanderLinger Brewing on September 27.
body: The Nooga Vintage Bazaar fills WanderLinger with vintage finds. Vendors sell vintage clothing, handmade goods, jewelry, and accessories. DJ Minks spins throughout the event. WanderLinger is a craft brewery on the Choo Choo property in downtown Chattanooga. The bazaar draws local and regional vendors. No ticket required to attend and browse. Check the WanderLinger social pages for the vendor list and specific event hours. The indoor and outdoor spaces at WanderLinger give vendors room to set up without crowding. Bring cash - many vintage vendors prefer it.

title: Scratch the Surface
description: Scratch the Surface brings a night of EDM and dancing to WanderLinger Brewing on October 3. Doors and beats start at 9pm on Station Street.
body: Scratch the Surface fills WanderLinger with EDM on October 3. The night runs on heavy beats and open floor space. Dancers take over as the sets build through the evening. The music starts at 9pm and keeps the room moving. Grab a cold pint on Station Street and find your spot near the speakers. This one is built for good vibes and late nights.

title: Scream Its Halloween at WanderLinger
description: WanderLinger Brewing throws a Halloween night party with live music and a costume contest with cash prizes. Doors at 9pm in Chattanooga's Southside.
body: WanderLinger hosts a Halloween night bash with live music and a packed dance floor. A costume contest hands out cash prizes to the best outfits of the evening. Live music runs through the night on the Choo Choo property. WanderLinger is a craft brewery in downtown Chattanooga. The Halloween party draws a crowd in costume from across the city. Check the venue social pages for the live music lineup, ticket details, and costume contest rules. Prizes go to multiple categories. The event runs into the late hours on October 31. Costumes are strongly encouraged.

title: Station FREQ
description: Station FREQ brings drum & bass and heavy bass to WanderLinger Brewing on October 16 at 9pm. Lineup includes Ployd, Heelwalker, Era-Step, and Kope.
body: Station FREQ runs a full night of drum & bass, heavy bass, and underground sounds at WanderLinger on October 16. The lineup features Ployd, Heelwalker, Era-Step, Kope, and a secret DNB headliner. Doors open at 9pm and the music runs late to 2am. Entry is $10 before midnight and $20 after. WanderLinger is a craft brewery on the Choo Choo property in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue for ticket details and start time.

title: The Halem Albright Band
description: The Halem Albright Band plays WanderLinger Brewing on November 27 at 8pm. Doors at 8, $10 cover, in Chattanooga's Southside.
body: The Halem Albright Band plays WanderLinger on November 27. Doors open at 8pm and the cover is $10. The Atlanta five-piece blends jazz, funk, jangle pop, indie rock, and folk. Halem Albright writes the songs and leads on guitar and vocals. The band draws on classic jam influences and leans into high-energy live sets. Catch them on Station Street in Chattanooga's Southside.

title: The Loop
description: The Loop brings nearly 70 vintage motorcycles from 1930 to 1959 to WanderLinger Brewing on September 6. Vendors, an artisan market, and live music.
body: The Loop rolls into WanderLinger on September 6 from 2 to 8pm with nearly 70 vintage motorcycles built between 1930 and 1959. Vintage vendors and an artisan market fill out the day. Gino Fanelli plays live at 5pm, so grab a beer on Station Street and take it all in. WanderLinger is a craft brewery on the Choo Choo property in downtown Chattanooga. No ticket required to attend and view the motorcycles. Check social pages for event hours.

title: Year of October
description: Nashville fuzz rock soul band Year of October plays WanderLinger Brewing on October 30. All ages.
body: Year of October is a fuzz rock soul band from Nashville. The trio pairs heavy, fuzzed-out riffs with powerful, soulful vocals. Fans describe their sound as Black Sabbath meets Amy Winehouse. They bring a loud, high-energy live show to WanderLinger. Music runs from 5 to 8pm. The show is all ages. WanderLinger is a craft brewery on the Choo Choo property in downtown Chattanooga. Check the venue for ticket details and start time.

title: World of Wheels Chattanooga
description: World of Wheels is an annual indoor automotive show at the Chattanooga Convention Center. The 59th edition runs January 8-10, 2027 with custom cars, hot rods, and motorcycles competing in ISCA-sanctioned judging.
body: Custom cars, hot rods, and motorcycles fill the Chattanooga Convention Center floor each January for the World of Wheels. The 59th edition runs January 8 through 10, 2027, across 110,000 square feet. Friday hours are 3 to 9pm, Saturday 10am to 9pm, and Sunday 10am to 6pm. Cars are judged for condition, design, and craftsmanship under ISCA rules. Advance tickets are $14 for adults and $5 for kids ages 6 through 11. Buy at worldofwheels.net to save over gate prices.

title: Forever Friday Bluegrass
description: Every Friday at 8pm at The Woodshop Listening Room in St. Elmo. Rotating regional musicians playing traditional bluegrass. $5 cover.
body: Regional musicians rotating through The Woodshop every Friday night in St. Elmo. Traditional bluegrass in a small listening room with a close stage. The rotating format means the lineup changes week to week, drawing from the strong Chattanooga-area acoustic music community. Expect banjo, fiddle, mandolin, guitar, and upright bass in tight bluegrass arrangements. The Woodshop on St. Elmo Avenue has hosted weekly bluegrass nights for years. Doors open at 5pm. Music typically starts at 6pm. Check the venue's social pages for the weekly artist announcement.

title: Scenic City Soul Night
description: Scenic City Soul Night every Thursday at 8pm at The Woodshop Listening Room. Bryant 'Bass Hitter' Russell brings '70s Motown, jazz, and smooth soul. $10 cover.
body: Bryant 'Bass Hitter' Russell and his band bring the groove every Thursday at The Woodshop in St. Elmo. The setlist runs through classic soul, funk, and R&B. Russell is a Chattanooga-area musician and bandleader known for his driving bass lines and energetic live shows. The Thursday night residency pulls from acts like James Brown, Sly Stone, and Al Green. The Woodshop is an intimate listening room on St. Elmo Avenue. The small stage puts the band close to the crowd. Check the venue for cover charge and start time.

title: Jhett Black's Tuesday Bluesday
description: Jhett Black's Tuesday Bluesday every Tuesday at 6pm at The Woodshop Listening Room. Live blues, rock 'n' roll, and American roots music. $10 cover.
body: Jhett Black plays blues every Tuesday night at The Woodshop in St. Elmo. Small room, close sound, doors at 8pm. $10 cover. Black is a Chattanooga-area guitarist and vocalist who plays electric blues and soul. The Tuesday night residency gives local blues fans a consistent weekly option in a listening room setting. The Woodshop is an intimate venue on St. Elmo Avenue. The cover includes the music and the room. Bar service runs all night. No reservations needed - walk in and find a table or lean against the wall near the stage.

title: Woodshop Trivia
description: Free trivia every Tuesday at 8pm at The Woodshop Listening Room in St. Elmo. Hosted by Rebekah Cecil with prizes and food specials.
body: Free trivia every Tuesday at 8pm at The Woodshop in St. Elmo, hosted by Rebekah Cecil. Prizes and food specials on the night. The trivia format runs multiple rounds covering music, pop culture, history, and general knowledge. Teams of up to six compete for prizes. Cecil has hosted the weekly night for multiple seasons and keeps the rounds fresh. The Woodshop is a small listening room on St. Elmo Avenue that doubles as a neighborhood bar on trivia nights. No cover. Walk in, form a team, and play.

title: 2nd Annual Bilbo's Birthday Bash - Day 2
description: Night two of the 2nd Annual Bilbo's Birthday Bash at The Woodshop on September 27: an instrumental performance from Innman & The Prancing Ponies, costume contest, and themed feast.
body: The second night of the LOTR celebration leans instrumental, with Innman & The Prancing Ponies, another costume contest, and the full hobbit menu. Night two of the event tends to draw the more dedicated fans. The band plays a setlist that leans into traditional folk tunes and original compositions inspired by Middle-earth. The Woodshop in St. Elmo is a close, intimate venue on St. Elmo Avenue. The costume contest runs alongside the music with cash prizes for best outfit. Check the venue for ticket details and start time.

title: 2nd Annual Bilbo's Birthday Bash - Day 3
description: Night three of the 2nd Annual Bilbo's Birthday Bash at The Woodshop on September 28, with a performance from Innman & The Prancing Ponies.
body: The third and final night of the Lord of the Rings celebration in St. Elmo. Innman & The Prancing Ponies perform again, closing out three nights of Tolkien-themed music and merriment. The final night typically draws the largest crowd of the three-day run. The hobbit-inspired menu and elven cocktails continue through the evening. A costume contest closes the weekend. The Woodshop is a small listening room on St. Elmo Avenue in Chattanooga. Check the venue for tickets and start time.

title: 2nd Annual Bilbo's Birthday Bash
description: 2nd Annual Bilbo's Birthday Bash at The Woodshop on September 26: a Lord of the Rings themed night with Innman & The Prancing Ponies, costume contest, hobbit menu, and elven cocktails. Sold out.
body: A Lord of the Rings themed party with Innman & The Prancing Ponies, a costume contest, a hobbit-inspired menu, and elven cocktails at The Woodshop in St. Elmo. This is the second year of the event. The band plays original music inspired by Tolkien's world alongside traditional folk and Americana. Cash prizes go to the best costumes. The menu runs all evening alongside a full bar. The Woodshop is a small listening room on St. Elmo Avenue in Chattanooga. Check the venue for tickets and start time.

title: A LVNDR Christmas
description: A LVNDR Christmas at The Woodshop Listening Room on December 12 and 13. Chattanooga neo-soul and funk band plays two holiday nights in St. Elmo.
body: LVNDR plays two holiday nights at The Woodshop in St. Elmo on December 12 and 13. The Chattanooga band blends neo-soul, R&B, and psychedelic funk under vocalist Maria Jordania. They competed on Season 21 of America's Got Talent and drew praise from every judge. A holiday menu runs both nights, and cocktail attire is encouraged. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Alma Russ
description: Alma Russ at The Woodshop Listening Room on January 29. The western North Carolina musician plays folk, bluegrass, and mountain ballads in St. Elmo.
body: Alma Russ plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on January 29. The western North Carolina musician blends folk, bluegrass, and mountain ballads. She plays fiddle, claw-hammer banjo, and guitar. Russ learned Scotch-Irish murder ballads as a child and took up fiddle at age twelve. She auditioned for American Idol in 2017 and earned praise from all three judges. Lionel Richie compared her to Dolly Parton. She released her first full album, Next Town, in 2020. Her Appalachian sound fits the intimate stage. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Anywhere, Suddenly
description: Anywhere, Suddenly at The Woodshop on November 8. A one-man play by Jason Tinney that blends storytelling, live music, and film. Matinee and dinner shows.
body: Jason Tinney performs this original one-man play in St. Elmo. The piece mixes storytelling, live music, and film into an Appalachian folk and alt-country road story. Kashun Parks directs and Jason Hackbarth scores the music. The work earned an ArtsBuild Artists Work in Partnership grant. Choose the matinee with doors at 1pm or the dinner show with doors at 6pm.

title: Ashes & Arrows
description: Ashes & Arrows at The Woodshop Listening Room on February 11. A country-folk trio with tight three-part harmonies in the intimate St. Elmo room.
body: Ashes & Arrows play The Woodshop in St. Elmo on February 11. The trio formed at an Asheville open mic in 2021. Members come from North Carolina and Arrowtown, New Zealand. Their sound blends country, Americana, and folk with tight three-part harmonies. They reached the semi-finals of America's Got Talent in 2024. The small listening room suits their close vocal blend. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Bird and Byron
description: Bird and Byron at The Woodshop Listening Room on January 28. The Nashville indie rock and soul duo plays the intimate St. Elmo listening room.
body: Bird and Byron play The Woodshop in St. Elmo on January 28. Blake Bird and Nick Byron are a Nashville indie rock and soul duo. They write warm, harmony-driven songs with a haunting edge. The pair reached the America's Got Talent quarterfinals and draw more than 180,000 monthly Spotify listeners. Their close vocals suit this small listening room well. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Brother and The Hayes
description: Brother and The Hayes at The Woodshop Listening Room on January 31. Texas-born, Nashville-based sibling duo playing Americana, folk, country, and blues in St. Elmo.
body: Brother and The Hayes play The Woodshop in St. Elmo on January 31. The Texas-born, Nashville-based duo pairs siblings Jeb and Seth Hayes with tight harmony and Americana songwriting. Their songs draw from country, folk, and gospel roots. The brothers have toured nationally and built a following in the Texas and Tennessee listening room circuit. The Woodshop is an intimate venue on St. Elmo Avenue that suits close, harmony-based performances. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Cory Branan
description: Cory Branan at The Woodshop Listening Room on November 15. A critically acclaimed singer-songwriter live in the intimate St. Elmo listening room.
body: Cory Branan plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on November 15. The critically acclaimed singer-songwriter fits the small listening room perfectly. Branan is from Memphis and writes in a style that spans punk folk, country, and Americana. He has released albums on Bloodshot Records and worked with producers across Nashville and Memphis. His songs are fast and dense with imagery. Jon Langford and others in the alt-country world have praised his writing. He plays solo or with a small band. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Daniel Kimbro & Sam Lewis
description: Daniel Kimbro and Sam Lewis at The Woodshop on November 12, a collaborative evening of songwriting about place, time, and the human experience.
body: Daniel Kimbro and Sam Lewis share a stage in St. Elmo for a night of collaborative songwriting. The set digs into place, time, and the human experience. Kimbro is a Nashville-based bassist and composer who has played with Alison Krauss, Sheryl Crow, and Hozier. Lewis is a Nashville songwriter with releases on Thirty Tigers. His songs draw on Southern literature and American folk tradition. Both artists cross genres easily. This one plays well in a small listening room. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: David Grier
description: Flatpick guitar great David Grier at The Woodshop on September 5, a three-time IBMA Guitar Player of the Year.
body: David Grier is widely regarded as one of the finest flatpick guitarists around - a three-time IBMA Guitar Player of the Year. He plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo. Grier grew up in a musical family in Virginia and has recorded multiple solo albums. His playing blends traditional bluegrass with jazz and swing influences. He has toured and recorded with Alison Krauss and others in the acoustic music world. The small room at The Woodshop puts the audience close to the guitar. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Derrick Dove & The Peacekeepers
description: Derrick Dove & The Peacekeepers at The Woodshop Listening Room on March 20. The award-winning Southern blues rock band plays St. Elmo.
body: Derrick Dove & The Peacekeepers play The Woodshop in St. Elmo on March 20. The South Georgia band mixes blues, soul, classic rock, and Southern spirit. Derrick Dove leads on guitar and vocals. In January 2026 the band won the International Blues Challenge in Memphis. Dove also took Best Guitarist honors there. Their albums Rough Time and Burn It Down topped the iTunes blues chart. They have shared stages with ZZ Top and Blackberry Smoke. Expect a high-energy set in the small room. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: DVL Blues Legends
description: DVL Blues Legends with The DVL Revue at The Woodshop on September 19. A high-energy tribute to Muddy Waters, John Lee Hooker, Howlin' Wolf, and B.B. King.
body: The DVL Revue returns with a high-energy blues tribute in St. Elmo. The set honors Muddy Waters, John Lee Hooker, Howlin' Wolf, and others who built the Chicago and Delta blues tradition. The DVL Revue is a Chattanooga-area band with a deep catalog of blues and soul. Their arrangements stay faithful to the originals while keeping the room moving. The Woodshop is a small venue on St. Elmo Avenue where blues guitar fills the whole space. Check the venue for start time and door price.

title: E.G. Kight
description: E.G. Kight at The Woodshop Listening Room on February 6. The Georgia Songbird plays blues, soul, and roots music in the intimate St. Elmo room.
body: E.G. Kight plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on February 6. Known as the Georgia Songbird, she sings blues, soul, and roots music. Her grandmother taught her guitar at age five. She turned to the blues after hearing Koko Taylor. Kight has shared stages and worked with B.B. King, Taj Mahal, and Pinetop Perkins. Her 2008 album It's Hot in Here topped the roots blues chart. She still lives on family land in Dublin, Georgia. The small room suits her sweet, Southern voice. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Freedom Sings USA Concert
description: A free Freedom Sings USA benefit concert with DANIMAL and more comes to The Woodshop Listening Room on November 7.
body: Freedom Sings USA hosts a benefit concert at The Woodshop. The lineup features DANIMAL, The Essentials, Blake Worthington, and others. Freedom Sings USA is an organization that uses music to advocate for First Amendment rights. Each show raises funds for programs that connect students with working musicians and free speech education. The Woodshop on St. Elmo Avenue is a small listening venue with a close stage. This show spans multiple artists and runs most of the evening. Check the venue for ticket details and start time.

title: Goldpine
description: Nashville Americana duo Goldpine at The Woodshop on September 13, known for bold harmonies and 'aggressive Americana'.
body: Goldpine is a Nashville husband-and-wife duo trading bold harmonies in what they call 'aggressive Americana.' The pair is Jamie Lin Wilson and Jonny Burke. Wilson is a Texas singer-songwriter and longtime member of The Trishas. Burke is a Texas-born guitarist and producer. Together they write songs that sit at the intersection of classic country and Americana. The small room at The Woodshop in St. Elmo suits their sound well. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Hayde
description: Norwegian bluegrass and Nordic folk group Hayde plays The Woodshop Listening Room on November 4.
body: Hayde is a seven-piece group from Norway that blends bluegrass with Nordic folk. Their sound pairs tight harmonies with fiddles, mandolin, and guitar in arrangements that feel both old and new. The group has toured Europe and the United States, playing festivals and listening rooms. Their albums have earned praise from both Scandinavian folk and American Americana audiences. The Woodshop in St. Elmo is a small, close room where the band's layered arrangements come through clearly. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Jake Blount
description: Performer and scholar Jake Blount at The Woodshop on September 9, a player of Black folk music who's appeared at Carnegie Hall and Newport Folk Festival.
body: Jake Blount is both a performer and a scholar of Black folk music, with stops at Carnegie Hall and the Newport Folk Festival. He plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo. Blount plays banjo and fiddle and builds his sets from the African American string band tradition. His album Spider Tales won the IBMA award for Emerging Artist. He has studied and performed traditional music alongside ethnomusicological research. The Woodshop is a small listening room in St. Elmo that suits this kind of close, careful playing. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Jill Andrews
description: Jill Andrews at The Woodshop Listening Room on January 22. The Nashville Americana singer-songwriter and former Everybodyfields member plays St. Elmo.
body: Jill Andrews plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on January 22. The Nashville singer-songwriter writes indie folk and Americana. She co-founded the band The Everybodyfields in Knoxville before going solo in 2009. That band played Bonnaroo and the Kennedy Center and toured with the Avett Brothers. Her solo records build broader arrangements on top of her roots sound. Her songs have appeared in shows like Grey's Anatomy and Nashville. The close listening room suits her clear voice and detailed writing. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Joe Kaplow
description: California singer-songwriter Joe Kaplow at The Woodshop on September 9. Personal narrative rooted in farm life and ocean living.
body: Joe Kaplow writes from specific places - California farm life, the coast - and the specificity is what makes it work. Singer, guitarist, and songwriter based in Northern California, Kaplow builds Americana and folk songs from quiet, observed details. His albums feature spare arrangements that keep the focus on the lyric. He tours nationally and plays listening room venues like The Woodshop in St. Elmo. The small room on St. Elmo Avenue puts the audience close enough to hear every word. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Joe Pug
description: Joe Pug at The Woodshop Listening Room on January 30. Austin singer-songwriter playing folk and Americana with Brother and The Hayes in St. Elmo.
body: Joe Pug plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on January 30. The Austin songwriter writes acoustic folk and Americana built on strong lyrical craft. Pug has released multiple albums on Nashville's Lightning Rod Records and toured with artists including Josh Ritter and Neko Case. Critics have drawn comparisons to early Bob Dylan and John Prine for his plainspoken precision. His live show is solo or small band and works best in intimate rooms. The Woodshop on St. Elmo Avenue holds a small crowd close to the stage. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Jonathan Peyton
description: Georgia singer-songwriter Jonathan Peyton at The Woodshop on October 3, with Hunter Blalock opening.
body: Jonathan Peyton is an independent Georgia singer-songwriter who leans on emotionally resonant storytelling. Hunter Blalock opens the show. Peyton writes in the folk and Americana tradition, with songs built around specific moments and places. His voice is warm and direct. Blalock is a Chattanooga-area singer-songwriter who has opened for numerous national acts at The Woodshop. This is a seated listening room show on St. Elmo Avenue. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Josh Harp
description: Chattanooga-born blues musician Josh Harp plays a homecoming show at The Woodshop Listening Room on November 28.
body: Josh Harp is a Chattanooga-born blues musician who also works as an actor and educator. He plays soulful blues rooted in the Delta and Chicago traditions. Harp has performed in theater productions and appeared in film and television roles. On stage as a musician, he focuses on acoustic and electric blues with strong original songwriting. His live shows are known for warmth and audience engagement. The Woodshop in St. Elmo is an intimate listening room where his storytelling lands close to the crowd. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Katie Lynne Sharbaugh
description: Katie Lynne Sharbaugh at The Woodshop Listening Room on January 8. The Nashville singer-songwriter blends jazz, pop, and soul storytelling in St. Elmo.
body: Katie Lynne Sharbaugh plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on January 8. The Nashville singer-songwriter fuses pop with jazz and R&B. She studied at Berklee College of Music and plays violin, viola, and piano. Her songs pair the nostalgia of 1970s soul with modern storytelling. She first learned Irish fiddle tunes by ear at a summer home in Ireland. Sharbaugh released her debut EP Little Blue Beetle Volume 1 in 2021. Her later work includes the concept album Upstaged. The intimate stage fits her cinematic, melodic sound. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Laid Back Country Picker
description: Outlaw country artist Laid Back Country Picker plays The Woodshop Listening Room on December 4.
body: Laid Back Country Picker is David Prince, a singer-songwriter from Louisa, Kentucky. His sound blends '70s guitar rock, honky-tonk, and country punk. He plays with his partner Honey and brings a loud, driving show. Prince has played the Ryman, Bonnaroo, and Red Rocks, and he spins on Sirius Outlaw Country Radio. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Leilani Kilgore
description: Blues-rock guitarist Leilani Kilgore brings searing guitar work and soulful vocals to The Woodshop Listening Room in St. Elmo on November 14, 2026.
body: Leilani Kilgore is a blues-rock guitarist known for searing guitar work and soulful vocals. Her sets pair big, driving riffs with a strong, expressive voice. The Woodshop is a small listening room in St. Elmo, so the guitar tone fills the space and nothing gets lost. Kilgore has toured nationally and built a following in the blues and roots rock community. She draws comparisons to artists like Bonnie Raitt and Susan Tedeschi for her combination of guitar skill and vocal range. Doors at 6pm. Check the venue page for ticket details.

title: Maggie Koerner
description: Maggie Koerner at The Woodshop Listening Room on November 5. A powerhouse vocalist on her UPSTATE tour, live in the St. Elmo listening room.
body: Maggie Koerner brings her powerhouse voice to The Woodshop in St. Elmo on her UPSTATE tour. It is a small listening room well suited to her vocal range. Koerner is a New Orleans-based singer and songwriter who blends Southern soul, gospel, and rock. She has toured with Anders Osborne and recorded in New Orleans studios. Her voice sits in a low, rich register and fills rooms easily. The UPSTATE tour marks new material after a period of recording. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Magic Birds
description: Magic Birds play Americana blending classic country, bluegrass, folk, and soul at The Woodshop Listening Room in St. Elmo on October 30, 2026.
body: Magic Birds are an Americana duo who pull from classic country, bluegrass, folk, and soul. Their songs mix old-time roots with a modern pop sensibility. The duo is based in Nashville and has released multiple recordings. Their vocal harmonies sit at the core of the arrangements. Magic Birds have played listening rooms and festivals across the Southeast and Midwest. The Woodshop in St. Elmo is a close venue where their blend of traditional and contemporary Americana comes through without amplification barriers. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Mama's Broke
description: Canadian Folk Music Award winners Mama's Broke at The Woodshop on November 13, with haunting harmonies and deep folk traditions.
body: Mama's Broke are Canadian Folk Music Award winners known for haunting vocal harmonies rooted in older folk traditions. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. The duo is Lisa Marie Bogert and Amy Lou Sherrill. They draw from Celtic, Appalachian, and Eastern European folk music. Their vocals interlock in a way that is rare in the genre. They have toured internationally and performed at major folk festivals across Canada and the United States. The Woodshop in St. Elmo is a small listening room where their harmonies carry across every corner. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Martha Spencer
description: Appalachian roots musician Martha Spencer plays guitar, fiddle, banjo, bass, and dulcimer at The Woodshop Listening Room in St. Elmo on November 21, 2026.
body: Martha Spencer is an Appalachian roots musician who plays guitar, fiddle, banjo, bass, and dulcimer. Her music draws on traditional mountain music from the Virginia and North Carolina highlands. Spencer grew up in Whitetop, Virginia, in a family with deep roots in Appalachian music. She has performed at the Kennedy Center and appeared on recordings with Ralph Stanley and other traditional artists. She teaches and advocates for the preservation of old-time music. The Woodshop in St. Elmo is a close listening room that suits traditional acoustic performance. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Mary McGuinness
description: Mary McGuinness at The Woodshop Listening Room on December 10. Nashville folk-Americana singer blending Laurel Canyon style with classic country in St. Elmo.
body: Mary McGuinness plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on December 10. The Nashville singer blends folk-Americana, Laurel Canyon, and singer-songwriter traditions. McGuinness writes songs built around clear images and direct emotion. Her voice sits in a warm, mid-range register. She has released recordings and toured the Southeast and Midwest. The Woodshop is an intimate listening room on St. Elmo Avenue where her acoustic sound fills the space. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Max Gomez
description: Max Gomez at The Woodshop Listening Room on December 9. Taos, New Mexico singer-songwriter playing Americana and folk in the St. Elmo listening room.
body: Max Gomez plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on December 9. The Taos, New Mexico songwriter writes Americana and folk with a southwestern edge. Gomez grew up between New Mexico and Missouri and has released several albums including work with producer Shooter Jennings. His songs pull from classic country, folk, and acoustic rock. He has toured with artists including Brandi Carlile and Neko Case. The small room at The Woodshop puts the audience within a few feet of his guitar. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Mid America
description: Western folk rock duo Mid America at The Woodshop on September 18: Mia Carruthers and Curtis Roush with '70s-influenced songwriting.
body: Mid America pairs Mia Carruthers and Curtis Roush for a western folk rock set steeped in '70s-influenced songwriting and high desert imagery. Carruthers is a New Mexico singer-songwriter with roots in Albuquerque. Roush is a guitarist and producer based in Nashville. Their songs move between gentle folk and driving Americana. The duo recorded their debut at a studio in the Southwest. The Woodshop in St. Elmo is a close, intimate room where their harmonies carry well. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for tickets.

title: Mike Zito
description: Blues-rock guitarist Mike Zito plays The Woodshop Listening Room on December 2.
body: Mike Zito is a blues and blues-rock guitarist with a heavy, soulful touch. He has won multiple Blues Music Awards over his long career. His songs mix raw electric blues with roots rock. Zito's live show hits hard in the small room. He has recorded for Ruf Records and Forty Below Records, collaborating with artists like Walter Trout and Devon Allman. His biography includes time in both St. Louis and New Orleans, and both cities shaped his sound. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Nick Lutsko
description: Nick Lutsko at The Woodshop Listening Room on January 9. The Chattanooga comedian and songwriter plays indie rock in St. Elmo with Jordan Burchel and Randy Steele.
body: Nick Lutsko plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on January 9. The Chattanooga musician built a following online with viral comedy songs and absurd parodies. His albums lean toward psychedelic indie rock and sharp character studies. He plays multiple instruments and shifts between humor and honest reflection. Jordan Burchel and award-winning banjo player Randy Steele join the bill. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: OBELISK
description: Local drum and bass duo OBELISK at The Woodshop on September 12, playing SciCo fusion and hard jazz. Standing room show.
body: OBELISK is a local drum and bass duo that plays SciCo fusion and hard jazz. This one runs as a standing room show in St. Elmo. The pair plays original compositions built on interlocking rhythms and improvised sections. Their sound pulls from avant-garde jazz, math rock, and electronic music. The Woodshop in St. Elmo is an intimate listening venue with no barrier between the audience and the stage. Expect volume and precision in equal measure. The show fills fast. Check the venue for the door price and start time.

title: Robbie Fulks
description: Robbie Fulks plays The Woodshop Listening Room on March 31. The Grammy-nominated alt-country songwriter brings sharp writing and bluegrass roots to St. Elmo.
body: Robbie Fulks plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on March 31. The Chicago songwriter helped define alt-country in the 1990s. His 2016 album Upland Stories earned two Grammy nominations. He has released 15 records across a career spanning more than 30 years. Fulks mixes folk, bluegrass, and country with dark humor and sharp lyrics. His 2023 album Bluegrass Vacation leaned fully into acoustic picking. He is a strong guitarist and a funny, direct performer between songs. The listening room format puts his words front and center. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Roland Dixon
description: Roland Dixon at The Woodshop Listening Room on December 18. The Knoxville singer-songwriter plays weathered, literary roots songs in St. Elmo.
body: Roland Dixon plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on December 18. The Knoxville singer-songwriter writes weathered, literary songs about love, loss, and everyday absurdity. His sound sits near Tom Waits, Leonard Cohen, and old Appalachian murder ballads. He delivers the words with dark wit and plain honesty. Dixon has four albums, including the 2026 release Songs For Dogs. He is a familiar voice across East Tennessee and has played WDVX's Blue Plate Special. The small listening room suits his close, story-driven style. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Sherry Cothran
description: Award-winning Americana artist Sherry Cothran at The Woodshop on September 17, blending rock and soul influences.
body: Sherry Cothran is an award-winning Americana artist who folds rock and soul into her songs. She plays the small listening room in St. Elmo. Cothran studied at Berklee College of Music and has released multiple solo albums. Her voice sits in a powerful mid-range, and her live shows lean on raw storytelling. She has toured the United States and Europe. Reviewers compare her work to Lucinda Williams and Emmylou Harris. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Smells Like Nirvana: MTV Unplugged Tribute
description: Smells Like Nirvana plays The Woodshop Listening Room on January 24. The Chicago tribute band recreates Nirvana's MTV Unplugged set in St. Elmo.
body: Smells Like Nirvana plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on January 24. The Chicago tribute band recreates the Nirvana sound with no click tracks or backing tracks. The set pulls from Nevermind, In Utero, Bleach, and rare deep cuts. Frontman Paul Wandtke leads a raw, grunge-fueled performance. The intimate listening room fits the stripped-down MTV Unplugged style. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Sofia Goodman Trio
description: Nashville drummer and composer Sofia Goodman leads her trio at The Woodshop Listening Room on November 20.
body: Sofia Goodman is a Nashville drummer and composer who leads her own trio. Her music sits in modern, melodic jazz with strong rhythmic foundations. Goodman studied at Berklee College of Music. Her compositions draw on jazz standards and original work. The trio format keeps the arrangements lean and allows space for improvisation. The Woodshop in St. Elmo is an intimate listening room suited to small jazz ensembles. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Sun Records Tribute Show
description: Sun Records Tribute Show at The Woodshop Listening Room on January 2. Emerald Butler, Mario Monterrosso, Jhett Black, and Joel Beaver play the Memphis sound.
body: A Sun Records Tribute Show comes to The Woodshop in St. Elmo on January 2. The night honors the Memphis label that Sam Phillips founded in 1952. Sun blended blues, country, gospel, and rhythm and blues into early rock and roll. The lineup features Emerald Butler, Mario Monterrosso, Jhett Black, and Joel Beaver. Butler is a fiddler and songwriter who has recorded at Sun Studio. Black is an awarded, internationally touring bluesman. Monterrosso is an Italian guitarist and singer who tours worldwide. The small room puts these players close to the crowd. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: The DVL Revue - Motown Night
description: The DVL Revue plays a Motown Night at The Woodshop on October 17. A high-energy tribute to The Temptations, Elton John, and classic soul and rock.
body: The DVL Revue brings a Motown tribute to St. Elmo. The band plays soul, Motown, and classic rock hits from acts like The Temptations, Marvin Gaye, and Stevie Wonder. The DVL Revue is a Chattanooga-area group known for high-energy tribute sets. The Woodshop is a small listening room on St. Elmo Avenue. For Motown Night, the band leans into the full orchestra arrangements and call-and-response vocal style of the era. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: The Encore Sessions
description: The Encore Sessions at The Woodshop on September 2. A free benefit showcase for the Musicians Mental Health Initiative with local artists.
body: Local artists share the stage for a free benefit night in St. Elmo. The show supports the Musicians Mental Health Initiative and raises awareness of mental health resources for working musicians. The Encore Sessions feature a rotating lineup of Chattanooga-area performers. Artists play short sets and pass the stage. The Woodshop is a small listening room on St. Elmo Avenue. No cover charge. Donations go directly to the initiative. Check the venue's social pages for the full artist lineup closer to the date.

title: The Family
description: The Family at The Woodshop on October 9: four Muscle Shoals musicians - Dylan LeBlanc, James LeBlanc, Angela Hacker, and Bay Simpson - blending '70s folk-rock and soul, recorded at FAME Studios.
body: The Family brings together four Muscle Shoals musicians - Dylan LeBlanc, James LeBlanc, Angela Hacker, and Bay Simpson - for a collaborative set at The Woodshop in St. Elmo. Dylan LeBlanc is a singer-songwriter with releases on Rough Trade Records. James LeBlanc is a Nashville guitarist and producer. Hacker and Simpson are session musicians rooted in the Muscle Shoals tradition. Together the four blend Southern soul, country, and Americana. The small room on St. Elmo Avenue is well suited to this kind of collaborative performance. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: The Fox & The Flame
description: Chattanooga singer-songwriter Caleb Lange brings The Fox & The Flame to The Woodshop Listening Room on October 24.
body: The Fox & The Flame is the project of Chattanooga singer-songwriter Caleb Lange. His music blends folk and Americana with atmospheric production. Lange records and performs locally and has built a following on the Chattanooga music scene. His songs move between quiet introspection and driving full-band arrangements. The Fox & The Flame has played local venues and festivals and continues to grow beyond the region. The Woodshop in St. Elmo is an intimate listening room well suited to this kind of songwriting. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: The New Quintet
description: The New Quintet at The Woodshop Listening Room on January 16. A five-piece string band playing folk, ragtime, old-time, and early country in St. Elmo.
body: The New Quintet plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on January 16. The five-piece band honors traditional folk, ragtime, old-time, and early country. The lineup pairs guitar, fiddle, upright bass, clarinet, and lap steel, with shared vocals. Nicholas Edward Williams leads the group as a storyteller and musicologist. The band formed in 2020 and has toured across the Southeast. In 2026 they reached the quarterfinals on Season 21 of America's Got Talent. Their warm, acoustic sound fits the small listening room well. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: The Two Tracks
description: The Two Tracks bring bluegrass, Americana, and folk-rock to The Woodshop Listening Room in St. Elmo on October 15, 2026.
body: The Two Tracks are a husband-and-wife duo who lead a full band through bluegrass, Americana, and folk-rock. Their sound builds on traditional string band roots and extends into rock territory. The duo writes original songs and covers classic Americana material. Their live show moves between quiet moments and full-band arrangements. The Woodshop in St. Elmo is a small listening room where the full band still fits comfortably on the stage. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Thomas Cassell & Tim Stafford
description: Bluegrass players Thomas Cassell and Tim Stafford play The Woodshop Listening Room on December 17.
body: Thomas Cassell and Tim Stafford bring a bluegrass evening to The Woodshop. Cassell is a sharp young mandolin player and songwriter from East Tennessee. Stafford co-founded Blue Highway, the five-time IBMA Group of the Year. Together they play traditional bluegrass and original Americana in the close confines of the St. Elmo listening room. Stafford's experience in the bluegrass world brings depth to the pairing, and Cassell's writing adds fresh material. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Toronzo Cannon
description: Chicago blues guitarist Toronzo Cannon plays The Woodshop Listening Room on November 22.
body: Toronzo Cannon is a Chicago blues guitarist and singer on Alligator Records. He plays hard-driving electric blues with strong original songwriting. Cannon spent years driving a city bus in Chicago while building his music career on the South Side blues circuit. He signed to Alligator Records and released to strong reviews. His guitar work is aggressive and rooted in the West Side Chicago style. The Woodshop in St. Elmo is a small listening room where his sound fills every corner. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm. Check the venue for ticket details.

title: Tyler Ramsey
description: Tyler Ramsey plays The Woodshop Listening Room on January 21. The former Band of Horses guitarist brings fingerstyle indie folk to St. Elmo.
body: Tyler Ramsey plays The Woodshop in St. Elmo on January 21. He spent nearly a decade as lead guitarist in Band of Horses. He played on their Grammy-nominated album Infinite Arms before going solo in 2017. Ramsey writes fingerstyle indie folk with pedal steel and quiet, open arrangements. His latest record, New Lost Ages, came out in 2024. He builds pieces where melody, bass, and rhythm all come from one guitar. That kind of detailed playing rewards a small room. The close stage at The Woodshop fits his sound well. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: 5 Points 50 Bike Race
description: Chattanooga's oldest mountain bike race returns to Lula Lake Land Trust on Lookout Mountain, with 50-mile and 25-mile courses.
body: The 5 Points 50 is Chattanooga's oldest mountain bike race. Riders start at Lula Lake Land Trust and climb into the 5 Points and Durham Mine trail systems on Lookout Mountain. Choose the full 50-mile course or the shorter 25-mile option. A Kids' Fun Ride runs for younger riders. All proceeds support trail building and maintenance at Lula Lake Land Trust. Register in advance through the Walker Rocks events page.

title: 5th Annual Jeep Fest
description: The 5th Annual Jeep Fest brings off-road culture and vehicle displays to Chickamauga, GA.
body: Jeep Fest returns to Chickamauga for its fifth year. Owners show off custom rigs, off-road builds, and lifted trucks across the day. The event celebrates Jeep culture in Walker County, Georgia. The Kensington area of Chickamauga has become the host location for this growing annual event. No ticket required to attend and view the vehicles. Walk the event grounds and talk to owners about their builds. Chickamauga is about 25 miles south of Chattanooga. Check the Walker Rocks events page for the specific location, entry details for Jeep owners, and the full schedule of activities.

title: Bats, Beer, & Bluegrass
description: An evening of bluegrass music, cold beer, and bat watching at Fricks Cave Preserve in Chickamauga, GA.
body: Fricks Cave Preserve hosts one of Walker County's most unusual evenings - live bluegrass, cold beer, and watching bats emerge at dusk from one of the largest hibernating bat colonies in the Eastern United States. Fricks Cave is managed by The Nature Conservancy. The bat emergence is a natural spectacle - thousands of gray bats and other species stream out of the cave opening at dusk. The event raises money for bat conservation. Check the Walker Rocks events page for tickets and details. The preserve is in Walker County, Georgia, about 30 minutes from Chattanooga.

title: Beginagin Farm Arts & Craft Show
description: Arts and craft show with vendors, live music, and animals at Beginagin Farm in LaFayette, GA.
body: Beginagin Farm hosts an arts and craft show on its grounds in LaFayette. Vendors show and sell handmade crafts, and artists run live demos. The day also features live music, farm animals, and food. A classic car cruise-in rolls in alongside the show. Admission is free. Bring the family and spend the day on the farm.

title: Blue Gray BBQ
description: Blue Gray BBQ at the Gordon Lee Mansion grounds in Chickamauga, GA.
body: The Blue Gray BBQ brings a full day of barbecue to the grounds of the Gordon Lee Mansion in Chickamauga. Check the Walker Rocks events page for entry and details. The event features barbecue competition alongside public tasting. The Gordon Lee Mansion is a National Historic Landmark that served as a field hospital during the Battle of Chickamauga. The name refers to the Blue and Gray of the Civil War. The event takes place in Chickamauga, Georgia, about 30 minutes from downtown Chattanooga. Local pitmasters compete across multiple barbecue categories.

title: Center Post Pumpkin Patch
description: A fall pumpkin patch in LaFayette, GA with extended daily hours through late October.
body: Center Post Pumpkin Patch opens each fall on GA-337 near LaFayette. Families pick pumpkins straight from the field and enjoy seasonal farm activities. The patch runs daily from mid-September through late October with wide open hours. Bring the kids for photos, hayrides, and a full afternoon in the crisp Walker County air. LaFayette is about 40 minutes south of Chattanooga. Cash and card are accepted. Bring a wagon if you have one - rows get long.

title: Chickamauga Birthday Celebration
description: Chickamauga's birthday celebration at the historic Gordon Lee Mansion.
body: Chickamauga celebrates its birthday at the Gordon Lee Mansion. A community afternoon on the historic mansion grounds. Check the Walker Rocks events page for details. The Gordon Lee Mansion is a National Historic Landmark in Chickamauga, Georgia. It served as a Union field hospital during the Battle of Chickamauga in 1863. The mansion stands near the Chickamauga Battlefield and is part of the city's historic identity. The birthday celebration marks the founding of the city with community programming, food, and local vendors on the grounds.

title: Chilimauga
description: Chilimauga chili cook-off and street fair in downtown Chickamauga, GA.
body: Chilimauga is a chili cook-off and street fair in downtown Chickamauga. Cooks of all skill levels compete with family recipes and restaurant-style chili. The cook-off runs from noon to 2:00pm, and judges announce winners at 2:45pm. Buy a tasting ticket to sample and vote. Live music and vendors fill the street. The event raises money for the Gordon Lee Marching Trojan Band.

title: Christmas at The Barn
description: A festive holiday market at Raulston Acres Christmas Tree Farm in Rock Spring, GA.
body: Christmas at The Barn brings holiday cheer to Raulston Acres in Rock Spring. The evening gathering features local vendors, handmade gifts, and sweet treats. Live music fills the barn and Santa greets visitors. The farm is a family-run choose-and-cut Christmas tree operation. The event runs into the evening. Check the Walker Rocks events page for the full schedule and dates.

title: Enchanted Garden of Lights @ Rock City
description: The Enchanted Garden of Lights returns to Rock City on Lookout Mountain with millions of LED lights, themed trails, and holiday characters.
body: The Enchanted Garden of Lights returns to Rock City for its 32nd year. The event runs nightly from November 13 through December 31, closed only on Christmas Eve. Millions of LED lights cover the trails with themed holiday displays and interactive scenes. Visitors meet costumed characters along the way, including elves, a toy soldier, and Santa Claus. Gates open at 4:00pm, with last entry 45 minutes before close. Tickets use timed entry and sell online only. Check the Walker Rocks events page for current admission prices.

title: Enchanted Pumpkin Patch @ Rock City
description: The Enchanted Pumpkin Patch returns to Rock City on Lookout Mountain with carved pumpkins, fall decor, and family activities.
body: The Enchanted Pumpkin Patch turns Rock City into a fall wonderland from September 18 through October 31. Master carvers cover the trails with hundreds of hand-carved pumpkins and glowing autumn scenes. Families can walk the gardens, meet costumed characters, and enjoy seasonal food and photo spots. The event runs during regular Rock City hours. Check the Walker Rocks events page for admission and ticket details.

title: Kensington Rodeo Broncs & Bulls
description: Broncs and bulls rodeo night at the Kensington Rodeo grounds in Chickamauga, GA.
body: The Kensington Rodeo brings a Broncs & Bulls night to the arena in Chickamauga. The card features bull riding, bronc riding, roping, and barrel racing. Kids can try mutton busting, where young riders hold on to a sheep. Clowns and trick riders keep the crowd going. Food booths sell burgers, barbecue, ice cream, and fry bread. Local charities run stands on the grounds.

title: Kensington Rodeo
description: Two-day rodeo event in Chickamauga, GA at the Kensington Rodeo grounds.
body: The Kensington Rodeo runs two full days - September 5 and 6 - at the rodeo grounds in Chickamauga. Check the Walker Rocks events page for tickets and details. The event features bull riding, barrel racing, steer wrestling, and team roping. Local and regional competitors participate across multiple events over the weekend. The Kensington Rodeo is a traditional community event in Walker County, Georgia. Concessions and vendors set up around the grounds. This is about a 30-minute drive from downtown Chattanooga and draws a crowd from across the North Georgia and Southeast Tennessee region.

title: Macbeth at Mars Theater
description: A live staging of Shakespeare's Macbeth at the historic Mars Theater in LaFayette, GA.
body: The Mars Theater stages Shakespeare's Macbeth across several evenings in fall 2026. The venue is an intimate 72-seat historic theater in the heart of LaFayette's arts district. Actors bring the tragedy of ambition and downfall to a close-up stage. The run spans late September into October. Check the venue for exact showtimes and seating. The Mars Theater is at 207 N. Commerce St in LaFayette, GA. LaFayette is about 40 minutes from downtown Chattanooga. Tickets are required - check the Mars Theater website for pricing and dates.

title: Music at the Mansion ft. Chattanooga Symphony & Opera
description: The Chattanooga Symphony & Opera plays a free porch concert at the Gordon Lee Mansion.
body: The Chattanooga Symphony & Opera performs on the front porch of the historic Gordon Lee Mansion. This concert is part of Chickamauga's Music at the Mansion series. Admission is free for all ages. Bring a chair or picnic blanket and settle on the lawn. Music starts in the evening under the mansion's old trees. The Gordon Lee Mansion is in Chickamauga, GA, about 30 minutes south of Chattanooga. Tickets are required - check the CSO website for pricing and availability.

title: Music on Main Featuring Bryanna Fuquea & Lone Cove
description: Bryanna Fuquea and Lone Cove play a free live music night on LaFayette Square.
body: Bryanna Fuquea headlines this Music on Main night on LaFayette Square. She is a North Georgia artist who blends country, bluegrass, rock, and R&B into a cross-genre performance style. Lone Cove opens the evening. Music on Main is a free live music series in downtown LaFayette, Georgia, organized by Walker Rocks. LaFayette is about 30 minutes from Chattanooga. The events take place on the downtown square with a stage set up for the evening. No ticket required. Check the Walker Rocks events page for start time and parking information.

title: Scare on The Square
description: A free downtown LaFayette Halloween event with trick-or-treating and a costume contest.
body: Scare on The Square fills downtown LaFayette with Halloween fun. Local business owners line the street and hand out candy to children. A costume contest runs at the Downtown Commons for kids and adults. The event is free to attend. Joe Stock started this tradition more than 30 years ago. Families return each year for the trick-or-treating and the downtown atmosphere.

title: Songwriter's Series: Billy Dean
description: Grammy-nominated country artist Billy Dean plays the Songwriter's Series at McLemore Resort in Rising Fawn, GA.
body: Billy Dean brings the Songwriter's Series to McLemore Resort for one night. Dean is a Grammy-nominated country singer-songwriter from Quincy, Florida. He wrote and recorded hits like "Somewhere in My Broken Heart," "Billy the Kid," and "Only Here for a Little While." His warm, story-driven style fits the intimate stage well. The show runs into the evening on the mountain. Check the Walker Rocks events page for tickets.

title: The Green Eyes Festival
description: A cryptid and fall festival in Chickamauga built around the legend of Old Green Eyes.
body: The Green Eyes Festival honors the folklore of Northwest Georgia in downtown Chickamauga. The event centers on the local legend of Old Green Eyes. More than 50 arts, crafts, and food vendors line the streets. Attendees enjoy live music, a beer garden, battlefield trolley tours, and a scavenger hunt. Costumes and cosplay are encouraged, with a contest sign-up at the info tent.

title: Veteran's Day Parade
description: A community parade through downtown LaFayette honoring military veterans.
body: Downtown LaFayette holds its Veteran's Day Parade to honor those who served. The route runs through the heart of town at midday. Community groups, school bands, veterans organizations, and local businesses march through downtown LaFayette, Georgia. The event is free to attend. Find a spot along the parade route and watch the procession pass. LaFayette is in Walker County, Georgia, about 30 minutes from Chattanooga. Check the Walker Rocks events page for the specific start time and parade route. The ceremony following the parade typically includes a brief program and wreath-laying.

title: Walker County Fall Festival
description: An evening fall festival at the Walker County Civic Center in Rock Spring, GA.
body: The Walker County Fall Festival fills the civic center grounds in Rock Spring for one evening. The event brings autumn entertainment, activities, and community booths together. Families gather for a few hours as the weather turns cool. Expect food, seasonal fun, and local vendors. The festival runs from late afternoon into the evening. Rock Spring is about 25 minutes south of Chattanooga on US-27. Admission is free. Parking on the civic center grounds.

title: Farmers on First Sunday Market
description: Weekly Sunday farmers market at First Street Square in downtown Cleveland, TN - open 11am to 2pm.
body: Farmers on First runs every Sunday from 11am to 2pm in downtown Cleveland's First Street Square pavilion. Twenty-plus vendors show up weekly with locally grown and made goods. The market runs in downtown Cleveland, Tennessee, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. Local farmers, food producers, bakers, and artisans set up under the pavilion each Sunday. No ticket required. Free to attend. The market runs from May through November. Check the Farmers on First social pages for the weekly vendor list and any special market days or events.

title: Abita Brewing Tap Takeover
description: Abita Brewing takes over the taps at Mash and Hops Craft Beers in Cleveland, TN.
body: Abita Brewing takes over the taps at Mash and Hops for the night. Abita is Louisiana's original craft brewery and has brewed since 1986. The lineup runs to the Amber lager, the Purple Haze raspberry lager, and the Turbodog brown ale. The Wrought Iron IPA rounds out the heavier end. Try these Louisiana beers on draft and find a new favorite. Check the site for the start time.

title: Beer Share at Mash and Hops
description: Monthly craft beer social on the third Sunday at Mash and Hops in Cleveland, TN.
body: The Beer Share happens on the third Sunday of every month at Mash and Hops. Bring a craft beer you love, taste what others bring, and talk beer with people who take it seriously. The format is informal. Bring one bottle or can per person - ideally something you think others haven't tried. Mash and Hops is a craft beer bar in Cleveland, Tennessee, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. Check the site for the specific start time. The Beer Share is free to attend beyond the cost of whatever you bring to share.

title: Copperhill Brewing Tap Takeover
description: Copperhill Brewery takes over the taps at Mash and Hops Craft Beers in Cleveland, TN.
body: Copperhill Brewery takes over the taps at Mash and Hops for the night. This woman-owned brewery has brewed on the Ocoee River since 2018. The lineup runs from hop-forward IPAs to smooth, rich stouts. Come try their beers on draft and pick a few favorites. Check the site for start time. Mash and Hops is in downtown Cleveland, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. Tap takeover nights are free to attend - you just pay for your pints.

title: Creature Comfort Tap Takeover
description: Creature Comforts takes over the taps at Mash and Hops Craft Beers in Cleveland, TN.
body: Creature Comforts takes over the taps at Mash and Hops for the night. Come try their beers on draft and see what the brewery pours. Creature Comforts Brewing is an Athens, Georgia brewery founded in 2014 and known for clean, flavorful craft beers. Their lineup includes Tropicália IPA and Classic City Lager alongside seasonal and experimental releases. Mash and Hops is a craft beer bar in Cleveland, Tennessee, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. Check the site for timing. Tap takeover nights are free to attend.

title: Halloween Customer Party
description: Mash and Hops Craft Beers hosts a Halloween customer party in Cleveland, TN.
body: Mash and Hops throws a Halloween party for its customers on October 31. The shop fills with craft beer fans in costume for the night. Wear your best costume and grab a beer. The taproom runs its usual craft lineup and a relaxed crowd. This party thanks the regulars who keep the Cleveland craft scene going. Check the site for the start time.

title: Monday Night Brewing
description: Monday Night Brewing takes over the taps at Mash and Hops Craft Beers in Cleveland, TN.
body: Monday Night Brewing takes over the taps at Mash and Hops for the night. This independent brewery started in Atlanta in 2011. They lean hard into hop-forward IPAs, barrel-aged beers, and bright fruited sours. Expect pours like their West Coast IPA and berry sour on draft. Try a flight and pick your favorites. Check the site for the start time.

title: Schultz Brau Tap Takeover
description: Schulz Bräu Brewing takes over the taps at Mash and Hops Craft Beers in Cleveland, TN.
body: Schulz Bräu Brewing takes over the taps at Mash and Hops for the night. This German family-owned brewery opened in Knoxville in 2016. They brew authentic old-world lagers and ales. The lineup runs to Helles, Munich Dunkel, Schwarzbier, and Hefeweizen. Come try their German beers on draft and pick a few favorites. Check the site for start time. Mash and Hops is in downtown Cleveland, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. Tap takeover nights are free to attend - you just pay for your pints.

title: Singles Night at Mash and Hops
description: Weekly singles social every Tuesday evening at Mash and Hops Craft Beers in downtown Cleveland, TN.
body: Mash and Hops runs Singles Night every Tuesday evening. Stop in, grab a craft beer, and meet other people in Cleveland's craft beer scene. Low-key, no pressure. Singles Night is an informal social event at the craft beer bar on 25th Street NW in Cleveland, Tennessee. No ticket or registration required. The bar pours a rotating selection of craft beers on draft. This is one of several recurring community events at Mash and Hops. Cleveland is about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga on US-11. Check the Mash and Hops social pages for the specific start time.

title: Tailgate Brewing Tap Takeover
description: Tailgate Brewing takes over the taps at Mash and Hops Craft Beers in Cleveland, TN.
body: Tailgate Brewing takes over the taps at Mash and Hops for the night. Come try their beers on draft and see what the brewery pours. TailGate Brewery has locations in Nashville and Chattanooga and brews a range of approachable craft beers. Their lineup typically includes IPAs, pale ales, and seasonal releases. Mash and Hops is a craft beer bar in Cleveland, Tennessee, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. Check the site for timing. These tap takeover nights are free to attend - you just pay for your pints.

title: Urban Chestnut Brewing Pint Night
description: Urban Chestnut Brewing Co. pint night at Mash and Hops Craft Beers in Cleveland, TN on Thursday, November 19.
body: Urban Chestnut Brewing Co. pours its beers at Mash and Hops on Thursday, November 19. The St. Louis brewery brews true-to-style German lagers and wheat beers. Its flagship Zwickel is an unfiltered Kellerbier that drinks smooth and bready. Schnickelfritz is a Bavarian Weissbier with notes of clove, banana, and nutmeg. Pint nights run from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m. Stop in to try these German-style beers on draft. Check the Mash and Hops site for pricing and the tap list.

title: Yazoo Brewing Night
description: Yazoo Brewing pours its Nashville craft beers at Mash and Hops Craft Beers in Cleveland, TN.
body: Yazoo Brewing brings its beers to Mash and Hops for the night. Yazoo started in Nashville in 2003 and helped shape the Tennessee craft scene. The brewery runs a wide range of styles. Expect pale ales, the Dos Perros brown, the Daddy-O pilsner, and the Hefeweizen. Try the lineup on draft and pick your favorites. Check the site for the start time.

title: Rooted Night Market
description: The November market leans cozy - handmade goods, warm drinks, and a slower pace as the season winds down.
body: Rooted Night Market is a free monthly outdoor market hosted by Take Root Studio in Cleveland on the first Saturday of each month. Local artisans, wellness vendors, and food makers set up for an evening of community shopping. Take Root Studio is a wellness and creative space in Cleveland, Tennessee, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. The night market runs outdoors in the warmer months and may move inside in colder weather. No ticket required. Check the Take Root Studio social pages for the specific vendor list and any entertainment or programming during the event.

title: Rooted Night Market
