title: Karaoke at The Diving Mouse
description: Karaoke every Wednesday starting at 4:30pm at The Diving Mouse in Cleveland, TN.
body: Karaoke every Wednesday at The Diving Mouse starting at 4:30pm. Cleveland's go-to midweek night out - smoke-free bar, covered patio, and a stage that's yours for a song. The Diving Mouse is a bar in Cleveland, Tennessee, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. The karaoke format covers a large song library across all genres and decades. No ticket required. Walk in and add your name to the list. The covered outdoor patio gives the venue extra capacity on busy karaoke nights. Check the social pages for any updates to the weekly schedule.

title: Live Music at The Diving Mouse
description: Live music every Friday and Saturday starting at 4:30pm at The Diving Mouse in Cleveland, TN.
body: Live music every Friday and Saturday at The Diving Mouse starting at 4:30pm. Local and regional acts on a real stage, with a full bar and covered patio out back. The Diving Mouse is a bar in Cleveland, Tennessee, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. The venue hosts live music most weekends with rotating acts covering rock, country, Americana, and blues. No ticket required for most shows - check the venue social pages for any cover charge on special events. The covered patio adds outdoor space when the weather cooperates.

title: Open Mic at The Diving Mouse
description: Open mic every Thursday evening at The Diving Mouse in Cleveland, TN.
body: Open mic every Thursday at The Diving Mouse. New musicians and returning performers welcome - sign up and take the stage. Starts at 4:30pm. The Diving Mouse is a bar in Cleveland, Tennessee, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. The open mic format is relaxed and supportive. Performers sign up on arrival. All instruments and styles welcome. No ticket required. The bar serves drinks and has a covered outdoor patio. Open mic nights at The Diving Mouse have become a consistent gathering point for musicians in the Cleveland area.

title: Singo at The Diving Mouse
description: Music bingo every Tuesday at The Diving Mouse in Cleveland, TN - mark off songs as they play.
body: Singo is music bingo - you mark off songs as they play instead of numbers. Every Tuesday at The Diving Mouse starting at 4:30pm. Free to play, open to everyone. The Diving Mouse is a bar in Cleveland, Tennessee, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. Singo runs at venues across the country and has a large library of songs. The game is easy to pick up and works well for groups. No ticket required. Walk in and grab a card. Check the Diving Mouse social pages for any updates to the weekly schedule or themed Singo nights.

title: School of Music Christmas Concert - Southern Adventist University
description: Free Christmas concerts from the SAU School of Music, held twice each December in Collegedale.
body: The SAU School of Music Christmas Concert runs twice in December - December 5 at the Iles P.E. Center (8:00pm) and December 12 at Collegedale Church (7:30pm). Both performances are free and open to the public. The concert features the School of Music's choral and instrumental ensembles performing traditional and contemporary holiday music. This is one of the most attended events in the SAU music calendar. No ticket is required. The Iles P.E. Center and Collegedale Church are both on the SAU campus in Collegedale, about 30 minutes east of Chattanooga.

title: Annual Christmas Tree Lighting - Annie Moses Band
description: Southern Adventist University's Annual Christmas Tree Lighting featuring the Annie Moses Band in Collegedale, TN.
venue: Iles P.E. Center, Southern Adventist University
body: The Annual Christmas Tree Lighting at Southern Adventist University features a live performance by the Annie Moses Band - a Nashville-based classical ensemble that blends classical music training with contemporary arrangements. The Annie Moses Band has toured nationally and appeared on major television programs. The event is free and open to the public on the SAU campus in Collegedale. No ticket required. Collegedale Church or an outdoor campus location typically hosts the lighting. Check the SAU website for the specific location and start time. The evening includes holiday music and the official campus tree lighting ceremony.

title: Concerto Competition Live Finals - Southern Adventist University
description: The SAU Concerto Competition live finals at Collegedale Church. Free and open to the public.
body: Student soloists compete in the live finals of the SAU Concerto Competition at Collegedale Church. Winners earn the chance to perform with the Symphony Orchestra. The competition is open to instrumentalists and vocalists from the SAU School of Music. Finals are judged by a panel of faculty and guest adjudicators. The event is free and open to the public. No ticket required. Collegedale Church is on the SAU campus. The competition final is both a performance event and a high-stakes academic milestone for the competing students. Check the SAU website for the start time.

title: Constellate: Early Music Concert - Southern Adventist University
description: Constellate, a student early music ensemble, performs free in Ackerman Auditorium at Southern Adventist University.
body: Constellate is a student ensemble at Southern Adventist University that performs early music. This free concert features music from the 1600s. The program includes Telemann's Suite Bizarre, Biber's Battalia, English viol consorts, and anonymous French dances. Student Alison Menzmer directs the group. The concert takes place in Ackerman Auditorium and streams live for remote viewers. Southern Adventist University is in Collegedale, about 20 minutes east of downtown Chattanooga. Parking is free on campus. No tickets required.

title: Evensong at Southern Adventist University
description: Free weekly music series from the Southern Adventist University School of Music at Collegedale Church.
body: Evensong is a free public music series hosted by the Southern Adventist University School of Music at Collegedale Church. Each week features a different ensemble, soloist, or instrumental group from the school. The format follows the tradition of vespers and evening worship music, blending sacred and classical repertoire. No ticket is required. Collegedale Church is on the SAU campus. The series runs through the academic year on Sunday evenings. Check the SAU School of Music website for the specific performers and program for each week.

title: General Recital #1 - Southern Adventist University
description: Free general student recital from the SAU School of Music in Ackerman Auditorium.
body: SAU School of Music students perform in a general recital at Ackerman Auditorium. Free and open to the public. A relaxed evening to hear the school's performers in a low-stakes recital setting. This is the first general recital of the semester. The program rotates through singers, pianists, and instrumentalists from across the music program. No ticket required. Ackerman Auditorium is on the SAU campus in Collegedale. Check the SAU School of Music website for the start time and program. These recitals typically run 60 to 90 minutes.

title: General Recital #2 - Southern Adventist University
description: Free general student recital from the SAU School of Music in Ackerman Auditorium.
body: SAU School of Music students perform in a general recital at Ackerman Auditorium. Free and open to the public. A relaxed evening to hear the school's performers in a low-stakes recital setting. The program rotates through singers, pianists, and instrumentalists from across the music program. No ticket required. Ackerman Auditorium is on the SAU campus in Collegedale, about 30 minutes east of Chattanooga. Check the SAU School of Music website for the specific start time and program. These recitals typically run 60 to 90 minutes.

title: General Recital #3 - Southern Adventist University
description: Free general student recital from the SAU School of Music in Ackerman Auditorium.
body: SAU School of Music students perform in a general recital at Ackerman Auditorium. Free and open to the public. A relaxed evening to hear the school's performers in a low-stakes recital setting. General recitals rotate through singers, pianists, instrumentalists, and small ensembles from across the music program. No ticket required. Ackerman Auditorium is on the SAU campus in Collegedale. Check the SAU School of Music website for the start time and program. These recitals typically run 60 to 90 minutes and are a good way to discover student musicians early in their careers.

title: General Recital #4 - Southern Adventist University
description: Free general student recital from the SAU School of Music in Ackerman Auditorium.
body: SAU School of Music students perform in a general recital at Ackerman Auditorium. Free and open to the public. A relaxed evening to hear the school's performers in a low-stakes recital setting. General recitals give students performance experience outside of juries and formal concerts. The program rotates through singers, pianists, instrumentalists, and ensembles. No ticket required. Ackerman Auditorium is on the SAU campus in Collegedale. Check the SAU School of Music website for the specific start time and program details. These recitals typically run 60 to 90 minutes.

title: Guest Recital: Peter Westerbrink, Organ - Southern Adventist University
description: Dutch concert organist Peter Westerbrink performs a free guest recital at Collegedale Church.
body: Dutch organist Peter Westerbrink plays a free guest recital at Collegedale Church. Westerbrink has served as organist of the Der Aa-kerk in Groningen since 1992. He specializes in North German Baroque organ music and performs across Europe, South America, and the United States. The concert is open to the public and streams live for anyone who cannot attend in person.

title: Honor Choir Festival Concert - Southern Adventist University
description: Free Honor Choir Festival concert at Collegedale Church to close the SAU music festival.
body: The Honor Choir Festival closes with a full concert at Collegedale Church. Student singers perform the works prepared during the festival. High school choral singers from across the region spend the day on campus before this final performance. Free and open to the public. The concert is typically the same evening as the festival day. The SAU Honor Choir Festival is an annual event that draws strong singers from across the Southeast. Check the SAU School of Music website for the program and start time. Collegedale Church is on the SAU campus.

title: Honor Choir Music Festival - Southern Adventist University
description: The SAU Honor Choir Music Festival runs all day across the Collegedale campus. Free and open to the public.
body: The Honor Choir Music Festival brings student singers to the SAU campus for a full day of rehearsals and workshops. Events run at various times and locations across campus. High school choral singers from across the region audition for spots in the honor choir. The day culminates in a final rehearsal and concert. The festival gives participants a chance to sing alongside peers from other schools under a guest conductor. Check the SAU School of Music website for the schedule and specific venues. The final concert is free and open to the public.

title: Horn Ensemble Concert - Southern Adventist University
description: Free Horn Ensemble concert from the SAU School of Music in Ackerman Auditorium.
body: The SAU Horn Ensemble performs at Ackerman Auditorium. Free and open to the public. An afternoon of brass music from the School of Music. The horn ensemble is a chamber group drawn from the SAU music program. French horns blend in ways that reward close listening - the overtones and harmonics stack differently than other brass instruments. Ackerman Auditorium is the main performance hall at Southern Adventist University in Collegedale. No ticket is required. Check the SAU School of Music website for the specific program, start time, and performer roster.

title: Pops Concert - Southern Adventist University
description: The SAU School of Music presents its annual Pops Concert at the Iles P.E. Center, featuring the Wind Symphony, Jazz Ensemble, and Steel Band.
body: The Southern Adventist University School of Music presents its annual Pops Concert at the Iles P.E. Center. This lively evening brings together the Wind Symphony, Jazz Ensemble, and Steel Band for an accessible program of popular and orchestral favorites. Each year carries a fresh theme, mixing classical showpieces with jazz standards and steel drum grooves. The concert is free and open to the public. The event is also livestreamed for those who cannot attend in person. No registration is needed.

title: Premiere Jazz Orchestra Concert - Southern Adventist University
description: The SAU Premiere Jazz Orchestra performs a free concert at Ackerman Auditorium in Collegedale.
body: The Premiere Jazz Orchestra is a student big band from the SAU School of Music. The concert runs at Ackerman Auditorium on campus. The program features jazz standards, swing arrangements, and big band charts. Students fill the brass, reed, and rhythm sections. The concert is free and open to the public. No registration is required. Doors open before the 7:30pm start.

title: President's Honors Concert - Southern Adventist University
description: Free President's Honors Concert from the SAU School of Music in Ackerman Auditorium.
body: The President's Honors Concert showcases top SAU music students at Ackerman Auditorium. Free and open to the public. An afternoon spotlighting the school's strongest performers across instruments and voice. Students are selected by faculty for this honor. The concert features soloists and small ensembles performing works from the standard repertoire. No ticket required. Ackerman Auditorium is on the SAU campus in Collegedale. Check the SAU School of Music website for the specific program and start time. The event honors student achievement at the end of the academic year.

title: Reflections: Piano Trio Recital - Southern Adventist University
description: A free piano trio recital titled Reflections at Ackerman Auditorium on the SAU campus in Collegedale.
body: Reflections is a chamber music recital from the SAU School of Music. A piano trio pairs piano with violin and cello. The program features classical trio repertoire in an intimate setting. The recital runs at Ackerman Auditorium on campus. Chamber music puts a small group of players in close dialogue. The event is free and open to the public. No tickets are needed for the 7:30pm start.

title: School of Music Choirs Concert - Southern Adventist University
description: The SAU School of Music choirs perform a free spring concert at Ackerman Auditorium in Collegedale.
body: The SAU choirs perform a spring concert from the School of Music. Student vocal ensembles share the program at Ackerman Auditorium. The concert features choral works across sacred and classical styles. Several choirs take the stage across the afternoon. The School of Music trains singers in vocal technique and ensemble skills. The concert is free and open to the public. The program starts at 3:00pm.

title: Steel Band Concert - Southern Adventist University
description: The SAU Steel Band performs a free concert of popular and classical arrangements on steel pans in Ackerman Auditorium.
body: The SAU Steel Band closes the spring semester with a free concert in Ackerman Auditorium. The ensemble plays on tuned steel pans, an instrument rooted in the music of Trinidad and Tobago. The program mixes popular songs with classical and Disney arrangements. Past concerts have featured hits such as "Don't Stop Believing" and "Under the Sea." Director Keith Lloyd leads the group, and several student soloists take featured turns on the pans. No ticket is required. Ackerman Auditorium sits on the SAU campus in Collegedale, about 30 minutes east of Chattanooga.

title: Symphony Orchestra Concert - Southern Adventist University
description: The Southern Adventist University Symphony Orchestra performs free public concerts each fall in Collegedale.
body: The Southern Adventist University Symphony Orchestra performs full concerts twice in the fall semester at Collegedale Church. Free and open to the public. The ensemble includes string, wind, brass, and percussion sections drawn from the SAU School of Music. The program covers standard orchestral repertoire from the Baroque through 20th-century periods. Collegedale Church seats several thousand and provides excellent acoustics for large ensemble performances. No ticket is required. Check the SAU School of Music website for the specific program and performance date. Concerts typically begin at 7pm.

title: Wind Symphony Concert - Southern Adventist University
description: Free Wind Symphony concert by Southern Adventist University's School of Music at Collegedale Church.
body: The SAU Wind Symphony performs at Collegedale Church. Free and open to the public. The ensemble is part of the SAU School of Music and performs multiple times through the academic year. Wind symphonies play original compositions and arrangements for large wind and percussion forces - no strings. The program typically includes one to two large works and shorter pieces. Collegedale Church seats several thousand on the SAU campus. No ticket is required. Concerts begin at 7pm unless otherwise noted. Check the SAU School of Music website for the specific program and performance date.

title: Christmas on the Square
description: Holiday shopping, handmade gifts, and the community tree lighting at 6pm in downtown Cleveland, TN.
body: Downtown Cleveland kicks off the holiday season with local vendors selling handmade goods, art, and gifts. Santa shows up in the afternoon and the community tree lighting closes the evening. Christmas on the Square is an annual event in downtown Cleveland, Tennessee, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. Local businesses and artisans set up along the downtown square. The tree lighting is the main community gathering moment of the event. Free to attend. Check the MainStreet Cleveland website for the specific vendor list, Santa arrival time, and tree lighting schedule.

title: Cleveland Christmas Parade
description: Cleveland's annual Christmas Parade with over 200 floats through downtown Cleveland, TN.
body: Over 200 floats work their way through downtown Cleveland starting at 6pm. One of the bigger small-city parades in the region - worth the drive up if you have kids along. The Cleveland Christmas Parade is an annual December tradition in downtown Cleveland, Tennessee, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. The parade draws marching bands, decorated floats, community organizations, and Santa Claus. Free to attend. Find a spot along the route early for the best view. Check the City of Cleveland or MainStreet Cleveland website for the specific route and start location.

title: Cleveland Apple Festival
description: Two-day fall festival in Cleveland, TN celebrating the apple harvest with food, vendors, and live music.
body: Two days of fall festival in downtown Cleveland. Apple-themed food, local vendors, live music, and the kind of crowd that shows up in flannels and stays all afternoon. The Cleveland Apple Festival is an annual community event in downtown Cleveland, Tennessee, about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. The festival draws vendors and visitors from across the region. Live music runs on a main stage through both days. Check the MainStreet Cleveland or Cleveland Apple Festival website for the specific dates, vendor list, and performance schedule. Free to attend.

title: Community Tree Lighting
description: Downtown Cleveland lights the community Christmas tree at 6pm at the corner of Broad and First Street.
body: The Community Tree Lighting closes out Christmas on the Square in downtown Cleveland. The town gathers at the corner of Broad and First Street to light the community Christmas tree at 6pm. It marks the start of the local holiday season. The lighting is free, outdoors, and open to everyone. Bring the family and stay warm. Cleveland is about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga on US-11. Parking in the downtown square area is free.

title: MainStreet Cruise-In - October
description: The final MainStreet Cruise-In of the year in downtown Cleveland, TN.
body: Last one of the season. The fall light makes for good photos and the weather usually cooperates. Downtown Cleveland is an easy 30-minute drive from Chattanooga. The MainStreet Cruise-In is a monthly car show on the downtown square in Cleveland, Tennessee. Classic cars, trucks, and hot rods park along the square while owners talk shop with passersby. The event is free to attend. No ticket required. Check the MainStreet Cleveland website for start and end times. October marks the last show before winter. Expect a strong turnout from regulars who have been showing all season.

title: Farmers on First
description: Cleveland's Sunday grocery market at First Street Square with 20-plus local farmers and food artisans.
body: Farmers on First runs every Sunday in downtown Cleveland. The market fills the grassy First Street Square from 11am to 2pm. More than 20 local vendors sell fresh produce, baked goods, bread, chocolate, tea, and handmade artisan items. Shop straight from the farmers and food makers who grew or made it. Downtown Cleveland sits a short drive north of Chattanooga.

title: Halloween Block Party
description: Cleveland's 35-year downtown Halloween tradition with live music, Treat Street, food, and a costume contest.
body: Downtown Cleveland's Halloween tradition runs 35 years deep. Treat Street hands out Mars chocolate by the fistful, there's live music on the square, food vendors set up along the route, and the whole thing runs from 4 to 8pm. The Halloween Block Party is one of the largest trick-or-treat events in the region. Cleveland, Tennessee, is about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga. The event draws thousands of attendees across the four hours. Free to attend. Check the MainStreet Cleveland or City of Cleveland website for the specific setup and route details.

title: Small Business Saturday
description: Small Business Saturday in downtown Cleveland, TN - shop local shops and eateries the Saturday after Thanksgiving.
body: Skip the big-box crowds and spend the Saturday after Thanksgiving downtown instead. Cleveland's locally-owned shops and eateries open their doors for Small Business Saturday, so you can knock out holiday gifts and keep your money in town. Wander Courthouse Square, grab a coffee, and see what the local makers have out. Cleveland is about 30 minutes north of Chattanooga on US-11. Parking downtown is free on weekends.

title: Christmas at Lookout Winery
description: Spend Christmas Day at Lookout Winery in Guild, TN with local wine and wood-oven pizza.
body: Lookout Winery stays open on Christmas Day in Guild, TN. The family-owned winery pours its own local wine and fires Neapolitan-style pizza in a wood-burning oven. Gather friends and family on the mountain for a relaxed holiday meal. Doors open at 11am and close at 8pm. Settle in with a glass and a fresh pie along Hwy 41. Guild is about 25 minutes south of Chattanooga near the base of Lookout Mountain. No reservation required for the standard tasting experience, but check the event link for any holiday hours.

title: Labor Day at Lookout Winery
description: Spend Labor Day at Lookout Winery in Guild, TN - open all day for the long weekend.
body: Lookout Winery stays open late on Labor Day - 11am to midnight. A good excuse to make the drive out to Guild and wind down the long weekend with local wine on the mountain. Lookout Winery is a family-owned winery in Guild, Tennessee, on Highway 41 on Lookout Mountain. The winery makes wine from locally grown and sourced grapes and also fires Neapolitan-style pizza in a wood-burning oven. The drive from downtown Chattanooga takes about 30 minutes. No ticket required. Check the Lookout Winery website for any special programming during the holiday hours.

title: National Pizza Day at Lookout Winery
description: Celebrate National Pizza Day at Lookout Winery in Guild, TN with wood-fired pizza and local wine.
body: Lookout Winery marks National Pizza Day on February 9th. The family-owned winery bakes Neapolitan-style pies in a wood-fired oven. Cooks build each pizza with imported Italian ingredients. Pair your slice with wine the Bordogna family blends and bottles on the property. The tasting room sits above the Tennessee River in Guild. Doors open at 11am and close at 7pm. Guild is about 25 minutes south of Chattanooga near the base of Lookout Mountain. Drive up the mountain and settle in along Hwy 41.

title: New Year's Eve at Lookout Winery
description: Ring in the New Year at Lookout Winery in Guild, TN with local wine and wood-oven pizza.
body: Close out the year at Lookout Winery in Guild, TN. The family-owned winery pours its own local wine and bakes Neapolitan-style pizza in a wood-fired oven. Bring friends and family up the mountain for a laid-back New Year's Eve. Doors open at 11am and close at 7pm. Raise a glass to the year ahead along Hwy 41. Guild is about 25 minutes south of Chattanooga near the base of Lookout Mountain. Reserve a spot in advance - this is a ticketed event with limited capacity.

title: Thanksgiving at Lookout Winery
description: Spend Thanksgiving Day at Lookout Winery in Guild, TN with local wine and wood-oven pizza.
body: Lookout Winery stays open on Thanksgiving Day. Bring family and friends out to Guild for a relaxed feast on the mountain. The winery pours its own local wine and fires up wood-oven pizza fresh to order. Doors open at 11am and close at 7pm, so there is plenty of time before or after your own holiday plans. Skip the crowded restaurants and settle in with a glass along Hwy 41.

title: Valentine's Day at Lookout Winery
description: Spend Valentine's Day at Lookout Winery in Guild, TN with local wine and wood-oven pizza over the Tennessee River.
body: Spend Valentine's Day at Lookout Winery in Guild, TN. The family-owned winery pours wine it blends and bottles on the property. Share a wood-fired pizza built with imported Italian ingredients. The tasting room overlooks the Tennessee River for a quiet date away from town. Doors open at 11am and close at 7pm. Guild is about 25 minutes south of Chattanooga near the base of Lookout Mountain. Raise a glass with your sweetheart along Hwy 41.

title: Apero on Main
description: Apero on Main is an evening community gathering on Main Street in downtown Jasper, TN.
body: Apero on Main is an evening out on Main Street in downtown Jasper - drinks, conversation, and community from 5 to 8:30pm. Think of it as a downtown happy hour with a European name. Jasper Main Street organizes the event to draw people downtown on a weekday evening. Local businesses participate with specials and open doors. No ticket required. Jasper is in Marion County, Tennessee, about 40 minutes northwest of Chattanooga on US-72. Check the Jasper Main Street website or social pages for the specific date and participating businesses.

title: Chili on Main - Chili Cook-Off
description: Chili on Main is a winter chili cook-off on Main Street in downtown Jasper, TN.
body: Chili on Main brings a chili cook-off to downtown Jasper in winter. Jasper Main Street hosts this community contest on Main Street. Local cooks compete for the best bowl of chili. Visitors taste the entries and warm up on a cold afternoon. The event runs four hours around midday. Check the Jasper Main Street website for entry rules and tasting details.

title: Downtown Throwdown
description: Downtown Throwdown community event on Main Street in Jasper, TN.
body: The Downtown Throwdown brings the community out to Main Street in Jasper. Organized by Jasper Main Street. Check their site for details on what to expect. The event is a community street festival in downtown Jasper, Tennessee, in Marion County. Jasper Main Street runs the event as part of its downtown revitalization mission. Main Street Jasper is about 40 minutes northwest of Chattanooga on US-72. The festival format includes vendors, food, and live entertainment. Free to attend. Check the Jasper Main Street website or social pages for the full lineup and event hours.

title: FallFest
description: FallFest brings autumn activities to Main Street in downtown Jasper, TN.
body: FallFest fills Main Street with autumn activities in downtown Jasper. Jasper Main Street runs this community gathering each fall. Families come out for seasonal fun on the square. The event runs two hours in the afternoon. Expect local vendors and a relaxed small-town feel. Check the Jasper Main Street website for the full lineup and any weather updates. Jasper is about 45 minutes northwest of Chattanooga on US-41. Street parking is available along Main Street. Admission to the festival is free.

title: Festival of Lights & Christmas on Main
description: Festival of Lights and Christmas on Main light up downtown Jasper, TN for the holidays.
body: Festival of Lights and Christmas on Main open the holiday season in downtown Jasper. Jasper Main Street lights the Christmas tree on Courthouse Square. Trolley rides run along Main Street with volunteers dressed as elves. Santa and Mrs. Claus pose for photos with kids. Dickens-style carolers sing through the crowd. The festivities run two hours in the early evening. Check the Jasper Main Street website for the final schedule.

title: Foothills Festival
description: Two-day Foothills Festival in downtown Jasper, TN - a community gathering on Main Street.
body: The Foothills Festival runs two days on Main Street in downtown Jasper. A community event organized by Jasper Main Street with local vendors, music, and food. The festival marks a key moment in the downtown Jasper calendar. Artisans, food vendors, and local organizations set up along the main street corridor. Live music runs on a stage through the afternoon. Jasper is in Marion County, Tennessee, about 40 minutes northwest of Chattanooga. Free to attend. Check the Jasper Main Street website for the full vendor and entertainment lineup, dates, and hours.

title: Holly Jolly Trolley
description: The Holly Jolly Trolley rolls through downtown Jasper, TN for a two-day holiday weekend.
body: The Holly Jolly Trolley carries riders through downtown Jasper for a holiday weekend. Jasper Main Street runs the trolley on Main Street. Families ride together and take in the seasonal sights. The event spans two days in December. Hours run from late morning through the afternoon on both days. Check the Jasper Main Street website for boarding details and any updates.

title: Jasper Live - A Concert Series
description: Jasper Live is a free evening concert series on Main Street in downtown Jasper, TN.
body: Jasper Live is an evening concert series in downtown Jasper. Jasper Main Street books live music on Main Street through the warm months. Shows run from April into October each year. Each concert fills the square with music for two hours. Bring a chair and settle in for the night. Check the Jasper Main Street website for the full artist lineup and show dates.

title: 5 Points 50 MTB Race at Lula Lake
description: Mountain bike race at Lula Lake Land Trust on Lookout Mountain. Register via BikeReg.
body: The 5 Points 50 is a mountain bike race held on the trails of Lula Lake Land Trust on Lookout Mountain. Registration through BikeReg. Check the Lula Lake events page for details. The race format covers approximately 50 miles of trail and gravel on Lookout Mountain. The land trust protects over 8,000 acres. Riders register online and receive a course map before race day. The race draws competitive and recreational mountain bikers from across the Southeast. Entry fees benefit the land trust. Check the Lula Lake Land Trust website for the specific course details and registration deadline.

title: Lula Lake Open Gate Days
description: Lula Lake opens to the public on the first and last weekends of each month. Reserve ahead - $16 per visit.
body: Lula Lake is only open to the public on the first and last weekends of each month - these are called Open Gate Days. The land trust protects over 8,000 acres on Lookout Mountain including two waterfalls, miles of trails, and old-growth forest. Gate closes at 1:00pm so arrive early. Reservations are required ($16) through Eventbrite - no walk-ups allowed. Book up to two months in advance.

title: Trail Blazer Race at Lula Lake
description: Trail running race at Lula Lake Land Trust on Lookout Mountain. Register via UltraSignUp.
body: The Trail Blazer Race is a trail running event on the grounds of Lula Lake Land Trust. Registration through UltraSignUp. Check the Lula Lake events page for distances, categories, and entry details. The Land Trust protects over 8,000 acres on Lookout Mountain including two waterfalls, miles of trail, and old-growth forest. The race takes advantage of the trust's trail system. Entry fees benefit conservation work. Lula Lake is only open on select public access days, making race events a rare chance to run the trails. Check UltraSignUp for registration and pricing.

title: Autumn Harvest Market - Cambridge Square
description: Autumn Harvest Market at Cambridge Square in Ooltewah with craft vendors and food.
body: Autumn Harvest Market brings together unique and traditional craft vendors plus food options at Cambridge Square. Free to attend. Cambridge Square is a commercial and residential development in Ooltewah, Tennessee, east of Chattanooga. The fall market features handmade crafts, seasonal produce, food vendors, and artisan goods. The outdoor setting on the Cambridge Square lawn makes for a relaxed fall shopping experience. No ticket required. Check the Cambridge Square website or social pages for the vendor list, specific hours, and any entertainment scheduled during the market.

title: Fall Market - Cambridge Square
description: Fall Market at Cambridge Square in Ooltewah with food trucks, craft vendors, kids activities, and free bounce house.
body: Fall Market at Cambridge Square features food trucks, a craft fair, kids and adult vendor markets, a free bounce house, and free activities. Pay-as-you-go craft stations run through the event. Cambridge Square is a commercial and residential development in Ooltewah, Tennessee, east of Chattanooga. The fall market is one of the larger seasonal community events at the property. No ticket required to attend and browse. Check the Cambridge Square website or social pages for specific vendors, food truck lineup, entertainment, and event hours.

title: Live at Cambridge Square - Band Night
description: Live band performance on the Cambridge Square lawn in Ooltewah. Free outdoor concert.
body: Live band performance on the lawn at Cambridge Square. Free outdoor show from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Check their Facebook page for artist details closer to the date. Cambridge Square is a commercial and residential development in Ooltewah, Tennessee, east of Chattanooga. Live band nights draw families and neighbors to the lawn for free outdoor music. The acts rotate weekly and cover country, rock, and Americana. Bring a chair or blanket. Food and drink options are available from Cambridge Square businesses. Check the Cambridge Square Facebook page for the specific artist playing each week.

title: Saturday Night Live Music - Cambridge Square
description: Free live music every Saturday night at Cambridge Square in Ooltewah, late April through October.
body: Cambridge Square hosts free live music every Saturday night from late April through October. Local musicians play classic rock, country, jazz, and bluegrass on the lawn. Cambridge Square is a commercial and residential development in Ooltewah, Tennessee, east of Chattanooga. The acts rotate each week. No ticket required. Bring a chair or blanket and find a spot on the lawn. Music runs from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Food and drink options are available from Cambridge Square businesses. Check the Cambridge Square Facebook page for the weekly artist announcement and any changes to the schedule.

title: Butterfly Festival
description: A community Butterfly Festival at Willow Tree Farms in Ringgold, GA, with music and a butterfly release in Katie Beth's memory.
body: The Butterfly Festival returns to Willow Tree Farms in Ringgold. The day brings laughter, live music, and a butterfly release held in Katie Beth's memory. This community tradition means more than a fun day out. Families gather at the farm from 10am to 3pm. Admission is free and the whole community is welcome. Willow Tree Farms is in Ringgold, GA, about 20 minutes south of Chattanooga on I-75. Admission fees apply - check the event link for ticket details and parking info.

title: Cruzin' the Depot
description: Classic car, truck, and bike show on the first Saturday of each month in historic downtown Ringgold, GA.
body: Cruzin' the Depot brings classic cars, trucks, and bikes to Nashville Street in historic downtown Ringgold on the first Saturday of each month. Free to attend and open to all makes and models. The event draws collectors and enthusiasts from across North Georgia and Southeast Tennessee. Owners park on Nashville Street near the historic Western and Atlantic Railroad depot. The depot is a National Historic Landmark - the starting point of the Great Locomotive Chase of 1862. Check the Nothin' Like Ringgold social pages for start and end times.

title: Fall Junk Market
description: A fall market of antiques, junktiques, and vintage treasures in downtown Ringgold, GA.
body: The Fall Junk Market fills downtown Ringgold with antiques, junktiques, and treasures. Browse vintage finds and one-of-a-kind pieces from local sellers and regional vendors. The market takes place on Nashville Street in historic downtown Ringgold, Georgia. This is a one-day outdoor market event. No ticket required to browse. Ringgold is about 20 minutes south of Chattanooga on I-75. The downtown area is walkable and has a few restaurants and coffee shops nearby. Check the Nothin' Like Ringgold social pages for vendor details and the specific start time.

title: Festival of Flags
description: Over 2,000 flags and crosses honor Catoosa County's fallen soldiers across downtown Ringgold, GA.
body: The Festival of Flags fills downtown Ringgold with more than 2,000 flags and crosses. Each one honors a fallen soldier who called Catoosa County home. Volunteers raise the display from November 4 through November 18 for Veterans Day. You can view the tribute by walking or driving through the downtown streets. The flags stay up for two full weeks.

title: Front Porch Fridays
description: Free live acoustic music every Friday evening at Benton Coal in historic downtown Ringgold, GA.
body: Front Porch Fridays is a free live acoustic music series at Benton Coal in downtown Ringgold, running every Friday evening through October. Local and regional singer-songwriters perform on the porch in an informal, relaxed setting. No ticket required. The series is designed to bring the community downtown on Friday evenings. Benton Coal is on Nashville Street in historic downtown Ringgold, Georgia, about 20 minutes south of Chattanooga on I-75. Check the Nothin' Like Ringgold social pages for the weekly artist lineup and start time.

title: Kids Christmas Art Class
description: Kids in grades 3-6 paint a nativity scene and make ornaments with artist Lesley Austin in Ringgold, GA.
body: Local artist Lesley Austin leads a Christmas art class for kids at The Ringgold Depot. Students in grades 3 through 6 paint a nativity scene and make handmade ornaments. The class runs from 9am to noon. Tickets cost $30 and seats are limited, so book ahead. Children take home their finished art as a keepsake for the holidays.

title: Nightmare on Nashville St 5K
description: A Halloween night 5K and fun run through downtown Ringgold, GA, raising money for the Evitt Foundation.
body: The Nightmare on Nashville St 5K runs through downtown Ringgold and down a spooky nature trail after dark. Runners dress in costume and pass spooky characters along the course. Every dollar raised supports local children and families through the Evitt Foundation. The event starts at the Ringgold Market Pavilion and includes a shorter fun run with trick-or-treat tables. Ringgold is about 20 minutes south of Chattanooga on I-75. Register in advance - race-day registration may be limited.

title: Rabbit Valley Farmers Market Holiday Market
description: Holiday market with handcrafted gifts, baked goods, and seasonal treats from local makers in Ringgold, GA.
body: The Rabbit Valley Farmers Market hosts a special holiday market on Nashville Street. Local makers sell handcrafted gifts, baked goods, and seasonal treats. You can shop for presents while you support small vendors from the Ringgold area. The market runs from 11am to 4pm. Come early for the best selection of handmade items and fresh seasonal food.

title: Rabbit Valley Farmers Market
description: Saturday farmers market in Ringgold, GA with fresh produce, local meats, artisan goods, and homemade breads.
body: The Rabbit Valley Farmers Market runs every Saturday from May through October at 7484 Nashville Street in Ringgold. Shop fresh produce, local meats, artisan goods, and seasonal items from North Georgia farmers and makers. The market is free to attend. It draws a consistent crowd of regulars and visitors from across Catoosa County and the Chattanooga area. Ringgold is about 20 minutes south of Chattanooga on I-75. The market runs from 8am to noon on most Saturdays. Check the Rabbit Valley Farmers Market social pages for any special market days or vendor announcements.

title: Ringgold Down-Home Christmas Parade
description: Santa leads the Christmas parade with a tree lighting along the route in downtown Ringgold, GA.
body: Santa leads the Down-Home Christmas Parade through downtown Ringgold. Floats, lights, and holiday music fill Nashville Street for the evening. A Christmas tree lighting marks the start of the season along the parade route. The parade runs from 6pm to 8pm. Find a spot on the sidewalk early and watch the lights roll through downtown.

title: Ringgold Haunted Depot
description: The Historic Ringgold Depot transforms into a haunted attraction with a haunted house, hayrides, ghost tours, and live music each October.
body: The Historic Ringgold Depot turns into a haunted attraction each October. Walk through the haunted house inside the old train depot for scares and surprises. The event adds a hayride along the Chief Richard Taylor Nature Trail and ghost tours through downtown Ringgold. A bonfire, movie screenings, face painting, and live music round out the night. Local performers play throughout the run. Buy a combo pass to see the haunted house, take a hayride, and join a ghost tour together.

title: The Ringgold Playhouse Presents: Eurydice by Sarah Ruhl
description: The Ringgold Playhouse stages Sarah Ruhl's Eurydice, a retelling of the Orpheus myth, over six performances in September in Ringgold, GA.
body: The Ringgold Playhouse presents Eurydice by Sarah Ruhl, which retells the myth of Orpheus through the eyes of its heroine. The run covers six performances. Sarah Ruhl's play premiered in 2003 and has become one of the most-produced contemporary American plays. It follows Eurydice as she descends to the underworld and must choose between her husband and her father. The Ringgold Playhouse is a community theater in Ringgold, Georgia, about 20 minutes from Chattanooga. Check their website for ticket details and performance schedule.

title: SEC Watch Party
description: All-day SEC football watch party with three games, food trucks, and drinks at the Ringgold Market Pavilion.
body: The Ringgold Market Pavilion hosts an all-day SEC football watch party. Fans watch three games on one large screen from 11am to 11pm. Food trucks and drinks keep the crowd fed through every kickoff. Bring a chair and settle in for a full day of rivalry games. Admission is free and open to all SEC fans.

title: The Ringgold Playhouse Presents: An Evening With Edgar Allan Poe
description: The Ringgold Playhouse stages six of Edgar Allan Poe's most haunting tales on Nashville Street in Ringgold, GA.
body: The Ringgold Playhouse brings six of Edgar Allan Poe's most haunting tales to the stage. The program spans classics from The Tell-Tale Heart to The Fall of the House of Usher. This live reading suits fans of gothic horror and dark storytelling. The show runs from 7:30pm to 10pm on Nashville Street in downtown Ringgold. The Ringgold Playhouse is in downtown Ringgold, GA, about 20 minutes south of Chattanooga. Tickets are required - check the event link for pricing and show dates.

title: The Ringgold Playhouse Presents: Scrooge, A Year Later
description: Matt Lyle's comedy sequel to A Christmas Carol runs December 11-13 at The Ringgold Playhouse in Ringgold, GA.
body: The Ringgold Playhouse stages Scrooge, A Year Later, a comedy by Matt Lyle. The play picks up one year after Ebenezer Scrooge changed his ways. Three spirits return to teach him about balance and setting limits. The show runs December 11 through 13 at the Playhouse's new downtown location. Performances start at 7:30pm each night.

title: Trick or Treat in Downtown Ringgold
description: Local businesses in downtown Ringgold, GA, host an afternoon of family trick or treating along the historic streets.
body: Local businesses in downtown Ringgold open their doors for an afternoon of trick or treating. Grab a costume and a candy bucket, then go shop to shop along the historic streets. The event runs from noon to 3pm and welcomes families. Kids collect candy while the whole downtown turns festive for Halloween. Ringgold is about 20 minutes south of Chattanooga on I-75. Street parking is free along Depot Street. This is a family event with no admission fee.

title: Trunk or Treat at the Colonnade
description: The Catoosa County Library hosts its 7th Annual Trunk or Treat at the Colonnade in Ringgold, GA.
body: The Catoosa County Library brings its 7th Annual Trunk or Treat to the Colonnade. Children collect candy from decorated trunks while wearing their costumes. The event also features chalk art, bubbles, and dancing. It runs rain or shine, so families have a safe indoor backup. The Colonnade sits at 264 Catoosa Circle in Ringgold. The Colonnade is in Ringgold, GA, about 20 minutes south of Chattanooga on I-75. This is a free community event. Bring a bag for candy and arrive close to the start time.

title: The Ultimate Fall Fest
description: Family-friendly fall festival in Ringgold, GA with food trucks, vendors, live music, and children's activities.
body: The Ultimate Fall Fest at The Colonnade in Ringgold is a free family day with food trucks, local vendors, live music, and kids' activities. Runs 10am to 4pm. Free to attend. The Colonnade is a commercial and event space on Nashville Street in Ringgold, Georgia. The fall festival draws families from across Catoosa County and the surrounding area. Live music runs through the day on the outdoor stage. Kids' activities include games, crafts, and seasonal fall fun. Ringgold is about 20 minutes south of Chattanooga on I-75. Check the Nothin' Like Ringgold social pages for the full entertainment lineup.

title: Veterans Flag Fund Car and Tractor Show
description: Classic cars and tractors on display with people's choice judging on Robin Road in Ringgold, GA.
body: Classic cars and tractors line up for display and judging on Robin Road. Owners and spectators vote in the people's choice awards. All proceeds support the Veterans Flag Fund, which pays for Ringgold's Festival of Flags. The show runs from 10am to 5pm. Bring the family and browse the vehicles while you back a local cause.

title: Chili Cook Off at Rabbit Valley Farmers Market
description: Chili Cook Off at Rabbit Valley Farmers Market in Ringgold, GA - a special market day with competing chili makers.
body: The Chili Cook Off is one of Rabbit Valley's signature market days. Come taste and vote while shopping the regular Saturday lineup of local farmers and artisans. Free to attend. The event runs at the Rabbit Valley Farmers Market on Nashville Street in historic downtown Ringgold, Georgia. Local cooks enter their best chili and market visitors taste and vote for a winner. The market runs Saturday mornings from 8am to noon. Check the Rabbit Valley Farmers Market social pages for the specific date and any entry details for cooks who want to compete.

title: Family Fall Festival at Rabbit Valley Farmers Market
description: Halloween Family Fall Festival at Rabbit Valley Farmers Market in Ringgold, GA.
body: The final market of the season goes all out for Halloween with a Family Fall Festival. Costumes welcome. Local vendors, fall produce, and seasonal goods on the final Saturday. The Rabbit Valley Farmers Market runs on Nashville Street in historic downtown Ringgold, Georgia. This special final market adds family-friendly activities alongside the regular vendor lineup. The market runs Saturday mornings from 8am to noon. No ticket required. Check the Rabbit Valley Farmers Market social pages for the vendor list and any special programming. Ringgold is about 20 minutes south of Chattanooga on I-75.

title: First Responders Day at Rabbit Valley Farmers Market
description: First Responders Day at Rabbit Valley Farmers Market in Ringgold, GA - a special market day honoring local first responders.
body: First Responders Day honors the local police, firefighters, and EMS crews who serve North Georgia. Come thank them in person while you shop the regular Saturday market. The Rabbit Valley Farmers Market runs on Nashville Street in historic downtown Ringgold, Georgia. This special market day dedicates time and visibility to first responders from Catoosa County and neighboring departments. The market runs Saturday mornings from 8am to noon. No ticket required. Check the Rabbit Valley Farmers Market social pages for the specific vendor lineup and any special demonstrations or activities on First Responders Day.

title: Rabbit Valley Holiday Market
description: Rabbit Valley Holiday Market in Ringgold, GA - a special extended-hours market for the holiday season.
body: The Holiday Market runs outside the regular season with extended hours - 11am to 4pm. Local artisans and food vendors set up for holiday shopping in downtown Ringgold. The Rabbit Valley Farmers Market returns for this special winter edition on Nashville Street in historic downtown Ringgold, Georgia. Shop handmade gifts, local food products, and seasonal items from the same makers you see at the summer market. No ticket required. Free to attend. Check the Rabbit Valley Farmers Market social pages for the specific date and vendor list. Ringgold is about 20 minutes south of Chattanooga on I-75.

title: Rabbit Valley Farmers Market
description: Weekly Saturday farmers market in downtown Ringgold, GA - open May through October, 9am to 1pm.
body: Rabbit Valley Farmers Market runs every Saturday morning from May through October in historic downtown Ringgold. Local farmers, food producers, and artisans from the North Georgia and Southeast Tennessee region set up each week. Shop fresh produce, local meats, baked goods, honey, and handmade goods. No ticket required. Free to attend. The market runs from 8am to noon on Nashville Street in Ringgold, Georgia. Ringgold is about 20 minutes south of Chattanooga on I-75. Check the Rabbit Valley Farmers Market social pages for the weekly vendor list.

title: National Cornbread Festival
description: Annual festival in downtown South Pittsburg, TN every last weekend of April - food, music, and cornbread competitions.
body: The National Cornbread Festival takes over downtown South Pittsburg every last weekend of April. It's a two-day outdoor festival 30 miles west of Chattanooga with cook-offs, live music, vendor markets, carnival rides, and more cornbread than you can eat. South Pittsburg is in Marion County, Tennessee, on the Tennessee River. The festival has run annually since 1997. The cornbread cook-off draws amateur and professional entries judged across multiple categories. Admission is charged. Check the National Cornbread Festival website for ticket prices, the music lineup, and the full schedule of events.

title: Ketner's Mill Country Arts Fair
description: Annual two-day country arts fair at the historic Ketner's Mill in Whitwell, TN - 150+ artisans, live bluegrass, food vendors, and a working grist mill.
body: Ketner's Mill has been running this fair since 1977. Over 150 artisans set up across the historic mill grounds in Whitwell - pottery, sculpture, jewelry, woodworking, and more. Live bluegrass and country music all weekend, 20+ food vendors, sorghum molasses demonstrations, wagon rides, canoe rides, and a petting zoo. Runs two days, October 3 and 4. $8 admission, kids 8 and under free.
